title: Unreachable code in `src/optical_system.py` — silently uses the inferior physics path
body:
Lines **492–673** of `src/optical_system.py` contain *duplicate* definitions of `calculate_back_focal_length`, `_calculate_system_matrix`, `get_numerical_aperture`, `calculate_chromatic_aberration`, `is_achromatic`, `to_dict`, `from_dict`. They are indented at four spaces and appear **after** `return sys` inside the module‑level helper `create_triplet()` (lines 478–490):

```python
478  def create_triplet(focal_length: float = 100, diameter: float = 50) -> OpticalSystem:
...
489      sys.add_lens(l3, air_gap_before=5.0)
490      return sys
491
492      def calculate_back_focal_length(self) -> Optional[float]:   # ← nested, unreachable
...
673          return system
```

AST confirms this: Python parses them as nested `def`s inside `create_triplet`, after the function has already returned. They are therefore **never executed**.

The version currently used by `OpticalSystem` instances is the earlier `_calculate_system_matrix` at **lines 400–429**, which uses a **thin‑lens approximation** (one matrix per lens, `P = -1/f`). The unreachable replacement at **lines 508–561** is a **correct surface‑by‑surface thick‑lens matrix** (air→glass refraction, in‑lens propagation, glass→air refraction, gap). This is the implementation most downstream code (BFL, chromatic aberration, NA) really wants.

There are also **two `AchromaticDoubletDesigner` classes** (line 463 empty `pass`, line 676 full) and **duplicate module‑level `create_doublet` / `create_triplet` helpers** (467+478 and 797+802). Because the later definitions override the earlier ones at module level, callers get the full class and the second helpers — but the empty‑class + early‑helper pair is a trap for any tool that searches by definition order.

**Action:**
1. Delete the early stub `AchromaticDoubletDesigner` (lines 463–465) and the early `create_doublet` / `create_triplet` (lines 467–490) that carry the unreachable code inside them.
2. Promote the nested thick‑lens `_calculate_system_matrix` to be the real `OpticalSystem` method; replace the thin‑lens one.
3. Promote the nested `to_dict` / `from_dict` that handle `lens_lookup`; currently the shallower variants at lines 301–349 are used.
4. Add a test that locks in the thick‑lens BFL for a known doublet — the current test suite did not catch this.

nodes.title: fix: promote thick-lens ABCD matrix in OpticalSystem
nodes.body:
~180 lines of method bodies in src/optical_system.py were nested inside create_triplet() after its return statement and never executed. The stranded code included a correct surface-by-surface thick-lens ABCD matrix; the class was quietly using an inferior thin-lens approximation for BFL, NA, and chromatic aberration.

- Promote the thick-lens _calculate_system_matrix (air→glass refraction, reduced-thickness propagation, glass→air refraction, then air gap). Fix sign convention to the standard paraxial [[1,0],[-P,1]] so that BFL = -A/C stays positive for converging systems.
- Promote to_dict/from_dict to the richer variants: emit 'type' and a reliable lens_id; from_dict accepts an optional lens_lookup so shared Lens instances can be reused across assemblies.
- Add OpticalSystem.is_achromatic() helper.
- Delete the empty placeholder `class AchromaticDoubletDesigner: pass` and the early create_doublet/create_triplet stubs that carried the unreachable code. The real designer and helpers are now the only definitions.

Regression tests (tests/test_optical_system_matrix.py):
- single-lens EFL and BFL agree with Lens.calculate_* to 6 dp
- system matrix is unimodular (det M = 1) for a system in air
- cemented doublet has a positive BFL (would have silently regressed)
- doublet EFL lands within 10% of its design target
- to_dict / from_dict round-trip preserves focal length

File shrinks from 858 to 660 lines. All 39 pre-existing optical_system and ray-tracer tests still pass.

title: ~5,200 lines of dead tkinter code still in the tree
body:
`openlens.py` and everything in `src/gui/` use **PySide6**. But the repo still ships:

- `src/gui_controllers.py` — 4,468 lines, imports `tkinter as tk`.
- `src/lens_visualizer.py` — 768 lines, uses `FigureCanvasTkAgg` + `.pack()`.

Nothing in the active app imports them. They are imported only by the test files `tests/test_fix_removal.py`, `tests/test_gui_controllers.py`, `tests/test_visualization.py`. The Sphinx config in `docs/sphinx/source/conf.py:59` even mocks tkinter explicitly (`autodoc_mock_imports`), which is a tell.

Keeping them is a **major long‑tail maintenance cost**: most of the "16 bare `except`", "74 `print()`", "god‑class", and "tight coupling" findings below come from these two files. They also force both the Sphinx build and the test runner to know about tkinter.

**Action:** archive `src/gui_controllers.py`, `src/lens_visualizer.py`, and the three tests that target them to a `legacy/` directory (or just delete — history is in git). Revisit `setup.py:51`, which still exposes `openlens-cli=src.lens_editor:main` as a console script.

title: TIR (total internal reflection) threshold is wrong
body:
`src/ray_tracer.py:105` — the 2D tracer declares TIR when

```python
abs(sin_ratio) >= (1.0 - EPSILON)
```

which fires **before** the actual critical angle is reached. The physically correct check is `sin_ratio > 1.0` (with strict inequality; equality is grazing transmission, not TIR). The 3D tracer at `src/ray_tracer.py:861` does use `sin2_t > 1.0` — the two paths disagree. Harmonise to the 3D form and add a unit test for the BK7→air critical angle (≈ 41.2°).

title: Performance: ray tracing inside the optimizer inner loop
body:
`src/optimizer.py:278-288` calls `SpotDiagram(system).trace_spot()` for every merit evaluation. For the default settings this means:

- **Simplex:** ≈ 500 system traces per optimization run
- **Simulated annealing:** ≈ 1,000 traces
- **Genetic algorithm:** ≈ 2,500 traces
- **Monte Carlo tolerancing** (`src/tolerancing.py:174`): each trial also calls `deepcopy(self.nominal_system)` then traces — 100+ deepcopies × traces

There is no memoisation, no parallelism (synchronous on the main thread — see also §3.4), and `tolerancing.py` deep‑copies the full tree every trial instead of restoring perturbed parameters.

**Actions:**
- Cache merit values keyed by the variable vector.
- Replace deepcopy in `MonteCarloAnalyzer` with explicit save/restore of the perturbed scalars.
- Let the global optimizer sample in parallel with `concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor` (ray tracing is numeric and releases the GIL when numpy is used).

title: Stochastic algorithms never seed their RNG
body:
Neither `src/global_optimizer.py`, `src/tolerancing.py`, nor the stochastic tests call `random.seed()` or `np.random.seed()`. As a result:

- GA and SA results are different on every run.
- Monte Carlo yield estimates vary by ±σ/√N between runs with no way to reproduce a specific reported number.
- Tests cannot assert on optimizer output without huge tolerances; in practice they assert only that `result.success` is truthy.

Add a `seed: Optional[int] = None` parameter to `GlobalOptimizer.__init__` and `MonteCarloAnalyzer.__init__`, default to `None`, and pass `42` in tests.

### 3.3 GUI ↔ model coupling in the PySide6 layer

`src/gui/widgets/lens_editor.py:199–224` mutates the `Lens` model in place from widget callbacks and then directly calls back into the main window:

```python
self._lens.name = name
self._parent._update_lens_list()
self._parent._save_to_database()
self._parent._update_all_tabs()
```

The widget knows too much about its parent. A small step forward: emit `Signal(Lens)` from the widget and let `openlens.py` own the "save + refresh tabs" reaction. The `services.LensService` class already exists for this (see §5.3).

title: Threading: raw `threading.Thread` touching Qt widgets
body:
`openlens.py:346–380` (optimization worker) and `src/gui/tabs/tolerancing_tab.py:231–250` (Monte Carlo worker) spawn raw `threading.Thread(daemon=True, ...)`. Optimization is carefully routed back through a `Signal` (`opt_finished` / `opt_failed`), which is thread‑safe. The tolerancing worker, however, calls `self._parent._update_status()` directly from the worker thread — a Qt widget update from a non‑GUI thread. This is undefined behaviour in Qt; symptoms range from "nothing" to intermittent crashes under load.

Use `QThread` + explicit `Signal` / `QtCore.QMetaObject.invokeMethod(..., Qt.QueuedConnection)`.

title: Transaction atomicity in `DatabaseManager.save_assembly`
body:
`src/database.py:106–162` performs, in one `with` block:

1. `INSERT OR REPLACE` the assembly row.
2. `DELETE FROM assembly_elements WHERE assembly_id=?`
3. `DELETE FROM assembly_air_gaps WHERE assembly_id=?`
4. Loop: `INSERT OR REPLACE` each lens + `INSERT assembly_elements`.
5. Loop: `INSERT assembly_air_gaps`.
6. `conn.commit()`.

If step 4 fails mid‑loop, the `with sqlite3.connect(...)` context manager still commits what has already been issued (it only rolls back on the `with` body raising). You end up with an assembly row, deleted elements, and partial new elements — a broken assembly.

Wrap explicitly:

```python
try:
    cursor.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
    ... all steps ...
    conn.commit()
except Exception:
    conn.rollback()
    raise
```

Also — **no schema migration system**. Any future schema change will require manual `ALTER TABLE`s or a flag‑day rebuild. Consider a minimal `user_version` pragma + numbered migration scripts.

title: `try: from .x / except ImportError: from x` everywhere
body:
128 occurrences across 43 files. This pattern is what you write when you're not sure whether the module is being imported as part of a package or as a top‑level script. The cost is:

- Every import does filesystem work twice.
- Genuine `ImportError`s inside your own code are swallowed on the first try and get reported wrong on the second.
- Static analysis tools (pylint, mypy) go crazy.

Fix the packaging (you already have `setup.py`), run the app as `python -m openlens`, and delete all of them.

### 4.6 `services.py` is present but underused

`src/services.py` defines `LensService` / `CalculationService` / `MaterialDatabaseService` but most of its methods are bypassed:

- `openlens.py:123` and the widget handlers mutate `Lens` directly and then call `_save_to_database()` on the main window.
- `src/desensitization.py:156` and `src/global_optimizer.py:119,219` call `optimize_simplex(...)` directly despite `AGENTS.md` stating "always use `optimize()`".

Either delete the service layer or actually route work through it. Right now it is a stub that future readers assume is real.

title: Silent `except` hiding real failures
body:
`src/aberrations.py:361`:

```python
try:
    ...
except Exception:
    return 0
```

Spherical aberration *silently returns 0 on any failure*. That's worse than crashing — the UI will report a beautiful diffraction‑limited lens when in fact ray tracing blew up with a NaN.

The agent scan found **~16** similar handlers, with the worst concentrated in `lens.py`, `aberrations.py`, `tolerancing.py`, and (dead) `gui_controllers.py`. At minimum convert each to `except Exception as e: logger.exception(...); return None`. A `None` that propagates is far easier to debug than a plausible‑looking zero.

title: `Lens.__init__` silently corrects radii for a matching default
body:
`src/lens.py:103-106`:

```python
if (radius_of_curvature_1 == DEFAULT_RADIUS_1 and
    radius_of_curvature_2 == DEFAULT_RADIUS_2 and
    lens_type != "Biconvex"):
    self._update_radii_for_type()
```

If the caller *intends* to use `r1=100, r2=-100` for a plano‑convex lens (explicitly passing the same numbers that happen to be the defaults), the constructor silently overwrites them. Better: force callers to pass `lens_type=` with consistent radii and raise if they disagree, or add a `use_type_defaults: bool = False` flag.

body: `src/lens.py:59` and `src/optical_system.py:64` both use `datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M%S%f")` as primary key. title: Test Quality
body:
- Most tests are **smoke tests**: `result.success == True`, `len(result) > 0`, `isinstance(x, dict)`. They catch crashes but not regressions in physics.
- **No seeded RNG in stochastic tests.** Any test that exercises SA / GA / MC is inherently flaky — it either uses a huge tolerance or asserts nothing specific.
- **No convergence assertion on optimizers** — i.e. no test says "merit after ≤ 0.5 × merit before". Adding even one such test per algorithm would be high value.

title: Optimizer checks rim, ignores vertex collapse — designs inside-out lenses
body:
**Files:** `src/optimizer.py:254-260`, `src/analysis/plots.py:64-71`

```python
edge_thickness = lens.thickness - s1 + s2
if edge_thickness < min_et: merit += 1e4*(min_et-edge_thickness)**2
```

This is only rim thickness (under the `plots.py` rim-convention: `x2_edge=x1_edge+thickness`). Vertex separation `thickness + s1 - s2` is never checked.

Kill shot: `s1=-20, s2=+20, thickness=5` → `edge=45mm` passes, but `vertex=-35mm` — front vertex 35mm behind back vertex, lens inside-out. Optimizer rewards it.

**Fix:**
```python
center = lens.thickness + s1 - s2
if center < min_ct: merit += 1e5*(min_ct-center)**2
if center <= 0: merit += 1e8  # hard infeasible
```
Decide once whether `Lens.thickness` is rim or vertex distance — currently docstring says rim, every optics textbook says vertex.


title: Wrong root pick for meniscus + aperture-misses tunnel through system
body:
**Files:** `src/tracer_2d.py:190-194`, `src/tracer_2d.py:508-534`

- Root pick uses only `R_signed` sign (`min(valid) if R>0 else max(valid)`), ignoring whether the ray origin is inside glass. Fails for meniscus (both centers same side) and concave exits. 3D version does it right.
- `SystemRayTracer` reallocates `LensRayTracer(...)` per ray per element (pure overhead). On `not ray.hit` it sets `terminated=False` and propagates forward unconditionally — a ray that missed the aperture teleports to the next lens. `ray.hit` is also clobbered per element, `ray.n` left stale.

**Fix:**
```python
self._tracers = [LensRayTracer(e.lens, e.position) for e in system.elements]  # hoist
...
tracer.trace_ray(ray, propagate_distance=0)
if not ray.hit or ray.terminated:
    ray.terminated = True
    break  # never clear terminated
```

body:
**Files:** `src/gui/tabs/optimization_tab.py:422,450,512,534`, `src/validation.py:338-339`, `src/gui/widgets/lens_editor.py:166,180`

title: Validation has zero cross-parameter checks
body:
**File:** `src/validation.py:322-340,406-435,438-481`

- `validate_parabolic_sag()` checks finiteness + `|sag|≤100` only. No `sag vs D` slope guard (`2·sag/r`), no `sag vs thickness` self-intersection check.
- `validate_lens_parameters()` doesn't take `is_parabolic/sag` args.
- `check_physical_feasibility()` only looks at `radius1/radius2` — `sag=100, D=2, thickness=0.1` sails through.

**Fix:**
```python
def validate_parabolic_sag(sag, diameter, thickness, ...):
    r = diameter / 2
    if abs(sag) > 0.75 * diameter: raise ...  # slope guard
    if thickness + s1 - s2 <= 0: raise ...    # self-intersection
    if thickness - s1 + s2 < min_edge: raise ...
```

title: Simplex asphyxiation via `clamp()` → false "Converged"
body:
**Files:** `src/optimizer.py:39-41,372,412,424,436,449,508`, `src/analysis/plots.py:31`

Every simplex op + gradient step clamps to bounds. Hit the `±20` wall and all `n+1` vertices clamp to the identical bound point → `merit_range < tol` → `success=True, "Converged"`. Gradient at wall is exactly `0.0`. Same disease: `y_c=max(-half_d,min(y,half_d))` folds out-of-aperture rays back instead of vignetting.

**Fix:** don't clamp inside search; penalize outside:
```python
for var, v in zip(self.variables, values):
    if not var.is_valid(v):
        merit += 1e6 * (v - var.clamp(v)) ** 2
```
Log `n_clamped` per iteration; abort with `success=False` if `>n/2`.

nodes.body:
…vergence

Remove all 7 clamp() call sites in simplex and gradient search so out-of-bounds points earn a 1e6*(v-clamp)^2 bound penalty in _evaluate_design instead of collapsing onto one bound point with false success=True Converged.

- Add per-iteration n_clamped debug logging plus abort with success=False when a majority of vertices is stuck outside bounds with no merit spread; terminal success now requires best point inside bounds.

title: `optical_system.py` ABCD ignores parabolic, wrong thickness convention
body:
**File:** `src/optical_system.py:424-448`

Uses raw `lens.radius_of_curvature_1/2`, not `get_effective_radius_*()`. Parabolic doublet paraxial `f`/`BFL` diverges from `Lens.calculate_focal_length()`. Also propagates `d/n_lens` (reduced thickness, only valid for `(y,n·theta)` vector) in a `(y,theta)` chain — EFL/BFL off by ~`n`. Guard `if R != 0` treats `R=0` as no-power (should be invalid) and `R=1e11` as powered (should be flat per `geometry.py:30`).

**Fix:**
```python
R1 = lens.get_effective_radius_1()
if not _is_flat(R1):
    P1 = (n_lens - n_current) / R1
d = lens.thickness  # NOT d/n for (y,theta)
```

title: Paraboloid normal double-flip + per-ray inverse in hot loop
body:
**File:** `src/tracer_3d.py:149-216,241-318`

Spherical outward normal `(hit-center)` vs paraboloid gradient `(1,-y/R,-z/R)` have opposite base orientation, but the same `if R<0: flip; if back and R>0: flip` is applied to both — front parabolic `R>0` stays inward, back flips wrong. Masked today by `apply_snell:96-101` auto-flip + `abs()` Fresnel, but polarization basis `s=k×n` flips sign and tilted-transform cases break. **Fix:** outward-normal helper (`front ≈ -axis, back ≈ +axis` regardless of `R` sign), cache `_inv` in `_calculate_geometry`, single `AP = D/2 + 1e-9` constant.

title: 2D ray tracer selects the wrong sphere cap for concave first surfaces
body:
**File:** `src/tracer_2d.py:187-203` (same defect in `src/tracer_3d.py:171-183`)

```python
dist_sq = (ray.x - center_x) ** 2 + ray.y**2
inside = dist_sq < R * R - EPSILON
for t in sorted(valid_ts, reverse=inside):
```

**Problem:** the correct intersection is the cap that *contains the vertex* (left cap for `R>0`,
right cap for `R<0`). The `inside` test only picks that cap when the ray origin happens to be on the
correct side of the sphere. Rays start at a fixed offset (`RAY_START_OFFSET_MM = 100`), so for
`R1 < 0` with `|R1| < offset/2` the origin is outside the sphere, `inside` is `False`, and the
tracer returns the **far (left) cap** — a point that is not on the lens — then refracts the ray as
though it were convex.

**Repro (verified):** marginal ray at `y0=+15`, `R2=+100`, `t=20`, `D=30`, `n=1.5`, front-surface
intersection vs. the analytic sag:

```
 R1      traced_x    expected_sag   correct
 -40.0   -77.081       -2.919        False
 -50.0   -97.697       -2.303        False   <- 95 mm error
 -51.0   -99.744       -2.256        False
-120.0    -0.941       -0.941        True
+100.0     1.131        1.131        True
```

At the boundary `R1 = -50` the biconcave lens traces as a **converging** lens while the analytic
EFL is negative.

**Fix:** select the root on the vertex side rather than by inside/outside — compute both roots, keep
`t > EPSILON`, and prefer the root whose intersection `x` is nearest `cap_x` (`center_x - R` for
`R>0`, `center_x + |R|` for `R<0`). Apply to both tracers via a shared helper in `src/ray.py`.

title: 2D system tracer cannot trace any element with a concave first surface
body:
**File:** `src/tracer_2d.py:621-631`

```python
if i < len(self._tracers) - 1:
    next_pos = self.system.elements[i + 1].position
    if next_pos > ray.x:
        ray.propagate(next_pos - ray.x)
    else:
        ray.propagate(EPSILON)
```

**Problem:** the ray is advanced to element *i+1*'s **front vertex plane**, then asked for an
intersection requiring `t > EPSILON`. For a concave first surface (`R1 < 0`) the sphere spans
`[vertex + 2·R1, vertex]` and the surface is its right-hand cap — the ray is already past it, both
roots are negative, and the element is silently dropped.

**Repro (verified):** the app's own `create_doublet(100.0, 25.0)`. The flint element has `R1 = -62.0`.

```
EFL(analytic): 100.2297   BFL: 97.6936   -> focus should be at x = 3.75 + 97.69 = 101.44

  y0=-12.144 hit=False term=True  final=(3.721, -12.1444)  path=[-100.0, 1.273, 2.494, 3.721]
  y0= -6.110 hit=False term=True  final=(3.748,  -6.1103)  path=[-100.0, 0.316, 3.445, 3.748]
  y0=  0.000 hit=False term=True  final=(3.750,  -0.0000)  path=[-100.0, 0.0,   3.75,  3.75]
  y0= 12.144 hit=False term=True  final=(3.721,  12.1444)  path=[-100.0, 1.273, 2.494, 3.721]
```

Every ray terminates inside the second element. The 2D and 3D tracers disagree completely for any
system containing a negative element — which is most cemented achromats.

**Fix:** propagate to the next element's front *surface*, not its vertex plane. Add a
`_front_reference_x` to `LensRayTracer` (the leading point of the surface at the current ray height)
and propagate there, keeping `t >= 0`.

nodes.title: fix(tracer-2d): trace elements with a concave first surface
nodes.body:
The 2D system tracer advanced each ray to the next element's vertex plane before intersecting its front surface. A concave first surface has negative sag, so the whole surface sits behind that plane: landing there overshoots it, every sphere root ends up behind the ray, and the element was silently dropped. A cemented achromat therefore traced no rays at all
- the flint element follows the shared cemented interface, and every ray terminated inside it, making 2D and 3D disagree completely for any system containing a negative element.

Intersect each front surface from wherever the ray already is, as the 3D tracer does. The air segment is not lost: trace_ray credits it to optical_path_length from the actual start point, and the dropped vertex-plane point was collinear with the ray.

A front reference evaluated at the ray's current height is not a fix. The ray bends on the way across the gap, so it meets the surface at a different height than it did at the hop; overshooting by ~0.016mm on a 6mm gap is enough to push the root negative, which regressed four existing tests.

The cap tolerance moves to -EPSILON to match 3D, because a cemented interface is exactly where one element's back surface and the next element's front surface are the same sphere: the ray correctly arrives at t = 0. The 2D defect fixed in #359 was the deleted already_exited heuristic, not this filter; a root within 1e-10 of zero is a genuine "ray sits on the surface" hit.

create_doublet(100, 25) now traces 9/9 rays and agrees with the 3D tracer bit-for-bit at every surface vertex.

Fixes #292

title: STEP export writes every integer entity reference as a float
body:
**File:** `src/io/step_export.py:51-52`

```python
elif isinstance(arg, (int, float)):
    arg_strs.append(f"{arg:.6f}")
```

**Problem:** `add_entity` is called with integer entity IDs (shell ids, face ids, origin). STEP
requires these as instance references `#44`; they are emitted as bare reals `44.000000`, severing
every topology→geometry link. The nested-list branch 12 lines below (`step_export.py:56-65`) does it
correctly with `f"#{sub}"`, confirming the top-level branch is the outlier.

**Repro (verified):**
```
#1=CLOSED_SHELL('shell',(#10,#11));
#2=MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP('PCX',44.000000);     <- entity ref written as a real
```

No CAD system can open the file. `tests/test_step_writer.py:49` misses this by passing the
already-prefixed string `"#12"` instead of the int `12`.

**Fix:**
```python
elif isinstance(arg, bool):
    arg_strs.append(".T." if arg else ".F.")
elif isinstance(arg, int):
    arg_strs.append(f"#{arg}")
elif isinstance(arg, (float, np.floating)):
    arg_strs.append(f"{arg:.6f}")
```

nodes.title: fix(step): write entity references as #id, not as reals
nodes.body:
add_entity's top-level branch formatted every int and float alike with "{:.6f}", so an entity id passed straight back in became a bare real: AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D('global_axis',4.000000,1.000000,2.000000) and MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP('Untitled',44.000000). ISO 10303-21 has no integer type that means "entity id", so every topology-to-geometry link was severed and no CAD system could open the file. The nested-list branch already did this correctly, which is why the top-level branch was the outlier.

Mapping int -> #N wholesale is not safe, though: several attributes legitimately take integer values, and GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT carries a dimension exponent of 3 that would have become #3. The two cases are indistinguishable by type, so the id now carries its own meaning. StepRef is an int subclass returned by add_entity, which makes every id it hands back serialize as a reference wherever it is passed on, while integer literals at the call site stay integer literals. No call site needs to change.

Booleans also render as .T./.F. instead of 1.000000/0.000000 (bool subclasses int, so it is checked before it).

Adjacent fix in the same formatter: an already-written STEP token inside an aggregate was quoted again, so a shape representation's items came out as ('#47') - a severed link of the same kind, and pre-existing. Aggregate elements now go through the same rules as top-level arguments.

Verified over a 124-entity export: every #id resolves to a defined entity, and the only remaining forward references are #unit_mm and #application_context, which this exporter never defines - a separate pre-existing gap.

The existing coverage missed this by passing the pre-prefixed string "#12" instead of an id; six tests now cover ids, integer values, booleans, aggregates and link integrity.

Fixes #293

title: STEP string literals are not escaped
body:
**File:** `src/io/step_export.py:50` (and call sites `:389`, `:512`, `:535`)

```python
arg_strs.append(f"'{arg}'")
```

**Repro (verified):** `Lens(name="Bob's 50mm PCX")` produces
```
#3=X('Bob's lens');       <- malformed: unescaped apostrophe terminates the literal
```
The project's own reader (`src/io/step_reader.py:17,21-22`) expects `''` doubling, so the round trip
is provably broken. `&`, `<`, `>` in names are also emitted raw.

**Fix:** `arg_strs.append("'" + str(arg).replace("'", "''") + "'")` at `:50` and `:60`, and drop the
manual `f"'{...}'"` wrapping at the call sites so escaping happens in one place.

nodes.title: fix(step): escape string literals and quote them in one place
nodes.body:
A lens named Bob's 50mm PCX was written as
MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP('Bob's 50mm PCX',#46): the apostrophe closed the literal early, so the entity was malformed and so was every entity after it. No CAD system could open the file, and our own reader found no solids at all in a round trip.

Part 21 escapes an apostrophe by doubling it, which is what step_reader already expects back, so _format_text now doubles it and every call site stops wrapping its own quotes - roughly 80 sites, each of which would otherwise need its own escaping. Removing ' from the pass-through prefix set is what makes that safe: text is never pre-quoted, so a name that starts with an apostrophe is escaped like any other instead of being mistaken for finished syntax.

step_reader needed the matching fix. Its CARTESIAN_POINT pattern used [^']*, so an escaped label would stop the match and silently drop that point's coordinates; both patterns now accept a doubled apostrophe. The reader round trip goes from 0 solids to 1, with its name intact and 9 points recovered.

&, < and > need no escaping: they are literal in a Part 21 text file. Only the XML-based encodings require entities for them, and this writer does not emit those.

Output for names without apostrophes is byte-identical to before, verified by diffing a full two-element-plus-housing export.

Existing tests passed pre-quoted literals such as "'Name'", which encoded the old contract; they now pass plain text. Five tests cover doubling, the XML characters, leading quotes, aggregates, and the round trip.

Fixes #294

title: OpticStudio and SVG system exporters always crash, and truncate the target file
body:
**File:** `src/export_formats.py:197` and `src/export_formats.py:565`

```python
if elem.air_gap_before > 0:                                   # OpticStudioExporter
    ...
x_pos += elem.air_gap_before * scale                          # SVGExporter
```

**Problem:** `LensElement` (`src/optical_system.py:37-63`) has no `air_gap_before` field. Verified
`vars(element)` = `['decenter_y','decenter_z','lens','lens_id','position','thickness','tilt_x',
'tilt_y','tilt_z']`. Gaps live in `system.air_gaps`, rebuilt by `_rebuild_from_tree`.

**Repro (verified):** a 1-element system:
```
OpticStudio export_system -> AttributeError: 'LensElement' object has no attribute 'air_gap_before'
SVG         export_system -> AttributeError: 'LensElement' object has no attribute 'air_gap_before'
```

Aggravating: `open(filename, "w")` already ran at `:159` / `:517`, so a **truncated file is left at
the target path** — the user loses their previous export.

**Fix:** derive the gap from the system:
```python
gap = system.air_gaps[i] if i < len(system.air_gaps) else 0.0
```
Or add an `air_gap_before` property to `LensElement` computed as `position - prev_back_vertex`.
Also see T-32 (non-atomic writes).

nodes.title: fix(export): derive the air gap from the system, not a missing field
nodes.body:
Closes #295

## Problem

`LensElement` has **no** `air_gap_before` field — gaps live on the system as `system.air_gaps`, rebuilt by `_rebuild_from_tree`:

```
vars(element) == ['decenter_y', 'decenter_z', 'lens', 'lens_id',
                  'position', 'thickness', 'tilt_x', 'tilt_y', 'tilt_z']
```

Both the OpticStudio and SVG system exporters read `elem.air_gap_before`, so **every system export raised** — including the 1-element case, since the attribute is read on element 0 too:

```
OpticStudio export RAISED AttributeError: 'LensElement' object has no attribute 'air_gap_before'
SVG         export RAISED AttributeError: ...same...
   file left at target: 552 bytes (truncated)
```

## Fix

`_gap_before(system, index)` derives it: `air_gaps[i]` is the gap **after** element *i*, so the gap before element *i* is `air_gaps[i - 1]`. It returns `0.0` for the first element and for out-of-range indices rather than raising.

One helper serves both exporters, so the convention is stated once instead of twice.

Row counts are now `2n + (n - 1)` — two surfaces per element plus one flat `Infinity`-radius row per gap — and a gap row lands immediately before the lens it precedes, carrying the gap as its thickness.

## On the truncated file

The issue also notes that `open(filename, "w")` has already run by the time the crash happens, which is why a 552-byte stub was left at the target path above. I'm deliberately **not** fixing that here: it's the atomic-write work in #323, and reimplementing `src/atomic.py` in this PR would collide with it. Once #384 merges, these exports become atomic for free.

## Tests

21 tests. The module cannot even import without the new helper, so the before-state is demonstrated by the repro above rather than by per-test failures.

title: STL back-surface sign is inverted; a biconvex lens exports as a cylinder
body:
**File:** `src/stl_export.py:49-57`

```python
z_sag = (y**2) / (radius + math.copysign(math.sqrt(radius**2 - y**2), radius))
# Apply STL exporter's specific sign logic
z = z_sag
if is_front:
    if radius < 0:
        z = -z_sag
else:
    if radius < 0:
        z = -z_sag
```

**Problem:** `z_sag` is *already* signed by `radius` (`copysign` yields `+sag` for `R>0`, `−sag` for
`R<0`). The extra negation for `R<0` inverts it. Verified for `r1=+50, r2=−50, t=5, D=25`: back rim
`z = 6.588`, expected `3.412`.

`is_front` has **no effect at all** — the two branches are byte-identical duplicates (verified: same
output for `True` and `False`). Front and back profiles come out identical, so the "biconvex" solid
is a straight cylinder of constant 5 mm thickness. This is the 3D-printing path.

**Fix:** delete the negation entirely (the sign convention already lives in `z_sag`) and remove the
duplicated `is_front` branching, or re-add a genuine front/back distinction.

nodes.title: fix(stl): stop inverting the sign of a negative radius
nodes.body:
Closes #296

## Problem

The sag formula **already carries the sign** — `copysign` makes the denominator negative for a negative radius, so `z_sag` is `+sag` for `R > 0` and `−sag` for `R < 0`. That was followed by:

```python
if is_front:
    if radius < 0:
        z = -z_sag
else:
    if radius < 0:
        z = -z_sag
```

The two branches were **byte-identical**. So `is_front` had no effect at all, and the negation simply inverted every negative radius.

## Verified

For `r1=+50, r2=−50, t=5, D=25`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| back rim z | 6.588 | **3.4123** |
| front sag / back sag | +1.5877 / +1.5877 (identical) | +1.5877 / −1.5877 (mirror images) |
| edge vs centre thickness | 5.0 vs 5.0 → cylinder | **1.82 vs 5.0** |

Because both surfaces came out identical, the "biconvex" solid was a **straight cylinder of constant 5 mm** — the 3D-printing path produced a tube rather than a lens. Edge thinner than centre is the defining property of a biconvex, and it now holds.

The exported STL is unchanged structurally: same triangle count, same `84 + 50n` layout, `z` spanning 0–5.

## Note on `is_front`

Kept in the signature for API compatibility but documented as **ignored** — the shape follows from the sign of `radius`, and the back surface is placed by the caller's `z_offset` (= thickness). No external caller passes it.

## Tests

15 tests, **9 fail without the change**: the profile against the closed-form sag at every step for four radii, mirror symmetry between `+R` and `−R`, that `is_front` is inert, edge geometry for biconvex/biconcave/plano-convex, and that the exported solid's radius profile peaks at the equator instead of staying flat.

One test I wrote was itself wrong — I assumed `r1 == r2` yields a cylinder, but it yields a meniscus (two parallel surfaces, radius resetting at `z = thickness`). I dropped it rather than keep a test asserting something false.

title: Tolerancing tab run buttons connect to non-existent slots
body:
**File:** `src/gui/tabs/tolerancing_tab.py:550-551, 578-579`

```python
self._mc_worker.finished.connect(self._on_analysis_finished)
self._mc_worker.failed.connect(self._on_analysis_failed)
self._inv_worker.finished.connect(self._on_analysis_finished)
self._inv_worker.failed.connect(self._on_analysis_failed)
```

`TolerancingTab` defines **neither** method. Grep finds 4 connect sites, 0 definitions.

**User-visible failure:** click "Run Monte Carlo" → text updates to "Starting Monte Carlo analysis
(100 trials)…", the progress bar enters busy mode (`setMaximum(0)` at `:540`) — then nothing. PySide6
swallows the slot exception, the worker is never `.start()`ed (`:552` unreachable), and the busy
progress bar spins **forever**. No `setMaximum(100)` or `setVisible(False)` exists anywhere after
`:571`, so state is never reset.

**Fix:** implement both slots as the single place that resets progress state, and add a
`_mc_running` / `_inv_running` guard:
```python
@Slot(str, dict)
def _on_analysis_finished(self, text: str, results: dict) -> None:
    self._tol_progress.setMaximum(100)
    self._tol_progress.setValue(100)
    self._tol_results_text.setPlainText(text)

@Slot(str)
def _on_analysis_failed(self, message: str) -> None:
    self._tol_progress.setMaximum(100)
    self._tol_progress.setValue(0)
    self._tol_results_text.setPlainText(message)
```

nodes.title: fix(gui): implement the tolerancing tab's missing worker slots
nodes.body:
Both run handlers connected their workers' signals to _on_analysis_finished and _on_analysis_failed, neither of which existed: four connect sites, zero definitions. PySide6 swallows the AttributeError from the missing slot, so worker.start() was never reached and the user saw "Starting Monte Carlo analysis (100 trials)..." followed by a progress bar stuck in busy mode - setMaximum(0) had no counterpart resetting it, because the only code that would have was the missing slot.

Both slots now exist and are the single place progress state is reset. _finished returns the bar to 0..100 at 100 and shows the report; _failed returns it to 0..100 at 0 and shows the error. A _mc_running / _inv_running pair, mirroring optimization_tab's _opt_is_running, stops a second click launching a thread that would race the first one's result.

Verified headless against the real widgets, including both workers driven end to end through their threads: the bar enters busy mode at start and the report replaces the "Starting..." text on completion, with the guard back to False. Seven tests, all failing with the slots removed.

Fixes #297

title: "Stop" does not stop the thread; the next "Run" aborts the process
body:
**File:** `src/gui/tabs/optimization_tab.py:407-414` and `:653-662`

```python
def _on_stop_optimization(self) -> None:
    if self._opt_is_running:
        self._opt_is_running = False
        self._opt_results_text.setPlainText("Optimization stopped by user.")
        ...
```

**Problem:** the QThread is never signalled, `quit()`ed, `wait()`ed or `terminate()`d.
`_opt_is_running = False` is a **lie**. The guard at `:600` is now defeated, so a second click
overwrites `self._opt_worker`, dropping the last Python reference to a live QThread; CPython
collects it and `QThread::~QThread` aborts.

**Repro (verified, real core dump):** Run Optimization → Stop → Run.
```
QThread: Destroyed while thread '' is still running
timeout: the monitored command dumped core
```

**Fix:**
```python
def _on_stop_optimization(self) -> None:
    if not self._opt_is_running:
        return
    if self._opt_worker and self._opt_worker.isRunning():
        self._opt_worker.requestInterruption()      # worker polls isInterruptionRequested()
        if not self._opt_worker.wait(3000):
            self._opt_worker.terminate()
            self._opt_worker.wait()
    self._opt_is_running = False
```
Guard the start path on `self._opt_worker and self._opt_worker.isRunning()` and set
`self._opt_worker = None` on completion.

nodes.title: fix(gui): make optimization Stop actually stop the thread
nodes.body:
Stop cleared _opt_is_running without touching the QThread, so the thread kept running while the guard that protected _opt_worker was now open. A second Run overwrote the attribute, dropping the last Python reference to a live QThread; CPython collected it and QThread::~QThread aborted. The tests reproduce the reported crash on the unfixed tab:

  QThread: Destroyed while thread '' is still running
  timeout: the monitored command dumped core   (exit 134 / SIGABRT)

Stop now requests interruption, waits 3s, and only falls back to terminate() + wait() if the thread ignored it. The reference is released once the thread is known to be stopped, and the start guard checks both the flag and _opt_worker.isRunning() so a stale flag alone can no longer permit an overwrite.

The worker cancels cooperatively rather than being killed. All three optimizers already take a per-iteration callback, so the worker passes one that raises a dedicated OptimizationCancelled, unwinds at the next iteration boundary, and emits nothing: Stop has already reset the UI, and reporting a half-converged design as a success would overwrite it with a value that never converged. Without this, requestInterruption() would always time out into terminate().

The completion slots deliberately do NOT clear _opt_worker. They run on the GUI thread while the worker may still be returning from run(), so clearing unconditionally would recreate the exact abort being fixed. _release_finished_worker drops the reference only after isRunning() says the thread is done, and keeps it otherwise - holding a reference to a finished thread costs nothing.

Eleven headless tests, including the Run -> Stop -> Run repro path, the concurrent-start guard, and the stale-flag case.

Fixes #298

title: Every UI edit runs full ray traces and a database reconcile on the GUI thread
body:
**Files:** `openlens.py:357-361`, `openlens.py:467-485`, `src/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:244,251,562`,
`src/gui/widgets/lens_editor.py:126,466`

**Chain:** every spinbox `valueChanged` and **every name keystroke** → `LensEditorWidget._on_property_changed`
→ `lens_modified` → `OpenLensWindow._on_lens_modified` → `_save_to_database()` + `_update_all_tabs()`
→ `PerformanceTab.refresh()` → `_on_calculate_performance_metrics()` → `calculate_all_aberrations()`
plus `calculate_chromatic_aberration()` — all synchronous full ray traces on the GUI thread. Each
`refresh()` also re-runs the matplotlib 3D redraw (`lens_viz_3d.py:224`).

**Repro (verified, offscreen):**
```
_on_lens_modified (single lens):                   364.3 ms
  _save_to_database:                               20.3 ms
8-char name setText (full save + refresh):         765.6 ms   (~96 ms per keystroke)
4-element assembly _on_assembly_modified:        ~1127 ms
```

Typing a 20-character lens name takes ~2 s of stuttering. The app is effectively unusable for
interactive editing.

**Fix (in priority order):**
1. Coalesce edits with a `QTimer` (`singleShot 300-500 ms`) so a burst of keystrokes triggers one save
   + one refresh.
2. Make `PerformanceTab.refresh()` non-computational — it should read a cached metrics dict. Move
   `calculate_all_aberrations` to the explicit "Calculate Metrics" worker (the button already exists
   at `performance_tab.py:112-113`).
3. Debounce `_save_to_database` and drop `reconcile=True` from the per-edit path (keep it for
   explicit Save / File > Open).
4. Skip the 3D canvas redraw when the 3D tab is not current.

nodes.title: perf(gui): debounce edits, stop recomputing metrics, defer the 3D redraw
nodes.body:
Closes #299

Every spinbox `valueChanged` and **every name keystroke** called
`_save_to_database()` and `_update_all_tabs()` synchronously, and that
refresh re-ran `calculate_all_aberrations()` plus
`calculate_chromatic_aberration()` on the GUI thread.

Measured on master, before this change:

| action | cost |
|---|---|
| 4 name keystrokes | **1018 ms** (~255 ms each) |
| 5 property edits (incl. 3D redraw) | **2002 ms** |
| one `PerformanceTab.refresh()` | **315 ms** |
| one `_save_to_database(reconcile=True)` | 12.6 ms |

A 20-character lens name cost roughly **five seconds** of stuttering.

## After

| action | cost |
|---|---|
| 4 name keystrokes | **0.2 ms** |
| 5 property edits (incl. 3D redraw) | **1.1 ms** |
| one `PerformanceTab.refresh()` | **0.3 ms** |
| `Calculate Metrics` (explicit button) | 284 ms — unchanged path |

## The four changes the issue asks for

1. **Coalesce edits.** A restartable single-shot `QTimer` (400 ms) collapses a
   burst into one save and one refresh. `_flush_pending_edit()` commits
   immediately and is called from `_on_new_lens()` and
   `_load_from_database()`, so a pending save is never dropped before an action
   reads the disk. The refresh runs in a `finally`, so a failed save still
   leaves the tabs showing the changed model.

2. **`PerformanceTab.refresh()` no longer computes.** It repaints the last
   result from a per-model cache and prompts for `Calculate Metrics` when there
   is none — the button already existed for exactly this. The explicit path
   caches what it computes.

3. **`reconcile` is now a flag** on `_save_to_database`. The per-edit path
   passes `reconcile=False` (12.6 → 7.5 ms); explicit saves keep `True`.

4. **The 3D redraw is deferred.** I profiled this rather than guessing, and the
   split is stark:

   ```
   2d.update_lens x5: 0.0 ms
   3d.update_lens x5: 604.6 ms      # ~121 ms per redraw
   ```

   `LensVisualizationWidget.update_lens` now redraws the 3D canvas only when
   its tab is current, otherwise recording the update and applying it on the
   switch. Verified both directions: edits deferred while hidden, flushed on
   `currentChanged`, and drawn immediately once 3D is on screen.

## Two tests updated, and why

`test_gui.py::test_deferred_load_adopts_working_lens` and
`::test_spinbox_edit_persists` asserted the edit was **on disk the instant the
spinbox moved** — the synchronous contract this issue exists to remove. They now
settle the pending commit first. The underlying guarantee is unchanged and still
asserted (the value reaches the row, including edge-lock compensation).

I also added `test_spinbox_edit_is_debounced_not_written_per_keystroke`, which
pins the new behaviour: nothing on disk mid-burst, one row after the flush. So
the timing change is deliberate and covered in both directions.

## Tests

New `tests/test_gui_edit_debounce.py` (17 tests) against a **real**
`OpenLensWindow` (shown, so `isVisible()` is meaningful). **14 of the 17 fail
on master** and pass here. Covers: `refresh()` not calling the calculator, the
per-model cache and its prompt path, the explicit button still caching, 3D
deferral and flush, burst collapsing to one commit, `reconcile=False` on the
edit path, refresh surviving a failed save, and flush being a no-op when idle.

Full suite: 1080 tests, 31 skipped, no new failures — and ~10 s faster as a
side effect. The 6 `tests.gui_flows` loader errors are pre-existing (no pytest
in the local system Python; CI runs them with pytest).

title: Analysis dialogs compute before showing, freezing the window for 3-8 s
body:
**Files:** `openlens.py:859-882, 884-902, 904-922`; `src/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:176,376,446,527`

```python
sensor = WavefrontSensor(system)
wf = sensor.get_pupil_wavefront(grid_size=64)   # <- 8 s, before any window exists
dialog = AnalysisPlotDialog("Wavefront Analysis", self)
plot_wavefront(ax, wf.W)
dialog.exec()
```

**Repro (verified, 4-element assembly):**
```
get_pupil_wavefront(grid_size=64):  8010.9 ms
calculate_psf(64):                  3387.5 ms
calculate_mtf:                      3564.5 ms
trace_ghosts(5):                     111.9 ms
```

**User-visible failure:** because the computation precedes `dialog.exec()`, there is no window in
which to show progress and the OS may not paint at all. The user cannot tell whether the app hung.

**Fix:** show the dialog first, then compute in a `QThread` and paint on `finished`. The pattern
already exists in this codebase (`MonteCarloWorker`, `OptimizationWorker`). Minimum viable: show a
"Calculating…" dialog, call `QApplication.processEvents()`, then compute.

nodes.title: fix(gui): compute analyses off-thread behind a visible dialog
nodes.body:
Closes #300

Every analysis dialog computed **before** it was constructed:

```python
sensor = WavefrontSensor(system)
wf = sensor.get_pupil_wavefront(grid_size=64)   # <- 8 s, before any window exists
dialog = AnalysisPlotDialog("Wavefront Analysis", self)
plot_wavefront(ax, wf.W)
dialog.exec()
```

Measured on a 4-element assembly: wavefront **8.0 s**, PSF **3.4 s**, MTF
**3.6 s**, ghosts 0.1 s. Because the compute preceded `dialog.exec()`, there
was no window in which to show progress and the OS might not paint at all —
the user could not tell the app from a hang.

## The fix

`AnalysisPlotDialog` now paints a status line, shows itself and forces a
repaint, then runs the analysis in an `AnalysisWorker` (`QThread`) and paints
on the `done` signal. Matplotlib painting stays on the GUI thread, which Qt
requires and the signal connection provides.

Verified against a real `QApplication` — all four handlers return in
**30–350 ms** with the window up, and every plot renders:

```
_on_show_ghost_analysis: return=324ms visible=True artists=20 failed=[]
_on_show_wavefront:      return=106ms visible=True artists=13 failed=[]
_on_show_psf:            return=128ms visible=True artists=13 failed=[]
_on_show_mtf:            return=29ms  visible=True artists=13 failed=[]
```

The dialog is deliberately **non-modal**: `exec()` would nest a second event
loop and the worker's signal still needs the current one running.

## QThread lifetime

Handled in `OpenLensWindow._open_analysis_dialog`, which holds the dialog
until its worker has finished. `OptimizationWorker` documents the hazard —
dropping the last Python reference to a live QThread makes CPython destroy it
and `~QThread` aborts the process — so a dialog closed mid-computation is
retired on `worker.finished` instead of immediately.

## Two bugs found while testing, not assumed

- `show_computing()` and `_on_done()` both called `get_axes()`, which **stacks
  a fresh subplot per run** and left the stale "Calculating" axes on the figure
  forever. They now share one reused `_content_axes()`. A test pins this at 1
  axes after 3 runs.
- `plot_ghost_analysis(ax, system, ghosts)` takes **three** arguments, so
  passing it straight through as the plot callback raised `TypeError` inside the
  finished handler — the ghost analysis silently rendered "Analysis failed".
  The ghost path now unpacks its payload.

## Tests

New `tests/test_analysis_async_dialog.py` (10 tests) driving a real
`QApplication` and event loop: the window is visible before the compute
starts, the handler does not block on the analysis, the payload reaches the
plot callback, a failing compute paints a message instead of vanishing, axes
are reused rather than stacked, the worker reference is cleared, and a
three-argument plotter is correctly wrapped.

Also adds `show_computing_dialog()` — the minimum-viable path the issue
suggests — for analyses with no canvas to reuse.

Full suite: 1072 tests, 31 skipped, no new failures (the 6 `tests.gui_flows`
loader errors are pre-existing: they only occur under `unittest` without
pytest, which is what the local system Python has).

Note the `performance_tab.py:176,376,446,527` line references in the issue are
stale — on current master that tab only computes a spot diagram, and it is not
one of the blocking paths, so it is untouched.

title: `GaussianBeam` has no `R_y`; beam-synthesis propagation always raises
body:
**File:** `src/analysis/beam_synthesis.py:411` (class at `:23-102`)

```python
Rx = beam.R_x
Ry = beam.R_y          # GaussianBeam has no R_y property
```

**Repro (verified):**
```
GaussianBeam attributes: ['w_x', 'w_y', 'R_x', 'propagate', 'refract']
has R_y: False
```
`BeamSynthesisPropagator.propagate_to_image` raises `AttributeError` as soon as one beamlet survives.

**Fix:**
```python
@property
def R_y(self) -> float:
    inv_q = 1.0 / self.q_y
    if inv_q.real == 0:
        return float("inf")
    return 1.0 / inv_q.real
```

nodes.title: fix(beam): add the missing GaussianBeam.R_y curvature radius
nodes.body:
propagate_to_image() reads beam.R_y for the sagittal phase term, but GaussianBeam only defined R_x, so every beam-synthesis propagation raised AttributeError on the first surviving beamlet. R_y mirrors R_x over q_y.

Also fixes the adjacent typo on the same statement group: the phase term computed k = 2*pi/wavelength, but the parameter is wavelength_mm, so the function raised NameError immediately after R_y was satisfied. flake8 was already reporting it as F821 undefined name 'wavelength'. Without this the feature still did not run, so the ticket's fix alone was not sufficient.

propagate_to_image now completes and returns a finite intensity map, and the pattern responds to the passed wavelength.

Ten tests, all failing without the change: R_y against the analytic |q|^2/Re(q) for positive, negative and near-zero real parts, infinite at the waist as for R_x, independence from R_x on an astigmatic beam, and propagation parity with R_x.

Fixes #302

title: `SpotDiagram.trace_spot` can raise `UnboundLocalError`, and `return` in `finally` swallows errors
body:
**File:** `src/analysis/spot_diagram.py:140, 167-186`

`spot_points` is initialised *inside* the `try` at `:140`; the statistics block that reads it lives in
the `finally` at `:174`.

**Repro (verified):** `SpotDiagram(OpticalSystem(name="empty")).trace_spot()` →
```
UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'spot_points' where it is not associated with a value
```
(the underlying `IndexError` from `self.system.elements[0]` at `:100`/`:138` is masked).

**Second defect:** a `return` inside `finally` **discards any in-flight exception**, so a tracer
failure after some rays have landed silently returns `rms_radius: 0.0` instead of raising.

**Fix:** hoist `spot_points = []` / `valid_rays = 0` above the `try`, and move the statistics block
into an `else:` clause (or an exception handler) rather than `finally`.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): stop trace_spot masking failures as a zero-radius spot
nodes.body:
spot_points was bound inside the try while the statistics block that reads it lived in the finally, so any failure before that point surfaced as UnboundLocalError instead of its cause:

  IndexError: list index out of range
  UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'spot_points' ...

Both are now hoisted above the try, so an empty system raises the IndexError it actually is.

The same block also returned from the finally, and a return there discards any in-flight exception. A tracer failure that happened before the first spot point landed was reported as a clean result - rms_radius 0.0, valid_rays 0, "No rays reached the image plane" - so a tracer bug looked exactly like a legitimate blocked/TIR outcome. Verified before the fix: a RuntimeError raised mid-trace came back as rms_radius 0.0.

The statistics block moves after the try statement rather than into an else clause, since Python requires an except before else and adding a re-raise would be noise. Code after try/finally is reached only when the body did not raise, which is the semantics wanted, and the finally still restores lens state on both paths.

The genuine no-rays case is unchanged and still returns its empty stats.

Note for callers: psf_mtf, tolerancing and chromatic_analyzer read rms_radius directly, so they now see a propagating tracer exception where they previously received a fabricated 0.0. That is the point of the fix, but it does convert silent wrong answers into visible failures.

Six tests; three fail without the change, three guard the legitimate paths.

Fixes #303

title: A fully vignetted system is scored as a perfect design
body:
**Files:** `src/analysis/spot_diagram.py:178-186` → `src/optimizer.py:168` → `src/tolerancing.py:465-466`

```python
# spot_diagram.py:178 — "no rays reached the plane" reported as a PERFECT spot
return {"rms_radius": 0.0, "geo_radius": 0.0, ...}
# optimizer.py:168
value = results.get("rms_radius", 0.0)      # defaults to 0.0 on any miss
# tolerancing.py:465-466
val = results["rms_radius"]
passed = val <= criterion_limit             # 0.0 <= limit -> PASS
```

**Repro (verified):** a 2-element system with a 1.0 mm stop on gap 0 (1 of 127 rays survives):
```
valid_rays: 1   rms: 0.0
MonteCarloAnalyzer(...).run(num_trials=5, criterion_limit=0.05)
  -> {'mean': 0.0, 'yield': 100.0, 'max': 0.0}
MeritFunction(s, [OptimizationTarget("rms_spot_radius", 0.0)]).evaluate(s) -> 0.0
```

A 99 %-vignetted system beats every physically real design in the optimizer, and Monte Carlo reports
**100 % production yield** on it. This inverts the purpose of both modules.

**Fix:** return `rms_radius: None` (or raise) with `"error"` set when `valid_rays < 2`; make
`MeritFunction._eval_rms_spot` return `INFEASIBLE_MERIT` for `None` (as `_eval_spherical:119-121`
already does) — never default to `0.0`; have `MonteCarloAnalyzer.run` fail the trial rather than pass it.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): never score a vignetted design as a perfect spot
nodes.body:
Closes #304

## Problem

`SpotDiagram.trace_spot` reported "no rays reached the image plane" as `rms_radius: 0.0`. Two consumers read that `0.0` as a genuine measurement:

| Site | Code | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `src/optimizer.py` | `results.get("rms_radius", 0.0)` | defaults to 0.0 on any miss |
| `src/tolerancing.py` | `passed = val <= criterion_limit` | `0.0 <= limit` → PASS |

A two-element system behind a 1 mm stop (1 of 127 rays survives) therefore scored a *perfect* spot, outranked every physically real design in the optimizer, and reported **100% production yield** in Monte Carlo.

```
valid_rays: 1   rms: 0.0
monte carlo -> {'yield': 100.0, 'mean': 0.0, 'max': 0.0}
merit       -> 0.0
```

This inverts the purpose of both modules.

## Fix

- `trace_spot` returns `rms_radius: None` with an `error` key when **fewer than two rays** arrive. One ray sits on its own centroid, so its RMS radius is identically 0.0 — not a reporting edge case, but the best possible score. Two rays is the minimum that defines a spot.
- `_eval_rms_spot` returns `INFEASIBLE_MERIT` for that case, matching what `_eval_spherical` already did for a `None` aberration, and never defaults to `0.0`.
- Vignetted Monte Carlo trials are counted as failures and contribute `inf`. Since `statistics.mean/stdev` cannot reduce `inf` (`inf - inf` is `nan`), the summary is taken over the finite trials while `max` keeps the `inf`, and a new `vignetted_trials` count reports how many there were.
- The inverse-sensitivity slope is `nan` when both ends are `inf`: the operand never moved the design between two unmanufacturable states, so there is no slope — and `inf` would wrongly imply an infinitely sensitive operand.

## After

```
vignetted : valid_rays=1 rms=None
  merit vignetted=1000000000.0  healthy=0.440376  -> healthy wins: True
  monte carlo yield=0.0 mean=inf max=inf vignetted_trials=5
  healthy monte carlo yield=0.0 mean=0.440369
```

## Tests

New `tests/test_vignetted_scoring.py` (10 tests, 8 fail without the change): the `None` contract, healthy systems still reporting real radii, optimizer merit ordering, yield no longer 100%, statistics surviving non-finite values, and both inverse-sensitivity paths.

title: `ImageSimulator` is a no-op against a real `OpticalSystem`
body:
**File:** `src/image_simulator.py:137, 164-165, 205-215`

```python
if hasattr(self.optical_system, "effective_focal_length"): ...
if hasattr(self.optical_system, "get_aberrations"): ...
if hasattr(self.optical_system, "aperture_diameter"): ...
```

**Repro (verified):** `OpticalSystem` has **none** of these three members (it exposes
`get_system_focal_length`, `get_f_number`, `get_numerical_aperture`).
```
has effective_focal_length: False
has aperture_diameter:       False
has get_aberrations:         False
_calculate_image_distance(100.0, 587.6) -> 100.0    # correct for f=100.23: ~32 mm
```

Aberration blur, diffraction blur (f/# ignored) and chromatic aberration are **all silently
skipped**; only cos⁴ vignetting survives, and magnification always reports `-1.0`. The only tests
use a `MockOpticalSystem` that supplies `aperture_diameter`, which is why this was never caught.

**Fix:** switch to the real API — `get_system_focal_length()`, `elements[0].lens.diameter` for the
stop, and `AberrationsCalculator(system).calculate_all_aberrations()`. Fail loudly rather than via
`hasattr`.

nodes.title: fix(image-sim): use the real OpticalSystem API, not probed attributes
nodes.body:
Closes #305

## Problem

`ImageSimulator` gated every physical effect behind a `hasattr` probe for three members that `OpticalSystem` does not have:

```python
has effective_focal_length     False
has get_aberrations           False
has aperture_diameter         False
```

`OpticalSystem` exposes `get_system_focal_length()`, and aberrations come from `AberrationsCalculator`. So every probe failed against any real system:

```
_calculate_image_distance(100.0, 587.6) -> 100.0   # echoed the object distance
true EFL = 50.8475  ->  true image distance should be ~103 mm
magnification: -1.0  (always)
```

Aberration blur was skipped, diffraction blur fell back to a flat 10 mm aperture so **f/# was ignored entirely**, chromatic scaling never ran, and the reported magnification was always `-1.0`. Only cos⁴ vignetting survived. The existing tests used a `MockOpticalSystem` that supplied `aperture_diameter`, which is why this went unnoticed.

## Fix

Three explicit accessors replace the probes:

- `_system_focal_length()` → `get_system_focal_length()`, or `calculate_focal_length()` for a bare `Lens`
- `_entrance_pupil_diameter()` → the first element's diameter, matching how the rest of the codebase estimates the entrance pupil
- `_aberrations_for()` → `AberrationsCalculator`

**Legacy targets still work.** All three accept a duck-typed target (a callable `effective_focal_length` / `get_aberrations`), because `tests/test_advanced_features.py`'s `MockOpticalSystem` — and any external wrapper — relies on it. But as an *explicit branch*, not a probe that silently no-ops. A target providing none of these now raises instead of quietly returning made-up numbers.

The chromatic path used a **fourth** `effective_focal_length` probe and skipped every channel. It now derives per-channel focus from the measured longitudinal chromatic aberration (`f / (f + lca)`), and leaves channels untouched when there is none to report — the honest answer for an achromat.

## Three existing tests needed a data change

`test_diffraction`, `test_diffraction_widens_with_wavelength` and `test_diffraction_honors_pixel_pitch` asserted that a point spreads at a **10 µm pixel pitch**. With the real 25.4 mm aperture the Airy radius is 0.047 px — genuinely below the sampling grid — so the assertion was only satisfiable because the old code's fictitious 10 mm aperture inflated σ by 2.5×. They now sample at 0.5 µm, where the blur is resolvable, and assert the same physical relationships:

```
pitch=0.0100 mm -> centre 1.0000, spread 3 px    (sub-pixel, nothing to see)
pitch=0.0005 mm -> centre 0.0437, spread 867 px  (blur resolved)
```

## Tests

10 new tests in `tests/test_image_simulator_api.py`; 8 fail without the change. One pins the premise itself — that `OpticalSystem` has none of the probed attributes — so a future rename cannot silently re-break the wiring.

title: Database migration is non-atomic and non-idempotent; one crash bricks the app permanently
body:
**File:** `src/database.py:64` (`isolation_level = None`), `:168-228`

Each `ALTER TABLE` and each `PRAGMA user_version = N` runs as its own implicit transaction under
autocommit. If the process dies between two ALTERs, `user_version` still holds the old value, so the
next launch re-runs the same ALTERs. `_initialize_db()` is called unguarded from `__init__` (`:55`),
so **every** subsequent launch dies identically. There is no recovery path. The same error occurs if
two instances start concurrently (the version read at `:189-228` and the writes are not in one
transaction).

**Repro (verified):** simulate a crash after the first v1→v2 ALTER:
```
user_version after partial migration: (1,)
DatabaseManager() -> OperationalError: duplicate column name: is_parabolic_1
```

**Fix:** wrap the entire version-detect + migrate block in `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` … `COMMIT`
(`ROLLBACK` on error), and guard each `ALTER` with a `PRAGMA table_info` column check so an
already-partially-migrated DB self-heals.

nodes.title: fix(db): make schema migration atomic and self-healing
nodes.body:
Closes #306

## Problem

The connection runs with `isolation_level = None` (autocommit), so each `ALTER TABLE` and each `PRAGMA user_version = N` was its own implicit transaction. A process dying between two ALTERs left `user_version` at the old value, so the next launch replayed them:

```
DatabaseManager() -> OperationalError: duplicate column name: is_parabolic_1
```

`_initialize_db()` runs unguarded from `__init__`, so **every subsequent launch died identically** — the app could not be started again without deleting the database. Two concurrent instances hit the same window, since the version read and the writes were not in one transaction.

## Fix

**Atomicity** — the whole version-detect-then-migrate sequence runs inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE … COMMIT` (`ROLLBACK` on error). DDL is transactional in SQLite, so a partial migration cannot survive, and `IMMEDIATE` takes the write lock up front so two processes serialise instead of interleaving.

**Self-healing** — every `ALTER` goes through `_add_column()`, which checks `PRAGMA table_info` first. A database already half-migrated by an older build now heals instead of raising forever.

## Verified

A crash injected after two ALTERs:

```
crash propagated: simulated crash mid-migration
lenses columns before=11 after=11  (equal => ROLLED BACK)
user_version after=1  (still 1 => nothing committed)
ATOMIC
recovery after crash: user_version = 5 lenses cols = 21
```

A half-migrated v1 database opens without raising; repeated opens are stable; a brand-new database still lands at v5.

## Scope guard

`_add_column` still raises on a genuinely missing table rather than papering over it — a test pins that, so self-healing cannot mask real corruption.

## Tests

5 tests in `tests/test_database.py`, reusing the existing `_make_v1_db` fixture. All 5 fail without the change.

title: `ChromaticAnalyzer.design_achromatic_doublet` raises `ZeroDivisionError` for one glass
body:
**File:** `src/chromatic_analyzer.py:345-347` (duplicate of `src/optical_system.py:675-681`)

```python
phi_total = 1.0 / focal_length
phi1 = phi_total * V1 / (V1 - V2)
phi2 = phi_total * V2 / (V2 - V1)
```

The `optical_system` twin has a `if v1 == v2:` guard; this copy does not.

**Repro (verified):** `ChromaticAnalyzer().design_achromatic_doublet(100.0, "BK7", "BK7")` →
`ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero`. The two implementations of the same physics have
diverged. `calculate_abbe_number` (`:301`) also has no `n_F - n_C` guard.

**Fix:** make `AchromaticDoubletDesigner` the single implementation and delegate; add
`if V1 == V2: raise ValueError(...)` to the analyzer.

nodes.title: fix(chromatic): reject unsolvable achromats instead of dividing by zero
nodes.body:
Closes #307

## Problem

`design_achromatic_doublet` splits optical power by Abbe number, dividing by `(V1 - V2)`. Given the same glass twice that is `1/0`:

```
design_achromatic_doublet(100.0, "BK7", "BK7")
  -> ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero
```

The condition has **no solution**: two glasses with equal dispersion cannot cancel chromatic aberration. `optical_system.AchromaticDoubletDesigner` already guarded exactly this — which is how two copies of the same physics diverged.

`calculate_abbe_number` had the same shape of hole: `V_d = (n_d - 1)/(n_F - n_C)` is undefined when a material has no dispersion across F..C.

## Fix

Both now raise `ValueError` with the glasses and their Abbe numbers named:

```
Cannot design an achromat from 'BK7' and 'BK7': both have Abbe number V=64.141.
```

The guard is `1e-12` on the Abbe difference rather than equality, so genuinely different glasses are unaffected.

**Worth knowing:** `BK7` and `N-BK7` are the same catalog entry and share V to 9 places, so pairing them is rejected for the same physical reason. A test pins that.

## On the suggested refactor

The ticket also suggested making `AchromaticDoubletDesigner` the single implementation and delegating. I did not do that: the two are not duplicates. `design_cemented_doublet` returns a built `OpticalSystem`; `design_achromatic_doublet` returns a dict of design parameters (power split only, no radii or thickness). Collapsing them changes a public return shape — a redesign, not a bug fix. What was fixed is the divergence that actually caused the crash.

## Tests

7 tests in `tests/test_chromatic_analyzer.py`; all fail without the change.

title: Optimizer and Monte Carlo reseed the process-global `random` module
body:
**File:** `src/global_optimizer.py:33-34` and `src/tolerancing.py:338-339`

```python
if seed is not None:
    random.seed(seed)          # global module state
```

**Repro (verified):**
```
random.seed(1);  a = random.random()   # 0.134364
random.seed(99); MonteCarloAnalyzer(None, [], seed=7)
b = random.random()                    # 0.323833   -> a != b
```

`GlobalOptimizer.__init__` runs inside a `QThread` (`optimization_tab.py:97-132`), so it mutates
RNG state the Qt thread may be consuming concurrently. Worse, `seed=` does **not** make these
reproducible: all draws come from the same shared global stream, so any unrelated `random` call
anywhere interleaves. No `numpy.random.default_rng(seed)` is used anywhere in `src/`.

**Fix:** add `self._rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)` (or `random.Random(seed)`) to `GlobalOptimizer`
and `MonteCarloAnalyzer`, thread it through `ToleranceOperand.generate_value(rng)`, and delete the
`random.seed` calls.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): stop the optimizers reseeding the process-global RNG
nodes.body:
Closes #308

## Two problems

**1. Constructing an optimizer rewrote process-global RNG state.**

```python
if seed is not None:
    random.seed(seed)
```

```
random.seed(99); MonteCarloAnalyzer(None, [], seed=7); random.random()
  before:  0.32383276483316237   <- seed 7's first draw, not seed 99's
  after:   0.40397807494366633   <- the caller's stream, bit-for-bit intact
```

`GlobalOptimizer.__init__` runs inside a **QThread** (`optimization_tab.py`), so this mutated RNG state the Qt thread could be consuming concurrently.

**2. `seed=` did not make a run reproducible at all.**

Every draw came from the one shared stream, so any unrelated `random` call anywhere in the process interleaved with it — which is exactly what a seed is supposed to prevent.

## Fix

Each class owns a `random.Random(seed)`. `GlobalOptimizer`'s eleven module-level `random.*` calls became `self._rng.*`, and `ToleranceOperand.generate_value` takes an optional `rng` that `MonteCarloAnalyzer` passes. `generate_value` still falls back to the module-level `random` when called without one, so standalone callers are unaffected.

Verified: two runs at `seed=7` return **identical** results with 25 unrelated global `random` draws interleaved between them, and `seed=8` differs.

## Tests

12 tests, **7 fail without the change**: the global stream is untouched by constructing either class and by running a full analysis; `seed=7` is reproducible with interleaved noise; the supplied rng is actually used and deterministic; gaussian draws stay clamped; two operands sharing one rng differ; and a scan of all of `src/` fails if `random.seed(` reappears — stripping comments, so these fixes can name the call they removed.

title: Lens names are interpolated into SVG with no XML escaping
body:
**File:** `src/export_formats.py:378, 499, 537`; `src/io/export.py:44, 164, 186, 318, 350`

```python
f'  <text x="{width/2}" y="25" class="title" text-anchor="middle">{lens.name}</text>\n'
```

`validate_lens_name` (`validation.py:491-515`) accepts any string ≤100 chars, and names arrive from
untrusted JSON. There is **no** `escape`/`html.escape` call anywhere in `src/`.

**Repro (verified):** `Lens(name='</text><script>alert(1)</script>')` exported to SVG:
```
raw <script> in SVG: True
SVG parses as XML: False -> mismatched tag: line 16, column 94
```

The file is both **script-bearing** when opened in a browser and structurally invalid XML — a plain
