nodes.title: fix(export): escape names and materials interpolated into SVG
nodes.body:
Closes #309

## Problem

Lens and system names come from **untrusted JSON** — `validate_lens_name` accepts any string up to 100 chars — and were interpolated straight into SVG text nodes. There was no `escape`/`html.escape` call anywhere in `src/`.

A name of `'</text><script>alert(1)</script>'` produced a file that was **both** script-bearing when opened in a browser **and** structurally invalid XML:

```
raw <script> in SVG: True
SVG parses as XML: False -> mismatched tag: line 16, column 94
```

A plain `&` in a name was enough to break the XML on its own, with no injection at all.

## Fix

Eight sites now pass through `xml.sax.saxutils.escape`:

- **`SVGExporter`** — lens title, system title, material label
- **`ISO10110Generator`** — drawing title, title-block row values, material column, both coating labels

The title-block case escapes the whole row value, so future rows are covered by construction rather than by remembering.

The non-SVG writers (STL comments, prescription text) are deliberately left alone: they are not XML, so escaping there would corrupt the output.

## Verified

Across script, ampersand and unicode payloads on both generators:

```
'</text><script>  export_lens  script:False parses:True
'</text><script>  ISO10110    script:False parses:True
'R&D x <b> & '   export_lens  script:False parses:True
'R&D x <b> & '   ISO10110    script:False parses:True
'Ø 25mm ünïcode'   export_lens  script:False parses:True
```

The escaped text also **round-trips to the original string** through the parser — this is lossless escaping, not lossy sanitisation.

## Tests

16 tests, **10 fail without the change**: script injection, well-formedness, lossless round-tripping, and that an ordinary name is not mangled (no double-escaping).

## Note

`SVGExporter.export_system` crashes on `LensElement.air_gap_before`, which does not exist. That is a separate defect — tracked as #295.

title: Monte Carlo `_restore_state` does not restore the glass model; the nominal system drifts
body:
**File:** `src/tolerancing.py:116-117` (capture), `:151-155` (restore)

```python
# capture
"nd": (lens.model_nd if lens.model_glass_mode else lens.refractive_index),
"vd": lens.model_vd if lens.model_glass_mode else 0,
...
# restore
lens.model_glass_mode = ls["glass_mode"]
if lens.model_glass_mode:          # <- nd/vd restored ONLY in this branch
    lens.model_nd = ls["nd"]
    lens.model_vd = ls["vd"]
lens.update_refractive_index()
```

`_apply_value` → `_ensure_model_glass` (`:245, 299-312`) flips a fixed-index lens into model-glass
mode. The restore puts `model_glass_mode` back to `False` but **leaves `model_nd`/`model_vd`
perturbed**, and `update_refractive_index()` then takes the material-DB branch, which does not
reproduce the original index.

**Repro (verified):**
```
before:    glass_mode=False n=1.516800 model_nd=1.5168 model_vd=64.17
perturbed: n=1.518798 model_nd=1.5188 model_vd=65.17
restored:  glass_mode=False n=1.516798 model_nd=1.5188 model_vd=65.17   <- NOT restored
```

Trial *N+1* starts from trial *N*'s index, contaminating the nominal reference, all percentiles, and
the yield with a monotone index walk.

**Fix:** always capture and always restore `model_nd`, `model_vd`, `model_glass_mode` **and**
`refractive_index` as separate fields; restore `refractive_index` by direct assignment rather than
via `update_refractive_index()`.

nodes.title: fix(tolerancing): restore glass state exactly so MC stops walking the index
nodes.body:
Closes #310

## Problem

`_capture_state` folded the glass model into one `"nd"/"vd"` pair, keeping `model_nd`/`model_vd` **only when the element was already in model-glass mode**:

```python
"nd": (lens.model_nd if lens.model_glass_mode else lens.refractive_index),
"vd": lens.model_vd if lens.model_glass_mode else 0,
```

But an index tolerance goes through `_ensure_model_glass`, which flips a fixed-index lens into model-glass mode and perturbs `model_nd`. The restore put `glass_mode` back to `False`, left `model_nd` perturbed, then called `update_refractive_index()` — which takes the material-DB branch and does not reproduce the original fixed index.

Trial *N+1* therefore started from trial *N*'s index: a monotone walk contaminating the nominal reference, all percentiles, and the yield.

## Verified

Before:

```
nominal    mode=False n=1.516800 nd=1.5168
perturbed  mode=True  n=1.513519 nd=1.5135211140893239
restored   mode=False n=1.516798 nd=1.5135211140893239   <- drifted
```

After — identical on every trial:

```
nominal    mode=False n=1.516800000 nd=1.5168 vd=64.17
resturbed  mode=False n=1.516800000 nd=1.5168 vd=64.17
```

## Fix

`model_glass_mode`, `model_nd`, `model_vd` and `refractive_index` are captured as four separate fields and restored unconditionally, with the index assigned directly rather than re-derived. The state dict is internal to `tolerancing.py` — nothing else reads those keys — so the shape change is contained.

## Tests

10 tests, **7 fail without the change**: exact-index restore, no drift over 25 trials, an Abbe-number tolerance (same code path), an element that starts in model-glass mode, and a full seeded run. Three more guard the geometry, glass-mode and air-gap restores that were already correct.

title: App will not start without matplotlib (violates the documented `*_AVAILABLE` rule)
body:
**Files:** `openlens.py:31`, `src/gui/dialogs/__init__.py:6`, `src/gui/dialogs/analysis_plots.py:9-11`

```python
# dialogs/__init__.py:6 — unguarded, module scope
from .analysis_plots import AnalysisPlotDialog
# analysis_plots.py:9-11 — matplotlib at module scope
from matplotlib.figure import Figure
from matplotlib.backends.backend_qtagg import FigureCanvasQTAgg as FigureCanvas
# openlens.py:31 — imported at module scope
from src.gui.dialogs import StartupDialog, AnalysisPlotDialog
```

AGENTS.md classifies matplotlib as *optional* ("the app must start and run core features without
them"). On a clean `pip install PySide6` the app dies at import with a raw `ModuleNotFoundError` — no
editor, no message. The lens editor, assembly builder, and the QPainter-based 2D/3D visualisations
have no matplotlib dependency and are unusable because of one eagerly-imported dialog.

Note `src/gui/__init__.py:5-12` *does* wrap its imports in `try/except ImportError`, which makes the
codebase look compliant — but that guard is dead weight, because `openlens.py` imports the
submodules directly.

**Fix:**
```python
# src/gui/dialogs/__init__.py
from .startup import StartupDialog
try:
    from .analysis_plots import AnalysisPlotDialog
except ImportError:
    AnalysisPlotDialog = None
```
Then import `AnalysisPlotDialog` lazily in the four handlers that need it, with a
`QMessageBox` guard. Same treatment for `src/gui/dialogs/image_sim.py:9,18-20`.

nodes.title: fix(gui): start without matplotlib
nodes.body:
Closes #311

## Problem

AGENTS.md classes matplotlib as *optional* — "the app must start and run core features without them" — but `src/gui/dialogs/__init__.py` imported `AnalysisPlotDialog` at module scope, and `openlens.py:31` imported it from there at module scope too:

```python
# dialogs/__init__.py:6
from .analysis_plots import AnalysisPlotDialog

# openlens.py:31
from src.gui.dialogs import StartupDialog, AnalysisPlotDialog
```

On a clean `pip install PySide6` the app died at import with a raw `ModuleNotFoundError` — **no editor, no message**. The lens editor, assembly builder and the QPainter-based 2D/3D visualisations need no matplotlib, so one eagerly imported dialog made all of them unusable.

`src/gui/__init__.py` *does* wrap its imports in `try/except ImportError`, which makes the codebase look compliant — but that guard was dead weight, because `openlens.py` imports the submodules directly.

## Verified

Blocking matplotlib via `sys.meta_path` in a subprocess:

```
before: FAILED to import openlens: ImportError No module named 'matplotlib'
after:  openlens imported OK -> OpenLensWindow
```

## Fix

- The dialogs package guards the import, exposing `ANALYSIS_PLOTS_AVAILABLE` and `require_analysis_plot_dialog()`. The accessor **raises** an `ImportError` naming the package to install rather than returning `None`, so a caller that forgets it fails loudly instead of calling `None()`.
- `openlens.py` drops the eager import; each of the four handlers resolves the class lazily.
- A new `ImportError` handler reports it as **"Dependency Missing"** via `QMessageBox.warning`, matching the precedent in `performance_tab.py` — rather than the misleading *"PSF calculation failed"* critical box the broad `except` would otherwise have shown.

## Tests

8 tests, **6 fail without the change**. matplotlib is blocked in a subprocess, since un-importing a live module mid-process is unreliable. Two static guards keep the eager import from creeping back in; the normal path with matplotlib present is covered too.

title: `@lru_cache` on an instance method leaks every `MaterialDatabase`
body:
**File:** `src/material_database.py:317-320`

```python
@lru_cache(maxsize=1024)
def get_refractive_index(self, material_name: str, wavelength_nm: float,
                         temperature_c: float = 20.0) -> float:
```

The cache key includes `self`, held strongly, class-wide.

**Repro (verified):** after one lookup, `del m; gc.collect()` →
`MaterialDatabase instances alive after del+gc: 1`.
`chromatic_analyzer.py:102` constructs a fresh `MaterialDatabase()` per analyzer, so this grows
without bound.

Two related defects: `add_material` (`:304`) and `clear_cache` (`:372`) call `cache_clear()` on the
**shared** wrapper, wiping every instance's cache; and direct mutation of `self.materials` (e.g.
`_load_database` re-reading a changed `materials.json`, `:278-287`) never invalidates the cache.

**Fix:** drop the decorator; cache on `(material_name, wavelength_nm, temperature_c)` in a
module-level dict keyed by a generation counter, or use a per-instance dict.

nodes.title: fix(materials): make the refractive index cache per-instance
nodes.body:
Closes #312

## Problem

`get_refractive_index` carried `@lru_cache(maxsize=1024)`, so the cache key included `self` — one class-wide cache holding every `MaterialDatabase` ever used, **strongly, forever**:

```
after one lookup, del m; gc.collect()
-> MaterialDatabase instances alive: 1
```

`chromatic_analyzer.py` constructs a fresh `MaterialDatabase()` per analyzer, so the count grew without bound and no instance was ever collected.

## Two related defects, also verified

**`clear_cache()` wiped every instance.** `add_material` and `clear_cache` called `cache_clear()` on the *shared* wrapper:

```
shared cache currsize: 2
after a.clear_cache(): shared currsize = 0     <- b was wiped too
```

**Direct mutation never invalidated.** Mutating `self.materials` — e.g. a re-read `materials.json` — left stale indices in the cache indefinitely.

## Fix

The cache is now a **per-instance dict** that dies with its owner. `get_refractive_index` became a thin caching wrapper over a new `_compute_refractive_index`, so the uncached body is directly testable and no longer needs a decorator to reach.

Bounded at `INDEX_CACHE_MAX` (1024, matching the old `maxsize`) and cleared wholesale when full — the working set is a handful of wavelengths per material, so a precise LRU policy buys nothing.

`clear_cache()` empties only this instance, and `_load_database` invalidates on the way out (harmless during `__init__`, correct if it ever gains a `reload()`).

## Tests

14 new tests, **13 fail without the change**: the instance is now collectable, 25 construct-and-drop cycles leave nothing behind, the method no longer exposes `cache_info`/`cache_clear`, each instance owns its dict, clearing one leaves the other populated, `add_material` clears only its own, `_load_database` invalidates, the cache stays bounded, and cached values match `_compute_refractive_index` exactly.

`tests/test_material_cache.py` asserted `cache_info()` on the method, which no longer exists; it now asserts on the per-instance dict, keeping the same three behaviours.

title: Three divergent `WavefrontSensor` / `PSFCalculator` implementations; the optimizer's MTF merit uses the wrong one
body:
**Files:** `src/optimizer.py:19` vs `src/analysis/__init__.py:4` vs `openlens.py:41`

`src.optimizer` and `src.analysis.__init__` import from `beam_synthesis`; `openlens.py:41` imports
from `diffraction_psf`. The implementations differ **physically**:

- `diffraction_psf.py:166-179` removes piston **and tilt** via a least-squares plane fit and
  references a real sphere through the chief ray.
- `beam_synthesis.py:205-209` removes **piston only** and references a flat plane at
  `ref_ray.path[-1].x`.

`MeritFunction._eval_mtf` (`optimizer.py:188-197`) therefore scores the MTF of a **tilt-contaminated**
wavefront. At any nonzero field the pupil function carries a linear phase ramp, the PSF smears
across the padded window, and the MTF is dominated by field angle rather than aberration.

**Fix:** delete `beam_synthesis.WavefrontSensor` and `beam_synthesis.PSFCalculator`; import the
`diffraction_psf` pair everywhere (they supersede them: `pad_factor`, NaN masking, tilt removal,
reference sphere).

nodes.title: refactor(analysis): one wavefront/PSF implementation, and it removes tilt
nodes.body:
Closes #313

## Two implementations, different physics

| | `diffraction_psf` | `beam_synthesis` |
|---|---|---|
| reference | real sphere through the chief ray | flat plane at `ref_ray.path[-1].x` |
| piston removed | yes | yes |
| **tilt removed** | **yes** (least-squares plane fit) | **no** |
| padding / NaN mask | yes | no |

`psf_mtf`, `aberrations` and `openlens` already used the good one. Only `optimizer._eval_mtf` used the other.

## Measured residual tilt in the returned wavefront

```
field      beam_synthesis (removed)   diffraction_psf (survivor)
  0 deg           -5e-14                      -5e-15
  5 deg       -1.84e+02                      +4e-14
 10 deg       -3.80e+02                      -2e-13
```

So the MTF merit was scoring a wavefront carrying a **184-wave linear phase ramp** at 5°. That ramp smears the PSF across the padded window — the merit was measuring **field angle, not aberration**, and the optimizer was being driven by it.

## Fix

The two divergent classes are deleted. `GaussianBeam` and `BeamSynthesisPropagator` stay — Gaussian beam synthesis is a separate, still-valid feature. `analysis.__init__` and `optimizer` both name `diffraction_psf` explicitly, so there is now **one** object rather than two that can drift again. `analysis.__init__` no longer exports the ambiguous name `PSFCalculator`.

## Bonus: numpy degradation

`diffraction_psf` imported numpy unguarded, and `openlens.py` imports `WavefrontSensor` from it at module scope — so the app could not start without numpy, contradicting AGENTS.md's rule that numpy is optional. With the guard, `src.optimizer` and `src.analysis` import cleanly without numpy and the MTF merit returns `INFEASIBLE_MERIT`. The one remaining GUI blocker is `gui/dialogs/analysis_plots.py` — **#311's** territory, already fixed in PR #388.

## Tests

15 new tests: the deleted names are gone, the survivor is exported, all four consumers resolve to the *same* class object, residual tilt is ~1e-14 at 0°/5°/10°, a genuine quadratic defocus survives the plane fit intact (so tilt removal isn't quietly flattening real aberration), the MTF merit is finite, and the Airy-pattern assertions dropped from `test_beam_synthesis.TestPSF` are preserved against the survivor — with `pad_factor=4` rather than the removed copy's 2.

One of my own tests was wrong and I removed it: I asserted that constructing a `WavefrontError` with a linear ramp would strip it. `WavefrontError` is a plain holder; the fit happens inside the sensor.

title: Unmasked zero-filled wavefront samples leak a perfect pupil into the MTF merit
body:
**File:** `src/analysis/beam_synthesis.py:185-203`

```python
W = np.zeros(...)            # :153
if ray.terminated:
    W[i, j] = float("nan")   # :190  masked
else:
    if not ref_ray.path:
        continue             # :194  W stays 0.0, NOT NaN
    ...
    if abs(ray.direction.x) > 1e-6:
        W[i, j] = (ray.optical_path_length - ref_opl) / wavelength
        valid_mask[i, j] = True   # :203  else branch: W stays 0.0, not NaN
```

The PSF masks on `np.isnan` (`:246-248`) — **not** on `valid_mask`. If the chief-ray trace fails
(`ref_ray.path` empty), every traced grid point leaks → the pupil becomes `ones` over the clear
aperture → the "PSF" is the ideal Airy pattern and the MTF merit hits the **textbook maximum**.
The optimizer then drives toward vignetted designs. `diffraction_psf.py` does not have this bug.

**Fix:** assign `W[i, j] = float("nan")` before each `continue`, and build the amplitude mask from
`valid_mask` and pass it as `intensity_map`.

nodes.title: fix(beam): an unusable wavefront sample must be NaN, never a zero OPD
nodes.body:
Closes #314

## Problem

`PSFCalculator` builds its pupil amplitude from `np.isnan(W)`. So a sample left at its `np.zeros` initialisation is read as a **perfect zero-phase pupil point** — full weight, no aberration. Two branches did exactly that.

**1. The steep-ray branch had no `else`:**

```python
if abs(ray.direction.x) > 1e-6:
    W[i, j] = ...
```

A ray too steep to project onto the reference plane left `W` at `0.0`.

**2. The chief-ray guard never fired at all.**

```python
if not ref_ray.path:
    continue
```

`Ray3D.__init__` seeds `path` with `[origin]` and nothing clears it, so `not ref_ray.path` was **always False**. A chief ray that was *blocked* (terminated) was therefore accepted as the OPD reference — `ref_end` became that ray's own origin, putting the reference plane at the wrong *x* for every grid point.

## Verified

```
before:  172 of 172 in-aperture samples at full amplitude,  PSF peak 1.0
after:     0 of 256,                          pupil amplitude 0.0,  PSF peak 0.0
```

A PSF peak of 1.0 with a uniform pupil **is** the ideal Airy pattern, whose MTF merit is the textbook maximum. The optimizer was being rewarded for precisely the vignetted designs that caused the failure.

## Fix

The chief ray is tested for what actually matters — did it reach a reference plane, and is it still alive — with a warning when not; every in-aperture sample is then marked invalid. The steep-ray branch marks its sample invalid too.

Then, rather than trusting each branch to have remembered:

```python
W[~valid_mask] = np.where(np.isnan(W[~valid_mask]), W[~valid_mask], np.nan)
```

The mask is reconciled against `valid_mask` before returning, so the `np.isnan` mask `PSFCalculator` relies on is **authoritative by construction**.

## Tests

11 tests, **5 fail without the change**: a blocked chief ray marks every sample NaN, leaves no zero-filled leaks, gives zero pupil amplitude and a non-ideal PSF; an emptied chief-ray path also invalidates; a ray with no axial component is not recorded as a zero OPD; and the healthy path is unchanged — same valid-sample count, same aperture NaNs, finite PSF on- and off-axis.

title: `calculate_psf` empty-points branch returns the wrong keys → `KeyError` in the GUI
body:
**Files:** `src/analysis/psf_mtf.py:98-105` vs `:144-151`, consumed by `src/analysis/plots.py:129-134`

```python
# psf_mtf.py:99-105 (empty branch)
return {"image": ..., "x_axis": ..., "y_axis": ..., "centroid": ..., "step_size": ...}
# psf_mtf.py:144-151 (normal branch)
return {"image": ..., "y_axis": ..., "z_axis": ..., ...}
# plots.py:129-134
extent = [psf_data["z_axis"][0], psf_data["z_axis"][-1], ...]
```

Verified key sets differ: `['centroid','image','raw_count','step_size','x_axis','y_axis']` vs a
`z_axis` key. `plot_psf` raises `KeyError: 'z_axis'`. `openlens.py:869-878` calls both back-to-back,
so any fully-blocked design turns the PSF dialog into *"Failed to calculate PSF: 'z_axis'"*.

**Fix:** make both branches return the same keys; assert the key set in one place.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): give every calculate_psf branch the same key set
nodes.body:
Closes #315

## Problem

`calculate_psf` had three return paths that had drifted apart. The empty-points branch returned `x_axis` and **no `z_axis`**; the geometric and diffraction branches returned `y_axis`/`z_axis`/`raw_count`.

`plot_psf` reads `z_axis`:

```
extent = [psf_data[z_axis][0], psf_data[z_axis][-1], ...]
```

…and `openlens.py` calls `calculate_psf` and `plot_psf` **back to back**, so any fully blocked design turned the PSF dialog into *"Failed to calculate PSF: 'z_axis'"*.

Verified before the fix:

```
empty branch keys : ['centroid', 'image', 'step_size', 'x_axis', 'y_axis']
plot_psf RAISED KeyError 'z_axis'
```

## Fix

- The empty branch returns the full key set, and builds its axes as **bin centers exactly as the populated branch does** — so an empty PSF has the same extent as a populated one, not a different one.
- Rather than restate the contract in a third return statement (which is how the branches drifted apart in the first place), `PSF_KEYS` + `_psf_result` assert it in **one place**, and all three branches route through it.

A missing key now fails at the source, rather than as a `KeyError` in a plotting function three modules away.

## Tests

11 tests, **8 fail without the change**: the key set of all three branches, that all three agree exactly, that `x_axis` is gone, that `plot_psf` accepts each of the three, and that empty axes match populated ones.

title: Global optimizers hardcode `success=True` and report fabricated `initial_merit` / `iterations`
body:
**Files:** `src/global_optimizer.py:140-150, 237-251` vs `src/optimizer.py:520-534`

```python
return OptimizationResult(
    success=True,                                                    # never validated
    iterations=generations * population_size + local_result.iterations,  # counts evaluations
    initial_merit=history_merit[0],                                  # best of gen 0, not the start
```

`optimize_simplex` computes `best_valid = all(var.is_valid(v) ...)` and reports `success=best_valid`;
both global paths discard it. `history_merit[0]` is the best design of generation 0 (after 50 random
mutations), not `current_design`, so `improvement` is computed against a fabricated baseline.

**Fix:** factor the "pick best, validate bounds, build result" tail of `optimize_simplex` into a
shared `_finalize(best_values, ...)` used by all three algorithms.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): report honest success, iterations and baselines
nodes.body:
Closes #316

## Problem

Both global optimizer paths discarded the bookkeeping `optimize_simplex` already did correctly:

```python
success=True,                                              # never validated
iterations=generations * population_size + local_result.iterations,   # evaluations
initial_merit=history_merit[0],                            # best of gen 0
```

`optimize_simplex` computes `best_valid = all(var.is_valid(v) ...)` and reports it — the global paths threw that away.

`history_merit[0]` is the **best design of generation 0**, i.e. after up to 50 random mutations — not the starting design. Improvement was therefore measured against a baseline the search never started from, inflating the reported percentage.

## Fix

The "pick best, validate bounds, build result" tail of `optimize_simplex` is factored into `_finalize()`, used by all three algorithms:

- `success` comes from the bounds check, never asserted. Out-of-bounds now yields `success=False` and a message naming the cause.
- `initial_merit` is the merit of the **actual starting design**. For SA the entry merit is captured before the annealing loop reassigns `current_merit`; for the GA the starting design is re-evaluated instead of reading generation 0.
- `iterations` counts iterations performed — the GA now reports `generations + local steps`, not `generations * population_size + local steps`.

## Why `best_values` was added to the result

The global paths refine with a second `optimize_simplex` pass. Without the settled design exposed on the result, they would have bounds-checked the *pre-refinement* point while returning the *refined* system — validating the wrong thing. `OptimizationResult.best_values` makes the reported design checkable, and the asphyxiation early-return in `optimize_simplex` populates it too.

## Tests

6 tests in `tests/test_global_optimizer.py`; 3 fail without the change.

Two notes from writing them, both pre-existing and left alone:
- The global paths assign `variables[i].current_value` **in place**, so a test must build fresh `OptimizationVariable` objects per run or an earlier run moves the next one's starting point.
- Merit evaluation touches the system's own lenses (wavelength-dependent indices), so a shared `OpticalSystem` across algorithms makes the baseline drift.

title: `optimize_genetic` crashes when no design ever beats `inf`
body:
**File:** `src/global_optimizer.py:180-181, 200-202, 210, 231-232`

```python
best_overall_design = None
if min_merit < best_overall_merit:        # NaN < inf is False
    best_overall_design = list(population[best_idx])
new_population.append(list(best_overall_design))    # TypeError
```

**Repro (verified):** `optimize_genetic(generations=0)` →
`TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`. The same happens for any merit that evaluates to
`NaN` — which `_eval_mtf` (`optimizer.py:196`, `float(np.sum(mtf))`) can produce from a
NaN-contaminated PSF (see T-24).

**Fix:** initialise `best_overall_design = current_design` before the loop, guard with
`math.isfinite`, and normalise NaN merits to `INFEASIBLE_MERIT` in `_evaluate_design`.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): stop a NaN or empty generation from crashing the GA
nodes.body:
Closes #317

## Problem

`optimize_genetic` kept its elite design in a variable that started as `None`:

```python
best_overall_design = None
if min_merit < best_overall_merit:        # NaN < inf is False
    best_overall_design = list(population[best_idx])
new_population.append(list(best_overall_design))    # TypeError
```

Any run where nothing ever beat infinity raised `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable` — reproduced with `generations=0`, and reachable with **any merit that evaluates to `NaN`**, which `_eval_mtf` can produce from a NaN-contaminated PSF.

## Fix

1. The elite is **seeded with the starting design**, so it is never `None`.
2. The improvement test is guarded with `math.isfinite`, so a NaN generation is skipped *deliberately* rather than by the accident of `NaN < x` being `False`.
3. `_evaluate_design` normalises a NaN merit to `INFEASIBLE_MERIT`. NaN poisons every comparison it joins (`min`, `<`, sorting); normalising at the single point all three algorithms pass through lets search code treat `INFEASIBLE_MERIT` as the ordinary worst case.
4. `history_merit` is empty for `generations=0`, so the reported baseline falls back to the seeded merit instead of indexing past the end.

## Verified

```
generations=0 -> ok success=True initial=2415.9724 final=1990.5322 hist=0
generations=1 -> ok success=True initial=2031.2633 final=1990.5322 hist=1
NaN merit generations=2 -> ok initial=1000000000.0 finite=True
_evaluate_design normalises NaN -> True
simulated annealing still ok -> final=1990.5322
```

## Tests

6 tests in `tests/test_global_optimizer.py`; 4 fail without the change. One guards that ordinary runs still improve, so the seeding cannot silently neuter the search.

nodes.title: refactor(psf): delete 70 unreachable lines from calculate_mtf
nodes.body:
Closes #319

## Problem

Immediately after `calculate_mtf`'s live `return` sat a **verbatim copy** of the block above it, calling `calculate_psf` with three keywords that do not exist:

```python
psf_data = self.calculate_psf(
    field_angle=field_angle,      # no such parameter
    wavelength=wavelength,        # no such parameter
    focus_shift=focus_shift,      # no such parameter
```

## It was a trap, not just dead code

The block was dead by accident of ordering: the `return` lives inside the `if use_diffraction:` branch, and the copy sits *after* that branch in the function body. Meanwhile the legacy-kwargs shim at the top of `calculate_mtf` exists **precisely to accept the old names** — so anyone widening that shim would have made the copy reachable, turning three `NameError`s into a silently different MTF path.

Nothing referenced it, so it could only ever rot.

## Fix

Deleted. **No behaviour change** — verified by dumping `freq`/`mtf_tan`/`mtf_sag` for the geometric and diffraction paths at on- and off-axis field, before and after: all 4 cases bit-identical.

## Guard tests

Three keep it out. The main one walks the function's **own body** as well as nested statement lists for statements following a `return`:

```python
# the block sat directly in calculate_mtf's body, so an AST check that only
# scanned nested bodies misses it - my first attempt did exactly that and
# passed on the unfixed file.
```

The other two check on the AST that no call to `calculate_psf` uses a legacy keyword, and that the stale comment marker appears once rather than twice.

Seven further tests pin the MTF behaviour itself: key sets, zero frequency, `max_freq` respected, MTF ≤ 1, and that the geometric and diffraction paths still differ (which would catch a short-circuit).

## Tests

10 tests, **3 fail without the change**.

title: `ImageQualityAnalyzer.simulate_image` fails on 2-D input and truncates on `uint8`
body:
**File:** `src/analysis/psf_mtf.py:543, 556, 580`

```python
output_image = np.zeros_like(image_array)        # :543 inherits uint8
channel = image_array[:, :, i]                   # :556 IndexError for 2-D
output_image[:, :, i] = convolved                # :580 truncates to 0/1
```

A 2-D grayscale array → `IndexError: too many indices for array`. A `uint8` input has the float
result truncated to 0/1 before `np.clip(0, 1)`. Note `ImageSimulator._create_grid_pattern` and
friends return 2-D arrays.

**Fix:** branch on `image_array.ndim`; allocate `output_image = np.zeros(image_array.shape, dtype=np.float64)`.

nodes.title: fix(psf): accept 2-D and integer images in simulate_image
nodes.body:
Closes #320

## Problem

`simulate_image` assumed an `(H, W, 3)` float input in two ways:

```python
output_image = np.zeros_like(image_array)   # :543 inherits uint8
channel = image_array[:, :, i]              # :556 IndexError for 2-D
output_image[:, :, i] = convolved           # :580 truncates to 0/1
```

Both reproduced:

```
--- 2-D grayscale input ---
  IndexError: too many indices for array: array is 2-dimensional, but 3 were indexed
--- uint8 3-D input ---
  dtype: uint8  unique values: [1]  max: 1
```

A uint8 image saturated to a single value — the entire image clipped to 1.

## Fix

- The array is validated: 2-D or 3-D, with channel count matching `wavelengths_nm`.
- Integer input is scaled by its dtype maximum, so the clip can't saturate it. Without this the `np.clip(0, 1)` still blows out any 0–255 image.
- Output is always `float64`, in the **input's shape**. A 2-D input returns 2-D: the per-wavelength results are averaged rather than inventing a third axis the caller didn't ask for.

## After

```
2-D grayscale : shape=(32, 32)    dtype=float64 range=[0.075, 0.445]
3-D float     : shape=(32, 32, 3) dtype=float64 range=[0.050, 0.499]
3-D uint8     : shape=(32, 32, 3) dtype=float64 range=[0.056, 0.510] distinct=3072
uint8 vs float agree: max abs diff = 0.0015
```

## Tests

7 tests in `tests/test_psf_mtf.py`; all fail without the change.

title: `ProcessPoolExecutor` inside a GUI `QThread` pickles the whole optimizer
body:
**File:** `src/optimizer.py:621-623`

```python
if n_vars > 4:
    with ProcessPoolExecutor() as executor:
        f_plus_list = list(executor.map(self._evaluate_design, perturbed_designs))
```

`self._evaluate_design` is a **bound method**, so `executor.map` pickles the entire `LensOptimizer` —
the deep-copied `OpticalSystem`, the targets, and the (large) `_merit_cache` — once per task.
Problems: (a) children get a *copy* of the cache, so all parent-side caching is wasted; (b) under
`spawn` (macOS/Windows/PyInstaller) the child re-imports `__main__`, which for `python3 openlens.py`
re-enters the Qt app; (c) a pool is constructed and torn down on *every* gradient call; (d) forking a
process holding Qt/matplotlib state is a known hang source.

**Fix:** use a module-level worker taking `(picklable_system, targets, values)`, or drop the pool —
`_evaluate_design` is dominated by a single-threaded Python ray trace anyway.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): stop forking worker processes inside the GUI thread
nodes.body:
Closes #321

`LensOptimizer._calculate_gradient` spread its finite-difference
perturbations over a `ProcessPoolExecutor`:

```python
with ProcessPoolExecutor() as executor:
    f_plus_list = list(executor.map(self._evaluate_design, perturbed_designs))
```

`self._evaluate_design` is a **bound method**, so each task pickled the
entire optimizer - the deep-copied `OpticalSystem`, the targets and the
whole merit cache. Each child then evaluated against a private copy of
that cache, so none of the parent-side caching was reused.

The part that actually bites: this runs inside `OptimizationWorker`, a
`QThread` holding live Qt state. Under the `spawn` start method (macOS,
Windows, PyInstaller) the child re-imports `__main__`, which for
`python3 openlens.py` starts a second Qt application. Forking a process
that holds Qt/matplotlib state is also a known hang source. And a pool
was constructed and torn down on *every* gradient call, so process
startup dominated the work it was meant to parallelise.

## The fix

A bounded `ThreadPoolExecutor`. No pickling, one shared merit cache, no
child process to re-enter `__main__`, and threads rather than whole
processes per call.

Fan-out is capped at `GRADIENT_MAX_WORKERS = 4`, because each evaluation
deep-copies the system and unbounded fan-out would compete for memory
rather than help. The `> 4` variable threshold is preserved.

## Honest note on the speedup

I measured this rather than assuming. On a 5-variable singlet:

| path | time |
|---|---|
| `ProcessPoolExecutor` gradient | 130 ms |
| `ThreadPoolExecutor` gradient | 238 ms |
| pure serial, same 5 evaluations | 216 ms |

The gradients are numerically identical in all three. The merit function
is GIL-bound Python ray tracing, so the old process pool bought ~1.6x by
paying four process spawns per call - and that factor shrinks on
realistic (slower) merit functions while the fork hazard stays constant.

So this is deliberately a safety fix, not a speed fix: it trades an
unreliable 1.6x that can deadlock or re-enter `__main__` under Qt for a
path that is no worse than serial and cannot hang.

## Tests

New `tests/test_optimizer_gradient_parallel.py` (7 tests):
- no process pool is imported or referenced anywhere in the module -
  checked via **AST**, not text matching, so the docstring can still
  explain what was replaced
- the threaded gradient matches a serial recomputation to 9 places
- every component is finite, and not NaN
- no child processes are spawned or leaked
- the merit cache is shared across perturbations (the thing the process
  pool silently defeated)
- the below-threshold serial path still works, and fan-out stays bounded

Full suite: 1069 tests, 31 skipped, no new failures. flake8 output on
`src/optimizer.py` is byte-identical to the master baseline.

title: `PerformanceMetrics.calculate_back_focal_length` returns the EFL for a system
body:
**File:** `src/performance_metrics.py:110-116`

```python
elif self.system:
    f = self.system.get_system_focal_length()
    if f and self.system.elements:
        last_elem = self.system.elements[-1]      # dead
        # Approximate: system focal length - distance to last surface
        return f                                 # <- comment says "minus", code returns f
```

The returned BFL equals the EFL — an error of the whole back focal distance (typically 10-50 mm).
`OpticalSystem.calculate_back_focal_length()` (`:597`) already exists and is not used.

**Fix:** `return self.system.calculate_back_focal_length()`.

nodes.title: fix(perf): report the real back focal length for a system
nodes.body:
Closes #322

## Problem

`PerformanceMetrics.calculate_back_focal_length()` returned `get_system_focal_length()` verbatim for a system target:

```python
elif self.system:
    f = self.system.get_system_focal_length()
    if f and self.system.elements:
        last_elem = self.system.elements[-1]
        # Approximate: system focal length - distance to last surface
        return f          # <- comment says minus, code returns f
```

The comment describes a subtraction that never happens, and `last_elem` is bound and never read. Every reported back focal distance was the EFL — too long by the whole distance from the last surface to focus, typically 10–50 mm.

```
PerformanceMetrics BFL : 200.59241626938237   <- the EFL
OpticalSystem BFL      : 180.8039744044078     <- the real BFL
```

## Fix

`OpticalSystem.calculate_back_focal_length()` already derives this from the system ABCD matrix (`-A/C`, measured from the last surface). The wrapper now delegates rather than duplicating a broken approximation.

```
BFL now           : 180.8039744044078
OpticalSystem BFL : 180.8039744044078 | match: True
```

The single-lens branch is untouched, and an empty system still returns `None`.

## Tests

5 tests in `tests/test_performance_metrics.py`; 3 fail without the change.

title: No atomic file writes; a crash mid-export destroys the previous file
body:
**Files:** `src/export_formats.py:24, 80, 159, 350, 517, 590, 636`; `src/io/export.py:22`;
`src/io/step_export.py:160`; `src/stl_export.py:277`; `src/preset_lenses.py:246`;
`src/material_database.py:293, 614`

`open(path, "w")` truncates immediately. Because T-05 raises *after* the open, and `StepWriter.generate()`
/ `json.dump` can raise partway, the user loses the previously exported file and is left with a
partial one. `add_material` (`:305`) calls `save_database()` per material, so `import_csv_catalog`
truncates and rewrites the whole file N times — any failure leaves `materials.json` destroyed.

**Fix:** write to `path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")` in the same directory, then
`os.replace(tmp, path)`.

nodes.title: fix(io): write exports atomically so a crash cannot destroy the last file
nodes.body:
Closes #323

## Problem

`open(path, "w")` truncates immediately, so any failure after that point leaves the user with a truncated file **and** the previous good one already gone — a serialiser raising partway, a geometry check, an interrupt.

`material_database` was the sharpest case: `add_material()` calls `save_database()` per material, so `import_csv_catalog` truncated and rewrote the whole file N times. Any failure left `materials.json` destroyed.

## Fix

New `src/atomic.py`:

- `atomic_write_text`, `atomic_write_bytes`, `atomic_write_json`
- each writes to `path + ".tmp"` **in the same directory**, then `os.replace()`s it over the target — atomic on POSIX and Windows as long as both paths share a filesystem, hence the same directory
- the temporary file is removed on any failure, so the target is untouched unless the write fully succeeded

All 13 open-for-write sites route through it: `export_formats` (7), `io/export`, `preset_lenses`, `optical_system.save`, `material_database` (×2), `io/step_export`, `stl_export`.

## Two judgement calls worth reviewing

**No implicit `mkdir`.** An earlier draft created missing parent directories, which silently changed `OpticalSystem.save()` into *succeeding* on a path inside a non-existent directory — behaviour `test_save_to_unwritable_path_fails_gracefully` depends on. Removed, and the test now pins the absence.

**Placed at `src/atomic.py`, not `src/io/atomic.py`.** Importing anything under `src.io` runs `src/io/__init__.py`, which imports `export.py`, which imports `optical_system` — so a helper there is circular from `optical_system`, itself one of the call sites.

## Tests

13 tests in `tests/test_atomic_writes.py`.

Only **one** discriminates the call sites (`test_material_database_save_keeps_previous_file`); the rest exercise the new helper directly, including `BaseException` so `KeyboardInterrupt` cannot truncate a target either.

Worth being straight about: `StepExporter.export()` turned out **not** to be a truncation risk — it writes the file as its last step, after all entities are built. Its test passes either way and is kept only as a guard.

title: `StepExporter.export()` accumulates entities across calls
body:
**File:** `src/io/step_export.py:94-96, 112, 157-161`

`self.writer = StepWriter()` runs only in `__init__`; `export()` never resets it, and `_create_context()`
re-appends a fresh context each time. Verified: 48 lines after the first export, 96 after the second,
with 6 `DIRECTION` entities and 2 `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`s in one file.

**Fix:** `self.writer = StepWriter(); self.id_counter = 1` at the top of `export()`.

nodes.title: fix(step): reset the entity buffer on every STEP export
nodes.body:
Closes #324

## Problem

`StepExporter` built its `StepWriter` only in `__init__`, and `export()` never reset it:

```
48 lines after the first export, 96 after the second, with 6 DIRECTION
entities and 2 MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP's in one file
```

Every `export()` call re-ran `_create_context()` and re-emitted every solid, appending to the previous export's lines.

## Fix

`export()` now starts from a clean `StepWriter` and a clean id sequence, and resets the cached context ids (`axis_id`, `dir_*`, `origin`, `context`, `geom_context`, …) alongside it.

## Verified

```
entity counts per export: [48, 48, 48]
MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP count in one file: 1
DIRECTION count: 3
```

## Tests

5 tests in `tests/test_step_writer.py`; 2 fail without the change — the growing entity count, and repeated exports not being identical.

title: STEP housing/solid skips are logged at `debug` only
body:
**File:** `src/io/step_export.py:134-135` and `:149-150`

```python
except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as e:
    logger.debug("STEP housing part skipped: %s", e)
```

A malformed spacer/barrel dict produces a mechanical STEP drawing with silently missing parts.

**Fix:** `logger.warning` including the part name, and report a skip count from `export()`.

nodes.title: fix(io): report skipped STEP parts at WARNING with a skip count
nodes.body:
Closes #325

## Problem

Three skip paths in `StepExporter` logged at `logger.debug` — invisible at default verbosity:

```python
logger.debug("STEP housing part skipped: %s", e)
logger.debug("STEP solid export skipped: %s", e)
logger.debug("STEP tube export skipped (bad dims): %s", name)
```

A malformed spacer/barrel dict produced a mechanical STEP drawing with parts **quietly absent**. For an assembly drawing that is a part you cannot assemble — and nothing said so at any normal log level.

## Fix

All three now log at `WARNING` with the part name. The bad-dimension path also reports the values, since those are what the user has to fix:

```
WARNING STEP housing part 'MISSING_KEYS' skipped - malformed or missing
       z0/z1/r_inner/r_outer: 'z0'
WARNING STEP tube 'bad_dims' skipped - need r_outer > r_inner > 0 and z1 > z0,
       got r_inner=10.0 r_outer=8.0 z0=5.0 z1=1.0
WARNING STEP export wrote 3 solid(s) but skipped 2 part(s): MISSING_KEYS, bad_dims
```

`export()` now returns a summary:

```
{'shapes': 3, 'skipped': 2, 'skipped_parts': ['MISSING_KEYS', 'bad_dims']}
```

It previously returned `None`, so every existing caller — all of which ignore the result — is unaffected.

## One subtlety

`_export_tube_solid` returns `None` both when it rejects the dimensions and when there is no shape to write, so a rejected part has to be counted by the caller. The caller checks for a falsy `solid_id` and records the name; the method keeps logging its own diagnostic with the values.

## Tests

12 tests, **10 fail without the change**. One asserts the skip is reported at `WARNING` *or above* even with the logger set to `DEBUG` — which is exactly what regressed before.

title: Every row in the library is re-verified against the database on every keystroke
body:
**File:** `openlens.py:357-361` (`_save_to_database`), `openlens.py:170-183`

`_save_to_database` runs on every model change and stamps `target.metadata['tolerances']` onto the
current lens/assembly. Grep finds exactly **one** occurrence of `metadata['tolerances']` in the whole
repo — the write. There is no reader: `TolerancingTab.refresh()` repaints the table from the same
in-memory `self._parent._tol_operands` list. Because `_tol_operands` is a single global list on the
window, the same operand set gets stamped onto whichever target happens to be current.

**User-visible failure:** build a tolerance set, save, close, reopen → every operand is gone, and the
UI reports an empty table as if nothing was set. Meanwhile the never-restored list has been written
into every lens's metadata.

**Fix:** either load it back in `TolerancingTab.refresh()` when the target changes, or drop the write
until the read path exists. The two should land together.

nodes.title: fix(gui): restore a saved tolerance set instead of showing an empty table
nodes.body:
Closes #326

`_save_to_database` stamped `metadata['tolerances']` onto whichever model
happened to be current, and **nothing ever read it back** — grep finds the
write as the only occurrence in the repo.

Because `_tol_operands` is a single list on the window, that produced the
worst of both outcomes:

- one lens's tolerance set was written into every other lens's metadata
- the set the user actually built vanished on reopen, and
  `TolerancingTab.refresh()` repainted an **empty table** as if nothing had
  been set

Build a tolerance set, save, close, reopen → every operand is gone.

## The fix

The write and the read are now the same operation, on both sides tracked by
the window:

- `_use_tolerances_for(target)` — switching models stamps the *outgoing*
  model's own set into its metadata, then loads the incoming model's set. So
  each lens and assembly keeps its own tolerances.
- `_tol_operands_target` records ownership, so re-refreshing the **same**
  model is a no-op. That matters: `_update_all_tabs` runs on every change,
  and an unconditional reload would silently discard in-memory edits.

## Serialisation

`serialize_operands` / `deserialize_operands` live in `src/tolerancing.py`
as the single pair. Two things fixed along the way:

- the old inline writer never persisted `std_dev` or `surface`, so gaussian
  distributions silently lost their sigma and every operand lost its surface
- stored metadata is user-editable, so the loader treats every field as
  untrusted — an unknown `ToleranceType`, a missing key or a non-numeric
  bound drops that one operand with a warning instead of raising inside a
  GUI refresh

Round-tripping is lossless.

## Tests

New `tests/test_tolerance_persistence.py` (14 tests) against the **real**
`OpenLensWindow` methods, constructed with `__new__` to skip the Qt
`__init__` rather than reimplementing the logic under test.

Coverage: save→reopen restores the set; a set is not leaked into other
models; two models with different sets both round-trip; switching back
restores the first set; edits made since the last save survive a switch;
re-refreshing the same model keeps in-memory edits; a model with nothing
stored loads empty.

I verified the ownership tests genuinely fail against the old
save-only behaviour before accepting them.

Full suite: 1076 tests, 31 skipped, no new failures (the 6
`tests.gui_flows` loader errors are pre-existing — they only occur under
`unittest` without pytest, which is what the local system Python has).

Note `openlens.py` is deliberately outside the Black scope in CI
(`black ... src/ tests/ --check`), and I kept it that way.

title: Monte Carlo and Inverse Sensitivity are impossible for assemblies
body:
**File:** `src/gui/tabs/tolerancing_tab.py:336, 397, 424, 526, 560`

```python
if not self._parent or not self._parent._current_lens:
    self._tol_results_text.setPlainText("No lens selected.")
    return
```

All five entry points are gated on `_current_lens`, which is explicitly `None` whenever an assembly
is current. "Add Tolerance", "Default Set" and "Load Grade" are **silent no-ops** (no message). The
entire multi-element tolerancing workflow — the tab's reason to exist — is unreachable.

**Fix:** resolve the target through a helper mirroring `openlens.py:711-717`:
```python
target = self._parent._current_assembly or self._parent._current_lens
```
and wrap a bare `Lens` in a throwaway `OpticalSystem` (the worker already does this at `:85-86`).

nodes.title: fix(gui): make tolerancing work for assemblies
nodes.body:
Closes #327

## Problem

Every entry point gated on `_current_lens`, which is explicitly `None` whenever an assembly is current — the two are mutually exclusive in the main window:

```python
if not self._parent or not self._parent._current_lens:
    self._tol_results_text.setPlainText("No lens selected.")
    return
```

So the entire multi-element workflow — **the tab's reason to exist** — was unreachable, and "Add Tolerance", "Default Set" and "Load Grade" were *silent* no-ops that returned without a word.

## Fix

**Target resolution** — `_resolve_target()` resolves `_current_assembly or _current_lens`, and `_require_target()` reports "No lens or assembly selected." instead of returning silently. All five gates go through it.

**Worker tracing** — both workers now route the target through `_as_system()`, which passes an `OpticalSystem` through untouched and only wraps a bare `Lens`. Both previously did `OpticalSystem(); add_lens(current_lens)` unconditionally, so an assembly would have been reduced to a single element — discarding its second element, its gap, and the meaning of every element index in the operands.

**Element count** — the Add Tolerance dialog read `_current_lens`, so an assembly always looked like one element.

## Verified

All four combinations (lens/assembly × Monte Carlo / inverse sensitivity) start busy, clear their flag, reset the progress bar to 100, and print their report.

## Tests

10 tests in a new `tests/test_tolerancing_assemblies.py`. Worth noting: **reverted, they don't merely fail — the process segfaults (exit 139)**, so this path was worse than the silent no-op the ticket describes.

`_resolve_target` uses `getattr` with a default, matching the `hasattr` guards this file already uses for parent attributes — the real window always has both, but the tab is also driven by tests and embedders that don't.

title: Optimization variable selection is silently reset by any unrelated edit
body:
**File:** `src/gui/tabs/optimization_tab.py:354-357` and `:396-400`

```python
cb = QCheckBox(f"{label} ({val:.2f})")
cb.setChecked(label in ["Radius 1", "Radius 2", "Parabolic Sag 1", "Parabolic Sag 2"])
```

`refresh()` tears down and rebuilds every checkbox from a hard-coded default, and is reached from
`_update_all_tabs()` on **every** model change.

**Repro (verified):**
```
before typing:            ['r1_0']
after a name keystroke:   ['r1_0', 'r2_0', 'th_0']
```

**Fix:** persist the checked state across rebuilds and add `refresh(preserve_selection=True)` so
`_update_all_tabs` is non-destructive.

nodes.title: fix(gui): keep the optimization variable selection across refreshes
nodes.body:
Closes #328

## Problem

`refresh()` tore down and rebuilt every variable checkbox from a hard-coded default list, and it is reached from `_update_all_tabs()` on **any** model change:

```python
cb = QCheckBox(f"{label} ({val:.2f})")
cb.setChecked(label in ["Radius 1", "Radius 2", "Parabolic Sag 1", "Parabolic Sag 2"])
```

So one keystroke in an unrelated field silently undid the user's variable selection:

```
before typing:            ['r1_0']
after a name keystroke:   ['r1_0', 'r2_0', 'th_0']
```

Both the system branch and the single-lens branch had the same default list.

## Fix

`refresh()` snapshots each key's ticked state before the teardown and reapplies it.

**Unticked matters as much as ticked.** The default list pre-ticks Radius 1, Radius 2 and Thickness, so preserving only the ticked set would silently re-enable optimizing over parameters the user had deliberately *excluded*. A test pins this specifically.

**Selection carries over only while the target is the same object.** Switching to a different lens or assembly is a deliberate change of subject and still gets fresh defaults — otherwise the previous lens's ticks would follow the user across. Keys that no longer exist drop out naturally, since the rebuilt map only holds keys for live variables.

`refresh(preserve_selection=False)` keeps the old behaviour as an explicit escape hatch.

## Verified

```
defaults             : ['r1_0', 'r2_0', 'th_0']
user selection       : ['r1_0']
after unrelated edit : ['r1_0'] <-- preserved
after another edit   : ['r1_0'] <-- still preserved
after switching lens : ['r1_0', 'r2_0', 'th_0'] <-- fresh defaults
```

## Tests

8 tests in a new `tests/test_optimization_variable_selection.py`; 6 fail without the change. Covers single lens, assemblies, explicitly-unticked variables, repeated edits, target switching, and the escape hatch.

title: Deleting the current assembly leaves the editor bound to the deleted object
body:
**File:** `openlens.py:555-559`

```python
else:
    idx = self._assemblies.index(self._current_assembly)
    self._assemblies.pop(idx)
    self._current_assembly = self._assemblies[0] if self._assemblies else None
    self._update_status("Deleted assembly")
```

The lens branch (`:547-554`) calls `load_lens(...)` and `_update_all_tabs()`; the assembly branch
calls neither.

**Repro (verified):** after delete, `_current_assembly` is `Second` but the Assembly Editor still
displays `Assembly 1` and `self._optical_system` still points at the deleted object.

**User-visible failure:** make any further edit in that tab and `_on_assembly_changed` →
`_save_to_database` **re-INSERTs the row you just deleted** (with a new id, so it now appears twice).

**Fix:** mirror the lens branch — call `_set_current_item(...)` or `_show_assembly_editor(False)`, then

nodes.title: fix(gui): re-point the editor after deleting the current assembly
nodes.body:
Closes #329

## Problem

The lens branch of the delete handler re-points the editor; the assembly branch did neither:

```python
if self._current_lens:
    ...
    self._lens_editor.load_lens(self._current_lens)
    self._update_all_tabs()          # <- assembly branch has no equivalent
else:
    idx = self._assemblies.index(self._current_assembly)
    self._assemblies.pop(idx)
    self._current_assembly = self._assemblies[0] if self._assemblies else None
    self._update_status("Deleted assembly")
```

The consequence is worse than a stale display. `_save_to_database` reads `_assembly_tab_widget._optical_system` and, finding no matching entry in `_assemblies`, appends it — **re-INSERTing the row that was just deleted**, under a new id, so it appears twice.

## Fix

- The assembly branch now calls `_set_current_item(..., is_assembly=True)` + `_update_all_tabs()`, mirroring the lens branch.
- When the last assembly goes, both the window's and the tab's copy are cleared explicitly — `_update_all_tabs()` early-returns once nothing is current, so it cannot do it for us.
- `_load_assembly` no longer guards its assignment with `hasattr`. That guard meant the window attribute only existed on some paths, leaving the window and the Assembly Editor free to disagree — and `_save_to_database` trusts the tab's copy.
- The branch is guarded against *neither* a lens nor an assembly being current, where `.index(None)` would raise `ValueError`.

## Scope note

`openlens.py` is **not** black-clean and was deliberately not reformatted: doing so buries this 25-line fix under ~430 lines of unrelated churn. The diff is 25 insertions, 3 deletions.

## Tests

4 tests added to `tests/test_deletion_persistence.py` (reusing its existing hermetic window harness); 3 fail without the change, including one that reproduces the duplicate-row re-insert end to end.

title: `AssemblyTab.refresh_lens_list` is a self-perpetuating 100 ms timer
body:
**File:** `src/gui/tabs/assembly_tab.py:186-188`

```python
if self._assembly_lens_list.count() == 0:
    from PySide6.QtCore import QTimer
    QTimer.singleShot(100, self.refresh_lens_list)
```

No retry cap, no cancellation, no give-up state. `openlens.py:159-164` explicitly sets
`self._lenses = []` on the database-load failure path.

**Repro (verified):** 24 invocations in 1.2 s with an empty library, never terminating.

**User-visible failure:** if the database load fails, the assembly tab wakes the Qt event loop
10×/second for the entire session — measurable constant CPU, and it masks the real failure because
the user only ever sees an empty list.

**Fix:** bound the retries and store the timer so it can be cancelled; show a
"(no lenses — check the database)" placeholder after the cap. Reset the counter on success.

nodes.title: fix(gui): bound the assembly tab's empty-lens-list retry
nodes.body:
Closes #330

## Problem

`refresh_lens_list` ended with:

```python
if self._assembly_lens_list.count() == 0:
    QTimer.singleShot(100, self.refresh_lens_list)
```

No retry cap, no cancellation, no give-up state. `openlens.py` sets `self._lenses = []` on the database-load **failure** path — so a library that never fills woke the Qt event loop 10×/second for the entire session: measurable constant CPU, and it **hid the real problem** behind a permanently empty list.

```
before: 25 invocations in 1.2 s, still scheduling more, no placeholder
after:  capped at 20, timer released, placeholder shown
```

## Fix

- Bounded by `LENS_LIST_MAX_RETRIES` (20) at `LENS_LIST_RETRY_MS` (100) — a slow-but-real database load still gets ~2 s of grace.
- The `QTimer` is **held and reused** rather than recreated per attempt. A fresh `singleShot` each time is precisely what could not be cancelled, so `_cancel_lens_list_retry()` can now stop it, and success calls that.
- Exhausting the budget logs a warning and inserts a **non-selectable** placeholder naming the likely cause, so the user sees *why* the list is empty. The text shown is:

      (no lenses loaded - check the lens database)

- The counter resets on success, so a later genuine reload is retried normally.
- `getattr` for the parent lens list, so a parent lacking `_lenses` (exactly the failure path) does not raise.

## Tests

14 tests, and **every one fails without the change**. They drive the real `QTimer` through `QEventLoop` rather than asserting on internals: the cap holds, invocations stop once capped, the timer is reused rather than recreated, the placeholder appears and is non-selectable, it disappears when real lenses arrive, and a populated library schedules no timer at all.

title: `OpticalSystem._update_positions()` indexes `root.children` by the flat element index
body:
**File:** `src/optical_system.py:325-339`

```python
for i, element in enumerate(self.elements):
    element.position = current_pos
    if i < len(self.root.children):
        node = self.root.children[i]                    # <- wrong node
        node.position = vec3(current_pos, node.position.y, node.position.z)
```

`self.elements` is the *flattened* list (assemblies expanded); `self.root.children` may contain
`OpticalAssembly` nodes. Index *i* of the flat list is generally not child *i*.

**Repro (verified):**
```
BEFORE elements: [('A0', 0.0), ('A1', 1.0), ('L', 5.0)]
AFTER  elements: [('A0', 0.0), ('A1', 4.0), ('L', 8.0)]   # flat list (2D tracer + ABCD)
AFTER  flat:     [('A0', 0.0), ('A1', 1.0), ('L', 4.0)]   # tree    (3D tracer)  <- L was MOVED
```

Called from `refresh_references` (`:262`), `design_air_spaced_doublet` (`:758`), `tolerancing.py:158/295/361`,
`desensitization.py:144`, `optimizer.py:671`, `analysis/environmental.py:139`,
`gui/tabs/assembly_tab.py:395` — so any of these silently changes the analysed geometry for
assembly-based systems, and the 2D and 3D tracers then disagree.

**Fix:** drop the flat-index→root-child write (positions are already derived from the tree by
`_rebuild_from_tree()`), or look the node up by identity.

nodes.title: fix(system): match nodes to elements by identity, not by flat index
nodes.body:
Closes #331

## Problem

`_update_positions` walked the flat elements list and wrote axial positions into `root.children[i]`. Those two are **not index-aligned**: `elements` is flattened (assemblies expanded) while `root.children` may hold `OpticalAssembly` nodes, so element *i* is generally not child *i*.

```python
for i, element in enumerate(self.elements):
    if i < len(self.root.children):
        node = self.root.children[i]          # <- wrong node
        node.position = vec3(current_pos, ...)
```

Reproduced with an assembly holding `A0`/`A1` followed by a standalone lens `L`:

```
BEFORE  flat: [('A0', 0.0), ('A1', 1.0), ('L', 2.0)]
        tree: [('A0', 0.0), ('A1', 1.0), ('L', 2.0)]
AFTER   flat: [('A0', 0.0), ('A1', 1.0), ('L', 2.0)]
        tree: [('A0', 0.0), ('A1', 1.0), ('L', 1.0)]   <- L was MOVED
```

Flat index 1 is `A1`, which lives *inside* the assembly, so the node owning `L` was handed `A1`'s position. Flat list and tree then disagreed — and since the 2D/ABCD tracer reads one and the 3D tracer reads the other, **they analysed different geometry**.

Called from `refresh_references`, `design_air_spaced_doublet`, `tolerancing`, `desensitization`, the optimizer and environmental analysis, so any of those silently changed assembly-based systems.

## Fix

Nodes are matched to elements by **identity of the lens model they wrap**, and only direct children of root take their axial position from the flat layout — nested positions belong to the enclosing assembly. Lateral offsets are still preserved.

## Scope note

A flat running sum cannot represent nesting, so a thickness change on a *nested* element is still not expressible in the tree. That is pre-existing and deliberately left alone: routing this through `_rebuild_from_tree()` would discard the air-gap thicknesses the optimizer sets via its `AIR_GAP` variable. What is fixed is that such a change no longer drags an unrelated root child along with it.

## Tests

14 tests, **5 fail without the change**. Nine pin the flat (1:1) case that must keep working unchanged — node positions, propagation of a thickness change, decenter preservation, air-gap positions, empty system. Five cover the nested case, including that flat and tree agree across repeated updates.

title: `design_cemented_doublet` designs with database indices but builds lenses with static defaults
body:
**File:** `src/optical_system.py:685-729`

```python
n1 = crown.nd          # 1.78472 for SF11 (from the database)
n2 = flint.nd
...
flint_lens = Lens(name=..., material="SF11", ...)   # no refractive_index= !
```

`Lens.__init__` falls back to `DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES["SF11"] = 1.78` (`lens.py:138`,
`constants.py:42`) — **not** the 1.78472 the radii were solved with.

**Repro (verified):** `design_cemented_doublet(100.0, 50.0)` returns EFL 100.879 (0.9 % long) with
residual LCA 0.0386 mm — an "achromatic" doublet that is not achromatic.

**Fix:** pass `refractive_index=n1` / `refractive_index=n2` (or use `Lens.for_material(...)`).

nodes.title: fix(achromat): build doublet lenses with the solved refractive index
nodes.body:
Closes #332

## Problem

`design_cemented_doublet` solves the element radii from the catalog refractive index but builds the lenses without passing one:

```python
n1 = crown.nd          # 1.78472 for SF11, from the database
...
flint_lens = Lens(name=..., material="SF11", ...)   # no refractive_index= !
```

`Lens.__init__` falls back to `DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES["SF11"] = 1.78` — **not** the 1.78472 the radii were solved with. Each doublet was designed against one index and built as another.

## Fix

Both lenses now carry the exact `n1`/`n2` used for the radii:

```
                before      after
BK7 Element     1.516800    1.516800   (= db nd 1.5168)
SF11 Element    1.780000    1.784720   (= db nd 1.78472)
```

`Lens.for_material` is deliberately **not** used: it re-evaluates Sellmeier and lands on `1.785107`, a third value matching neither `nd` nor the static default. The designer must hand the lens the number it solved with.

## Note

The thick-lens approximation still leaves the built EFL above nominal (101.26 vs 100) — that is the designer's thin-lens solution applied to lenses with real thickness, and is a separate concern from this index mismatch.

## Tests

4 tests in `tests/test_optical_system_functional.py`; 3 fail without the change (the 4th pins the intended +/- power split).

title: `AberrationsCalculator.get_aberration_summary()` crashes for an `OpticalSystem`
body:
**File:** `src/aberrations.py:904-905`

```python
Lens: {self.lens.name:<52} ║
Material: {self.lens.material:<48} ║
```

`self.lens` is only assigned in the `else` branch of `__init__` (`aberrations.py:62-67`); for a
system target only `self.is_system` is set. Reproduced:
`AttributeError: 'AberrationsCalculator' object has no attribute 'lens'`.

**Fix:**
```python
name = self.lens.name if not self.is_system else f"{self.target.name} ({len(self.target.elements)} elements)"
material = self.lens.material if not self.is_system else "-"
```

nodes.title: fix(aberrations): report the system name in the summary header
nodes.body:
Closes #333

## Problem

`get_aberration_summary()` read `self.lens.name` and `self.lens.material`, but `AberrationsCalculator.__init__` only assigns `self.lens` in the single-lens branch (`aberrations.py:62-67`). For a system target only `self.is_system` is set.

```
AttributeError: 'AberrationsCalculator' object has no attribute 'lens'
```

`calculate_all_aberrations()` works fine on an `OpticalSystem` — it is only the *report* that crashes, so the analysis was reachable but its summary was not.

## Fix

The header now describes the target it was actually given:

```
║ Lens: Doublet (2 elements)                                 ║
║ Material: -                                                ║
```

The frame's line widths are unchanged — a test asserts the system and single-lens summaries produce the same set of box-line widths, so the substitution cannot silently break the alignment.

## Tests

4 tests in `tests/test_aberrations.py`; 3 fail without the change (the 4th pins the single-lens header, which was never broken).
