title: Legacy databases (user_version 0) are stamped v5 without their columns; every save then fails
body:
**Where:** `src/database.py:166-240`

Databases created before the `user_version` pragma existed have `user_version = 0` but already contain the old `lenses` table. The `version == 0` branch assumes a new file. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` does nothing, and then `user_version` is set to 5. The columns added since v1 (`is_parabolic_*`, `clear_aperture_*`, `bevel_*`, `coating_*`) are never added, and they never will be because the version already says 5.

**Repro:** build a DB with `git show a2b08aa^:src/database.py`, then open it with the current code:
```
Failed to save lenses: table lenses has no column named is_parabolic_1
save -> False
```

**Fix:**
- When the version is 0 and `lenses` exists, run `_add_column` for every v2-v5 column before stamping. `_add_column` already skips columns that exist, so this is safe.
- Refuse to open (or open read-only) a DB whose `user_version` is higher than the app supports. Today `user_version=99` opens and gets written to.
- Add a migration test with a fixture DB for each historical version.

nodes.title: fix(database): migrate pre-pragma databases instead of stamping them current
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(database): migrate pre-pragma databases instead of stamping them current

A database written before the `user_version` pragma existed reads
`user_version = 0` but already holds a real `lenses` table in the v1 shape. The
`version == 0` branch assumed a brand-new file, so its `CREATE TABLE IF NOT
EXISTS` statements did nothing, the file was stamped **5**, and none of the
columns added since v1 was ever added.

Because the version then read 5, no later launch would add them either. Every
save failed with:

```
Failed to save lens: table lenses has no column named is_parabolic_1
```

and stayed broken for as long as the user kept the file — with no way out but
deleting their library.

Reproduced before the fix: a v1-shaped database left unstamped ended at
`user_version 5`, `is_parabolic_1: False`, `coating_1: False`, and
`save_lens` raised.

### The fix

- Detect an unstamped database that already has tables and stamp it **1**
  instead, so the existing `v1 → v5` ladder adds whatever it is missing.
  `_add_column` already skips columns that exist, so this is safe for any
  legacy shape.
- The ladder's `v1 → v2` step now re-reads `PRAGMA user_version` instead of
  testing the value read on entry, which lets a file stamped 1 a moment earlier
  take that step. All five steps are now one consistent sequential chain.
- Table creation stays ahead of that check, so a file missing some tables
  entirely still gets them before the ladder tries to `ALTER` them.

### Also refuses a database from a newer OpenLens

`user_version = 99` opened happily and was written to, so an old build could
stamp an older version over a newer library. It now raises
`UnsupportedSchemaVersionError`, naming both versions and the file. The
version check and the whole migration already run inside one
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, so raising leaves the file untouched.

### Notes

- `SCHEMA_VERSION` replaces the hardcoded `5`s. It stays local to `database.py`
  rather than moving to `constants.py`, because it is meaningless outside this
  ladder and the module deliberately takes no intra-package imports.
- The test fixtures are **cumulative** per version. The ladder only ever moves
  forward, so a fixture that stamped a v1-shaped table "v4" would describe a
  shape no released build ever wrote — the first attempt at these tests failed
  exactly that way and was the fixture's fault, not the migration's.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #429

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      confirmed by reverting *only* the two behavioural repairs (keeping the
      new exception importable): **9 of 14 new tests fail**, all 14 pass with
      them restored
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_database_migrations` — 14 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_database tests.test_tolerance_persistence tests.test_deletion_persistence tests.test_gui` — 102 tests with the migration suite, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1596 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors that exist on clean
      `master` (they need `pytest`, which cannot be installed in this dev
      container because of PEP 668), no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — clean for this branch
- [x] `flake8 src/database.py` — no new findings. The one remaining `E501` at
      the `INSERT INTO assembly_air_gaps` SQL literal is pre-existing; verified
      by running flake8 against `git show master:src/database.py`
- [x] Coverage includes: every historical version (1–5) migrating forward, the
      unstamped legacy case, a partially-present schema, row preservation
      across each migration, migration idempotency on reopen, defaults on
      pre-existing rows, and that a refused future database keeps both its
      `user_version` and its columns

title: GUI never reports a failed save; 'Saved to database' is shown regardless
body:
**Where:** `openlens.py:101`, `:249-265`, `:750-751`, `:183-188`; `src/gui/storage.py:163-166`

`LensStorage.save_lenses` catches every exception, reports it through `status_callback` and returns `False`. The main window creates `LensStorage(self._db_path)` with no callback and `_save_to_database` ignores the return value. `_on_save` always says "Saved to database". Nothing calls `logging.basicConfig`, so the error is only visible through Python's last-resort stderr handler. A failed load (`:183`) is only logged and resets `_current_lens` to `None` while the editor still holds a lens, so later edits go nowhere.

Combined with the migration bug (legacy DB), every edit is lost silently.

**Fix:**
- Pass `self._update_status` as the storage status callback.
- Check the return value and show `QMessageBox.critical` the first time a save fails.
- Configure logging in `main()`.
- Tell the user when a load fails instead of silently resetting state.
- Consider making `save_lenses` raise and letting the caller decide.

nodes.title: fix(gui): report a failed save instead of claiming it succeeded
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(gui): report a failed save instead of claiming it succeeded

`LensStorage.save_lenses` catches every exception, reports it through an
optional status callback and returns `False`. The main window built its storage
with no callback, discarded the return value, and `_on_save` said **"Saved to
database"** regardless. Nothing called `logging.basicConfig`, so the only trace
of the failure was Python's last-resort stderr handler.

The effect was that any failing save looked like a successful one. On a
database this app could not write to, the user typed, saw "Saved to database",
reopened the app, and found every edit gone with nothing explaining why. This
is the reporting half of #429's failure mode: the migration bug made every save
fail, and this bug meant the user was never told.

### Changes

- pass `self._update_status` as the storage callback, so storage's own failure
  messages reach the status bar (it defaulted to a no-op `lambda`)
- `_save_to_database` returns a `bool` and `_on_save` reports success only when
  it is `True`
- `LensStorage` keeps `last_error`, because `save_lenses` swallows the
  exception and `False` is all the caller would otherwise get — the dialog
  needs the real reason, not a generic message
- show the problem **once per failure streak**, re-armed by the next success.
  Saving runs on every edit, so a dialog per keystroke would be unusable; the
  status bar still reports every failure
- a failed **load** now says so instead of silently emptying the library — if
  the editor still holds a lens, that lens's edits have nowhere to go
- configure logging in `main()`, so `logger.error` reaches stderr at all

### Why the problem reports are non-modal

The first attempt used `QMessageBox.critical` and **hung the entire test
suite** — `exit 124`, no output. `exec()` runs a nested event loop, and because
the library load is fired from a deferred startup timer (`QTimer.singleShot`),
a report raised during one test froze the suite when a later test spun the
event loop.

Reports now go through `_notify_problem`, which uses `show()` and clears window
modality. That is also the better behaviour for users: the box is visible and
the status bar carries the same message permanently, but the app never freezes
before the user can act. `TestProblemReportsDoNotBlock` asserts `isModal()` is
`False`, so this cannot silently regress.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #430

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      confirmed, the pre-fix run produced 9 failures + 3 errors, including
      `AssertionError: 'Saved to database' unexpectedly found in the status bar`
      after a database that raises
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_gui_save_reporting` — 17 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_gui_save_reporting tests.test_gui_delete_shortcut tests.test_gui_export_wiring tests.test_database_migrations` — 40 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1602 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors that exist on clean
      `master` (they need `pytest`, which cannot be installed in this dev
      container because of PEP 668), no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 211 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 src/gui/storage.py` — no new findings. The `E402`/`F401` there are
      pre-existing; verified by running flake8 against
      `git show master:src/gui/storage.py`
- [x] Coverage includes: a real database failure, a `save_lenses`-returns-
      `False`-only failure (no exception visible to the caller), a success
      still reporting success, three consecutive failures producing exactly one
      report, the status bar remaining truthful throughout, the report
      re-arming after a success, the storage callback actually reaching the
      status bar, a failed load being reported, and the non-blocking properties
      of the report itself

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: Tolerance sets (and any `metadata`) are never persisted to the database
body:
**Where:** `openlens.py:209-211` (`_sync_tolerances_to_metadata`), `src/optical_system.py:434-458`, `Lens.to_dict` in `src/lens.py`

`_sync_tolerances_to_metadata` writes `target.metadata['tolerances']`. Neither `Lens.to_dict()` nor `OpticalSystem.to_dict()` includes `metadata`, and neither `from_dict` restores it. `tests/test_tolerance_persistence.py` only checks in-memory state.

**Repro:**
```
a.metadata={'tolerances':[{'x':1}]}; save; reload -> meta: None
Lens has no `metadata` attribute at all after reload
DB lenses.metadata = {"type":"Biconvex","wavelength":587.6,...}  # no tolerances
```

**Fix:** make `metadata` a real attribute on both models, include it in `to_dict`, and restore it in `from_dict`. Add a save-reload-compare test that goes through SQLite.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): give Lens and OpticalSystem a real, persisted metadata attribute
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(analysis): give `Lens` and `OpticalSystem` a real, persisted `metadata`

The GUI keeps a target's tolerance set on `target.metadata['tolerances']`
(`OpenLensWindow._sync_tolerances_to_metadata`), but **neither model had a
`metadata` attribute at all** — the window conjured one up on demand. The save
path therefore worked in memory and then lost everything:

- `Lens.to_dict()` and `OpticalSystem.to_dict()` omitted `metadata`, so the
  tolerance set never reached the database;
- `load_all` flattened the metadata blob into the row dict and then `del`-ed the
  key, so a reloaded `Lens` had no `metadata` attribute to read.

The tolerance table came back empty on reopen with nothing to say why.
`tests/test_tolerance_persistence.py` only asserted in-memory state — the half
that worked.

### The blob stays flat

The model's own `metadata` is folded in **beside** the keys that have never had
a column (that is already how `lens_type`, `wavelength` and the model-glass
numbers are persisted), not nested under a `metadata` key. Nesting would write
`{"metadata": {"metadata": ...}}` and break every existing reader, which expects
the blob to be flat. `_metadata_merge` now *returns* the parsed blob so the
loader can hand it to the model instead of discarding it.

### `metadata` holds only what has no home on the model

`from_dict` subtracts the keys `to_dict` emits. Without this, `metadata` came
back holding `type`, `wavelength`, `temperature`, `model_nd`, … — a duplicate
of every attribute, and the reason `metadata["type"]` collided with the row
marker. `_LENS_SERIALIZED_KEYS` and `_SYSTEM_SERIALIZED_KEYS` live beside
`to_dict` and are **asserted against it**, so the two cannot drift apart and
start leaking fields into `metadata` on every reload.

Pre-existing flat blobs still resolve: `lens_type`, `wavelength` and `material`
keep reaching the model, covered by a dedicated test.

`to_dict` returns a **copy** of `metadata`; handing out the live dict would let
an exported dict edit the model.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #431

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      confirmed, the pre-fix run produced 17 errors + 1 failure, including
      `AttributeError: 'Lens' object has no attribute 'metadata'`
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_metadata_persistence` — 20 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_metadata_persistence tests.test_database tests.test_database_migrations tests.test_gui_save_reporting tests.test_coating tests.test_tolerance_persistence` — 118 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1605 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors that exist on clean
      `master` (they need `pytest`, which cannot be installed in this dev
      container because of PEP 668), no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 212 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 src/lens.py src/optical_system.py` — no new findings. The `E402` /
      `F401` / `F841` there are pre-existing; verified by running flake8 against
      `git show master:<file>` (1 and 3 findings respectively, unchanged)
- [x] Coverage includes: a full save/close/reopen round trip through SQLite for
      both `Lens` and `OpticalSystem`, the GUI `LensStorage` path, the blob
      staying flat, column-backed keys keeping their own columns, legacy flat
      blobs still reaching the model, absent metadata staying empty, defaults on
      models being unshared (no mutable-default leak), and the serialized-key
      sets matching `to_dict`

## Notes

- **Found while working on this, not fixed here:** `load_all` returns
  `type='Biconvex'` for a lens, because the blob's `type` overwrites the row's
  `'Lens'` marker. Harmless in production — `LensStorage.load_lenses` dispatches
  on `!= "OpticalSystem"` — but any filter written as `== "Lens"` matches
  nothing, including `tests/test_database.py::_load_lenses`. Verified
  pre-existing on `master`; filed as #488 rather than widening this PR.

title: Deleting from the CLI or the startup dialog does not delete the DB row; the item comes back
body:
**Where:** `src/lens_editor.py:320-323`, `src/gui/dialogs/startup.py:406-414`, `src/gui/storage.py:106-157`

Both call `save_lenses(remaining)` with the default `reconcile=False`. That path only inserts or replaces rows and never deletes (the docstring says so). The CLI prints "Lens deleted successfully!" and the lens is back on the next start. The startup dialog also bypasses the "lens is used by an assembly" check that `delete_item` enforces, and hard-codes `"openlens.db"`. `save_lenses` returns `False` instead of raising, so the dialog's `except` at `:413` never fires.

**Fix:** call `storage.delete_item(item.id)` in both places and handle `LensInUseError`. Inject the storage object into the startup dialog instead of letting it open its own.

nodes.title: fix(storage): deleting must actually remove the row
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(storage): deleting must actually remove the row

Both delete paths dropped the item from an in-memory list and then called
`save_lenses(remaining)`. That method defaults to `reconcile=False`, and its own
docstring says it *only inserts or replaces rows and never reconciles
deletions* — so nothing was ever deleted. The CLI printed **"✓ Lens deleted
successfully!"** and the lens reappeared on the next start:

```
=== All Optical Lenses (2) ===
1. Alpha - BK7 (Biconvex) - f=97.58mm
2. Beta  - BK7 (Biconvex) - f=97.58mm
✓ Lens deleted successfully!
AssertionError: Lists differ: ['Alpha', 'Beta'] != ['Beta']
```

`save_lenses` also returns `False` rather than raising, so the dialog's
`except` branch never fired.

Both paths now call `storage.delete_item(id)`, the only thing that actually
removes a row. The CLI keeps the lens in memory and reports honestly when the
row cannot be deleted, instead of printing success and dropping it from the list.

### The startup dialog had two more problems

- it built its own `LensStorage("openlens.db")`, so it deleted from a
  **different file** than the rest of the app was using. It now takes an
  optional `storage` argument and defaults to the previous behaviour, so
  `main()` is unaffected.
- it bypassed `delete_item`, which is the only thing enforcing the *"lens is
  still used by an assembly"* guard — so an assembly could be left pointing at a
  deleted lens. `LensInUseError` is now caught and shown as a warning, and the
  row survives.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #432

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      confirmed, the pre-fix run produced 2 failures + 4 errors, including the
      quoted CLI output above
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_delete_row_removal` — 7 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_delete_row_removal tests.test_deletion_persistence tests.test_database tests.test_gui tests.test_metadata_persistence tests.test_startup_persistence` — 103 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1606 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors that exist on clean
      `master` (they need `pytest`, which cannot be installed in this dev
      container because of PEP 668), no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 213 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 src/lens_editor.py src/gui/dialogs/startup.py` — no new findings;
      the 5 `E402`/`F541` in `lens_editor.py` are pre-existing (verified against
      `git show master:<file>`)
- [x] Tests go through a real SQLite file: delete, close, reopen, assert. Covers
      both entry points, a declined confirmation, the untouched neighbour, the
      injected-database path, and the in-use guard

### A detail worth flagging

One test selects its row **by id** rather than by position. `load_lenses` does
not return insertion order: `save_assembly` re-inserts every lens it references,
and SQLite's `INSERT OR REPLACE` deletes the old row, so a referenced lens moves
to the end of the scan. My first version assumed row 0 and was asserting about
the wrong lens — it failed to notice the guard working.

title: Zemax AGF glass catalog importer misreads the file format; imported glasses have wrong optics
body:
**Where:** `src/material_database.py:564-575`, `:600-618`, `:642-648`

- **NM line:** `parts[3]` is read as Nd. In the real format (`NM name formula MIL# Nd Vd ...`) that field is the MIL number, so Nd and Vd are both shifted.
- **CD line:** for Sellmeier, coefficients are interleaved `K1 L1 K2 L2 K3 L3`, but the code maps them as `B1 B2 B3 C1 C2 C3`.
- **IT line:** the real format is `IT lambda T thickness`, one line per wavelength. The code reads `IT thickness lambda T lambda T ...`, and each line overwrites the previous one.
- The formula number (`parts[2]`) is ignored. TCE and density are read from the wrong fields (they are on the `ED` line).

**Repro:** importing a standard Schott N-BK7 entry gives `nd 517642.251`, `vd 1.5168`, `n(587.6)=1.4490` (should be 1.5168) and `T(500nm,10mm)=9.09e+27`.

**Fix:** parse by real field positions, de-interleave CD for formula 2, reject unsupported formulas, collect all IT lines, read ED/TD for thermal data, and validate that transmission is in [0, 1]. Add a test with a real AGF excerpt.

nodes.title: fix(material): parse the real AGF glass catalog format
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(material): parse the real AGF glass catalog format

Every defect here made imported glasses **optically wrong** rather than merely untidy. A standard Schott N-BK7 entry came out as:

```
nd = 517642.0        (should be 1.5168)
vd = 1.5168          (should be 64.17)
n(587.6 nm) = 1.4490
```

### NM line

Real layout is `NM <name> <formula> <MIL#> <Nd> <Vd> <TCE> <DP>`. `parts[3]` is the **MIL number**, which was being read as `Nd` — so `Nd` and `Vd` were both shifted by one field and the thermal data landed on the wrong columns. Now parsed by real position, and the formula number is captured instead of ignored.

### CD line

Coefficients are interleaved `K1 L1 K2 L2 K3 L3`; the code mapped them as `B1 B2 B3 C1 C2 C3`, so **every** glass got the wrong dispersion curve. Now de-interleaved into `(B1,C1), (B2,C2), (B3,C3)`.

### IT line

Real layout is `IT <lambda_nm> <T> <thickness_mm>`, **one wavelength per line**. The code read a single packed line, so each `IT` line overwrote the previous one, the thickness was read as a wavelength, and wavelengths were scaled as if they were micrometres. Lines now accumulate, the thickness is read from its own field, and a transmission outside `[0, 1]` is dropped — `n = 1 - k·ln(T)` turns a stray `9.09e+27` into an absurd absorption coefficient rather than a skipped row.

### ED line

`TCE` and density are taken from `ED` when present, since the `NM` line commonly carries a placeholder `0.0`. Both are normalised to K⁻¹ at parse time so nothing downstream carries the `1e-6` factor.

### Robustness

Unsupported dispersion formulas are skipped rather than mis-mapped, and `_process_agf_glass` now reports whether it stored anything, so `import_agf_catalog`'s return count no longer includes glasses it refused.

## The existing test was asserting the bug back at the importer

`tests/data/test_catalog.agf` was itself written **to match the broken parser** — an `NM` line with no MIL field, and invented `Nd`/`Vd` values that did not follow from its own coefficients. So `test_import_agf` validated the misparse.

It now holds real N-BK7 and SF11 entries in the real layout, and the invariant asserted is the one that actually catches a mis-mapped coefficient:

> the index recomputed from the Sellmeier terms must reproduce the glass's own declared `Nd`.

A wrong pairing does not reproduce it (it gives 1.4490).

## Test isolation

All 19 new tests pass a temporary `db_path`. `MaterialDatabase(None)` does **not** mean in-memory — it falls back to the real `data/materials.json`, and `add_material` writes to it, so a test using `db_path=None` persists whatever it imported into the user's catalog. That happened during this work: a mis-parsed N-BK7 and a fabricated `UNKNOWN_F` were written into a real materials file, and because the stale values survived the fix they looked like the new code wasn't being used at all. Filed as #490 with the details.

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #433

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      confirmed, the pre-fix run produced 16 failures + 1 error, including
      `AssertionError: 517642.0 != 1.5168` and `1.4490 != 1.5168`
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_agf_import` — 19 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_agf_import tests.test_material_database tests.test_sellmeier_guards tests.test_material_cache tests.test_material_database_resilience` — 65 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1635 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors that exist on clean
      `master` (they need `pytest`, which cannot be installed in this dev
      container because of PEP 668), no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 213 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 src/material_database.py tests/test_agf_import.py` — clean
- [x] Dispersion coverage includes: NM field positions (Nd, Vd, TCE, density),
      pair de-interleaving, `ED` refining thermal data without disturbing the
      optics, every `IT` line accumulating with its own value, thickness read
      from its own field and *not* leaking in as a wavelength, out-of-range
      transmission dropped, unsupported formulas skipped, the reference glass
      reproducing its published `Nd`, and the Abbe number checking out via
      `n_F − n_C`

title: STL export: stray inverted triangles, inconsistent winding, not watertight
body:
**Where:** `src/stl_export.py:195`, `:84-129`, `:247-274`

- `generate_edge_triangles` still contains a debug leftover, `triangles.append((p1, p3, p2))  # 1-3-2?`, before the two correct triangles. It adds an extra inverted triangle to every edge segment.
- `generate_surface_triangles` uses the same winding for the front and back surfaces, so the front surface normals point into the glass.
- Parabolic sag, clear apertures and bevels are ignored. If |R| < D/2, the `ValueError` is caught and the sag silently becomes 0.

**Repro:** R=100/-100, t=5, D=25 gives 80 bad directed edges out of 1552 (a closed manifold needs 0), signed volume 1344 (expected about 2070 mm^3), and front-surface normal z = +0.99997 (should be negative).

**Fix:** delete line 195, flip the front-surface winding (or add an `outward` flag), and raise instead of using zero sag when |R| < D/2. Add a manifold/volume test.

nodes.title: fix(export): make the STL a closed, outward-wound solid
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(export): make the STL a closed, outward-wound solid

Every export was unusable in a slicer or mesh checker. Four defects — the
issue lists three, but fixing those only got halfway.

### 1. Debug leftover in `generate_edge_triangles`

```python
triangles.append((p1, p3, p2))  # 1-3-2?
# Let's check: 1->2 is CCW around Z...
# Correct is likely (p1, p4, p3) and (p1, p3, p2) or similar.
```

An extra inverted triangle per edge segment, plus the scratch reasoning that
went with it. Deleted.

### 2. Front and back surfaces wound the same way

`generate_surface_triangles` wound both identically, so **every** front-surface
normal pointed *into* the glass — 2450 of them for the test lens. It now takes
`is_front` and reverses the winding, matching what `generate_flat_surface`
already did.

### 3. The ring never closed on itself

Not in the issue, and the reason fixing 1–2 stalled at 102 unpaired edges with
no combination of winding fixes closing it:

```python
angle2 = (seg + 1) * angle_step     # last segment -> 2*pi
math.sin(2 * math.pi)               # 6.43e-16, not 0.0
```

The final segment's vertex was **not** the same point as the one segment 0
starts from, leaving a hairline seam right around every surface — invisible to
the eye, fatal to any watertightness check. The angle now wraps with
`((seg + 1) % num_segments)`, which is exact.

### 4. Impossible sag silently flattened

`sag` raising (`|R| < D/2`, where no sphere reaches that far) was caught and
replaced with `0.0`, silently exporting a flat disc where a curved surface
belonged. It now raises with a message naming both radii. A genuinely flat
surface is the `|R| ~ 0` case and still works.

## Measured

For `r1=100, r2=-100, thickness=5, diameter=25`:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unshared edges | 250 | **0** |
| unpaired directed edges | 349 | **0** |
| signed volume | 1376 mm³ | **2070 mm³** |
| front normals facing inward | 2450 | **0** |

The reference volume is **2069.9 mm³**, computed by numerical revolution of the
same analytic profile, matching the issue's "~2070".

## Why the tests assert properties, not counts

They check that every undirected edge is shared by exactly two triangles, every
directed edge is paired with its reverse, the signed volume is positive and
matches the reference, and both caps' normals point out of the glass. Each of
those catches a *different* defect — counting triangles would not have
distinguished a correct ring from one with a stray triangle in it, and that
distinction is what defect 3 turned on.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #434

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      confirmed, the pre-fix run produced 5 failures including
      `2450 != 0 : 2450 of 2450 front-surface triangles face +Z (into the glass)`
      and `102 != 0 : 102 directed edges are not paired with their reverse`
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_stl_manifold` — 8 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_stl_manifold tests.test_stl_export tests.test_export_formats tests.test_step_export tests.test_agf_import` — 41 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1663 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors that exist on clean
      `master` (they need `pytest`, which cannot be installed in this dev
      container because of PEP 668), no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 215 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 src/stl_export.py tests/test_stl_manifold.py` — clean
- [x] A flat surface (`r=0`) is still exported successfully, so raising on an
      impossible sag did not break the legitimate degenerate case

title: STEP export: lens names are written unquoted or unescaped, producing invalid Part 21
body:
**Where:** `src/io/step_export.py:39`, `:50-66` (names reach it via `_solid_label`, `:599`)

`_format_text` writes a string unquoted if it starts with `#`, `.`, `*` or `$`, or if `float()` parses it. That includes names like `"50"`, `"Infinity"` and `"nan"`. Backslashes are not doubled and non-ASCII text is not encoded as `\X2\...\X0\`, though Part 21 requires both.

```
'50' -> 50    'Infinity' -> Infinity    'nan' -> nan    '#3 doublet' -> #3 doublet    '.T.' -> .T.
'C:\lens' -> 'C:\lens'    'f=50mm u' -> not encoded
```

**Fix:** don't guess types from a string. Use explicit `StepRef`/`StepEnum` marker types for internal tokens, always quote real text, double backslashes and encode non-ASCII.

nodes.title: fix(io): STEP text is quoted, escaped and ASCII - never guessed
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(io): STEP text is quoted, escaped and ASCII — never guessed

`StepWriter._format_text` guessed types from the string:

- a value starting with `#`, `.`, `*` or `$` was returned **unquoted** as pre-written syntax;
- anything `float()` could parse was returned **bare**.

A lens named `50` was written as the real number `50`; `Infinity` and `nan` likewise; `#3 doublet` became a dangling reference. Part 21 also requires backslashes to be doubled and non-ASCII to be encoded as `\X2\…\X0\`, and neither was done — a name like `C:\lens` or `f=50mm ü` produced an invalid file.

### The fix: no guessing, explicit markers

| Value | Marker |
| --- | --- |
| `#id` reference | `StepRef` (already existed) |
| `.T.` / `.F.` enumeration | `StepEnum` + `STEP_TRUE` / `STEP_FALSE`, validated |
| `*` derived attribute | `StepDerived` + `STEP_DERIVED` |
| `$` unset | `None` (Python) |
| everything else | real text, always quoted |

The issue's examples now render as:

```text
'50'          -> #1=X('50');
'Infinity'    -> #1=X('Infinity');
'nan'         -> #1=X('nan');
'#3 doublet'  -> #1=X('#3 doublet');
'.T.'         -> #1=X('.T.');
'C:\lens'     -> #1=X('C:\\lens');
'f=50mm ü'    -> #1=X('f=50mm \X2\00FC\X0\');
"Bob's"       -> #1=X('Bob''s');
```

Escaping doubles apostrophes and backslashes, and encodes non-ASCII as `\X2\` with UTF-16BE code units (adjacent characters share one directive; non-BMP becomes a surrogate pair).

`step_reader._unescape` learns to reverse exactly that with a **left-to-right scan**. That matters: the writer doubles a literal backslash, so a name literally containing `\X2\00FC\X0\` arrives as `\\X2\\00FC\\X0\\`, and an order-dependent replacement pass would "decode" text that never encoded anything.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Breaking change — exported files change for the previously-mangled cases only; everything else is byte-identical

## Related Issues

Closes #435

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] 15 new/strengthened tests in `tests/test_step_writer.py`
- [x] **Part-by-part reverts:**

  | Reverted | Failures |
  | --- | --- |
  | old guessing `_format_text` | 16 |
  | reader back to apostrophe-only unescape | 4 |
  | one call site passing `".T."` as text | 1 |
  | one call site passing `"*"` as text | 1 |

- [x] The first call-site revert **passed** and exposed a gap: it only exercised the lens export. The call-site test now covers both the lens solid and the housing-tube export, which carry separate call sites; the revert then failed as intended.
- [x] Round-trips through `read_step_solids`: `ü`, `µ`, non-BMP emoji, trailing backslash, and a literal `\X2\00FC\X0\` name
- [x] Targeted: `test_step_writer`, `test_step_export`, `test_step_export_multi`, `test_step_assembly`, `test_gui_export_wiring`, `test_clear_aperture` — 64 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2195 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six pre-existing `gui_flows` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --check` — 250 files unchanged; `flake8` — identical to the master baseline for both source files (`step_export.py`'s pre-existing `E402`/`F401`/`F841` set is untouched)

### Coverage

Numbers and token lookalikes as names; enum marker validation; derived/unset markers; backslash doubling; apostrophe + backslash together; single- and multi-character non-ASCII and non-BMP encoding; reader round-trips for all of the above including the literal-directive trap; and a real-export call-site check that neither the lens nor the tube path leaks a quoted `.T.`/`*`.

- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (docstrings on every marker and both escape routines)
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: Zemax import: a lens whose front surface is the STOP is dropped; DIAM semi/full diameter mismatch
body:
**Where:** `src/export_formats.py:896-899` (STOP) and `:76`, `:89`, `:694`, `:716`, `:730`, `:906-923` (DIAM)

**1. STOP drops the element.** The `STOP` branch handles the surface and `continue`s before the `GLAS` check. A surface that is both the stop and a lens front surface (common in real files) never opens an element, so the back surface is skipped and the element vanishes with no warning. A singlet with `STOP` on SURF 1 imports with 0 elements. Removing the `STOP` line gives 1.

**2. DIAM is semi-diameter in Zemax.** The exporter writes the full clear aperture (25.0 for a 25 mm lens), so Zemax shows a 50 mm lens. The importer does the opposite: a real file with `DIAM 12.5` becomes a 12.5 mm lens. Export and import agree with each other, so tests pass, but foreign files are wrong.

**Also:** parabolic surfaces are exported as plain `STANDARD` with no `CONI -1`, and material names containing spaces are truncated.

**Fix:** record the pending stop and fall through to the GLAS handling. Write and read `DIAM` as diameter/2. Emit `CONI -1`. Quote or sanitise material names. Add tests from real Zemax files.

nodes.title: fix(io): a Zemax STOP is a flag, and DIAM is a semi-diameter
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(io): a Zemax STOP is a flag, and DIAM is a semi-diameter

Four defects in the `.zmx` dialect, all found through **foreign** files rather than through the exporter's own output agreeing with its importer:

### 1. STOP dropped the element (data loss)

The `STOP` branch handled the surface and `continue`d before the `GLAS` check. A surface that is both the stop and a lens front surface — common in real files — never opened an element, so its back surface was then skipped as an orphan and the element vanished **with no warning**. Reproduced before the fix:

```text
elements: 0   (singlet, STOP on SURF 1)
```

`STOP` is a flag, not a surface kind. It is now recorded and the surface goes through the normal front/back handling. A stop that cannot be mapped onto an air gap is still ignored (a front vertex has no gap in this model), but the element survives.

### 2. DIAM is a semi-diameter

The exporter wrote the full clear aperture, so Zemax showed a 25 mm lens as 50 mm; the importer read a foreign `DIAM 12.5` as a 12.5 mm lens. Export now halves and import doubles, including the stop surface. `tests/test_clear_aperture.py` encoded the old full-width output and is updated deliberately: a 36 mm CA is `DIAM 18.0` now.

### 3. Parabolic surfaces were plain spheres

They are exported at their vertex radius (`get_effective_radius_*`) with `CONI -1`, and the importer turns `CONI -1` back into the stored sag at the clear aperture, so a parabola survives a round trip. Spherical surfaces gain no `CONI`.

### 4. Material names with spaces were truncated

`GLAS Fused Silica` became `Fused`. Export quotes a name containing whitespace; import takes the whole argument, with or without quotes. As a consequence of preserving the name as written, the catalog lookup became case-insensitive — otherwise `"Fused Silica"` still fell back to BK7.

> **Not wired to the GUI.** `export_formats.py` has no menu entry; the Zemax paths are reachable from the API only. The units were still wrong for anyone using it, and the fix does not pretend the feature is discoverable.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Breaking change — import/export of `.zmx` changes meaning for DIAM, which is the point of the fix

## Related Issues

Closes #436

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] 13 new tests in `tests/test_zemax_roundtrip.py`
- [x] **12 of 13 fail on the old code** (the thirteenth is the spherical-has-no-CONI counter-case); the pre-fix run showed the failures before any implementation change
- [x] Part-by-part reverts, each restoring exactly one piece:

  | Reverted | Failures |
  | --- | --- |
  | exact-case catalog lookup | 1 |
  | `refractive_index` not passed to the Lens | 1 |
  | STOP branch continuing again | 2 |
  | CONI ignored on import | 1 |
  | GLAS truncated to the first token | 3 |

- [x] Targeted: `test_zemax_roundtrip`, `test_clear_aperture`, `test_export_formats`, `test_system_export_gaps`, `test_coating`, `test_svg_escaping` — 108 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2180 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six pre-existing `gui_flows` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --check` — 250 files unchanged; `flake8` — no new findings (the touched file's pre-existing `E402`/`E501` set is unchanged, and `E226` count drops 6 → 4)

### Coverage

STOP on the front surface and on the back surface; DIAM read as a semi-diameter for a lens and for a stop; both exporters write semi-diameters; single-lens export (25.4 mm → `DIAM 12.7`); parabolic export carries vertex curvature + `CONI -1`, spherical carries none, and a parabola round-trips its sag; foreign `GLAS Fused Silica` (unquoted) keeps both words and resolves n = 1.4585; the case-insensitive lookup on `fused silica`; quoted export and round trip.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (docstrings + importer/exporter comments)
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: 3D tracer: back parabolic surfaces intersected in the wrong local frame
body:
**Where:** `src/tracer_3d.py:305-309`, `:327-357`, `:452`

`_to_local_point()` returns coordinates relative to the lens transform, but `_intersect_paraboloid()` treats them as relative to the back vertex. The back surface is therefore solved at about the front vertex. The back-surface normal calculation has the same mismatch.

**Repro:** for a 5 mm thick plano/parabolic lens, the 2D trace reaches the back at x=4.99 and survives. The equivalent 3D trace stops at the front: `3D back True [(-10,1,0), (0,1,0)]`.

**Fix:** subtract the vertex's local coordinate when building the ray and normal coordinates, and add it back when transforming the hit to world space. Add a 2D/3D agreement test for parabolic surfaces on both sides.

nodes.title: fix(tracer): solve the 3D paraboloid at its own vertex, not the lens origin
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(tracer): solve the 3D paraboloid at its own vertex, not the lens origin

`_to_local_point` claims to return *"the surface-local frame (vertex at origin)"*, but its two branches disagree about the origin:

```python
if self._inv is not None:
    return self._inv.multiply_point(point)   # lens-frame origin
return point - vertex                        # vertex origin
```

`_intersect_paraboloid` solves `x = (y² + z²) / (2R)`, which is only correct when the vertex really is at `x = 0`. With a transform set it is not: for the back surface of a thick lens the origin sits **a whole thickness too far forward**, so the back paraboloid was solved at the front vertex.

Measured on a 5 mm thick plano/parabolic lens, the 3D trace exited **exactly 5.0 mm early at every ray height**:

```
height=0.5   99.834 != 104.834   (Δ 5.0)
height=2.0   96.832 != 101.832   (Δ 5.0)
height=5.0    3.125 !=   8.125   (Δ 5.0)
height=8.0    8.000 !=  13.000   (Δ 5.0)
```

The 2D tracer solves the same geometry in its own frame and was correct throughout, which is why the tests compare against it rather than against hard-coded numbers.

### The fix

The vertex is shifted to the origin before the quadratic and shifted back before the hit is transformed to world. In the fallback branch `_to_local_point(vertex, vertex)` is exactly zero, so the no-transform path is unchanged.

### Also fixed: the aperture was on the wrong circle

The aperture check reads `local_hit.y`/`.z`, which were **lens-frame** — not vertex-relative. For a decentered lens that is simply the wrong circle: a ray that belongs inside the clear aperture can be clipped, and one that should be clipped can pass.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #437

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] Verified by reverting **only** the vertex offset (keeping the file otherwise
      identical): **6 of 6 fail, 6 of 6 pass** with it restored. A 15-line change
      needs that evidence more than a larger one does.
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_paraboloid_vertex_frame` — 6 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_paraboloid_vertex_frame tests.test_stl_manifold tests.test_ray_tracer_3d tests.test_system_ray_tracer_3d` — 31 tests, OK after rebasing onto the merged #493
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1668 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors that exist on clean
      `master` (they need `pytest`, which cannot be installed in this dev
      container because of PEP 668), no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 216 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 src/tracer_3d.py tests/test_paraboloid_vertex_frame.py` — clean
- [x] Coverage includes: thick plano/parabolic back, parabolic front, paraboloids
      on both sides, four ray heights, a decentered lens that must *not* be
      clipped, and a ray outside the clear aperture that must *still* be blocked —
      the last two so that "fixing" the frame by disabling the check would fail

### A test-writing note

My first version of the decentered test set `tracer.transform` after
construction and called a `_invalidate_cache` that does not exist. The tracer
caches its inverse transform in `__init__` and documents that it never changes,
so the test was patching an object the code had already snapshotted. It passes
now via the constructor — which is also the only way a caller can legitimately
decenter a 3D lens.

title: OpticalSystem.to_dict/from_dict loses assemblies, transforms and absolute element positions
body:
**Where:** `src/optical_system.py:434-458`, `:474-502`

`to_dict()` saves only the flattened elements. `from_dict()` rebuilds them with `add_lens()` using gaps. It neither restores the assembly tree nor reads the saved element `position`.

**Repro:** an assembly at x=20 comes back as a root-level `OpticalElement` at x=0. A standalone first element saved at x=15 loads at x=0. `OpticalNode` also has `# TODO: Serialize modifiers` (`src/optical_node.py:135`).

**Fix:** round-trip the tree, transforms and modifiers. Or explicitly restore positions and document that assemblies are not supported by this format. Add a property-style round-trip test comparing traced results before and after.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): restore the element positions OpticalSystem.to_dict saved
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(analysis): restore the element positions OpticalSystem.to_dict saved

`to_dict` writes each element's absolute `position`, but `from_dict` never read
it back. It rebuilt the system from the air gaps alone, and `add_lens` places
every element relative to the one before it — so the gaps reproduced the
**spacing** and threw the **offset** away.

Concretely:

- a system whose first element sat at `x = 15` loaded at `x = 0`;
- an assembly at `x = 20` came back root-level at `x = 0`.

The saved position was ignored data.

The tree is the authority for positions (`_rebuild_from_tree` reads them from
it), so each child's position is now restored from the saved value and the tree
rebuilt. Air gaps follow from the tree, so they come out consistent too.

### Scope, stated rather than left as a surprise

This format is **flat** — it stores a list of elements and cannot represent a
nested assembly tree — so a nested assembly still comes back flattened. That is
now documented in the code instead of being a silent behaviour.

Node **modifiers** also remain unserialized (`optical_node.py` still carries a
`# TODO: Serialize modifiers`). Both are worth their own issues rather than a
format change folded into a position fix.

title: OpticalSystem.refresh_references() leaves the 3D node tree pointing at the old lens objects
body:
**Where:** `src/optical_system.py:259-263`

`refresh_references()` replaces lenses in the flat `elements` list but never replaces `OpticalElement.element_model` in the tree. The flat/2D calculations and the tree-based 3D tracer can analyse different optics.

**Repro:** after refreshing a one-lens system to lens `b`: `s.elements[0].lens is b` -> `True`, `s.root.children[0].element_model is b` -> `False`.

**Fix:** update the matching tree nodes too, or derive `elements` from the tree so there is one source of truth.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): refresh the tree's lens models, not just the flat list
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(analysis): refresh the tree's lens models, not just the flat list

`refresh_references` replaced the lens in each flat `LensElement` wrapper but
left the tree's `OpticalElement.element_model` pointing at the old Lens:

```python
s.elements[0].lens is b              # True
s.root.children[0].element_model is b # False
```

Two consequences follow.

**The flat/2D calculations and the tree-based 3D tracer analysed different
optics** — the same system, two different lenses.

**The identity match broke.** `_update_positions` matches nodes to elements by
the identity of the lens model they wrap, so a stale `element_model` broke the
pairing that keeps the flat list and the tree in step.

The tree nodes are now updated to the refreshed lens as well, before
`_update_positions` runs so the identity match still pairs them.

### Why not derive `elements` from the tree?

The issue offers that as the alternative — one source of truth. It is the better
design, but it is a refactor of how the flat list is maintained rather than a fix
to a stale reference, and it would touch every caller that reads
`system.elements`. This change fixes the defect; the refactor stays a separate
consideration.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #439

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] Verified by reverting **only** the tree update: **3 of 5 fail, 5 of 5
      pass** with it restored
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_refresh_references` — 5 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_system_tracer tests.test_system_ray_tracer_3d tests.test_metadata_persistence tests.test_database tests.test_gui tests.test_optical_system_round_trip tests.test_ray_tracer_3d` — 120 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1689 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors that exist on clean
      `master` (they need `pytest`, which cannot be installed in this dev
      container because of PEP 668), no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — clean
- [x] `flake8 src/optical_system.py tests/test_refresh_references.py` — no new
      findings; the `F401`/`F841` in `optical_system.py` are pre-existing
- [x] Coverage includes: the tree node receiving the new lens, the flat list and
      the tree agreeing on it, the replacement's own thickness being used, a
      multi-element system where every node is refreshed, and positions
      surviving a refresh

### A test I had to correct

The position test originally asserted that positions were unchanged after a
refresh that replaced a 5 mm lens with a 7 mm one. That is **not** a bug — a
thicker lens legitimately shifts the elements that follow it. The test now keeps
the thickness constant, so it isolates the refresh from the geometry. Worth
recording because the "corrected" assertion is the one that would have hidden a
real regression.

title: Lens.refractive_index_at() ignores an explicit refractive_index for materials not in the catalog
body:
**Where:** `src/lens.py:399-415`

When the material database is available, `refractive_index_at()` accepts its BK7 fallback even for a material that is not in the catalog. Wavelength-dependent calculations then use a different index from the one stored and used by the tracer.

**Repro:** `Lens(material="Custom", refractive_index=1.7).refractive_index_at(587.6)` returns `1.5168`.

**Fix:** check that the material exists before querying; otherwise keep the stored index (optionally with a Cauchy/Abbe model).

nodes.title: fix(analysis): do not invent a refractive index for an unknown material
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(analysis): do not invent a refractive index for an unknown material

`refractive_index_at` queried the material database for whatever string the lens
carried. When the material is not in the catalog, the lookup falls back to a
**BK7 default** and returns it — so a lens explicitly given its own index came
back with a different one:

```python
Lens(material="Custom", refractive_index=1.7).refractive_index_at(587.6)
# -> 1.5168, not 1.7
```

The stored index is what the tracer uses, so the wavelength-dependent numbers
and the geometry disagreed: a lens built to a stated index of 1.7 was analysed
as if it were 1.5168.

The catalog is now only asked about a material it actually has. An unknown
material keeps the index the lens was given, **at every wavelength**.

Known glasses are unaffected: BK7 still comes from the Sellmeier data, still
disperses, and model-glass mode still computes from `nd`/`vd` rather than from
the catalog.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

Closes #440

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      confirmed, the pre-fix run produced
      `AssertionError: 1.5168 != 1.7 within 6 places`
- [x] Verified by reverting **only** the existence check: **4 of 5 fail, 5 of 5
      pass** with it restored
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_refractive_index_at` — 5 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_refractive_index_at tests.test_lens_menu tests.test_aberrations tests.test_chromatic_analyzer tests.test_ray_tracer tests.test_material_database` — 140 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1686 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors that exist on clean
      `master` (they need `pytest`, which cannot be installed in this dev
      container because of PEP 668), no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 218 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 src/lens.py tests/test_refractive_index_at.py` — no new findings.
      The `E402` in `lens.py` is pre-existing (verified against
      `git show master:src/lens.py`)
- [x] Coverage includes: an explicit index kept at the d-line, the same at the F
      and C lines (not just one wavelength), a known material still coming from
      the catalog, a known material still dispersing (blue above red), and
      model-glass mode being unaffected

### Note on the "at every wavelength" case

The fix is not only about the d-line. Before it, an unknown material returned
the BK7 fallback at *every* wavelength, so a dispersion calculation over an
unknown glass silently produced BK7's dispersion. The test pins three
wavelengths for that reason.

title: Lens constructor: model-glass mode starts with the catalog index, and type presets undo parabolic settings
body:
**Where:** `src/lens.py:123-138` and `:142-160`, `:623-637`

1. The constructor records `model_glass_mode` and `model_nd` but resolves the working `refractive_index` from the material unless an explicit index is passed. A BK7 model-glass lens with `model_nd=1.7` starts at `n=1.5168` (EFL 97.58 mm); after `update_refractive_index()` it is `n~1.7` (EFL 72.17 mm).
2. `use_type_defaults` calls `_update_radii_for_type()` before the parabolic flags and sags are assigned, which undoes the method's reset. A plano-convex preset with `is_parabolic_1=True, parabolic_sag_1=4` keeps the flag (effective R1=50), while `set_lens_type("Plano-Convex")` clears it (R1=100).

**Fix:** initialise the working index from the model-glass parameters when that mode is requested, and apply the type preset after the parabolic properties are set, with a documented precedence rule.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): start a model-glass lens at its own index
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(analysis): start a model-glass lens at its own index

Two defects in `Lens.__init__`, both of the same shape: the constructor
disagreed with the methods that are supposed to run after it.

### 1. Model glass was resolved from the material

The constructor recorded `model_glass_mode` and `model_nd`, then resolved the
working `refractive_index` from the material. A model-glass lens is defined by
its `nd`/`vd` pair — the material name is only a label — so a BK7-named lens with
`model_nd=1.7` was built like BK7:

```
construction:  n = 1.5168   ->  EFL 97.58 mm
after update:  n ≈ 1.7000   ->  EFL 72.17 mm
```

Nothing in between said why the lens had changed focal length.

The index now comes from the same resolution `update_refractive_index()` uses —
`refractive_index_at(wavelength)` — so the two agree.

**Precedence is unchanged for the cases that already worked:** an explicit
`refractive_index` still wins, which is what keeps serialization round-trips
exact, and a real glass is still resolved from its material.

### 2. `use_type_defaults` ran before the parabolics were assigned

`_update_radii_for_type()` clears the parabolic flags and sags. The constructor
called it *before* those properties existed, so the reset had nothing to clear:

```python
Lens(lens_type="Plano-Convex", use_type_defaults=True,
     is_parabolic_1=True, parabolic_sag_1=4)   # keeps the paraboloid
lens.set_lens_type("Plano-Convex")             # clears it
```

The same preset behaved differently depending on how it was applied. The preset
now runs after the parabolics are set, so both paths agree.

**Precedence: the preset wins.** A type preset is spherical and cannot be
combined with a paraboloid — which is what `set_lens_type()` already did, and
what `_update_radii_for_type()`'s own docstring says. The default path
(`use_type_defaults=False`) still touches nothing, so an explicit paraboloid
survives.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #441

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      **6 of 13 failed** on the original `lens.py`
- [x] Verified by reverting **each fix on its own**:
  - the model-glass index resolution → **5 of 13 fail**
  - the preset ordering → **2 of 13 fail**
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_lens_model_glass_init` — 13 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_lens tests.test_lens_menu tests.test_lens_editor tests.test_lens_comparator tests.test_lens_outline tests.test_parabolic_conic_consistency tests.test_paraboloid_vertex_frame tests.test_preset_catalogue tests.test_thick_lens_bfl` — 129 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1777 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors that exist on clean
      `master` (they need `pytest`), no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 227 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 tests/test_lens_model_glass_init.py` — clean. The `E402` in
      `lens.py` is pre-existing (1 finding on `master`, unchanged)
- [x] Coverage includes: the index coming from the model, the index *not moving*
      on the first update, the focal length being stable across an update, two
      model glasses with different `nd` starting differently, an explicit index
      still winning, a real glass and a default lens being unaffected, the
      constructor agreeing with `set_lens_type` on flags *and* effective radius,
      the preset clearing sags, parabolics surviving without the preset, the
      preset still setting radii, and an unknown type preserving everything

### Why the focal length is asserted, not just the index

Asserting `refractive_index` alone would pass for a lens that was numerically
right and optically wrong. The EFL comparison is the user-visible consequence:
a lens that reports `n=1.7` but images like BK7 is still broken, and only the
focal length notices.

title: Lens.get_coating_*()/to_dict() return live mutable coating dicts
body:
**Where:** `src/lens.py:272-278`, `:486-488`

The getters copy only the outer list, and `to_dict()` returns the coating lists directly. Mutating a returned layer silently mutates the lens and bypasses `set_coating()` and its `modified_at` update.

**Repro:** `lens.get_coating_1()[0]["n"] = 99` changes `lens.coating_1[0]["n"]` to `99`.

**Fix:** deep-copy coating layers at these API boundaries, or return immutable dataclasses.

nodes.title: fix(lens): deep-copy coating layers at the API boundaries
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(lens): deep-copy coating layers at the API boundaries

`Lens.get_coating_1/2()` copied only the outer list, and `Lens.to_dict()` returned the `coating_1` / `coating_2` lists themselves. The layer dicts stayed shared, so

```python
lens.get_coating_1()[0]["refractive_index"] = 99
```

silently edited the lens and bypassed `set_coating()` and its `modified_at` update. `Lens.from_dict(lens.to_dict())` was not an independent copy either: it shared every layer with the original.

### The fix

Return `copy.deepcopy` from both getters and from `to_dict()`, matching the defensive copy the same method already performs for `metadata`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking)

## Related Issues

Closes #442

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] **5 new tests** in `tests/test_coating.py`: mutating a getter layer, appending to a getter list, fresh layers on every call, mutating a `to_dict` layer, and a round-trip guard that both surfaces still deserialize
- [x] **Red before the fix**: `FAILED (failures=3)` — the mutation reached `lens.coating_1[0]` and the two getter calls returned identical layer objects
- [x] `tests.test_coating` — 28 tests OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2258 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6)` — master (2253) plus the five new tests; the six errors are the pre-existing `gui_flows` loader failures (pytest is not installed locally)

title: Aberrations: Strehl cache key omits trace-relevant parameters (stale results)
body:
**Where:** `src/aberrations.py:555-579`, `:582-616`

The cache key covers radii, thickness, diameter and index, but not clear apertures, parabolic flags/sags, alignment or the aperture stop. Editing those returns the previous Strehl result.

**Repro:** changing `lens.clear_aperture_1` to 5 leaves `_strehl_state_key(550, 32)` unchanged.

**Fix:** key on a hash of the lens's full `to_dict()` (plus tracer settings), or invalidate the cache from a lens change signal.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): key the Strehl cache on the serialized lens state
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(analysis): key the Strehl cache on the serialized lens state

`_strehl_state_key` enumerated a hand-picked list of attributes — radii,
thickness, diameter, index, position — and **everything not on that list was
invisible to the cache**. Clear apertures, parabolic flags and sags,
per-surface alignment and the aperture stop all change the pupil trace and left
the key identical, so the previous Strehl result came straight back:

```python
lens.clear_aperture_1 = 5.0
calculator._strehl_state_key(550, 32)   # unchanged
```

The test pins the user-visible consequence too: pinching the clear aperture
returned byte-identical Strehl and WFE.

### The list was the actual defect

The interesting part isn't the fields that were missing — it's that the key was
*an enumeration*. Any field added to `Lens` in future would be missing too,
because nobody remembers to extend a list of attributes sitting in a different
file. The key is now built from the serialized lens state, so new fields are
covered by construction.

### A key that never hits is a key that's worse than useless

The serialized state includes `id`, `name`, `created_at`, `modified_at` and
`metadata`. None of those describe optics. Including them would mean the cache
is invalidated on every rename and on every reload from the database — and a
cache that always misses is pure overhead.

So those are dropped via an explicit `_STREHL_NON_OPTICAL_FIELDS` set. The set
is the narrow part of the change; everything else is automatic.

The state is JSON-encoded because it contains lists and dicts (coating stacks)
that are not hashable.

### System keys were missing more

A system's key also now covers each element's decenter and tilt and the
aperture stop, which were absent for the same reason.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #443

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      **12 of 17 failed** on the original `aberrations.py`
- [x] Verified by reverting **each half on its own**:
  - the attribute-subset snapshot → **7 of 17 fail**
  - dropping the alignment and stop coverage → **2 of 17 fail**
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_strehl_cache_key` — 17 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_strehl_cache_key tests.test_aberrations` — 60 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1794 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors that exist on clean
      `master`, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 228 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 src/aberrations.py` — **15 findings, identical to `master`**
- [x] Coverage includes: clear apertures, parabolic flags and sags, Fresnel,
      model glass, per-element alignment, and the aperture stop all changing the
      key; plus renaming *not* changing it, identical lenses sharing an entry,
      the key being stable across recomputation, wavelength and grid size still
      differing, a system key never colliding with a lens key, the reported
      Strehl actually changing when the aperture is pinched, and a repeat call
      returning **the same object** so the cache is proven to be serving rather
      than coincidentally re-tracing

### Two tests that would have passed for the wrong reason

- Asserting the key changes is not enough on its own; a key that churned on
  *every* call would pass that and be useless. `test_the_cache_actually_serves_a_repeat_call`
  and `test_a_cache_hit_is_the_same_object` pin the other direction.
- `test_renaming_a_lens_does_not_invalidate` guards against the obvious way to
  "fix" this — hashing all of `to_dict()` unfiltered — which would trade a
  correctness bug for a performance one.

title: Aberrations: summary crashes on missing metrics, spot RMS failure becomes 0, negative field angles mixed, object distance ignored
body:
**Where:** `src/aberrations.py`

1. **`:974-980`** `get_aberration_summary()` formats `None` values with float format specifiers. An invalid result with `coma=None` raises `TypeError: unsupported format string passed to NoneType.__format__`.
2. **`:208-213`, `:722-762`** `_calculate_spot_rms()` returns `None` on trace failure, but `or 0.0` publishes it as a perfect zero, and `valid` does not consider it.
3. **`:307-324`** `max(field_angle, 0.1)` turns every negative requested angle into 0.1 degrees for field curvature and distortion, while coma and astigmatism use the requested negative angle. One result mixes different fields.
4. **`:98-179`** `calculate_all_aberrations()` accepts and forwards `object_distance_mm`, but `_calculate_all_at_wavelength()` never uses it, so finite-conjugate requests silently return infinity-object results.

**Fix:** check `valid` and print "unavailable" for missing metrics; preserve `None` and include spot RMS in validity; use `abs(field_angle)` consistently; implement or reject finite object distances.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): do not invent aberration metrics that cannot be measured
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(analysis): do not invent aberration metrics that cannot be measured

Four defects, all the same family: a value that could not be measured was
formatted as though it existed, published as a fictional zero, or taken from a
different field than the rest of the block.

### 1. The summary crashed instead of showing a gap

```python
TypeError: unsupported format string passed to NoneType.__format__
```

`get_aberration_summary()` formatted `None` with float specifiers, so an invalid
result lost the **entire** summary rather than showing that one number is
missing. Metrics now render as `unavailable`, and the interpretation labels
degrade with them.

### 2. A failed spot trace was published as a perfect one

`_calculate_spot_rms()` returns `None` on trace failure, but `or 0.0` turned that
into a **zero** spot size — indistinguishable from a better-than-diffraction-limited
design, for a lens that could not be traced at all. `None` is preserved and
`spot_rms` now feeds the validity check.

### 3. One dict, two fields

```python
max_field_angle_deg=max(field_angle, 0.1)
```

A `-10°` request was evaluated at `+0.1°` for field curvature and distortion,
while coma and astigmatism in the **same dict** used the requested `-10°`. Now
the magnitude is used, with the `0.1°` floor kept to avoid a degenerate
zero-width sample on axis.

### 4. A finite object distance was silently ignored — now refused

Every Seidel estimator here assumes an object at infinity (conjugate factor
`C = -1`). `object_distance_mm` was accepted, forwarded, and then dropped, so a
finite-conjugate request returned infinity-conjugate numbers **labelled with the
caller's own distance**. That is now a `ValueError`.

Refusing beats answering here: the result was wrong in a way nothing downstream
could detect, and actually supporting a finite conjugate means threading a
conjugate factor through each estimator — a physics change, not a guard. Flagged
in the PR as a deliberate behaviour change for callers to adapt to.

## An existing test caught a real mistake in my own fix

`test_box_alignment_matches_between_target_kinds` failed after my change. The
new `_metric` helper took a format spec and **ignored it**, so every value
printed at full float precision:

```
║ Focal Length:          58.86167144396433 mm      (mine)
║ Focal Length:               58.86 mm              (master)
```

The summary's box stopped lining up. Fixed, and the box is now byte-identical to
master for a valid design — verified by diffing the rendered lines, not by
assuming the width test was sufficient.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #444

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      **11 of 17 failed** on the original `aberrations.py`
- [x] Verified by reverting **each of the four fixes on its own**:

  | Reverted | Failures |
  | --- | --- |
  | `None`-safe summary formatting | 1 of 17 |
  | `spot_rms or 0.0` | 2 of 17 |
  | `max(field_angle, 0.1)` | 2 of 17 |
  | the `object_distance_mm` guard | 4 of 17 |

- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_aberration_summary_missing` — 17 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_aberrations tests.test_aberration_summary_missing tests.test_strehl_cache_key` — 77 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_aberrations tests.test_system_tracer tests.test_ray_tracer tests.test_optical_system` — 126 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1811 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 229 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 src/aberrations.py` — **10 findings, down from 15 on `master`**
- [x] Coverage includes: a summary surviving all-`None` and partially-`None`
      results, a valid design still printing numbers, an error result still
      reporting as an error, `None` vs `0.0` spot RMS, validity reacting to a
      missing spot, `+10°`/`-10°` agreement for curvature and distortion
      magnitude, the positive case unchanged, and finite object distances
      refused (including `0.0`) while `None` is still accepted

### A test I rewrote after it failed for the wrong reason

The field-angle tests originally mocked `GeometricTraceAnalysis`. That mock was
wrong in two ways — a constructor arity mismatch, and patching
`src.aberrations` when the symbol is imported *inside* the method — and it made
the test fail with `IndexError` rather than for the reason it existed. Rewritten
against the real sampler: the property that matters is the one a user sees, and
the real thing reproduces the bug directly (`field curvature: -2.688 vs
-0.0018`).

### Two assertions I had to correct

- I asserted `calculate_all_aberrations(object_distance_mm=None)` returns an
  `error` key. It does not, and should not — that is the *supported* case.
- `test_a_zero_spot_rms_is_still_valid` asserted nothing useful. Zero is a real
  measurement and `None` is not; keeping them distinguishable is the point, so
  the distinction is now asserted through the main path instead.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings

- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: LensRayTracer 2D: trace_parallel_rays ignores x_offset of a shifted lens
body:
**Where:** `src/tracer_2d.py:463-479`

`trace_parallel_rays()` computes starting heights using `lens_x=0.0` rather than the tracer's `x_offset`. For a non-zero field angle, a shifted lens receives rays at different heights than requested.

**Repro:** a 0-height 5 degree ray for a flat lens at `x_offset=50` hits the front surface at `y=4.3744 mm` instead of `y=0`.

**Fix:** project the bundle onto `self.front_vertex_x` and place starts relative to that vertex.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): reference the parallel-ray bundle to the front vertex
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(analysis): reference the parallel-ray bundle to the front vertex

`trace_parallel_rays()` built its bundle against a hard-coded `lens_x = 0.0` and a
start plane at `-RAY_START_OFFSET_MM`, whatever the tracer's `x_offset` was. The
back-projection that places a ray at its requested height at the front surface
therefore used the wrong reference plane, so a lens placed anywhere but the
origin received its fan at the wrong heights:

```
0-height, 5° ray, flat lens at x_offset=50
  → arrives at y = 4.3744 mm instead of y = 0
```

Both the bundle reference **and** the start plane now move with the front
vertex, so the ray still begins in front of the lens and the requested heights
are the heights it receives.

The system tracer already did this correctly (`start_x = first_pos -
RAY_START_OFFSET_MM`, `tracer_2d.py:591`); this brings the single-lens tracer in
line with it.

### Both halves are load-bearing

Fixing only the bundle reference while leaving the start plane at the origin
still fails a test, so this is not a one-line change that happens to pass.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #445

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after —
      **27 failures across 8 tests** on the original `tracer_2d.py` (many via
      `subTest`)
- [x] Verified by reverting:
  - the original hard-coded origin → **27 fail**
  - bundle fixed but start plane left at the origin → **1 still fails**
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_tracer2d_parallel_offset` — 8 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_tracer2d_parallel_offset tests.test_ray_tracer tests.test_system_tracer tests.test_ray_tracer_3d tests.test_interactive_ray_tracer tests.test_aberrations` — 110 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1802 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=31)` — the same
      six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 229 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8 src/tracer_2d.py tests/test_tracer2d_parallel_offset.py` — clean
- [x] Coverage includes: the issue's zero-height repro, the unshifted case
      still working, a height sweep across four offsets and five heights, the
      result being independent of the offset, a curved lens tracing identically
      when translated along the axis, and rays starting in front of the lens
      for both positive and negative offsets

### Four mistakes in my own test, each masking the bug

All four made the test fail for the wrong reason before it caught anything:

- **The 2D `Ray` is not the 3D one.** It has `x`/`y` and `angle_rad`, not
  `origin`/`direction`.
- **`ray.x`/`ray.y` are where the ray *ended up*.** The arrival height has to
  be read from `path[0]`/`path[1]`; reading the ray's current position measures
  the wrong span entirely.
- **`num_rays=1` forces `height = 0`** and ignores `ray_height_range` entirely,
  so the height sweep silently tested only the zero ray. It needs `num_rays=2`.
- **A curved front surface is struck at its sag, not at the vertex.** Measuring
  arrival at the intersection leaves a residual proportional to the sag that is
  *geometry, not a bug* — I nearly "fixed" that by loosening the tolerance. The
  bundle is referenced to the vertex plane, so the test back-projects to the
  vertex, which is both correct and what the fix actually guarantees.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
