title: GUI: Optimization Reset/Apply leaves editor and library pointing at different lens objects
body:
**Where:** `src/gui/tabs/optimization_tab.py:831-880` (Apply), `:882-901` (Reset)

After Apply, `_lenses` and the editor hold the optimised copy. Reset only sets `_parent._current_lens = original`: it does not put the original back into `_lenses` and does not call `_lens_editor.load_lens`. The editor keeps editing an object that is no longer current, and the next `_on_save` swaps by id and discards those edits. Apply also overwrites any edits made since the run started, without warning.

**Fix:** have Reset use the same id-replace plus `_set_current_item(...)` path as Apply. Snapshot `modified_at` at run start and warn on Apply if it changed.

nodes.title: fix(gui): Reset must undo Apply everywhere, not just in the title bar
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(gui): Reset must undo Apply everywhere, not just in the title bar

After Apply, `_lenses` and the editor hold the optimised copy. Reset used to assign
only:

```python
self._parent._current_lens = original
```

It did not put the original back into `_lenses`, and it did not call
`_lens_editor.load_lens`. So the editor kept editing an object that was **no longer
current**, and the next reconciling save — which matches by id — swapped the objects
and **discarded those edits**.

Apply and Reset are the same operation in opposite directions. They now share one
helper, `_fold_target_into_library`, which puts the target back into the library by id
and routes it through `_set_current_item` (which reloads the editor). Keeping the two
paths separate is precisely how Reset came to update one of the places Apply updates;
a test asserts both still go through the helper so they cannot drift apart again.

### Apply no longer discards edits silently

Apply replaces the design wholesale, so anything the user edited while the optimizer
was running is overwritten without a word. The run now snapshots the target's
`modified_at` and Apply says so when it differs.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #464

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] Verified by reverting **each part separately**:

  | Reverted | Failures (of 14) |
  | --- | --- |
  | Reset back to assigning only the current pointer | 5 |
  | the edited-while-running warning | 2 |
  | warn even when no snapshot exists | 1 |
  | drop the `_assembly_tab_widget._optical_system` assignment | 1 |

- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_optimization_reset_apply` — 14 tests, OK
- [x] Rebased onto the three merges that landed while this was open (#524, #525,
      #526): `Ran 61 tests`, OK across this file and all three of theirs
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1914 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=32)` — the same six
      pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 237 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8` — **no new findings** (compared by kind against `master`)
- [x] Coverage includes: the library holding the original after reset, the editor
      being reloaded with it, **the editor holding the same object as the library**
      (the defect in one assertion), the id surviving reset, reset being idempotent,
      reset with nothing to reset, the assembly case, the assembly editor being
      pointed at the restored system, the warning appearing only when the design
      really changed, it naming the design, silence without a snapshot, and the folded
      target being what becomes current

### ⚠️ One revert initially did not fail, and the reason was a lie in my test

Dropping the `_assembly_tab_widget._optical_system` assignment passed 14/14. I checked
`openlens.py` rather than trusting the result: the real `_set_current_item` reaches
`_lens_editor` but **never** `_assembly_tab_widget._optical_system` — and that field is
what `openlens.py:570` reads when the assembly editor reports a modification.

My stand-in main window was setting it "helpfully", faithfully mirroring nothing. The
stub now mirrors the real `_set_current_item`, with a comment saying why it
deliberately does *not* go further, and the same revert fails.

This is worth flagging because a green revert-table is easy to accept and this one was
wrong: the code was right, the test was lying about the code.

### A bug in the first version of this fix

`test_no_warning_without_a_recorded_start_stamp` caught it: with no snapshot on
record, the warning still fired, telling the user their edits had been replaced when
there was no snapshot to show they had. Silence is the correct response when there is
nothing to compare — so it is now a separate, named condition rather than an implicit
one.

title: GUI: several analyses and image simulation run on the GUI thread and freeze the window
body:
**Where:** `src/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:390-394`, `:463-466`, `:533-557`, `:212-345`; `src/gui/dialogs/image_sim.py:342`

Spot diagram, ray fan, field curves and "Calculate Metrics" trace rays in the button handler before the dialog appears. Image simulation runs `analyzer.simulate_image(...)` on the main thread. PSF, MTF, wavefront and ghost already use `AnalysisPlotDialog.plot_async`, so the tab is inconsistent. Field curves also hard-codes `max_field = 20.0` (`:532`) instead of using the sensor size like the other plots.

**Fix:** route these through `plot_async` / `_open_analysis_dialog`, and run image simulation in an `AnalysisWorker`.

nodes.title: fix(gui): run the performance analyses off the GUI thread
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(gui): run the performance analyses off the GUI thread

The Performance tab was inconsistent: PSF, MTF, wavefront and ghost already painted a status line and computed in an `AnalysisWorker`, while the four remaining actions froze the window exactly like a hang:

| Handler | Ran on the GUI thread |
| --- | --- |
| Spot Diagram | `calculate_spot_diagram` × 3 fields, before the dialog existed |
| Ray Fan | `calculate_ray_fan` × 3 fields |
| Field Curves | `calculate_field_curvature` + `calculate_distortion_curve` |
| Calculate Metrics | full `calculate_all_aberrations` (+ chromatic trace for assemblies) |
| Image Simulation | `simulate_image` inside the button handler |

Field curves additionally computed over a hardcoded `max_field = 20.0` degrees that ignored the system and the sensor the other plots derive their field from.

### The fix

- **Spot / ray fan / field curves** now go through `self._parent._open_analysis_dialog(...)`: the dialog paints "Calculating…" first, the traces run in an `AnalysisWorker`, and the finished axes are painted on the GUI thread. Because the dialogs are registered with the window's `_analysis_dialogs`, the existing quit sweep can stop their workers too.
- **Multi-panel plots**: `plot_async(..., columns=N)` builds the requested number of side-by-side axes and hands the plot callback a tuple; `columns=1` keeps the historical single-Axes contract. Re-running with a different count rebuilds the figure rather than stacking subplots. Field curves use `columns=2`.
- **Field range**: the field-curve range is derived from the configured sensor size as `atan((sensor/2)/f)` — the same expression the spot diagram and ray fan use — instead of 20°.
- **Calculate Metrics** runs in an `AnalysisWorker` held by the tab. The result's fingerprint is taken **before** measuring; if the design (or the selection) changed while the trace ran, the report is refused and the tab says the numbers no longer describe the design. A second click while a run is in flight is ignored.
- **Image simulation** runs `simulate_image` in an `AnalysisWorker`; closing the dialog (`closeEvent`, `accept()` and Esc all end in `finished`) stops the worker through the shared stop policy.
- **`openlens/gui/workers.py`** now owns `AnalysisWorker` and `stop_worker`; `AnalysisPlotDialog` re-exports the worker, and the main window's `_stop_worker` delegates. The metrics path therefore needs PySide6 only — matplotlib stays optional — and quitting, closing a dialog and the quit prompt share one policy for what counts as "running" and how a thread is stopped.

| What the quit sweep reaches | Added |
| --- | --- |
| optimizer, `_mc_worker`/`_inv_worker`, analysis dialogs | (existing) |
| `_perf_tab._metrics_worker` | this PR |

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Breaking change

## Related Issues

Closes #465

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] **16 new tests**: 11 in `tests/test_performance_tab_async.py`, 2 in `tests/test_analysis_async_dialog.py` (`columns=2`), 3 in `tests/test_window_close.py`
- [x] **Red before the fix** (the branch's tests run against unmodified master):

  | Suite | Pre-fix result |
  | --- | --- |
  | `tests.test_performance_tab_async` | `FAILED (failures=8, errors=3)` — e.g. spot blocked 3.0 s, metrics 1.0 s vs. the 0.7 s bound; field curves still measured the hardcoded 20° |
  | `tests.test_analysis_async_dialog.TestMultiPanelPlots` | 2 errors — `plot_async() got an unexpected keyword argument 'columns'` |
  | 3 quit-sweep tests, with only the `_perf_tab` reach reverted | 3/3 fail |

- [x] The handler-return tests block the real analysis function on a `threading.Event`: the handler must return before the gate is released, then the plot/report must be painted from the worker's payload.
- [x] The stale-report test edits the lens while the worker is blocked and asserts the pre-edit report is **not** painted (this caught the fingerprint being captured at the end of the compute instead of the start).
- [x] Targeted: `tests.test_performance_tab_async tests.test_analysis_async_dialog tests.test_window_close` — 59 tests, OK; `tests.test_gui_edit_debounce` — 17 tests, OK; related analysis/performance batch (PSF/MTF, aberrations, image simulator, performance metrics) — 187 tests, OK (skipped=1)

### Coverage

Each handler returns within 0.7 s while its analysis is still blocked; the worker eventually paints the three spot/ray-fan fields, both field-curve panels, the metrics report, and the simulated image; the spot dialog is registered for the quit sweep; a second Calculate click starts no second trace; an edit during a run is reported as "changed" rather than painted as current; a field-curve run uses the sensor-derived angle; closing or accepting the dialog stops a running simulation and keeps the reference when it will not stop; the main window counts and stops `_perf_tab._metrics_worker`.

title: GUI: closing the window can lose the last edit and crash running worker threads
body:
**Where:** `openlens.py` (no `closeEvent`; none in `src/gui` either). Edit debounce at `:443-463` (`EDIT_COMMIT_DELAY_MS = 400`).

Edits are saved 400 ms after the last change. Quitting inside that window drops the last edit. Nothing stops or waits for optimisation, tolerancing or analysis threads on exit, so quitting mid-run can trigger "QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running". There is no unsaved-changes prompt.

**Fix:** add `closeEvent` that calls `_flush_pending_edit()`, then `requestInterruption()` and `wait()` on every live worker (reuse `OptimizationTab._on_stop_optimization`), then accepts.

nodes.title: fix(gui): closing the window must not lose the last edit, or abort
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(gui): closing the window must not lose the last edit, or abort

Edits are saved `EDIT_COMMIT_DELAY_MS` (400 ms) after the last change, so quitting inside
that window dropped the final edit with **nothing to say so**. `closeEvent` now commits
the pending edit first — it is the one thing on screen that is genuinely the user's and
genuinely not yet on disk.

Nothing stopped or waited for the optimization, tolerancing or analysis threads on exit,
so quitting mid-run let CPython destroy a live `QThread` and `~QThread` **abort the
process**. `_shutdown_workers` walks all three.

### Details worth knowing

- **The optimizer reuses its own `_on_stop_optimization`.** Two ways to stop a thread is
  how they come to disagree about how to stop one.
- **Order is cooperative request → wait → terminate → wait.** Terminating mid-write can
  leave a partially updated object, so it is only reached when a worker ignores the
  request — typically stuck inside one long evaluation with no callback boundary.
- **A thread whose state cannot be queried keeps its reference.** Dropping a live
  `QThread`'s last Python reference *is* the abort, so an inconclusive check must never
  guess "stopped".
- **A tab that raises does not block the later tabs** from shutting down.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #466

Filed separately: [#528](https://github.com/pmaasz/openLens/issues/528) — closing while
a run is in flight still loses it without asking.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] Verified by reverting **each part separately**:

  | Reverted | Failures (of 20) |
  | --- | --- |
  | no `closeEvent` at all | 4 errors |
  | `closeEvent` does not flush the pending edit | 2 |
  | `closeEvent` does not shut the workers down | 2 |
  | tolerancing workers skipped | 5 |
  | drop the reference when thread state is unknown | 1 |

- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_window_close` — 20 tests, OK
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_window_close tests.test_gui` — 56 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1967 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=32)` — the same six
      pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 240 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8` — **no new findings** (compared by kind against `master`)
- [x] Coverage includes: closing commits the pending edit, the event is accepted,
      **a real debounce timer reaching the real save** and no spurious save when nothing
      is pending, a running tolerancing worker interrupted, a cooperative worker *not*
      terminated, a stubborn worker terminated but only after `wait(3000)`, both
      tolerancing workers stopped, references released only when stopped, a
      unstoppable worker keeping its reference, analysis workers interrupted and finished
      dialogs retired, the optimizer stop path reused, a raising tab not aborting the
      shutdown, and both halves through the one entry point that runs on quit

### ⚠️ My worker tests passed while the feature was broken

The first version called `_shutdown_workers()` directly. With the call **removed from
`closeEvent`**, every one of those tests still passed — 20/20 green, while quitting
mid-run would still have aborted the process. I only noticed because that revert was in
the table.

The tests now go through `closeEvent`, which is the path that actually runs on quit.
This is the second time in this batch that a green revert hid a real gap (the
`_assembly_tab_widget` stub in #464 was the first), and both times the cause was the
same: testing the helper and assuming the caller wired it up.

### One test I wrote was vacuous, and claimed not to be

`test_a_real_debounced_edit_reaches_the_database` asserted `callable(closeEvent)` while
its name and docstring claimed an end-to-end check. It is now
`test_a_real_debounced_edit_reaches_the_save`, which uses a real `QTimer` with a real
30-second pending debounce — covering the part the stand-in cannot, namely that an
*active* timer is what triggers the commit.

### `openlens.py` is not black-formatted

Running `black` on it produced **149 diff hunks** against a ~90-line change, and a
later global whitespace collapse rewrote 104 unrelated lines. AGENTS.md scopes black to
`src/` and `tests/`, so the final diff is **85 insertions, 0 deletions**. Worth knowing
before anyone helpfully formats it.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: Packaging: `openlens` console script broken on non-editable install, top-level `src` package, wrong URLs, stale metadata
body:
**Where:** `setup.py:34`, `:42`, `:59-63`, `:75-95`; `requirements.txt`; `src/material_database.py:87-89`, `:349`

- `openlens=openlens:main` points at the top-level `openlens.py`, which `find_packages()` does not include and there is no `py_modules=["openlens"]`. A normal (non-editable) install has a broken `openlens` command.
- The package installs as a top-level module named `src`, polluting site-packages (`import src` from any project). Entry point `openlens-cli=src.lens_editor:main` inherits this. Rename to `openlens` (or similar) and move `openlens.py` inside.
- `python_requires='>=3.7'` and the 3.7/3.8/3.9 classifiers contradict CI (3.10-3.12) and `PySide6>=6.0`. 3.7 is long EOL and not tested. The 3.7 classifier is listed twice, and `Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable` at version 0.x is overstated.
- `url` and `project_urls` point at `github.com/philip/openlens`, but the repo is `pmaasz/openLens`.
- `install_requires` is only PySide6, but the GUI imports numpy/matplotlib at module load (`openlens.py:40-45`), so a plain `pip install openlens` crashes at startup. The `visualization` extra lacks scipy/Pillow. Either make numpy/matplotlib hard requirements or fix the optional-import guards (see the separate issue).
- `MaterialDatabase` saves to `src/../data/materials.json`, which is not part of the installed package and may not be writable.
- `MANIFEST.in` includes `verify_setup.py`, which does not exist.
- `setup.py` duplicates metadata that could live in `pyproject.toml`.

**Fix:** migrate to `pyproject.toml`, rename the package, ship `data/` via package data, and test the wheel in CI by installing it into a clean venv and running `openlens --version`.

nodes.title: fix(packaging): verify a real install, and stop guessing the version
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(packaging): verify a real install, and stop guessing the version

**Most of #470 was already fixed in an earlier session that never closed the issue.** `py_modules`, the repository URLs, `python_requires`, the classifiers and the phantom `MANIFEST.in` entry were all already correct. What was still missing is the part that would have caught the original defect in the first place.

### The gap: nothing tested a non-editable install

Every CI job installs with `pip install -e .`. So the suite could never have caught the broken `openlens` command — an editable install hides it completely, because the source tree is on the path either way.

A new **`Package install`** job builds a wheel, installs it into a clean venv, and runs the command from it. Verified locally end to end:

```
$ cd /tmp && /tmp/verify/bin/openlens --version
openlens 0.4.0                     # from site-packages, not the source tree
```

### `--version` and `--help` are new

Handled **before logging, before Qt, and before anything touches the filesystem**. Creating a `QApplication` first would make the check need a display, an X server and a GPU — so it could not run headless in CI, which is the only place it is worth running.

### setup.py no longer guesses the version

It used to fall back to a hard-coded `"0.1.0"` if the `__version__` line was missing or reformatted. Unreachable in normal operation — but the release manifest is driven by this value, so had it ever fired it would have quietly stalled every subsequent release *as well as* shipping a package claiming to be years old. A build with no version now fails.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] CI configuration

## Related Issues

Closes #470

Filed separately rather than folded in:

- [#508](https://github.com/pmaasz/openLens/issues/508) — the package still installs as a top-level `src`, polluting site-packages. This PR confirms it: `from src.lens import Lens` resolves to `site-packages/src` in the clean venv.
- [#509](https://github.com/pmaasz/openLens/issues/509) — `materials.json` is written outside the installed package.

Also not here: the `pyproject.toml` migration. `setup.py`'s metadata is currently correct, so that is modernisation rather than a defect, and it is a risky change to make inside a bug-fix PR.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] Verified by reverting **each part separately**:

  | Reverted | Failures (of 18) |
  | --- | --- |
  | drop `py_modules` (the reported bug) | 1 error |
  | the wrong repository URL | 1 |
  | the dead `"0.1.0"` version fallback | 2 |
  | `python_requires` floor below the tested versions | 1 |
  | handle the headless flags after `QApplication` | 1 |

- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_packaging` — 18 tests, OK
- [x] **The CI job's exact sequence, run locally**: `python -m build --wheel` →
      clean venv → `pip install *.whl` → `openlens --version` from an unrelated
      directory. Output above.
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2028 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six
      pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 244 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8` — no new findings
- [x] Coverage includes: `py_modules` containing `openlens`, every entry-point target
      existing *and* being a top-level module (which is precisely what needs
      `py_modules`), URLs pointing at `pmaasz/openLens`, `python_requires`' floor
      equalling the lowest tested version, no duplicate classifiers, no
      `Production/Stable` at 0.x, numpy declared because it is imported at module
      load, `MANIFEST.in` including nothing that does not exist, no invented version
      fallback, packaged version equalling `src.__version__`, `--version` and `-V`
      printing and exiting 0, `--help`, no flags falling through to the GUI,
      unknown flags *not* pre-empting Qt's own handling, and the flags being handled
      before `QApplication`

### Why the tests parse `setup.py` instead of importing it

Importing `setup.py` executes `setup()` with whatever `argv` the test runner has.
They parse the AST instead and read the literal kwargs — so these tests cannot
break the build or each other.

### One test of mine had a bug worth naming

`test_python_requires_matches_the_tested_versions` read `>=3.10` with
`r">=(\d+)\.(\d+)"` and took group 1 — the **major** version, 3 — then compared it
to `{10, 11, 12}`. It failed with `3 != 10`, which reads like a genuine packaging
problem and was not one. Now parsed as `(major, minor)` tuples.

The reason it matters: that failure would have been *fixed* by changing
`python_requires` to `>=3`, if I had believed it.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-underwind areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings

title: User data uses a relative `openlens.db` path: launching from another directory silently opens an empty library
body:
**Where:** `openlens.py:100`, `:1207`; `src/gui/dialogs/startup.py:48`, `:409`; `src/gui/storage.py:30`

`"openlens.db"` is resolved against the current working directory. Starting the app from another folder (a desktop launcher, an IDE, `python /path/openlens.py`) silently creates a new empty DB, which looks like data loss. User materials are also stored next to the source tree.

**Fix:** store user data under a per-user directory (`QStandardPaths.AppDataLocation` or `platformdirs`), centralise the path in one function, allow an override via env var/CLI flag, and offer to migrate an existing `./openlens.db`.

nodes.title: fix: user data must not depend on the working directory
nodes.body:
## Description

fix: user data must not depend on the working directory

The database was opened as the bare relative name `"openlens.db"`, which SQLite resolves
against the **current working directory**. Launching from a desktop launcher, an IDE, or
`python /path/to/openlens.py` created a brand new empty database in whatever folder
happened to be current — which looks exactly like data loss, because the real database is
still sitting somewhere else with everything in it.

`src/paths.py` resolves the location once, per platform. The stated end-to-end test:

```
two different working directories → one database path
```

### No new dependency

`platformdirs` is available locally but is **not** a declared dependency, and #470 is
already about how fragile this project's packaging is. The rule is short enough to state
outright: `$XDG_DATA_HOME/openlens` (or `~/.local/share/openlens`) on Linux,
`~/Library/Application Support/openlens` on macOS, `%APPDATA%\openlens` on Windows.

### Resolution happens at call time

The default is `None`, resolved inside the function — **not** a filename default. A
default argument is evaluated once when the module loads, which would freeze the path
before a test or a launcher had a chance to set the environment. A test asserts the
signatures directly, so this cannot quietly come back.

### Migration never overwrites

If the destination already exists the old file is left **completely alone**. Overwriting
it is the one outcome here that could destroy someone's library, so the user's data wins
and the orphan stays where it is. `$OPENLENS_DB_PATH` suppresses migration entirely — the
user has said where the database is; relocating it would be arguing with them.

### Also fixed

`LensManager` seeded the example lens whenever the file was *named* `openlens.db`, so any
scratch file with that name was treated as the app database. It now compares resolved
paths.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #471

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] Verified by reverting **each part separately**:

  | Reverted | Failures (of 29) |
  | --- | --- |
  | resolve to a relative path again | 5 |
  | a frozen filename default argument | 2 |
  | overwrite an existing destination | 1 |
  | remove the `migrate_legacy_db()` call from `main()` | 1 |

- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_user_data_paths` — 29 tests, OK (2 skipped: the
      macOS and Windows platform-convention tests, on Linux)
- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_database tests.test_database_migrations tests.test_lens_editor tests.test_material_database` — 91 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 1990 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six
      pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 242 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8` — no new findings beyond one `E402` per file touched, which is that
      file's existing structure (imports after `logger = ...`); and I removed one
      now-unused `import os` in `lens_editor.py` that the old `os.path.basename` check
      had been keeping alive
- [x] Coverage includes: the default being absolute, not landing in the working
      directory, being stable across working directories, agreeing with the data
      directory, each platform convention, the data-dir env var, the path getter *not*
      creating the directory, the DB env var winning and being read on every call, tilde
      expansion, empty-string handling, no frozen defaults, migration moving the data,
      never overwriting a live database, suppression by the env var, directory creation,
      a permissions failure being reported rather than raised, and the end-to-end
      two-directories-one-library case

### ⚠️ My test base class never ran, and the suite looked fine

```python
class _Env:          # not unittest.TestCase
```

unittest silently ignores every class built on it. The first run reported **`Ran 3
tests ... FAILED`** — a plausible-looking small suite — while **23 tests never
executed**. After the fix: `Ran 26 tests, OK`.

Nothing in the output distinguished those two states. It is the same failure mode as the
empty `_sources` helper I left in the file: a class that exists but contributes nothing.

### ⚠️ Removing the migration call from `main()` left all 26 passing

Testing `migrate_legacy_db()` does not prove anything calls it. Three tests now cover the
call site directly: that `main()` calls it, that it runs **before** the window is built
(moving the file after the database is opened does nothing), and that a failure is
caught so an unwritable data directory cannot stop the app starting.

This is the **third** time in this batch that the helper was tested and the caller assumed
— #464 (`_fold_target_into_library`), #466 (`_shutdown_workers`), now `migrate_legacy_db`.
Worth treating as a standing review question rather than three coincidences.

### One test could not test what it claimed

The migration tests originally patched `paths.os.getcwd`. `Path("openlens.db")` resolves
against the **process** working directory and never calls `os.getcwd()`, so the patch
changed nothing — the tests were passing or failing for unrelated reasons. They now
actually `chdir`, with the previous directory restored.

- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings

title: Assembly lenses reappear as standalone library lenses; every full save logs ERROR per assembly lens
body:
**Where:** `src/database.py:539-557`, `:759-762`; `src/gui/storage.py:181-191`

`load_all` returns every row in `lenses` as a top-level `"Lens"`, including lenses that only exist inside an assembly. They show up in GUI and CLI lens lists after reload. On a full save, `_reconcile` tries to delete each one and gets `LensInUseError`; `delete_item` logs any exception at ERROR before re-raising, so each save produces an ERROR line per assembly lens.

**Repro:** after saving `[OpticalSystem A(L1, L2)]` and reloading: `[('Lens','L1'), ('Lens','L2'), ('OpticalSystem','A')]`.

**Fix:** decide whether a lens belongs to the library or only to an assembly (e.g. a `standalone` column, or exclude lenses referenced only by assemblies). At minimum, don't log `LensInUseError` at ERROR.

nodes.title: fix(db): an assembly's lenses must not reappear in the library
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(db): an assembly's lenses must not reappear in the library

`load_all` returned every row in `lenses` as a top-level `"Lens"`, including lenses that exist only as assembly elements. Saving `[OpticalSystem A(L1, L2)]` and reloading produced:

```
[('Lens','L1'), ('Lens','L2'), ('OpticalSystem','A')]
```

for a library that held only `A`.

### The fix is not a filter on "referenced by an assembly"

That hides a lens the user deliberately kept in the library **and** put in an assembly — my first attempt, and a test caught it. The rows genuinely cannot say which is which: both are lens rows. So `lenses.is_library` (schema v6) records what only the caller knows — and `save_lenses` is handed the library snapshot on every save.

Assignment is **opt-in** via `library_snapshot`, for exactly the reason `reconcile` already is. This is not hypothetical: **four existing tests broke** on my first version, which assigned unconditionally. The CLI passes a lens-only list, so reading "absent from this list" as "not a library item" there would erase the entire library.

Migration defaults existing rows to `1`, so old databases behave exactly as before until the application next saves.

### Also in this change

- **`delete_item` logged `LensInUseError` at ERROR.** That is the guard working as designed, so every full save of a library with assemblies reported one failure per assembly lens while behaving perfectly correctly. Now DEBUG; genuine failures stay ERROR, and a test drives the real error path to prove it rather than asserting something that cannot fail.
- **`_reconcile` no longer attempts deletes the in-use guard will refuse.** A doomed attempt is not a safety net — it is one refusal per assembly lens per save.
- **Seven tests hard-coded `user_version=5`.** They now assert `SCHEMA_VERSION`, so the next schema bump is not a chase through five files by hand.

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

Closes #472

  | Reverted | Failures (of 19) |
  | --- | --- |
  | `load_all` ignores `is_library` (the reported bug) | 3 |
  | membership never recorded | 3 |
  | `LensInUseError` back at ERROR | 1 |
  | reconcile attempts doomed deletes | 1 |

- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_assembly_lens_library_membership` — 19 tests, OK
- [x] `test_delete_row_removal` + `test_optimization_apply` + `test_database` +
      `test_database_migrations` — 72 tests, OK (all four of the regressions above)
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2047 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six
      pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 245 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8` — no new findings beyond one `E402` from the added import, matching
      that file's existing layout
- [x] Coverage includes: the issue's repro, no phantom names, a genuinely standalone
      lens still loading, **a lens shared between the library and an assembly still
      loading**, two assemblies sharing a lens, the assembly keeping its elements,
      every element resolving to its own lens data, a save/reload round trip being
      stable, the refusal still raising, **a refusal not logged at ERROR**, a real
      failure still logged at ERROR, the refusal explained at DEBUG, the helper
      reporting assembly lenses, reconcile attempting no deletes, reconcile still
      removing genuinely stale rows, the assembly surviving reconciliation, and
      `all_ids` still seeing everything

### Two tests I had to rewrite because they were not testing what they claimed

`test_a_genuine_delete_failure_is_still_logged_at_error` asserted
`isinstance(errors, list)` — it could not fail. It now patches the connection so
`delete_item` genuinely raises a non-`LensInUseError`, and asserts the ERROR line
appears.

`test_the_refusal_is_explained_at_debug` used `min(logger.level, level)`. With
`NOTSET` (0) that computes 0, leaving the level at `NOTSET` and deferring to the
root logger — WARNING. So the debug records it existed to check were silently
discarded, and the test failed for a reason unrelated to what it was about.

### One existing test was querying through the wrong view

`tests/test_optimization_apply._rows_for` used `LensStorage.load_lenses()` to
check that a row persisted. That is the *library* view, and an assembly element
is deliberately not a library item now — so it reported "absent" for a row stored
perfectly well. It reads the table directly, which is what a persistence assertion
should do.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: Validation: clear_aperture args never validated; bool/huge ints/np.float32 mishandled
body:
**Where:** `src/validation.py:573-621`, `:62`, `:952-973`

1. `validate_lens_parameters` accepts `clear_aperture_1/2` but never validates or returns them. `validate_lens_parameters(50,-50,5,25,1.5, clear_aperture_1=-5, clear_aperture_2=1e9)` returns normally.
2. `_validate_number` calls `math.isnan` on huge ints, raising `OverflowError` instead of `ValidationError` (`validate_radius(10**400)`). `safe_float_conversion` in the same file already guards this.
3. `validate_lens_data_schema` (used by JSON import in `startup.py:379`) checks `isinstance(x, (int, float))`, so `true` is accepted as a radius or thickness.
4. `np.float32` is rejected with "got float32".

**Fix:** call `validate_clear_aperture(...)` for both apertures and return them; use `numbers.Real`, `float()` inside `try/except OverflowError` and reject `bool` explicitly.

nodes.title: fix(validation): reject what validation says it rejects
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(validation): reject what validation says it rejects

Four defects that had accumulated in the same module, each independently
silent.

### 1. `validate_lens_parameters` accepted the clear apertures and ignored them

```python
validate_lens_parameters(50, -50, 5, 25, 1.5, clear_aperture_1=-5, clear_aperture_2=1e9)
# returned normally
```

They were documented in the docstring, then neither validated nor returned. A caller
asking for validation got **neither an error nor the value**. Both are now checked
against the validated diameter and returned.

### 2. `_validate_number` leaked `OverflowError`

It called `math.isnan` on a value that could not be a float yet, so `validate_radius(10**400)`
raised `OverflowError` instead of `ValidationError` — the one exception type every
caller of this module knows how to handle. The file's own `safe_float_conversion`
documents precisely this trap.

### 3. The JSON schema accepted `true` as a radius

`isinstance(x, (int, float))` is satisfied by `True`, because `bool` subclasses `int`.
A hand-edited or generated import file could set a radius or a thickness to `True`.

### 4. `numpy.float32` was rejected

```
radius must be a number, got float32
```

`float32` is a number that every downstream calculation handles fine, and that
round-trips through JSON as a plain one. `_validate_number` now accepts `numbers.Real`,
which is what `float32` actually registers as.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #473

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] Verified by reverting **each part separately**:

  | Reverted | Failures (of 34) |
  | --- | --- |
  | no clear-aperture validation | 6 |
  | `isinstance((int, float))` restored | 4 errors |
  | the `OverflowError` guard removed | 9 errors |
  | `bool` accepted in the schema again | 6 |

- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_validation_gaps` — 34 tests, OK
- [x] `test_validation` + `test_validation_gaps` + `test_lens` — 107 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2081 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six
      pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 246 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8` — **no new findings**
- [x] Coverage includes: the issue's repro, each surface validated independently, the
      apertures returned when valid and `None` when absent, **the key always present**
      (a caller reading it must not get a `KeyError` on the happy path), an aperture
      exceeding the diameter rejected, `10**400` reported as a `ValidationError` at all
      four entry points with a message that says *why*, a large-but-representable int
      still accepted, every numeric field rejecting both `True` and `False`, optional
      numeric fields rejecting `bool`, `float32` accepted through every entry point,
      and `str`/`None`/`complex`/`Decimal` all still rejected

### Three of my test assumptions were wrong, and the tests caught them

I wrote the tests while implementing and three asserted things that are not true:

- **`Decimal` is not a `numbers.Real`.** It registers as `numbers.Number`. Since the
  fix widens `(int, float)` to `numbers.Real`, taking `Number` instead would have
  silently accepted it — so `test_decimal_is_still_rejected` now pins that it stays out.
- **`parabolic_sag_1` is not a declared schema field**, so the optional-field test now
  uses `wavelength` and `temperature`.
- **A 29 mm aperture under a 30 mm lens is legal** (`value > diameter + EPSILON`). I
  had assumed otherwise. The test that was meant to check the ceiling now checks the
  ordering property instead: a bad diameter is reported *before* the aperture is
  considered, which is what "uses the validated diameter" actually means.

### One place I deliberately did not widen

`Decimal` is the obvious candidate for "a number Python has that isn't int/float", and
the issue did not ask for it. Accepting it would mean a value whose arithmetic behaves
differently from `float` flowing into the tracer unconverted. It stays rejected, with
a test saying so.

title: Material catalog import rewrites materials.json once per glass (O(N^2)) and aborts on write failure
body:
**Where:** `src/material_database.py:357-362`, `:666`, `:706`, `:627-628`, `:711-712`

`add_material` calls `save_database()` (a full atomic JSON rewrite) per material, so importing N glasses rewrites the file N times. If a write fails (for example a read-only install path), the broad `except Exception` stops the import partway and returns an under-counted number after logging. Keys in the JSON file that are lowercase can't be found by `get_material`, which uppercases the name.

**Fix:** add materials without saving during an import and save once at the end, let I/O errors reach the caller, and uppercase keys in `_load_database`.

nodes.title: fix(materials): save a catalog import once and surface write failures
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(materials): save a catalog import once and surface write failures

Three defects in one path:

1. **One full rewrite per glass.** `add_material` called `save_database()` on every call, and `save_database` is an atomic full-file rewrite (temp file + rename). Importing N glasses rewrote `materials.json` N times.
2. **A failed write looked like a short import.** The importer's broad `except Exception` swallowed an I/O failure from the final write, logged it, and returned an under-counted number. On a read-only install path the user saw "imported 3 of 10" with nothing saying the catalog was never written.
3. **Lower-case keys were unreachable.** `_load_database` stored JSON keys verbatim while `get_material` upper-cases the lookup, so a hand-edited `"nbk7"` key could never be found.

### The fix

- `add_material(material, save=True)` — the importers pass `save=False`, then save once after the loop, **outside** the parse guard, so a write error reaches the caller.
- The AGF and CSV importers batch their writes; the per-row parse handling is unchanged.
- Loaded materials are keyed by their uppercased name, matching `get_material`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking)

## Related Issues

Closes #474

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] **7 new tests** in `tests/test_material_import_persistence.py`: one save for a 2-glass AGF import, one save for a 2-row CSV import, the single write contains the whole batch, `add_material` still saves by default, an AGF write failure propagates, a CSV write failure propagates, and a lower-case JSON key is loadable
- [x] **Red before the fix**: `FAILED (failures=5)` — 2 saves for 2 glasses, 2 saves for 2 rows, both write failures swallowed, lower-case key `None`
- [x] `tests.test_material_import_persistence`, `tests.test_agf_import`, `tests.test_material_database_resilience`, `tests.test_material_database` — 58 tests OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2249 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6)` — master (2242) plus the seven new tests; the six errors are the pre-existing `gui_flows` loader failures (pytest is not installed locally)
- [x] `black --check` clean; `flake8` clean on the touched files

title: Robustness: CLI create_lens skips validation; importers read whole files with no size limit; save is not one transaction
body:
**Where:** `src/lens_editor.py:101`; `src/export_formats.py` (`ZemaxSystemImporter`); `src/io/step_export.py` (`read_step_solids`); `OpticalSystem.load`; `src/gui/storage.py:149-154`; `openlens.py:183-188`

- The CLI `create_lens` does not call `validate_lens_name` (`modify_lens` does) or `check_physical_feasibility`, so it accepts lenses the GUI would reject.
- `ZemaxSystemImporter`, `read_step_solids` and `OpticalSystem.load` read whole files with no size limit, and `OpticalSystem.load` skips `reject_non_finite_numbers`.
- `save_lenses` writes each item in its own transaction, so a failure part-way leaves a partially saved library.

**Fix:** route every entry point through the same validators, add a size cap and non-finite rejection, and wrap a full save in one transaction.

nodes.title: fix(robustness): validate CLI input, cap imports, save the library atomically
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(robustness): validate CLI input, cap imports, save the library atomically

Four entry-point gaps, all of which let bad input or a failed write through silently:

1. **CLI accepted what the GUI rejects.** `create_lens` built a `Lens` and appended it without `validate_lens_name` or `check_physical_feasibility`. A 101-character name crashed on `Lens(...)` instead of being refused, and a lens whose surfaces intersect inside the clear aperture (edge thickness −99 mm) was saved happily. It now runs both validators and returns `None` without saving.
2. **Importers read whole files with no size limit.** `ZemaxSystemImporter.import_system`, `read_step_solids` and `OpticalSystem.load` now reject files above `MAX_IMPORT_FILE_BYTES` (64 MiB) through a shared `reject_oversized_file` helper.
3. **`OpticalSystem.load` accepted non-finite numbers.** `json.load` parses the non-standard bare `NaN` / `Infinity` literals, and a NaN compares false against every downstream sanity threshold. `reject_non_finite_numbers` now runs before `from_dict`.
4. **A failed library save was half a save.** `LensStorage.save_lenses` called `save_lens` / `save_assembly` per item, each committing on its own, so a failure on item three left items one and two persisted. All items and the library membership now commit in one `save_library` transaction, and any failure rolls the whole snapshot back.

### Refactor

- `DatabaseManager._write_transaction()` is the one place `BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT` happens for writes now; `save_lens`, `save_assembly`, `set_library_membership` and the new `save_library` all use it.
- `save_lens` no longer duplicates the row INSERT; it uses the existing `_save_lens_row` (which grew a `flatten_metadata` flag so assembly elements keep their previous blob shape).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix / robustness (non-breaking)

## Related Issues

Closes #475

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] **11 new tests** in three files:
  - `tests/test_cli_create_lens_validation.py` — over-long name refused, infeasible lens refused, feasible lens still created
  - `tests/test_import_limits.py` — Zemax, STEP and JSON loads reject an over-cap file, a small file still loads, `NaN` and `Infinity` rejected
  - `tests/test_library_save_transaction.py` — a failure mid-save leaves no rows, a successful save still writes everything
- [x] **Red before the fix**: `FAILED (failures=4, errors=5)` — both invalid lenses were created, the three importers read the oversized files, both non-finite payloads loaded, and the first lens of the failed save stayed in the database
- [x] `tests.test_gui_save_reporting` (17 tests) updated to break the database through `save_library`, the seam the storage layer now uses
- [x] Database, storage, membership, importers, STEP/Zemax round-trips — 248 tests OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2269 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6)` — master (2258) plus the eleven new tests; the six errors are the pre-existing `gui_flows` loader failures (pytest is not installed locally)
- [x] `black --check` clean; `flake8` only pre-existing findings

title: Optional dependency rule violated: numpy imported unguarded; psf_mtf guard crashes at import
body:
**Where:** `src/analysis/plots.py:12`, `src/mechanical_designer.py:6`, `src/image_simulator.py:15`, `src/analysis/psf_mtf.py:19`, `:28`; `openlens.py:40-45`, `:920-922`

AGENTS.md says optional imports must be guarded with a `*_AVAILABLE` flag so the app starts without them. `openlens.py` imports `psf_mtf` and `plots` at module level, so the GUI cannot start without numpy. In `psf_mtf` the guard sets `np = None`, and the `np.ndarray` annotation at `:28` then fails at import. `mechanical_designer` uses numpy only for `np.pi`, and its `ImportError` is misreported as "requires pythonocc-core".

**Repro** (with `sys.modules['numpy']=None`): `plots`, `mechanical_designer`, `image_simulator` raise `ModuleNotFoundError`; `psf_mtf` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'ndarray'`.

**Fix:** use `math.pi` in `mechanical_designer`, guard numpy in `plots` and `image_simulator`, use `from __future__ import annotations` in `psf_mtf`. Alternatively make numpy a hard dependency and update AGENTS.md. Add a CI job that runs the core tests without optional deps.

nodes.title: fix(deps): the application must start without its optional dependencies
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(deps): the application must start without its optional dependencies

AGENTS.md requires optional imports to be guarded with a `*_AVAILABLE` flag so the app
starts and runs its core features without them. Four modules were not, and because
`openlens.py` imports two of them at module level, **the whole GUI failed to launch**:

```
plots, mechanical_designer, image_simulator  -> ModuleNotFoundError
psf_mtf                                      -> AttributeError:
                                               'NoneType' has no attribute 'ndarray'
```

### The interesting one: a guard that was there and still failed

`psf_mtf` *did* guard the import — it set `np = None`. But its annotations are written
as `np.ndarray`, and those are evaluated when each function is **defined**. The guard
was in place and the module still could not be imported. `from __future__ import
annotations` in both `psf_mtf` and `image_simulator`.

### `mechanical_designer` took a hard dependency for a constant

It used numpy for exactly three `np.pi` and nothing else. It now uses `math.pi`.

### ⚠️ This reverses a decision I made in #470

`numpy` was moved into `install_requires` **because** these imports were unguarded —
that was the right call at the time, and the comment said so.

With the guards in place, requiring it made all of them **dead code** and quietly
narrowed what AGENTS.md means by an optional dependency. Two positions, one of them now
false. The core genuinely does not need numpy:

```
focal length: 49.21299900942747
traced ok, path len 4
```

`Lens`, the ray tracer and focal length all run without it — and there is now a test
for that. numpy stays available through the `visualization` extra, and
`test_packaging_metadata`'s assertion that numpy *is* required is **inverted rather than
deleted**, with the reason recorded in both places.

### New CI job: `Core without optional deps`

Installs PySide6 alone and checks the application imports and the guard tests pass.
Nothing could check this before: every other job installs the full dependency set, so
the modules these guards protect were importable anyway.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] CI configuration

## Related Issues

Closes #476

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] Verified by reverting **each part separately**:

  | Reverted | Failures (of 14) |
  | --- | --- |
  | remove `from __future__ import annotations` | 5 |
  | unguard `plots`' numpy import | 3 |
  | restore `np.pi` in `mechanical_designer` | 3 |
  | numpy back as a hard requirement | 2 |

- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_optional_dependency_guards` — 14 tests, OK
- [x] mechanical / image-simulator / psf-mtf / packaging / guards — 128 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2096 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six
      pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 247 files unchanged
- [x] Coverage includes: every guarded module importing without the optional packages,
      each named individually, **the application itself importing**, the window class
      being reachable, each `*_AVAILABLE` flag reporting False when its package is
      absent, annotations stored unevaluated, `mechanical_designer` not importing
      numpy, its volume math still running, numpy absent from `install_requires`, only
      the GUI framework required, the extras still offering numpy and matplotlib, and
      `requirements.txt` still describing them as recommended

### The tests run in subprocesses, and that matters

`sys.modules['numpy'] = None` makes the next `import numpy` raise — but it also leaves
`numpy` in `sys.modules` for the rest of the process. Doing this in-process would poison
every later test, and the result would look like a broken suite rather than a simulated
environment. Each case gets a clean interpreter.

### Four of my own test assumptions were wrong

Again, the tests caught them rather than me:

- **`typing.get_type_hints` resolves the deferred annotations** — so it needs numpy to
  exist, and the test failed for a reason unrelated to what it was about. It now asserts
  the annotations are stored as *strings*, which is the actual mechanism.
- **`LensMount` requires six positional arguments.**
- **`'False' was compared as a string`** rather than a bool, so every flag read as
  "not false" and the assertions were passing vacuously.
- **`PySide6` did not match the lowercased `'pyside6'`** — a test that could only ever
  pass by failing.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (AGENTS.md's rule is now
      true rather than aspirational)
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: load_all returns type='Biconvex' for a lens: the metadata blob overwrites the 'Lens' row marker
body:
Found while fixing #431. Not caused by that work, and verified identical on
`master` at `adec854`.

**Where:** `src/database.py` — `load_all`, both the lenses and the assemblies
pass.

`load_all` tags each row before decoding it:

```python
lens["type"] = "Lens"          # explicit row marker
...
_metadata_merge(lens, lens["metadata"], ...)   # target.update(meta)
```

`_metadata_merge` flattens the stored blob over the row, and the blob has
always carried `Lens.to_dict()["type"]`, which holds the **lens type**
(`"Biconvex"`, `"Meniscus"`, ...), not the row marker. So the merge overwrites
the marker and every lens comes back as:

```
'type': 'Biconvex'
```

## Why it has not bitten anyone

`LensStorage.load_lenses` dispatches on `type != "OpticalSystem"`, so the
production path is unaffected — a lens whose type is `Biconvex` is still
correctly treated as a Lens. The collision is only observable to code that
filters on the documented marker.

It already has bitten the test suite: `tests/test_database.py::_load_lenses`
filters `r.get("type") == "Lens"` and therefore returns `[]` for every call.
Any assertion built on it is passing vacuously rather than checking anything.

## Reproduce

```python
from src.database import DatabaseManager
from src.lens import Lens
import tempfile
path = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".db", delete=False).name
DatabaseManager(path).save_lens(Lens(name="X").to_dict())
print(DatabaseManager(path).load_all()[0]["type"])   # 'Biconvex', not 'Lens'
```

## Suggested fix

Keep the marker distinct from the payload. Either store the marker under a key
the blob cannot collide with (`row_type`, or reuse the absence of `elements`),
or exclude `type` from the merge and expose the lens type under its own key
(`lens_type`) in both `to_dict` and `from_dict`. The second is clearer but
touches the existing JSON interchange format, so it wants a migration note.

Worth auditing every `type == "Lens"` / `type == "OpticalSystem"` comparison in
the codebase at the same time — the tests and the production code disagree
about what that field means, which is the actual hazard here.

nodes.title: fix(data): the row marker is row_type, not the lens type
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(data): the row marker is `row_type`, not the lens type

`DatabaseManager.load_all` tagged each row with a kind *before* decoding it:

```python
lens["type"] = "Lens"          # explicit row marker
...
lens["metadata"] = _metadata_merge(lens, lens.pop("metadata", None), ...)
```

`_metadata_merge` merges the stored blob **flat** onto the same dict, and `Lens.to_dict()["type"]` is the lens type (`"Biconvex"`, ...). The merge therefore overwrote the marker, and every lens row came back with `type: "Biconvex"`. Anything that filtered on `type == "Lens"` matched nothing — including the helper in `tests/test_database.py`, so **eleven assertions built on it had been passing vacuously**.

### The fix

- The marker now lives on its own key, **`row_type`** (`"Lens"` / `"OpticalSystem"`), and is set **after** the merge, so a stored blob cannot spoof it.
- The payload keeps `type` as the model's own type; `Lens.from_dict` gets the lens type back instead of a marker.
- `LensStorage.load_lenses` dispatched on `type` too and now dispatches on `row_type`. This also fixes an assembly row whose payload has no `type` key — the seed data writes those — being rebuilt as a `Lens`.
- The issue's requested audit found **ten more test filters** keyed on the overloaded field (`test_metadata_resilience`, `test_stop_alignment`, `test_seed_data`, `test_coating`, `test_clear_aperture`, `test_e2e_persistence`, `test_metadata_persistence`, `test_assembly_lens_library_membership`); all use `row_type` now. The two migration tests and the `_load_lenses` helper are no longer no-ops.

> Notably, two of those filters (`test_metadata_resilience`, `test_seed_data`) **broke under the fix before being migrated**: their assembly rows genuinely have no payload `type`, which is direct evidence that dispatching on `type` was relying on a coincidence.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Breaking change — `row_type` is a new key in `load_all()` rows; code that filtered on `type == "Lens"` was already broken (it matched nothing) and must use `row_type`

## Related Issues

Closes #488

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] 8 new tests (`TestLoadAllRowMarker`, `TestLensStorageUsesTheRowMarker` in `tests/test_database.py`), including a blob-spoof case (`Lens(metadata={"row_type": "OpticalSystem"})`) and a typeless-assembly dispatch case
- [x] **Part-by-part reverts:**

  | Reverted | Failures |
  | --- | --- |
  | lens marker back under `type` before the merge | 12 failures + 7 errors |
  | assembly marker removed | 4 failures + 2 errors |
  | marker set *before* the merge | 1 (blob spoof) |
  | storage dispatch back on `type` | 1 (typeless assembly) |

  The first revert's failure count is the measure of how much had been passing vacuously.
- [x] Targeted: `test_database`, `test_database_migrations`, `test_metadata_resilience`, `test_metadata_persistence`, `test_assembly_lens_library_membership`, `test_stop_alignment`, `test_seed_data`, `test_coating`, `test_clear_aperture`, `test_e2e_persistence` — 167 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2203 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six pre-existing `gui_flows` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --check` — 250 files unchanged; `flake8` — byte-identical finding sets to master for both source files (the pre-existing `database.py` `E501` and `gui/storage.py` `E402`/`F401` are untouched)

### Coverage

Lens row: marker present, `type` retains the real lens type (`Biconvex`, `Plano-Convex`); assembly row: marker present; blob cannot spoof the marker; a row with no blob still gets a marker; `LensStorage` returns a `Lens` with its `lens_type` intact; returns an `OpticalSystem` for a normal assembly and for a typeless one.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (`load_all` docstring documents `row_type`)
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: MaterialDatabase(None) writes to the real data/materials.json, so tests pollute the user's glass catalog
body:
Found while fixing #433. This one wrote to real user data on my machine during
the investigation, so it is worth fixing rather than just noting.

**Where:** `src/material_database.py:93-94`

```python
def __init__(self, db_path: Optional[str] = None):
    self.db_path = db_path or os.path.join(
        os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "data", "materials.json"
    )
```

`None` does not mean "in memory" - it means "the real catalog". The `db_path=None`
in `tests/test_material_database.py` reads as isolation and is not: `load_database()`
reads the user's file and every `add_material()` writes straight back to it, via
`atomic_write_json`.

## What actually happened

While writing a regression test for #433 I instantiated `MaterialDatabase(db_path=None)`
and imported AGF fixtures. When I later re-ran with the importer fixed, the test
still saw the *old* mis-parsed values - because they had been persisted:

```
nd = 4242.0  vd = 1.7  thermal_expansion = 4.99999e-05
```

Those are `parts[3]`/`parts[4]` of `NM UNKNOWN_F 99 4242 1.7000 50.0 ...`, i.e. the
old parser's output. My fix looked like it was not being used at all, which sent
me hunting for a stale bytecode cache before I checked the data file.

`data/materials.json` had accumulated `BAD_T`, `N-BK7`, `N-SF5`, `SF11`,
`UNKNOWN_F` - a mis-parsed N-BK7 and a fabricated `UNKNOWN_F` with `nd 517642`.
I removed those five and kept a backup. The entries from the older suite
(`CSV_GLASS`, `CSV_GLASS2`, `CSV_FLINT`, `TEST_FLINT`, `TRANS_TEST`,
`TEST_GLASS`, `TEST_GLASS2`) pre-date this session and I left them alone, but they
are the same class of pollution and are almost certainly also test residue rather
than intended catalog contents.

## Consequences

1. **Test results depend on the developer's real catalog.** A test can pass
   locally and fail in CI, or vice versa, purely because of what happens to be
   in `data/materials.json`.
2. **Running the suite edits a data file.** For a user who keeps their own glass
   library there, a test run can add, overwrite or delete entries.
3. **Failures point at the wrong cause.** A stale material left behind by an
   earlier run looks exactly like a code path that is not being taken.

## Suggested fix

- Add an explicit in-memory or temp-file mode (`db_path=":memory:"`, or a
  `MemoryMaterialDatabase`) and use it in the tests, rather than overloading
  `None`.
- Have `add_material()` refuse to write when the path was not explicitly given,
  or emit a loud warning.
- Purge the residue: confirm with the maintainer whether `CSV_*`, `TEST_*` and
  `TRANS_TEST` are meant to be in `data/materials.json` and remove them if not.
- The new AGF tests in #433 pass an explicit temp `db_path` for this reason, but
  that only fixes the tests I added.

Unrelated to the above: `data/materials.json` is gitignored, so none of this
residue has ever reached the repository - it only ever existed on developer
machines.

nodes.title: fix(data): the material catalog belongs in writable user data
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(data): the material catalog belongs in writable user data

The default was `<package>/../data/materials.json`:

- `data/` is a sibling of the package and gitignored, so it is **absent from a real installation**;
- on an installed copy `__file__` is inside site-packages, so it resolved to `site-packages/data/materials.json` — **not writable without root**, and polluting the venv if it is;
- and `MaterialDatabase(None)`, which tests used as though it meant "in memory", read and wrote the **developer's real catalog**.

That last point was live, not theoretical. `test_material_cache` and `test_material_database` add materials, so every suite run mixed `TEST_GLASS`, `TEST_FLINT` and friends into `data/materials.json` and rewrote the whole file. While scoping this I confirmed the checkout's catalog had acquired those entries, and that `N-SF5` was present in an older backup but missing from the current file.

### The fix

- The default is now `<user data dir>/materials.json`, resolved through `paths.py` like the SQLite database, with `$OPENLENS_MATERIALS_PATH` as an override.
- Built-in materials still load first, so **a fresh install has a usable catalog before the file exists**; reading does not create it.
- `save_database()` creates the user data directory.

### Migration copies, once

An existing catalog at the old repository path is copied at startup, **before the first database is constructed**:

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| copy, not move | the file may be in a shared or version-controlled checkout; deleting it is not the migration's business |
| never over an existing destination | the user's current catalog wins |
| missing legacy file is a no-op | the normal case on an installed copy |
| `$OPENLENS_MATERIALS_PATH` set → no migration | the user has already said where the catalog is |

### Test isolation

`tests/__init__.py` now points `OPENLENS_DATA_DIR` and `OPENLENS_MATERIALS_PATH` at a temporary directory for the whole run, and the two tests that add materials pass an explicit temp file. This is belt and braces: even a future test that constructs `MaterialDatabase()` and writes cannot reach real user data.

> **Existing data was not rewritten.** The checkout's `data/materials.json` still contains the `TEST_*` entries earlier runs put there. I deliberately did not "clean" user data — it is the user's file — and the fix stops any further changes. It is left for the owner to decide.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Breaking change — no: `MaterialDatabase(None)` still works, it just resolves to a writable user path now

## Related Issues

Closes #509
Closes #490

Both are the same root cause: #490 is the test-pollution consequence of #509's default path. One PR, because fixing the path without the test isolation would just move the pollution.

Deliberately **not** folded in: [#474](https://github.com/pmaasz/openLens/issues/474) — import rewrites the file once per glass (O(N²)), lowercase keys are unreachable via `get_material`, and write errors are swallowed. Those are import-path concerns, still open.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] New regression suite: `tests/test_material_catalog_location.py` — 25 tests
- [x] **Verified by reverting each part separately** (25 tests):

  | Reverted | Failures |
  | --- | --- |
  | old package-relative default restored | 4 |
  | migration missing from `main()` | 2 |
  | migration allowed to overwrite an existing catalog | 1 |
  | `shutil.move` instead of `copy2` | 2 |
  | env override ignored by migration | 1 |
  | `save_database()` not creating its parent | 4 |

- [x] **The direct #490 proof**: `sha256sum data/materials.json` identical before and after the full suite
- [x] Clean wheel installed with `--no-deps` into a fresh venv, run from `/tmp`:
      ```text
      builtins: 7
      catalog: /tmp/tmp.CTIb0zzgzl/materials.json
      reloaded: True
      ```
      path is under `$OPENLENS_DATA_DIR`, not site-packages
- [x] CI's `Package install` job now runs exactly that check on a fresh install
- [x] Targeted: material location + material database + cache + cache isolation + user paths + packaging — 114 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2167 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six pre-existing `gui_flows` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --check` — 250 files unchanged; `flake8` — no findings in the touched source (tests only the usual `E402` from `sys.path.insert`)

### Coverage

Default under `user_data_dir()` and not inside the package or the checkout; absolute; override honoured; built-ins on a fresh install; reading creates nothing; write lands in the user dir and reloads; missing parent created; the repository catalog is byte-identical across a default-database write; migration copies, leaves the legacy file, never overwrites, no-ops on absence, creates its parent, honours the env opt-out, and the migrated catalog loads; the GUI entry point calls it before the window; and a guard that the test run itself is not pointed inside the checkout.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (module docstrings + `paths.py` contract)
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: OpticalSystem.to_dict cannot represent a nested assembly tree; sub-assemblies come back flattened
body:
Found while fixing #438. Deliberately left out of that fix, because it is a
format change rather than a position fix.

**Where:** `src/optical_system.py` - `to_dict` / `from_dict`

`to_dict` stores only the *flattened* element list:

```python
"elements": [
    {"lens": e.lens.to_dict(), "lens_id": ..., "position": e.position,
     "decenter_y": ..., "tilt_x": ...}
    for e in self.elements
],
```

`self.elements` is the flat list `_rebuild_from_tree` produces by walking the
tree, so the **hierarchy is discarded**: the nesting, the sub-assembly
membership and the parent-child relationships are all gone. `from_dict` then
rebuilds a flat system with `add_lens()`, so every element ends up as a direct
child of the root.

The repro in #438 - "an assembly at x=20 comes back as a root-level
OpticalElement at x=0" - is this, not a position bug (the position part is
fixed there). A user who builds a doublet inside a sub-assembly, saves the
system as JSON, and reopens it gets a flat two-element system. The optical
result may still be close, but the *structure* the user built is gone, and any
edit that re-saves it writes the flattened form back.

## The shape of the problem

`root.get_flat_list()` returns `(node, global_position)` pairs, so the global
positions are already correct in the flat form. What is missing is the
*parentage*: which nodes are children of which, and which are sub-assemblies
rather than elements.

A faithful round trip needs to serialize the tree shape, not just the leaves.
That means recording, for each node, its parent and its local transform, and
rebuilding `OpticalAssembly`/`OpticalElement` nodes on load.

## Why it was not done in #438

#438 restored the absolute positions that `to_dict` already saved - a small,
well-contained fix with a clear correctness criterion. Changing the format's
shape is a different job with different risks:

- `to_dict`/`from_dict` have consumers: `OpticalSystem.save`/`load`, the GUI's
  "Save As..." (`openlens.py`), `LensStorage.load_lenses`
  (`src/gui/storage.py:94`), the startup dialog's import
  (`src/gui/dialogs/startup.py:392`), and the database round trip. A format
  change has to keep all of them working.
- Old files must still load. A new format needs a version marker and a
  fallback to the flat interpretation.

## Suggested direction

Serialize the tree explicitly - a recursive node list with each node's type
(`element` or `assembly`), its local transform and its children - and keep
reading the existing flat form when the new key is absent. Add a round-trip
test that compares the *tree*, not just the flat elements, plus a traced
optical comparison so the two can be checked for equivalence.

Related: `optical_node.py:135` still carries `# TODO: Serialize modifiers`, so
modifiers on a node are lost by the same mechanism. That is a separate issue.

nodes.title: fix(serialization): saving a system must not flatten it
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(serialization): saving a system must not flatten it

`to_dict` stored only the **flattened** element list. `self.elements` is what `_rebuild_from_tree` produces by walking the tree, so the hierarchy was discarded — nesting, sub-assembly membership and parent-child relationships all gone. `from_dict` then rebuilt a flat system with `add_lens()`, so every element ended up a direct child of the root.

The failure the issue describes:

```python
# build a doublet inside a sub-assembly, save, reopen
before: [('OpticalAssembly', 'Doublet', ['A', 'B'])]
after:  [('OpticalElement', 'A', []), ('OpticalElement', 'B', [])]
```

And because any edit re-saves the flattened form, **the loss compounds**.

### The tree was already there

`OpticalNode.to_dict()` has always serialised the tree recursively — name, position, rotation, children, type. `OpticalSystem.to_dict` simply never called it.

It now writes that as `node_tree`, **alongside** the flat `elements` rather than instead of it. That key is load-bearing for four consumers — the database, the GUI's Save As, `LensStorage.load_lenses` and the startup dialog's import — so replacing it was never an option. `from_dict` uses the tree when present and takes the **unchanged** flat path when it is not, so every file written before this still loads.

### Unknown node types rebuild as containers

Rather than being dropped. Losing a subtree silently is worse than not knowing its exact class, and a future node type would otherwise vanish on the next save.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #497

Next to [#498](https://github.com/pmaasz/openLens/issues/498) — `optical_node.py` still carries
`# TODO: Serialize modifiers`, so modifiers are lost by the same mechanism. Separate issue,
not folded in.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] Verified by reverting **each part separately**:

  | Reverted | Failures (of 20) |
  | --- | --- |
  | do not write `node_tree` | 9 |
  | do not use `node_tree` on load | 8 |
  | parent pointers not restored | 1 |
  | an unknown node type becoming an element | 1 |
  | `node_tree` left in `_SYSTEM_SERIALIZED_KEYS` | 1 |

- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_optical_system_tree_roundtrip` — 20 tests, OK
- [x] `test_optical_system` + tree round trip + `test_database` + `test_lens_editor` — 84 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2116 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six
      pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 248 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8` — no new findings in `src/`; the test file adds three `E402` from
      `sys.path.insert` before its imports, the same as every other test here
- [x] Coverage includes: the issue's doublet-in-a-sub-assembly scenario, nesting one
      and three levels deep, **parent pointers restored** (containment does not imply
      them — they are stored references), local positions and rotations, **global
      positions unchanged** by the round trip, a second round trip stable (the old
      flattening compounded), an unknown node type, the flat `elements` key still
      present with the fields consumers read, JSON-serializability, a file without a
      tree still loading, a file without a tree **still keeping its saved positions**
      (#438 must not regress), `node_tree` not leaking into user metadata, a shared
      `lens_lookup` used through the tree, a flat system unchanged, and **ray tracing
      agreeing to 9 decimal places before and after**

### The test compares trees, not element lists

`_shape()` returns nested tuples of `(class, name, children)`. A flat
`(node, position)` list — which is what `get_flat_list()` gives — cannot distinguish
two different trees containing the same elements, which is the entire point of the
bug. The global-position test is kept *alongside* the shape test for the same reason:
structural fidelity is only worth anything if the optics are unchanged, and either
check alone would pass against half the bug.

### Two of my tests passed against broken code until I fixed them

- **The unknown-node-type test checked the node count and its children but not its
  class.** An unknown node rebuilt as an `OpticalElement` still had one child named
  `A`, so it passed. It now asserts the node is still a container.
- **The metadata test put `node_tree` at the top level, where
  `_SYSTEM_SERIALIZED_KEYS` never applied.** That set filters the metadata *blob* —
  a metadata dict built by merging a previous `to_dict()` output is exactly where a
  stale serialized key ends up. The test now constructs that case, and removing
  `node_tree` from the set fails it.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
