title: OpticalNode modifiers are never serialized ('# TODO: Serialize modifiers')
body:
Found while fixing #438. The TODO has been there since the node tree was
introduced.

**Where:** `src/optical_node.py:135`

```python
# TODO: Serialize modifiers
```

Every node in the optical tree can carry *modifiers* - the local transforms
applied on top of a node's own position and rotation. They are not written by
`OpticalSystem.to_dict`, and nothing reads them back, so they are lost on any
save/load cycle.

## Why it matters

The tree is the authority for element geometry: `_rebuild_from_tree` derives
each element's global position from the tree, and the per-element decenter and
tilt it stores come from `node.position` and `node.rotation`. A node with a
modifier has its contribution applied *on top* of those.

So the loss is not just "an extra field went missing" - it can move elements.
A tree where a sub-assembly is offset by a modifier serializes to a tree
without that modifier, and the elements inside it come back at different
absolute positions.

## Relationship to the tree-shape issue

Both this and the tree-shape problem (#497) come from the same root cause:
`to_dict` serializes the flat element list rather than the tree, so anything
that only exists in the tree is dropped. A tree-shape format that records each
node's parent and local transform would naturally carry modifiers too.

## Suggested direction

- Record each node's modifiers in the tree serialization, alongside the parent
  and local transform.
- Add a test that builds a tree with a modifier, round-trips it, and compares
  the *global positions* of the elements inside - not just the modifier
  objects, which could compare equal while being applied to the wrong parent.
- Until then, consider whether the modifier API should warn when a system
  containing modifiers is saved, the way the loss of the assembly tree is now
  documented in `from_dict`.

nodes.title: fix(serialization): a node's modifiers must survive a save/load cycle
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(serialization): a node's modifiers must survive a save/load cycle

`OpticalNode.to_dict` dropped `modifiers` entirely, behind a
`# TODO: Serialize modifiers` that had been there since the node tree was introduced.
Any node carrying a modifier lost it on save — which made `to_dict` **lossy**: it
returned a dict that did not describe the node.

Modifiers are now serialized polymorphically (each via its own `to_dict`, so a
subclass that adds state carries it) and rebuilt on load through a registry.

### An unknown type is preserved, not dropped

`SurfaceModifier` is registered by definition; anything else must opt in. An
unregistered type is rebuilt as a generic modifier that keeps its name **and records
what it was**, with a warning:

```
Modifier type 'FromTheFuture' is not registered; restored as a generic
SurfaceModifier named 'Mystery'. Its behaviour is not guaranteed.
```

The data survives and the uncertainty is stated. Dropping it is the failure this
issue is about.

### ⚠️ What this does NOT do, stated plainly

The issue predicts the loss "can move elements". **It does not, today.**
`get_local_transform` uses only `position` and `rotation`, and nothing in the tree
applies a modifier — I verified this before writing the fix:

```
global pos before modifier: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
global pos after  modifier: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
=> modifiers move elements? False
=> to_dict drops them:      True
```

What is true is the lossy `to_dict`, and that is what this fixes. Shipping a fix
that implies a data-loss severity that does not exist would be the wrong kind of
confident.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #498

With [#497](https://github.com/pmaasz/openLens/pull/535) — both come from `to_dict`
ignoring the tree, which is now written and now carries modifiers.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] Verified by reverting **each part separately**:

  | Reverted | Failures (of 24) |
  | --- | --- |
  | modifiers dropped from `to_dict` again | 13 |
  | not restored on load | 6 |
  | an unknown type dropped instead of preserved | 1 |
  | the restoration warning removed | 1 |
  | the registry lookup bypassed | 3 |

- [x] `python3 -m unittest tests.test_optical_node_modifiers` — 24 tests, OK
- [x] `test_optical_system_tree_roundtrip` + `test_optical_system` — 54 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2140 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six
      pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --line-length=100 src/ tests/ --check` — 249 files unchanged
- [x] `flake8` — `optical_node.py` clean; `optical_system.py`'s three findings are
      pre-existing and byte-identical on `master`
- [x] Coverage includes: a node dict having a `modifiers` key, name and type recorded,
      a subclass recording its own type and fields, ordering preserved across several
      modifiers, an empty list when there are none, an assembly unaffected,
      JSON-serializability, everything surviving a round trip, **a subclass's own type
      and field surviving**, several round trips being stable, global positions
      unchanged, an unregistered type keeping its name and its `original_type` and
      warning, the base and registered types *not* warning, an unknown modifier
      surviving a whole-system round trip, and the registry being reversible

### A test that passes for the wrong reason, labelled as such

`test_positions_match_across_a_round_trip` is the comparison the issue asks for, and
it passes. But it passes because **no modifier is applied to anything** — not because
the round trip preserves geometry under a modifier.

So it is paired with:

```python
def test_a_modifier_does_not_move_anything_today(self):
    """Records the current truth, so it cannot be mistaken for the fix."""
```

with a failure message that says what to do if it ever fails: *"a modifier now moves
the element - good, but the docstrings and tests that say modifiers are inert must be
updated with it."* A test whose comment quietly becomes false is worse than no test.

### The stale marker is checked

`test_no_todo_remains` asserts the string `TODO: Serialize modifiers` is gone. A
leftover TODO reads identically whether the work is done or not, which is exactly the
condition that let this sit for as long as it did.

- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings

- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: Package installs as top-level 'src', polluting site-packages for every project on the machine
body:
Found while fixing #470, where the other packaging defects were fixed. Left out
of that PR deliberately: renaming the package touches every import in the
codebase and every test, which is a different scale of change from fixing
broken metadata.

## The problem

`find_packages()` finds `src`, so the distribution installs a top-level package
named **`src`** into site-packages:

```python
>>> import src
>>> src.whatever
```

Any project on the machine that happens to have a `src` directory now has it
shadowed, or shadows it. This is a well-known packaging anti-pattern for
exactly this reason.

The `openlens-cli=src.lens_editor:main` console script inherits it, so the
installed command imports `src.lens_editor` — which works, and is precisely the
problem: it silently works in ways a consumer would not expect.

## What renaming would touch

Not a mechanical change:

- every relative import stays as-is (they are already `from .x import y`), but
  every **absolute** `from src.` import must become `from openlens.`;
- `openlens.py` sits at the repo root and imports `from src....`. Moving it
  inside the package would put `openlens/openlens.py`, which then shadows the
  distribution name on the module path — so it needs a different module name
  (`__main__.py`, `app.py`, or `gui.py`) and the entry point updated;
- the test suite: every `tests/test_*.py` does `from src.lens import Lens`;
- `setup.py`: `find_packages()` plus the `py_modules` entry added in #470;
- anything that references the on-disk path `src/`: the docs, `MANIFEST.in`,
  CI workflow paths, the database schema/migrations if they store module paths;
- `MaterialDatabase`'s default path, which is already `src/../data/materials.json`
  and is itself wrong on an installed copy (see the sibling issue).

## Suggested approach

Rename the directory to a proper package name (`openlens/`, or a `src`-layout
with the importable package named for the project), move the GUI entry module
inside it under a non-shadowing name, update the console scripts to
`openlens.__main__:main`, and do it as a single mechanical commit whose only
reviewable question is whether any behaviour changed - it should not.

Worth doing in CI: install the built wheel into a clean venv and assert
`import openlens` works from an unrelated directory. That catches both this and
the class of bug in #470 without anyone having to remember.

## Suggested regression test

```python
def test_the_top_level_package_name_is_not_generic(tmp_path):
    """A package called `src` shadows every project's src/ directory."""
    # build the wheel, install into a venv, run `python -c "import openlens"`
    # from an unrelated cwd
```

Refs #470.

nodes.title: fix(packaging): the distribution must not install a package called src
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(packaging): the distribution must not install a package called `src`

`find_packages()` found `src`, so a **real install put a top-level package named `src` into site-packages**. `src` is the most generic directory name there is: every other project on the machine with a `src/` directory either shadowed it or was shadowed by it. The console script inherited it too, silently importing `src.lens_editor` — working, in exactly the way a consumer would not expect.

The directory is now **`openlens/`**. Every absolute `from src.` import became `from openlens.`; the package's own modules were already relative and are unchanged.

### The entry module could not just move to `openlens/openlens.py`

A module of that name shadows the package on the module path, which is the same class of bug. It is now `openlens/__main__.py`, reachable both as:

```bash
python3 -m openlens              # documented in AGENTS.md / README
openlens --version               # console script: openlens.__main__:main
```

The root `openlens.py` and its `py_modules` entry are **gone**.

### Constrained packaging

```python
packages=find_packages(include=['openlens', 'openlens.*']),
```

So no stray top-level directory can be shipped by accident again — the only thing this distribution installs is `openlens`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #508

Sibling: [#509](https://github.com/pmaasz/openLens/issues/509) — `MaterialDatabase`'s default path is `openlens/../data/materials.json`, still wrong on an installed copy. The rename does not change that (it was `src/../data`, equally wrong); deliberately not folded in.

## How Has This Been Tested?

The load-bearing evidence is a **real wheel installed into a clean venv**, because every other CI job is editable and hides this class of defect:

```text
wheel top-level entries: ['openlens', 'openlens-0.4.0.dist-info']
has src package:  False
has root openlens.py: False

/tmp/venv508/bin/python  (cwd = /tmp)
openlens from: /tmp/venv508/lib/python3.12/site-packages/openlens/__init__.py
from openlens.lens import Lens                        -> OK
from openlens.gui.storage import LensStorage          -> OK
importlib.util.find_spec('src') is not None           -> False

/tmp/venv508/bin/openlens  entry point:
from openlens.__main__ import main
```

> Note: the first wheel I built still contained `src/` and a root `openlens.py`. That was **stale `build/lib` content from the previous build**, not the new config — setuptools assembles the wheel from there without cleaning. `rm -rf build openlens.egg-info` and a rebuild produced the clean wheel above. CI builds from a fresh checkout, but the trap is worth recording: a wheel is not evidence until the build directory is gone.

- [x] Clean wheel: only `openlens/` + dist-info; no `src/`, no root `openlens.py`
- [x] Clean venv, `--no-deps`, imports from an unrelated cwd: OK
- [x] `python3 -m openlens --version` → `openlens 0.4.0` from the repo and from `/tmp` via `PYTHONPATH`
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2142 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six pre-existing `tests/gui_flows/test_*` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --exclude 'openlens/__main__.py' openlens/ tests/ --check` — 249 files unchanged
- [x] `python3 -m openlens.lens_editor --help` — interactive CLI with no flag handling, exits 1 on EOF; verified byte-for-byte the same on `master`
- [x] **Load-bearing**: reverting `packages=find_packages(include=[...])` to an unconstrained `find_packages(exclude=[...])` fails `test_the_declared_packages_are_all_inside_openlens`

### Tests

The old `test_openlens_is_declared_as_a_module` asserted `py_modules` — now removed, because the entry point no longer needs it. Its replacement is four tests for the actual defect:

- no top-level `src` package exists in the tree
- no root `openlens.py` exists to shadow the `openlens/` package
- declared packages all live inside `openlens` (guards the `include` pattern)
- the GUI entry point is `openlens.__main__:main` and `openlens/__main__.py` defines `main()`

Tests were updated where they imported the GUI module as `openlens` (`from openlens import OpenLensWindow`, `openlens.QMessageBox`, `openlens.main`, `openlens.StepExporter`): those names now live in `openlens.__main__`, so the imports and patch targets name it explicitly. This is the call site, not a helper — the recurring trap.

### What changed outside Python source

Because the on-disk path moved, these would silently rot otherwise:

| Consumer | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `setup.py` | packages, version path, both entry points |
| `ci.yml` | black/flake8/coverage paths; `Package install` imports `openlens` and asserts no `src` package |
| `release.yaml` + `openlens.spec` | PyInstaller script `openlens/__main__.py`, `--paths .` / `pathex=['.']` |
| release-please config | `openlens/__init__.py` |
| Sphinx autodoc | repo root on `sys.path`; `automodule:: openlens.*`; all `src.` targets |
| README, AGENTS.md, docs, launcher scripts, `.opencode/` | `python3 -m openlens`, `openlens/` paths, lint commands |

`CHANGELOG.md` and the versioned `specs/OpenLens-v0.*` artifacts are left alone: they record history, not current layout.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: MaterialDatabase writes to src/../data/materials.json, which is not shipped and may not be writable
body:
Found while fixing #470, where the other packaging defects were fixed. This one
needs a product decision about where user data lives, so it is not folded into a
metadata fix.

## The problem

`src/material_database.py:87`:

```python
self.db_path = db_path or os.path.join(
    os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "data", "materials.json"
)
```

Three separate problems:

1. **Not shipped.** `data/` is in `.gitignore` and is a sibling of `src/`, not
   inside a package, so it is not part of the distribution at all. A fresh
   `pip install openlens` has no catalog.

2. **Not writable.** On an installed copy `__file__` is inside site-packages, so
   this resolves to `site-packages/data/materials.json`. Writing there needs
   root, fails on most system installs, and pollutes the venv if it succeeds.

3. **Depends on layout.** The `..` hard-codes the repo layout. It works in an
   editable checkout and is wrong everywhere else - which is why the whole
   test suite passes and a real install does not.

The `MaterialDatabase(None)` default is also what the earlier finding recorded
as #490: constructing one without a path and calling `add_material` writes to the
developer's real catalog. Tests always pass an explicit `db_path` to avoid it.

## What a fix needs to decide

This is a design question rather than a patch:

- **Where does the shipped default catalog live?** As package data inside the
  package (`openlens/data/materials.json`) it ships, but is still not the right
  place for *user* edits.
- **Where do user edits go?** Platform convention: `~/.local/share/openlens/`
  on Linux, `%APPDATA%` on Windows, `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS.
  A read-only shipped catalog plus a writable user overlay is the usual shape.
- **What happens on first run?** Copy the shipped catalog to the user location,
  or read the shipped one until the user writes?

The shipped catalog should be read-only and identified as such; the overlay
should be the only writable copy. `AGF` import (#433) and `add_material` both
write, so both paths need to land in the overlay.

## Suggested regression test

```python
def test_a_default_database_path_is_writable():
    """The default path must not be inside site-packages or the repo."""

def test_the_shipped_catalog_is_found_on_a_fresh_install():
    # build + install the wheel in a venv, construct MaterialDatabase() with no
    # arguments, and assert the catalog loaded and is non-empty
```

The second is the one that would have caught this, and also the `openlens`
console script bug in #470.

Refs #470, related to #490.

nodes.title: fix(data): the material catalog belongs in writable user data
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(data): the material catalog belongs in writable user data

The default was `<package>/../data/materials.json`:

- `data/` is a sibling of the package and gitignored, so it is **absent from a real installation**;
- on an installed copy `__file__` is inside site-packages, so it resolved to `site-packages/data/materials.json` — **not writable without root**, and polluting the venv if it is;
- and `MaterialDatabase(None)`, which tests used as though it meant "in memory", read and wrote the **developer's real catalog**.

That last point was live, not theoretical. `test_material_cache` and `test_material_database` add materials, so every suite run mixed `TEST_GLASS`, `TEST_FLINT` and friends into `data/materials.json` and rewrote the whole file. While scoping this I confirmed the checkout's catalog had acquired those entries, and that `N-SF5` was present in an older backup but missing from the current file.

### The fix

- The default is now `<user data dir>/materials.json`, resolved through `paths.py` like the SQLite database, with `$OPENLENS_MATERIALS_PATH` as an override.
- Built-in materials still load first, so **a fresh install has a usable catalog before the file exists**; reading does not create it.
- `save_database()` creates the user data directory.

### Migration copies, once

An existing catalog at the old repository path is copied at startup, **before the first database is constructed**:

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| copy, not move | the file may be in a shared or version-controlled checkout; deleting it is not the migration's business |
| never over an existing destination | the user's current catalog wins |
| missing legacy file is a no-op | the normal case on an installed copy |
| `$OPENLENS_MATERIALS_PATH` set → no migration | the user has already said where the catalog is |

### Test isolation

`tests/__init__.py` now points `OPENLENS_DATA_DIR` and `OPENLENS_MATERIALS_PATH` at a temporary directory for the whole run, and the two tests that add materials pass an explicit temp file. This is belt and braces: even a future test that constructs `MaterialDatabase()` and writes cannot reach real user data.

> **Existing data was not rewritten.** The checkout's `data/materials.json` still contains the `TEST_*` entries earlier runs put there. I deliberately did not "clean" user data — it is the user's file — and the fix stops any further changes. It is left for the owner to decide.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Breaking change — no: `MaterialDatabase(None)` still works, it just resolves to a writable user path now

## Related Issues

Closes #509
Closes #490

Both are the same root cause: #490 is the test-pollution consequence of #509's default path. One PR, because fixing the path without the test isolation would just move the pollution.

Deliberately **not** folded in: [#474](https://github.com/pmaasz/openLens/issues/474) — import rewrites the file once per glass (O(N²)), lowercase keys are unreachable via `get_material`, and write errors are swallowed. Those are import-path concerns, still open.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] New regression suite: `tests/test_material_catalog_location.py` — 25 tests
- [x] **Verified by reverting each part separately** (25 tests):

  | Reverted | Failures |
  | --- | --- |
  | old package-relative default restored | 4 |
  | migration missing from `main()` | 2 |
  | migration allowed to overwrite an existing catalog | 1 |
  | `shutil.move` instead of `copy2` | 2 |
  | env override ignored by migration | 1 |
  | `save_database()` not creating its parent | 4 |

- [x] **The direct #490 proof**: `sha256sum data/materials.json` identical before and after the full suite
- [x] Clean wheel installed with `--no-deps` into a fresh venv, run from `/tmp`:
      ```text
      builtins: 7
      catalog: /tmp/tmp.CTIb0zzgzl/materials.json
      reloaded: True
      ```
      path is under `$OPENLENS_DATA_DIR`, not site-packages
- [x] CI's `Package install` job now runs exactly that check on a fresh install
- [x] Targeted: material location + material database + cache + cache isolation + user paths + packaging — 114 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2167 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six pre-existing `gui_flows` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --check` — 250 files unchanged; `flake8` — no findings in the touched source (tests only the usual `E402` from `sys.path.insert`)

### Coverage

Default under `user_data_dir()` and not inside the package or the checkout; absolute; override honoured; built-ins on a fresh install; reading creates nothing; write lands in the user dir and reloads; missing parent created; the repository catalog is byte-identical across a default-database write; migration copies, leaves the legacy file, never overwrites, no-ops on absence, creates its parent, honours the env opt-out, and the migrated catalog loads; the GUI entry point calls it before the window; and a guard that the test run itself is not pointed inside the checkout.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (module docstrings + `paths.py` contract)
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: GUI: closing the window while work is still running loses it without warning
body:
**Where:** `openlens.py` (`closeEvent`, added in #466)

#466 added a `closeEvent` that commits the pending debounced edit and stops every worker on quit. What it does **not** do is tell the user they are closing with work in flight.

Two situations are indistinguishable from the outside:

- a Monte Carlo or optimisation run that has been going for four minutes and will be thrown away on quit
- an analysis plot dialog still computing in the background

Nothing on screen says "this will be lost". The user finds out by losing it.

**Suggested fix:** on `closeEvent`, if any worker is still running (or a debounced edit is genuinely pending beyond the normal commit), ask first via `QMessageBox` — "N operations are still running. Quit anyway?" — and only then accept. Reuse `_shutdown_workers`' existing reach over `_opt_tab`, `_tol_tab` and `_analysis_dialogs` rather than walking the threads again.

Filed as a follow-up rather than folded into #466: every edit made outside the 400 ms debounce window is already saved on quit, so this is a confirmation/UX concern, not a data-loss bug. It should be designed on its own terms rather than as a patch.

nodes.title: fix(gui): ask before quitting with work in flight
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(gui): ask before quitting with work in flight

`closeEvent` (from #466) committed the pending edit and stopped every worker, but said nothing about the work it was stopping. Two situations were indistinguishable from the outside:

- a Monte Carlo or optimization run that has been going for four minutes and will be thrown away on quit;
- an idle window.

The user found out by losing it.

### The fix

`closeEvent` now counts what `_shutdown_workers` already reaches, then asks once:

```
N operations are still running.

Quitting now stops it and discards the work in progress.
```

| What is counted | How it is detected |
| --- | --- |
| optimizer | `_opt_is_running` **or** a live `_opt_worker` (the flag is set before the thread exists) |
| tolerancing | `_mc_worker`, `_inv_worker` |
| analysis dialogs | each dialog's `_pending_worker` |

- **Default button is No** — a stray Return keeps the work.
- **Declining** ignores the close event; the pending edit is *not* flushed and no worker is stopped, so the window and every thread keep running.
- **Confirming** runs the existing flush → `_shutdown_workers()` → `accept()` path unchanged.
- **Unknown worker state counts as running.** A needless prompt costs one click; silently discarding a four-minute run costs the run. (This is deliberately the opposite bias from `_stop_worker`, which must not drop a live QThread's reference.)

The count reach is written once, beside `_shutdown_workers`, so the prompt and the shutdown cannot come to disagree about what is running.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Breaking change

## Related Issues

Closes #528

## How Has This Tested?

- [x] 13 new tests in `tests/test_window_close.py`
- [x] **Part-by-part reverts:**

  | Reverted | Failures |
  | --- | --- |
  | `closeEvent` ignoring the count | 5 |
  | optimizer counted only from its worker object | 1 |
  | unknown worker state treated as stopped | 1 |
  | default button switched to Yes | 1 |

- [x] The real dialog is covered with `QMessageBox.question` patched out: Yes → True, No → False, the count appears in the text, singular wording for one operation, default button is No
- [x] Targeted: `tests.test_window_close` — 33 tests, OK
- [x] Full suite: `Ran 2216 tests`, `FAILED (errors=6, skipped=34)` — the same six pre-existing `gui_flows` loader errors, no new failures
- [x] `black --check` — 250 files unchanged; `flake8` on `__main__.py` — identical finding set to master (the file is excluded from black and unchanged in style)

### Coverage

A running tolerancing worker triggers one confirmation; declining keeps the window open, saves nothing and leaves the worker alive; an idle window never asks and closes normally; three in-flight operations (two tolerancing + one analysis, with a finished dialog excluded) are counted as 3; the optimizer is counted from its flag before a worker exists; finished workers are not counted; confirming still stops the worker; a worker that raises on `isRunning()` is counted.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation (docstrings on `_worker_still_running`, `_running_work_count`, `_confirm_close_with_work`, `closeEvent`)
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: Keyboard Shortcuts dialog advertises Ctrl+1-6 but no shortcuts exist
body:
Split from #469.

`_on_show_shortcuts` (`openlens/__main__.py:1060`) lists Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+6 as tab-switching shortcuts, but the application creates no `QShortcut` for them (no `QShortcut` exists anywhere in `openlens/`). The dialog documents behaviour the user cannot invoke.

Do one of:

- Implement them: `Ctrl+1` Lens Editor, `Ctrl+2` Assembly Editor, `Ctrl+3` Simulation, `Ctrl+4` Performance, `Ctrl+5` Optimization, `Ctrl+6` Tolerancing, switching `_editor_tabs`. Handle a hidden tab (no current assembly) explicitly, e.g. a status message instead of a silent no-op.
- Or remove the tab-switching block from the dialog.

Preferred: implement the shortcuts, and test that each one selects the right tab (and that Ctrl+2 does something sensible while the assembly tab is hidden).

## Description

fix(gui): add the advertised Ctrl+1-6 tab shortcuts

Fixes #565.

The Keyboard Shortcuts dialog has always listed Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+6 under
"Tab Switching", but no `QShortcut` existed anywhere in the application, so
the keys did nothing.

- One `TAB_SHORTCUTS` table (tab index, sequence, display name) builds the
  six window-level shortcuts after the editor tabs are created.
- `_switch_to_tab()` selects the tab and shows its name.
- Ctrl+2 is advertised even when no assembly is loaded. The assembly tab is
  hidden then and Qt will not select a hidden tab, so the shortcut now says
  "Assembly Editor: no assembly loaded" instead of looking dead.
- Creating an assembly makes Ctrl+1/Ctrl+2 switch in both directions.

The tests also cover real key dispatch with `QTest.keyClick`, not only

title: release: PyPI publish fails because the 'openlens' name belongs to an unrelated project
body:
The 0.5.0 release proved the new release path works, but the `publish` job is red at the PyPI step:

- Run: https://github.com/pmaasz/openLens/actions/runs/39414106103
- `Attach dist to GitHub Release` succeeds; the wheel and sdist are on the release.
- `Publish to PyPI` fails.

`setup.py` declares `name="openlens"`, but https://pypi.org/project/openlens/ is a
different, existing project: a placeholder OCR package owned by `nuhmanpk`. We
cannot publish to that name without ownership. Every release will therefore end
red even though the GitHub Release assets are fine.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The release workflow does not fail when the PyPI distribution name is not
      ours to publish.
- [ ] PyPI publishing is gated behind an explicit opt-in (repository variable),
      with a comment explaining why it is off by default.
- [ ] Building and attaching the wheel/sdist to the GitHub Release still runs.
- [ ] A follow-up decision records whether to rename the distribution before
      turning publishing on.

nodes.title: fix(release): gate PyPI publishing on a repository variable (#591)
nodes.body:
## Description

fix(release): gate PyPI publishing on a repository variable

Fixes #591.

The 0.5.0 release (run 39414106103) built and attached the wheel/sdist, then
turned red at `Publish to PyPI`. `setup.py` publishes as `openlens`, but that
name on PyPI is an unrelated placeholder OCR package owned by another account.
We cannot publish to it, so every release would end red even though the GitHub
Release assets are correct.

The action log also reports `invalid-publisher` because PyPI Trusted Publishing does not
currently support reusable workflows (the parent is `release-please.yaml`). A renamed,
owned project would still need a direct release workflow. Both blockers are recorded
in #591; this gate keeps the release itself green meanwhile.

This change makes the PyPI step opt-in through the repository variable
`PYPI_PUBLISH_ENABLED`, with a comment pointing at #591. Building the
wheel/sdist and attaching them to the Release still runs unconditionally.

title: bug(data-loss): JSON round-trip drops any system with a plano (infinite-radius) surface
body:
## Summary

`OpticalSystem.save()` writes a plano surface's infinite radius as the bare JSON literal `Infinity`; `OpticalSystem.load()` rejects every non-finite number and returns `None`. Any system containing a flat surface therefore cannot be round-tripped through the application's own interchange format.

## Impact

- Data loss: the save reports success (`True`) but the file can never be loaded back.
- Affects the documented JSON interchange path (`OpticalSystem.save/load`, GUI "Save As...", CLI export).
- A plano (R = ∞) surface is a normal design choice, so this is not a rare corner case.

## Reproduction

```python
import tempfile
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem

s = OpticalSystem()
s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=float("inf"), radius_of_curvature_2=-50.0))
p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".json")
print("save:", s.save(p))          # True
print("load:", OpticalSystem.load(p))  # None
```

Output:

```
save: True
Error loading optical system: optical system['elements'][0]['lens']['radius_of_curvature_1'] contains a non-finite number: inf
load: None
```

The file contains `"radius_of_curvature_1": Infinity` (Python's `json` accepts the non-standard literal, but the project's own validator does not).

## Root cause

- `openlens/lens.py:589` — `to_dict()` writes `self.radius_of_curvature_1` / `_2` directly, and the model stores plano as `float("inf")`.
- `openlens/optical_system.py:663` — `load()` calls `reject_non_finite_numbers(data, "optical system")`.
- `openlens/validation.py:1008` — validator deliberately rejects `NaN`/`Infinity` in imported JSON.

So the writer produces a value the reader is explicitly designed to reject.

## Expected behaviour

Plano surfaces survive a save/load round-trip with the same optical meaning (`inf` radius on both sides), and no file written by the app is rejected by the app.

## Suggested fix

Pick one canonical encoding (e.g. `null` for an infinite radius, or a documented sentinel such as `"inf"`) and apply it symmetrically in `Lens.to_dict` / `Lens.from_dict` (`openlens/lens.py:589`, `:633`). Keep accepting legacy files that already contain `Infinity` where safe. Add a round-trip regression test covering plano R1, plano R2, and both-plano.

nodes.title: fix(data-loss): make a flat surface survive the JSON interchange format
nodes.body:
## Description

A flat surface is an infinite radius in the model, and JSON has no way to
spell one. `OpticalSystem.save()` wrote the bare `Infinity` literal, which is
not valid JSON and which the application's own reader rejects
(`reject_non_finite_numbers`). A system with a plano surface could therefore
never be loaded back: the save reported success and the file was dead.

A flat radius is now written as `null` - valid JSON, and unambiguous.

## What changed

- `openlens/lens.py`
  - `json_safe_radii(payload)` returns a copy of a payload whose infinite
    radii are `null`. Only the radius fields of a lens dict are touched (a
    lens dict is recognised by its radius keys, so the flat `elements` list
    and the `node_tree` are both covered); every other value is copied
    unchanged, so a NaN elsewhere still fails the write loudly.
  - `decode_radius(value)` maps the JSON `null` back to the model's own
    spelling (`inf`), and `Lens.from_dict` uses it.
  - `Lens.to_dict()` is unchanged: it keeps the numeric radius, because the
    database columns are `NOT NULL REAL`.
- `openlens/optical_system.py`
  - `save()` writes `json_safe_radii(self.to_dict())` with
    `allow_nan=False`, so the file it writes is a file it can read.
  - `load()` normalises the radii before the non-finite check, so a file
    written by an older version (bare `Infinity`) still loads while every
    other non-finite value is still rejected.
- `openlens/gui/services/export_service.py` - the "Save As JSON" export uses
  the same encoding.
- `openlens/gui/dialogs/startup.py` - the JSON import normalises the radii
  before rejecting non-finite numbers, so a legacy file still imports.
- `openlens/validation.py` - the lens schema validator accepts `null` for the
  two radius fields (a flat surface).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #601

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New tests (all fail on the unfixed code):

- `tests/test_optical_system.py::TestFlatSurfaceRoundTrip`
  - `test_plano_first_surface_round_trips`
  - `test_plano_second_surface_round_trips`
  - `test_both_surfaces_flat_round_trip`
  - `test_written_file_is_valid_json` (a strict parser must accept the file)
  - `test_legacy_file_with_infinity_literal_still_loads`
- `tests/test_lens.py::TestLensSerialization::test_from_dict_null_radius_is_a_flat_surface`
- `tests/test_lens.py::TestLensSerialization::test_to_dict_keeps_the_numeric_radius_for_the_database`
- `tests/test_validation.py::test_validate_lens_data_schema_accepts_a_null_radius`
- `tests/test_export_service.py::test_save_lens_json_writes_a_flat_surface_as_null`

Full local suite: `Ran 2586 tests ... OK (skipped=35)` (2577 before this
change, plus the 9 new tests), `black` clean, `ruff` clean, `mypy` clean.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(data-loss): partial library saves reset is_library and leak assembly-only lenses into the library
body:
## Summary

`DatabaseManager._save_lens_row()` uses `INSERT OR REPLACE` but does not include the `is_library` column. Every save therefore rewrites the row with the column's schema default (`1`), silently promoting a lens that lived only inside an assembly into the global lens library.

## Impact

- Data pollution: assembly members reappear as standalone library lenses after a partial save.
- Observed with a full save (`library_snapshot=True`) producing `['library', 'asm']`, while a subsequent partial save (`demote=False`, the default) produces `['library', 'member', 'asm']`.
- Affects the CLI (`openlens/lens_editor.py`) and module-level `save_lenses` in `openlens/gui/storage.py:260`, both of which save with the default partial semantics.
- A user's library slowly fills with internal assembly elements that they never saved there.

## Reproduction

1. Build a library lens plus an assembly whose member lens is *not* in the library.
2. Save with `library_snapshot=True` and list library lens names.
3. Save again through the partial path (`demote=False`) and list names again.

Observed: `['library', 'asm']` → `['library', 'member', 'asm']`.

The structural proof is direct:

```python
import inspect
from openlens.database import DatabaseManager
src = inspect.getsource(DatabaseManager._save_lens_row)
assert "INSERT OR REPLACE" in src     # true
assert "is_library" not in src        # true
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/database.py:490` — `save_lens()` delegates to `_save_lens_row`.
- `openlens/database.py:499-520` — column list omits `is_library`; `INSERT OR REPLACE` deletes the old row and inserts a new one, so the omitted column takes its default `1`.
- `openlens/gui/storage.py:139-190` — `save_lenses(..., demote=library_snapshot or reconcile)` only passes `demote=True` for full saves; the default partial save relies on the DB layer preserving membership, which it does not.

## Expected behaviour

Saving a lens that is not in the library must not add it to the library. `is_library` must be preserved (or explicitly set) on every write.

## Suggested fix

Include `is_library` in the insert/update, reading the current value when the caller does not supply one (or use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET ...` and omit `is_library` from the update set). Add a regression test that saves an assembly-only lens through the partial path and asserts it is not listed by `load_all`/library queries.

nodes.title: fix(data-loss): keep the library membership when a lens row is rewritten
nodes.body:
## Description

Saving a lens row replaced it wholesale with `INSERT OR REPLACE`, and the
statement did not mention the `is_library` column. The column therefore fell
back to its schema default (`1`), so every write promoted the lens into the
global library.

A full save repaired it afterwards - the membership write that follows
demotes everything that is not in the library - but a *partial* save (the
default for the CLI and for the per-keystroke autosave) only promotes, so the
leak survived:

```
after the full save : ['A', 'Library']
after a partial save: ['A', 'Library', 'Member']
```

## What changed

- `openlens/database.py::_save_lens_row` now writes the `is_library` column:
  - a row that was loaded from the database keeps the membership it was
    loaded with;
  - an existing row keeps the membership it already has;
  - a new row takes the caller's default - a standalone lens is a library
    item (`1`), an assembly member is not (`0`).
- `openlens/database.py::_save_assembly_rows` passes `library_default=0` for
  the assembly's elements, so a lens that exists only inside an assembly is
  not a library item. The membership write that follows still has the final
  say and promotes the ids that really are in the library.
- `is_library` is excluded from the metadata blob: it is a column, not user
  metadata, and storing it twice let the blob shadow the column on the way
  back.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #602

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New tests in `tests/test_assembly_lens_library_membership.py`
(`TestPartialSaveKeepsLibraryMembership`), all failing before the fix:

- `test_a_partial_save_does_not_promote_an_assembly_member`
- `test_a_partial_save_keeps_a_shared_lens_in_the_library`
- `test_a_partial_save_keeps_a_standalone_lens_in_the_library`

Full local suite: `Ran 2583 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`, `black` clean,
`ruff` clean, `mypy` clean.

- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

title: bug(physics): 2D tracer ignores wavelength for tilted or decentered elements
body:
## Summary

When a 2D-traced element has non-zero decenter or tilt, `SystemRayTracer._trace_aligned_element()` rebuilds a local `LensRayTracer` without forwarding the wavelength. The element is then traced at its stored design index for every wavelength, so chromatic dispersion disappears for exactly the elements where alignment is being modelled.

## Impact

- Wrong physics: a tilted/decentered singlet returns identical focal results at C, d and F lines.
- 2D and 3D disagree: the 3D tracer applies the node transform but keeps the per-wavelength index.
- Any tolerance/ Monte Carlo run that tilts or decenters elements loses chromatic sensitivity in 2D.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.tracer_2d import SystemRayTracer
from openlens.constants import (WAVELENGTH_C_LINE, WAVELENGTH_D_LINE,
                                WAVELENGTH_F_LINE, NM_TO_MM)

def spot(tilt):
    s = OpticalSystem()
    s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=100.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
                    refractive_index=1.5168, thickness=5.0))
    s.elements[0].tilt_z = tilt
    out = []
    for wl in (WAVELENGTH_C_LINE, WAVELENGTH_D_LINE, WAVELENGTH_F_LINE):
        tr = SystemRayTracer(s, wavelength_nm=wl)
        r = tr.trace_parallel_rays(num_rays=5, wavelength_mm=wl * NM_TO_MM)
        out.append(round(r[-1].y, 6))
    return out

print("tilt 0    :", spot(0.0))
print("tilt 1e-6 :", spot(1e-6))
```

Output (this checkout):

```
tilt 0    : [-11.986917, -12.143562, -12.496574]
tilt 1e-6 : [-12.143661, -12.143661, -12.143661]
tilt 1e-3 : [-12.14369,  -12.14369,  -12.14369]
```

A 1e-6° tilt — physically indistinguishable from aligned — flattens the chromatic spread entirely. The same happens for `decenter_y`.

## Root cause

`openlens/tracer_2d.py:841`:

```python
local = LensRayTracer(lens, x_offset=0.0)
```

The surrounding `SystemRayTracer` has the wavelength (`self._wavelength_nm`) and the per-call ray carries `ray.wavelength_mm`, but neither is passed to the local tracer, so `LensRayTracer.__init__` falls back to `lens.refractive_index` (`openlens/tracer_2d.py:64-68`).

## Expected behaviour

The aligned path must refract at the same wavelength-dependent index as the centered fast path, so results are continuous as tilt/decenter → 0.

## Suggested fix

Pass the active wavelength when constructing the local tracer (`LensRayTracer(lens, x_offset=0.0, wavelength_nm=... )`), using the tracer's wavelength or converting `ray.wavelength_mm` to nm. Add a regression test asserting that C/F results differ for a tilted element and converge to the centered result as tilt → 0.

nodes.title: fix(physics): refract a tilted or decentered element at the traced wavelength
nodes.body:
## Description

The 2D tracer traces an element that has decenter or tilt in the element's
own frame: it rebuilds a local `LensRayTracer` for that purpose. That local
tracer was built without a wavelength, so it fell back to the lens's stored
design index and the element was traced at one index for every wavelength.

A 1e-6 degree tilt - physically indistinguishable from aligned - flattened the
chromatic spread to zero:

```
tilt 0    : [-11.986917, -12.143562, -12.496574]   chromatic spread = 0.509657
tilt 1e-6 : [-12.143661, -12.143661, -12.143661]   chromatic spread = 0.000000
```

The same happened for a decentered element.

## What changed

- `openlens/tracer_2d.py::_trace_aligned_element` now builds the local tracer
  with the tracer's wavelength, exactly like the per-element tracers the
  centered path uses (`_sync_tracers`). The aligned path therefore refracts
  at the same index as the centered one, and the result is continuous as
  tilt/decenter -> 0.
- The helper's `tracer` argument was unused (the local tracer needs
  `x_offset=0.0`, so the element's own tracer cannot be reused); it is gone.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #603

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New tests in `tests/test_system_tracer.py`
(`TestAlignedElementKeepsTheWavelength`), all failing before the fix:

- `test_a_centered_element_has_a_chromatic_spread` (the reference)
- `test_a_tilted_element_keeps_the_chromatic_spread`
- `test_a_decentered_element_keeps_the_chromatic_spread`
- `test_a_tilted_element_stays_close_to_the_centered_one`

Full local suite: `Ran 2590 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`, `black` clean,
`ruff` clean, `mypy` clean.

title: bug(physics): field curvature and distortion differ between Lens and one-element OpticalSystem
body:
## Summary

`AberrationsCalculator` reports `field_curvature` and `distortion` in different quantities depending on whether it was constructed with a `Lens` or a one-element `OpticalSystem`. The GUI labels the value as `mm (Petzval radius)`, so the system path is displaying a millimetre-scale focus shift under a radius label.

## Impact

- Same optical element, same field angle, radically different numbers:
  - `field_curvature`: `147.52` (Lens) vs `-1.213` (OpticalSystem)
  - `distortion`: `0.0` (Lens) vs `-0.0262` (OpticalSystem)
- Users comparing a single lens with the same lens inside a system see a ~100× discrepancy; automated targets/optimization that read one path get inconsistent values.
- The Lens path returns exactly `0.0` distortion "by construction", while the system path returns a traced non-zero value for the identical geometry.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.aberrations import AberrationsCalculator

kw = dict(radius_of_curvature_1=100.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
          refractive_index=1.5168, thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0)
lens = Lens(**kw)
s = OpticalSystem(); s.add_lens(Lens(**kw))

rl = AberrationsCalculator(lens).calculate_all_aberrations(field_angle_deg=5.0)
rs = AberrationsCalculator(s).calculate_all_aberrations(field_angle_deg=5.0)
print(rl["field_curvature"], rs["field_curvature"])
print(rl["distortion"], rs["distortion"])
```

Output:

```
field_curvature: Lens=147.52109839887657  System=-1.2132056985950896
distortion:      Lens=0.0                 System=-0.02617806300815217
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/aberrations.py:239-240` / `:449-462` — Lens path returns `field_curvature = n * f` (Petzval *radius*, mm) and hard-codes distortion to `0.0` as a third-order singlet result.
- `openlens/aberrations.py:341-359` — System path reads `analysis.calculate_field_curvature_distortion()`, whose `field_curvature` is a best-focus shift in mm and whose distortion is a traced percentage/ratio.
- `openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py` displays the key as `mm (Petzval radius)`, which only matches the Lens path.

## Expected behaviour

One documented quantity and unit per key, identical for Lens and the equivalent single-element system (within numerical tolerance). Either return Petzval radius in both paths or return focus shift in both, and label it accordingly.

## Suggested fix

Normalize both paths to the same definition/unit at the `AberrationsCalculator` boundary (e.g. always report Petzval radius and derive the system value from the traced sagitta/curvature data, or always report focus shift and convert the Lens value). Update the GUI label to the chosen quantity. Add a test asserting Lens and one-element OpticalSystem agree.

nodes.title: fix(physics): a lens and the one-element system report the same field numbers
nodes.body:
## Description

`AberrationsCalculator` reported `field_curvature` and `distortion` in
different quantities depending on how it was constructed. The lens path
returned the Petzval *radius* (`n * f`) and a distortion of exactly zero "by
construction"; the system path returned the traced tangential focus shift and
the traced distortion. The same optics, a hundred-fold different numbers,
under a GUI label (`mm (Petzval radius)`) that only fitted the analytic one:

```
field_curvature: Lens=147.52  System=-1.213
distortion     : Lens=0.0     System=-0.0262
```

Users comparing a single lens with the same lens inside a system saw a ~100x
discrepancy, and optimization targets that read one path got inconsistent
values.

## What changed

- `openlens/aberrations.py`: the lens path now measures field curvature and
  distortion with the same trace the system path uses (the lens is wrapped in
  a one-element system), so both report the same numbers: the tangential focus
  shift in mm and the traced distortion in %.
- The analytic singlet estimates stay available under names that say which
  quantity they are: `_calculate_petzval_radius` and
  `_calculate_third_order_distortion`. They are a different quantity, not a
  cheaper way of measuring the same one.
- The report's label becomes `mm (tangential focus shift)`, which is what the
  number is - and what the field-curvature panel already called it.
- On-axis distortion is now the trace's numerical residue (~1e-5 %) rather
  than exactly `0.0`; the two tests that pinned the exact zero allow for it.

title: bug: diffraction PSF/MTF crash on an empty optical system
body:
## Summary

`ImageQualityAnalyzer.calculate_psf(use_diffraction=True)` and `calculate_mtf(use_diffraction=True)` raise `ValueError: Invalid number of FFT data points (0) specified.` for an empty `OpticalSystem`. The code already has a degenerate-spacing guard, but it runs only *after* the FFT that crashes, and its early-return dict is missing the required `captured_fraction` key.

## Impact

- Crash on a legitimate state: a new/empty system is what the GUI shows before the user adds a lens; any analysis auto-refresh on that state raises.
- The MTF path has the same failure surface.
- The unreachable fallback returns a dict that violates `PSF_KEYS`, so even if it were reached, downstream consumers expecting `captured_fraction` would fail.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.analysis.psf_mtf import ImageQualityAnalyzer

a = ImageQualityAnalyzer(OpticalSystem())
for method in ("calculate_psf", "calculate_mtf"):
    try:
        getattr(a, method)(use_diffraction=True)
        print(method, "ok")
    except Exception as e:
        print(method, type(e).__name__, e)
```

Output:

```
calculate_psf ValueError: Invalid number of FFT data points (0) specified.
calculate_mtf ValueError: Invalid number of FFT data points (0) specified.
```

Traceback ends at:

- `openlens/analysis/psf_mtf.py:594` → `DiffractionPSFCalculator.calculate_psf(...)`
- `openlens/analysis/diffraction_psf.py:392` → `np.fft.fft2(...)`

## Root cause

- `openlens/analysis/psf_mtf.py:570-594` — the empty system produces a zero-size pupil wavefront; the FFT is attempted before any size check.
- `openlens/analysis/psf_mtf.py:615-640` — the `dx_psf <= 0` degenerate branch is below the FFT and therefore unreachable for this input. Its returned dict also omits `captured_fraction`, while `PSF_KEYS` at `:98` requires it.

## Expected behaviour

An empty/degenerate system returns a well-formed zero PSF/MTF result (all `PSF_KEYS` present) and logs a warning, instead of raising.

## Suggested fix

Validate the wavefront shape / pupil sample count before calling `DiffractionPSFCalculator.calculate_psf`, and route degenerate cases through `self._psf_result(...)` with `captured_fraction=0.0` so the key contract is satisfied. Add tests for `OpticalSystem()` with both diffraction flags.

nodes.title: fix(psf): return a well-formed zero result for an empty or degenerate system
nodes.body:
## Description

`ImageQualityAnalyzer.calculate_psf(use_diffraction=True)` and
`calculate_mtf(use_diffraction=True)` passed a zero-length pupil wavefront to
`np.fft` and raised `ValueError: Invalid number of FFT data points (0)`. The
geometric paths indexed `self.system.elements[0]` and raised `IndexError`.
The existing `dx_psf` degenerate branch sat below the FFT (unreachable for
this input) and its dict omitted `captured_fraction`, violating `PSF_KEYS`.

## What changed

- **`openlens/analysis/psf_mtf.py`**
  - An empty system returns a well-formed zero PSF (all `PSF_KEYS`,
    `captured_fraction=0.0`) and an empty MTF (`freq`, `mtf_tan`, `mtf_sag`)
    for both diffraction flags, with a warning.
  - `_wavefront_is_degenerate()` rejects a non-empty system whose pupil
    wavefront has too few samples before the FFT.
  - The `dx_psf` fallback now goes through `_psf_result()` and satisfies
    `PSF_KEYS`.
- **`tests/test_psf_empty_system.py`** (new)
  - PSF/MTF on `OpticalSystem()` with both `use_diffraction` values.
  - A forced empty pupil on a non-empty system is rejected before the FFT.
- **`tests/test_psf_resample_indices.py`**
  - The zero-wavelength test asserted the old incomplete key set; it now
    checks `captured_fraction` too.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #605

title: bug(physics): radius tolerances silently do nothing on plano surfaces
body:
## Summary

Radius tolerances are applied by adding the perturbation to the stored radius (`lens.radius_of_curvature_1 += value`). Plano surfaces are stored as `float("inf")`, and `inf + finite == inf`, so every radius perturbation on a flat surface is silently discarded. `_apply_value` still returns `True`, so the Monte Carlo reports a successful application and underestimates the yield impact of flat-surface tolerances.

## Impact

- Wrong tolerance results: a ±0.5 mm radius tolerance on a plano surface has exactly zero effect in every Monte Carlo trial.
- No warning or error: the caller believes the perturbation happened.
- Same mechanism applies to any `inf`-stored parameter and to the flat-surface `IRREGULARITY` path (`_radius_for_fringes` returns `None` for flat radii and is skipped).
- Flat surfaces are common (plano-convex, windows, prisms), so this is a routine design case.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.tolerancing import _apply_value, ToleranceType

s = OpticalSystem()
s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=float("inf"), radius_of_curvature_2=-50.0))
before = s.elements[0].lens.radius_of_curvature_1
applied = _apply_value(s, ToleranceType.RADIUS_1, 0, 0.5)
after = s.elements[0].lens.radius_of_curvature_1
print(applied, before, after, before != after)
```

Output:

```
apply RADIUS_1 +0.5 -> True | r1: inf -> inf | changed?: False
```

## Root cause

`openlens/tolerancing.py:363-366`:

```python
if param_type == ToleranceType.RADIUS_1:
    lens.radius_of_curvature_1 += value
elif param_type == ToleranceType.RADIUS_2:
    lens.radius_of_curvature_2 += value
```

Infinite arithmetic makes the update a no-op. `_apply_value` has no finiteness check and returns success.

## Expected behaviour

A plano surface under a radius tolerance becomes a long-radius surface (finite curvature perturbation), or the operand is reported as unsupported/inapplicable. It must not silently succeed without changing the design.

## Suggested fix

For `RADIUS_1`/`RADIUS_2`, perturb curvature (`1/R`) rather than radius: convert `inf` to a finite curvature (0), add `value` in the appropriate units, and convert back. Alternatively map a radius tolerance on a plano to a curvature tolerance and document it. Return `False`/warn when a perturbation cannot be represented. Add a test asserting a plano radius actually changes and the traced spot responds.

nodes.title: fix(physics): report a radius tolerance that cannot be applied
nodes.body:
## Description

A flat surface is stored as an infinite radius, and `inf + finite == inf`, so
a radius draw on a plano surface changed nothing while `_apply_value`
reported success:

```
apply RADIUS_1 +0.5 -> True | r1: inf -> inf | changed: False
```

The Monte Carlo therefore counted a tolerance that was never applied, and the
yield it reported was too good.

A radius tolerance does not apply to a flat surface, so it is now reported as
such instead of being silently swallowed.

## What changed

- `openlens/tolerancing.py::_apply_value` returns `False` for a radius draw on
  a flat surface - the existing "this operand addresses nothing" contract,
  already used for `FOCUS` and for out-of-range operands. A finite radius is
  perturbed exactly as before.
- `openlens/tolerancing.py::MonteCarloAnalyzer._apply_tolerances` collects the
  operands it could not apply; `run()` logs them once and reports them as
  `skipped_operands` in the statistics, so the yield is read with the
  omission in sight.
- `openlens/gui/tabs/tolerancing_tab.py` names the skipped operands in the
  Monte Carlo report.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #606

title: bug(physics): catalog material names do not resolve, causing missing dispersion and BK7 index jumps
body:
## Summary

Material names used by the UI/defaults (`"Fused Silica"`, `"Sapphire"`, `"Crown Glass"`, `"Flint Glass"`) do not match the catalog keys (`"FUSEDSILICA"`, etc.). `MaterialDatabase.get_material()` only uppercases and does not strip spaces, so catalog lookups miss. Two different failure modes result:

1. `Lens.refractive_index_at()` falls back to the stored index — no dispersion at all.
2. `Lens.update_refractive_index()` does not have that guard, so the database returns its BK7 fallback (`1.5168`) and the lens's index jumps from the correct value to BK7.

## Impact

- `Lens(material="Fused Silica", refractive_index=1.4585).refractive_index_at(486.1)` returns `1.4585` for every wavelength (no dispersion).
- Calling `update_refractive_index(486.1)` on the same lens changes the stored index to `1.5168` — a physically wrong jump to BK7.
- Same for other display-name materials, and for `"Sapphire"` / `"Crown Glass"` / `"Flint Glass"`.
- Chromatic analyses, ghost/Fresnel calculations, and tolerancing that call `update_refractive_index` silently use BK7 for these materials.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.material_database import MaterialDatabase

db = MaterialDatabase()
print(db.get_material("Fused Silica"))   # None
print(bool(db.get_material("FUSEDSILICA")))  # True

l = Lens(material="Fused Silica", refractive_index=1.4585)
print(l.refractive_index_at(486.1))      # 1.4585 (no dispersion)
l.update_refractive_index(486.1)
print(l.refractive_index)                # 1.5168 (BK7)
```

Output:

```
get_material('Fused Silica'): None
get_material('FUSEDSILICA'): True
n@486.1: 1.4585
after update_refractive_index(486.1): 1.5168
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/material_database.py:231` — catalog key is `"FUSEDSILICA"`; `DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES` at `openlens/constants.py:54-61` uses display names with spaces.
- `openlens/material_database.py:370-372` — `get_material` only uppercases, no space/punctuation normalization.
- `openlens/material_database.py:424-430` — unknown material returns `1.5168  # Default to BK7`.
- `openlens/lens.py:519+` — `refractive_index_at` guards with `db.get_material(...) is not None`, so it returns the stored index instead (no dispersion).
- `openlens/lens.py:477-515` — `update_refractive_index` has no such guard and assigns the BK7 fallback.

## Expected behaviour

A material name that appears in `DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES` resolves to the same catalog entry as its canonical key, with correct dispersion. An unknown material must never silently become BK7; it should keep the stored index or raise/warn.

## Suggested fix

Normalize catalog keys on both write and read (uppercase, collapse spaces/punctuation, e.g. `"Fused Silica" → "FUSEDSILICA"`), and/or add explicit aliases for the default-material names. Make `get_refractive_index` distinguish "material not found" from a real value and have `update_refractive_index` preserve the stored index on a miss (matching `refractive_index_at`). Add tests for every entry in `DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES`.

nodes.title: fix(physics): resolve catalog material names by spelling-insensitive lookup
nodes.body:
## Description

The lens model, the defaults and the UI call the catalog by display name -
`"Fused Silica"` - while the catalog is keyed by the glass name,
`"FUSEDSILICA"`. `MaterialDatabase.get_material()` only uppercased the name
before looking it up, so the lookup missed, and the miss was silent in two
different ways:

- `Lens.refractive_index_at()` fell back to the stored index, so a fused-silica
  lens had **one index for every wavelength** - no dispersion at all;
- `Lens.update_refractive_index()` stored `get_refractive_index()`'s BK7
  fallback, so moving the wavelength **turned the lens into BK7** (1.5168).

```
n(486.1) before: 1.4585 (stored, no dispersion)
n(486.1) after:  1.463128
update_refractive_index(486.1) before: 1.5168  # BK7
update_refractive_index(486.1) after:  1.463128
```

## What changed

- `openlens/material_database.py`: lookups try the exact uppercased key first,
  then a normalised alias index that ignores case, spaces and punctuation, so
  `"Fused Silica"`, `"fused-silica"`, `"FUSEDSILICA"`, `"N BK7"` and `"nbk7"`
  all find their glass. The alias index is built on the first miss and dropped
  by `clear_cache()`, which `add_material()` already calls, so a catalog edit
  can never leave a stale name behind.
- `MaterialDatabase.has_material(name)` reports a miss explicitly.
- `Lens.update_refractive_index()` asks `has_material()` first and keeps the
  lens's own index for a name the catalog does not hold, matching what
  `refractive_index_at()` already did. Names such as `"Sapphire"`,
  `"Crown Glass"` or `"Flint Glass"` have no catalog entry and therefore no
  dispersion to apply; they keep their stored index instead of quietly
  becoming 1.5168.
- `refractive_index_at()` and `_coating_substrate_index()` use the same
  `has_material()` test instead of spelling out `get_material(...) is not None`.

`get_refractive_index()` keeps its historical BK7 fallback for callers that
cannot handle a miss (the chromatic analyzer's per-wavelength lookups); its
docstring now says to ask `has_material()` first when the caller can.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #607

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_material_name_resolution.py` (all eight tests fail on
the unfixed code):

- `test_display_name_resolves_to_the_catalog_entry`
- `test_lookup_ignores_case_spacing_and_punctuation`
- `test_unknown_name_is_still_a_miss`
- `test_has_material_accepts_display_names`
- `test_added_materials_are_reachable_by_normalised_name`
- `test_display_name_lens_has_dispersion`
- `test_update_refractive_index_does_not_replace_the_glass`
- `test_unknown_material_keeps_its_stored_index`

Full local suite: `Ran 2655 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`.

- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

title: bug(io): STEP export emits quoted/dangling entity references and omits unit/context entities
body:
## Summary

The STEP writer now quotes raw string arguments, which exposed several long-standing reference bugs: entity references are emitted as quoted text (`'#unit_mm'`, `'#application_context'`, `'#47'`) instead of references, and the referenced entities (`LENGTH_UNIT`, `APPLICATION_CONTEXT`) are never written. The `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` call also passes a string where the uncertainty argument is expected. The result is syntactically invalid / semantically dangling STEP.

## Impact

- Exported `.step` files contain dangling references and missing units/context entities; a compliant CAD/STEP reader will reject or misread them.
- Length unit is implied only by the quoted `'#unit_mm'` string, and `LENGTH_UNIT`/`APPLICATION_CONTEXT` are absent entirely.
- The B-rep shape references the string `'#47'` rather than entity `#47`.

## Reproduction

```python
import tempfile
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.io.step_export import StepExporter

s = OpticalSystem(); s.add_lens(Lens())
p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".step")
StepExporter(s).export(p)
print(open(p).read())
```

Relevant output lines:

```
#7=UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(0.000001,'#unit_mm','distance_accuracy_value','confusion accuracy');
#8=PRODUCT_CONTEXT('part definition','#application_context','mechanical');
#48=ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION('lens_geom',('#47'),#9);
LENGTH_UNIT present: False
APPLICATION_CONTEXT present: False
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/io/step_export.py:332` — `"UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT"` args use the raw strings `"#unit_mm"` and an unset unit entity.
- `openlens/io/step_export.py:337` — `"PRODUCT_CONTEXT"` uses `"#application_context"`.
- `openlens/io/step_export.py:345` — `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` receives `["3D", "Geometric Context", 3]`; the third argument should be a plane-angle unit/uncertainty reference or `$`.
- `openlens/io/step_export.py:708` — `ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` puts `"#47"` in the items list as a string instead of a `StepRef`.
- The writer's `StepRef`/`StepEnum`/`StepDerived` markers exist (`:16-63`) but these call sites were never migrated.

## Expected behaviour

All entity references are written as `#n` tokens, and every referenced entity is emitted (`LENGTH_UNIT`, `APPLICATION_CONTEXT`, etc.) or replaced by `$` where optional. The file validates as STEP AP203/AP214.

## Suggested fix

Replace the raw strings with `StepRef` values, emit the missing `(LENGTH_UNIT() NAMED_UNIT(*) SI_UNIT(.MILLI.,.METRE.))` and `APPLICATION_CONTEXT(...)` entities, and pass `$`/a proper unit reference to `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT`. Add a test that parses the output and asserts every `#n` has a defining entity.

nodes.title: fix(io): write STEP entity references as references and define what they name
nodes.body:
## Description

The STEP writer learned to quote text properly, which exposed the call sites
that were passing pre-written syntax as strings. The exported file referred to
its length unit and its application context by name - `'#unit_mm'`,
`'#application_context'` - and the B-rep items as `('#47')`, so a reader
resolved none of them. The entities themselves were never written: the file
had **no `LENGTH_UNIT` and no `APPLICATION_CONTEXT` at all**, and its geometry
therefore had no unit.

```
before:
#7=UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(0.000001,'#unit_mm','distance_accuracy_value','confusion accuracy');
#48=ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION('lens_geom',('#47'),#9);
LENGTH_UNIT present: False
APPLICATION_CONTEXT present: False

after:
#6=(LENGTH_UNIT()NAMED_UNIT(*)SI_UNIT(.MILLI.,.METRE.));
#7=UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(LENGTH_MEASURE(1.E-06),#6,'distance_accuracy_value','confusion accuracy');
#8=APPLICATION_CONTEXT('core data for automotive mechanical design processes');
#9=PRODUCT_CONTEXT('part definition',#8,'mechanical');
#10=MECHANICAL_CONTEXT('3D Mechanical Context',#8);
#11=(GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT(3)GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT((#7))
     GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT((#6))REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT('',''));
#50=ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION('lens_geom',(#49),#11);
```

## What changed

- `openlens/io/step_export.py`:
  - the millimetre unit, the application context, the product/mechanical
    contexts and the uncertainty are now actually written, and referenced as
    `StepRef`s rather than text;
  - the geometric context is a complex entity carrying
    `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`,
    which is where a Part 21 file states what its numbers mean. Its third
    argument stays the dimension count (`3`) - the issue's suggestion that it
    should take the uncertainty reference is not what the schema says;
  - `MECHANICAL_CONTEXT` takes `(name, frame_of_reference)`; the old call
    passed three text arguments, none of them a reference;
  - the `ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` items are the solids'
    `StepRef`s, not interpolated `"#47"` strings;
  - `StepWriter.add_complex_entity()` writes multi-type instances
    (`#6=(LENGTH_UNIT()NAMED_UNIT(*)SI_UNIT(...));`) and `StepTyped` carries
    the typed parameter `LENGTH_MEASURE(1.E-06)` that the uncertainty's
    select requires. `add_entity`/`add_complex_entity` share one argument
    formatter.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #608

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_step_entity_references.py` parses the exported file the
way a Part 21 reader does: text literals are not references, and every
remaining `#n` must have a definition. Seven of its ten tests fail on the
unfixed code:

- `test_a_single_lens_has_no_dangling_references`
- `test_a_system_has_no_dangling_references`
- `test_no_reference_is_written_as_quoted_text`
- `test_the_brep_shape_lists_the_solids_as_references`
- `test_the_millimetre_length_unit_is_written`
- `test_the_application_context_is_written`
- `test_the_product_context_points_at_the_application_context`
- `test_the_geometric_context_assigns_units_and_uncertainty`
- `test_the_uncertainty_is_a_length_measure_of_the_unit`
- `test_a_lens_name_with_a_hash_is_not_a_reference`

Full local suite: `Ran 2663 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; the five existing STEP
suites (58 tests) still pass.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug: _update_positions desynchronizes flat elements from the nested assembly tree
body:
## Summary

After `_rebuild_from_tree()`, the flat `elements` list and the node tree agree on global positions. Calling `_update_positions()` then re-lays the flat list out from x=0 using only element thicknesses, ignoring the enclosing assembly's offset, while the tree keeps its global positions. 2D/ABCD tracing (flat list) and 3D tracing (tree) then analyse different geometry.

## Impact

- Nested assemblies (a doublet/group inserted at a non-zero position) are traced at different axial positions by the 2D and 3D paths.
- `_update_positions()` is called from the GUI assembly tab, tolerancing, desensitization, environmental analysis, and the optimizer — so the desync can be introduced by routine edits.
- Symptoms are confusing: spot/MTF results change depending on which tracer/analysis path runs, and saved flat positions no longer match the tree.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.optical_node import OpticalAssembly, OpticalElement
from openlens.vector3 import vec3

s = OpticalSystem()
asm = OpticalAssembly("doublet")
e1 = OpticalElement(Lens(), "e1"); e1.position = vec3(0, 0, 0)
e2 = OpticalElement(Lens(), "e2"); e2.position = vec3(20, 0, 0)
asm.add_child(e1); asm.add_child(e2)
s.add_assembly(asm, position=50.0)

print([e.position for e in s.elements])                 # [50.0, 70.0]
s._update_positions()
print([e.position for e in s.elements])                 # [0.0, 20.0]  <- flat
print([n.get_global_position().x for n, _ in s.root.get_flat_list()
       if getattr(n, "is_element", False)])             # [50.0, 70.0] <- tree
```

Output:

```
after add_assembly flat: [50.0, 70.0]
after add_assembly tree: [50.0, 70.0]
after _update_positions flat: [0.0, 20.0]
after _update_positions tree: [50.0, 70.0]
```

## Root cause

`openlens/optical_system.py:368-405` — `_update_positions()` starts `current_pos = 0.0` and assigns every flat element `element.position = current_pos`, accumulating only through `element.thickness`/`air_gaps`. It updates root-level nodes by model identity, but nested element nodes are deliberately left alone ("Nested positions belong to the enclosing assembly"). The flat positions therefore lose the assembly's `50 mm` translation.

## Expected behaviour

After `_update_positions()`, flat element positions equal the global positions from the tree, including assembly offsets; 2D and 3D tracers agree.

## Suggested fix

Derive flat positions from `self.root.get_flat_list()` (the same source `_rebuild_from_tree()` uses), or treat a node's global position as authoritative and only recompute gaps. Add a regression test that builds a nested assembly at x=50, calls `_update_positions()`, and asserts flat positions == tree global positions.

nodes.title: fix(physics): keep the assembly offset when the flat layout is rebuilt
nodes.body:
## Description

`_update_positions()` laid the flat `elements` list out from `x = 0`, using
only element thicknesses. For a system whose first element sits inside an
assembly inserted at 50 mm, that moved the flat list back to the origin while
the node tree kept its global positions:

```
after add_assembly        flat [50, 70]   tree [50, 70]
after _update_positions   flat [ 0, 20]   tree [50, 70]
```

The 2D/ABCD tracer reads the flat list and the 3D tracer reads the tree, so
the same system was analysed at two different axial placements. And
`_update_positions()` runs after routine edits - GUI gap changes,
tolerancing, desensitization, environmental analysis, the optimizer - so the
desync was easy to introduce and hard to explain: spot/MTF numbers changed
depending on which analysis path ran.

## What changed

- `openlens/optical_system.py`: the layout now starts at the global position
  of the first element instead of zero, so an assembly's offset is part of
  the rebuilt layout.
- Every element node follows the re-laid-out list: a root-level node takes the
  global position, a nested one the same position minus its assembly's global
  `x`. That keeps the two views equal after a nested thickness or gap edit
  too, which previously drifted apart (a nested element stayed put while the
  flat list moved on).
- Flat systems - the common case - are unchanged: their first element already
  sits at zero.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #609

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_update_positions_assembly_offset.py` (seven of its ten
tests fail on the unfixed code):

- `test_the_flat_positions_include_the_offset`
- `test_the_flat_list_and_the_tree_agree`
- `test_an_element_inside_an_assembly_is_not_moved_to_zero`
- `test_template_positions_survive_an_assembly_at_zero`
- `test_a_nested_thickness_change_moves_the_following_element`
- `test_a_gap_change_moves_the_following_element`
- `test_repeated_updates_are_stable`
- `test_a_root_child_after_the_assembly_keeps_its_distance`
- `test_a_flat_system_still_starts_at_zero`
- `test_a_thickness_change_still_moves_the_next_element`

`tests/test_update_positions_identity.py` follows the new contract: nested
nodes now move with the flat layout instead of being left behind (the old
test pinned the drift as a "pre-existing limit").

Full local suite: `Ran 2671 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`.

- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
