title: bug(io): Zemax import stores BK7 index for materials missing from DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES (e.g. F2)
body:
## Summary

`ZemaxSystemImporter._build_validated_lens()` resolves the refractive index from `DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES`, a small display-name table that lacks most catalog glasses (e.g. `F2`). For a missing material it falls back to BK7 (`1.5168`) and stores that on the lens without calling `update_refractive_index()`. The material name is preserved, so the lens later disperses like F2 while its stored index is BK7.

## Impact

- Imported designs have the wrong design index and therefore the wrong paraxial properties until some later operation happens to call `update_refractive_index`.
- Inconsistent state: `lens.refractive_index == 1.5168` but `lens.refractive_index_at(486.1) == 1.6321`.
- Round-trip of any glass outside the six default names (F2, N-BK7, SF2, ...) corrupts the index.
- Silently changes the optics; no warning.

## Reproduction

```python
import tempfile
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.export_formats import ZemaxSystemExporter, ZemaxSystemImporter

s = OpticalSystem()
s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=50.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-50.0,
                thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0, material="F2",
                refractive_index=1.6200))
p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".zmx")
ZemaxSystemExporter.export_system(s, p)
lens = ZemaxSystemImporter.import_system(p).elements[0].lens
print(lens.material, lens.refractive_index, lens.refractive_index_at(486.1))
```

Output:

```
material: F2 | stored n: 1.5168 | n@486.1: 1.632086765232914
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/export_formats.py:911-927` — the importer builds a name→index map from `DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES` and uses it when the glass is not found in that table, defaulting to BK7.
- `openlens/constants.py:54-61` — `DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES` has only `BK7`, `Fused Silica`, `SF11`, `Crown Glass`, `Flint Glass`, `Sapphire`.
- The constructed `Lens` is never refreshed from `MaterialDatabase` (no `update_refractive_index()` call).

## Expected behaviour

The imported lens's stored `refractive_index` matches the catalog index for the imported glass at the design wavelength (or at least matches `refractive_index_at()`), for any glass the catalog knows.

## Suggested fix

Resolve the index through `MaterialDatabase.get_refractive_index(material, wavelength)` (falling back to `DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES` only when the catalog misses), or construct the lens with a placeholder and call `update_refractive_index()` before returning. Warn on unresolvable glass. Add a round-trip test for `F2` and another non-default catalog glass.

nodes.title: fix(io): resolve the Zemax glass in the catalog, not in a six-glass table
nodes.body:
## Description

A `.zmx` file names its glass and says nothing about its index, so the index
has to come from the catalog. `ZemaxSystemImporter` looked only in
`DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES` - six display names - and stored BK7 for
everything else. A lens imported with `GLAS F2` kept the name, so
`refractive_index_at()` dispersed like F2, while its stored index was BK7's:

```
material: F2 | stored n: 1.5168 | n@486.1: 1.6321
```

The paraxial properties came from one glass and the traced ones from another,
and any glass outside the six (`F2`, `N-BK7`, `SF2`, ...) round-tripped
corrupted - silently.

## What changed

- `openlens/export_formats.py`: new `_material_design_index()` resolves the
  glass through `MaterialDatabase` at the d-line. The catalog is asked first
  (and accepts any case, spacing or punctuation after #607); the static table
  is the fallback for names no catalog holds, then BK7. An unreadable catalog
  degrades to the static table instead of failing the import.
- `_build_validated_lens()` uses it, so the stored `refractive_index` agrees
  with `refractive_index_at()` - one glass for the paraxial maths and the
  trace.
- Three assertions in `tests/test_zemax_roundtrip.py` move from `places=7`
  (the rounded 1.4585 of the static table) to `places=3`: the stored index is
  now the catalog's Sellmeier value, 1.458462, which is what makes it agree
  with the dispersion.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #610

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_zemax_material_index.py` (three of its five tests fail
on the unfixed code; the two that pass cover names the old table happened to
hold):

- `test_a_catalog_glass_keeps_its_index` - F2 stores 1.6200, not 1.5168
- `test_the_stored_index_agrees_with_the_dispersion`
- `test_another_non_default_glass_round_trips` - SF11 stores 1.7847, not 1.78
- `test_a_display_name_glass_round_trips` - `"Fused Silica"`
- `test_an_unknown_glass_falls_back_to_bk7` - custom glasses keep the old default

Full local suite: `Ran 2676 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; the existing Zemax
suites (47 tests) pass.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(physics): BeamSynthesisPropagator defaults to total_length+50 instead of paraxial focus
body:
## Summary

`BeamSynthesisPropagator.propagate_to_image(image_plane_x=None)` documents/assumes a paraxial image plane but hard-codes `system.get_total_length() + 50`. For a typical system this is far from focus, so the synthesized image is evaluated in a defocused plane.

## Impact

- Beam-synthesis PSF/spot results are computed at an arbitrary plane 50 mm past the last surface, not at focus.
- For the default biconvex singlet, BFL ≈ 95.9 mm while the chosen plane is 55 mm — a ~40 mm defocus.
- Any comparison with diffraction PSF/MTF (which use the Gaussian focus) is invalid unless the caller explicitly passes `image_plane_x`.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem

s = OpticalSystem()
s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=100.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
                refractive_index=1.5168, thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0))
print("total_length:", s.get_total_length())          # 5.0
print("BFL:", s.calculate_back_focal_length())        # 95.918...
print("default plane:", s.get_total_length() + 50)    # 55.0
```

The source confirms the default:

```
openlens/analysis/beam_synthesis.py:260-262
    if image_plane_x is None:
        # Default to paraxial focus (approx)
        image_plane_x = self.system.get_total_length() + 50
```

## Root cause

`openlens/analysis/beam_synthesis.py:260-262` — the comment claims paraxial focus, but the value is a fixed offset past the last vertex. The system exposes `calculate_back_focal_length()` (`openlens/optical_system.py:771`), which is the observable focus.

## Expected behaviour

With `image_plane_x=None`, the detector is placed at the system's paraxial focus (back focal length from the last surface), falling back to a documented finite plane only for afocal systems.

## Suggested fix

Use `system.calculate_back_focal_length()` (plus the last element's position/thickness as needed) and handle `None`/non-finite values explicitly. Add a test that the default plane equals the paraxial focus for a singlet and a doublet.

nodes.title: fix(physics): place the beam-synthesis detector at the paraxial focus
nodes.body:
## Description

`BeamSynthesisPropagator.propagate_to_image(image_plane_x=None)` documented a
paraxial image plane and then placed the detector at `get_total_length() + 50`
- an arbitrary plane 50 mm past the last vertex.

For the default biconvex singlet (BFL ≈ 95.9 mm, last vertex at 5 mm) that is
55 mm instead of ≈ 101 mm: a ≈ 46 mm defocus, so the synthesized PSF was
evaluated far from focus and could not be compared with the diffraction
PSF/MTF, which use the Gaussian focus.

```
total_length: 5.0
BFL:          95.918...
old plane:    55.0
new plane:    ≈101.0  (paraxial focus)
```

## What changed

- `openlens/analysis/beam_synthesis.py`: the default plane now comes from
  `find_paraxial_focus()` - the same shared focus search `diffraction_psf.py`
  uses - so both analyses of one system are measured at the same plane.
- A system with no focus to find (an afocal plate, an untraceable exit ray)
  falls back to `get_total_length() +
  BeamSynthesisPropagator.DEFAULT_IMAGE_PLANE_PAST_LAST_SURFACE` (50 mm, the
  old behaviour) and logs a warning saying so.
- An explicit `image_plane_x` is still used verbatim.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #611

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_beam_synthesis_focus.py` (four of its five tests fail on
the unfixed code; the fifth pins the afocal fallback, which the old code made
for every system):

- `test_the_default_is_the_paraxial_focus`
- `test_the_default_is_not_fifty_millimetres_past_the_last_vertex`
- `test_the_default_agrees_with_the_paraxial_back_focal_length`
- `test_an_afocal_system_uses_the_documented_fallback`
- `test_the_default_map_equals_the_map_at_the_focus` - the public API: the
  default intensity map equals the one at an explicitly passed focus

Full local suite: `Ran 2686 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; the existing beam
synthesis and PSF suites (65 tests) pass.

title: bug(physics): ImageSimulator image distance ignores wavelength; blank-image Nyquist ratio is nan
body:
## Summary

`ImageSimulator._calculate_image_distance(object_distance, wavelength)` accepts a wavelength but calls `self._system_focal_length()`, which always evaluates the design index. The class already has a correct wavelength-aware helper, `_system_focal_length_at(wavelength)`, which is never used here. Image distance, magnification, and vignetting are therefore identical at every wavelength.

## Impact

- Chromatic focal shift is absent from simulated images: C-line and F-line image distances are bit-identical despite a ~1.5 mm EFL difference for a BK7 singlet.
- `magnification = -image_distance / object_distance` and `_apply_vignetting(image_distance_mm=...)` inherit the wrong plane.
- A separate but related numerical bug: `_calculate_nyquist_spectral_ratio` divides by the DC bin, so a blank image returns `nan` with a `RuntimeWarning`.

## Reproduction

```python
import numpy as np
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.image_simulator import ImageSimulator
from openlens.constants import WAVELENGTH_C_LINE, WAVELENGTH_F_LINE

s = OpticalSystem()
s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=100.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
                refractive_index=1.5168, thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0))
sim = ImageSimulator(s)
img = np.zeros((32, 32))
for wl in (WAVELENGTH_C_LINE, WAVELENGTH_F_LINE):
    r = sim.simulate_image(img, object_distance=500.0, wavelength=wl)
    print(wl, r["image_distance"])
print("focal @C/F:", sim._system_focal_length_at(WAVELENGTH_C_LINE),
      sim._system_focal_length_at(WAVELENGTH_F_LINE))
print("blank nyquist:", sim._calculate_nyquist_spectral_ratio(np.zeros((64, 64))))
```

Output:

```
image_distance @C: 121.242121 | @F: 121.242121 | differ: False
_system_focal_length_at(C): 98.047981
_system_focal_length_at(F): 96.544197
blank image ratio: nan | warnings: ['invalid value encountered in scalar divide']
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/image_simulator.py:277-279` — `f = self._system_focal_length()` ignores the `wavelength` argument; the wavelength-aware `_system_focal_length_at` exists at `:257`.
- `openlens/image_simulator.py:617` — `ratio = magnitude[mask].mean() / magnitude[cy, cx]`; for a blank image the DC bin is 0, producing 0/0.

## Expected behaviour

Image distance and all derived quantities use the index at the requested wavelength, so C/F produce different image planes. The Nyquist ratio returns a finite value (e.g. `0.0`) for a blank image without emitting a warning.

## Suggested fix

Replace `self._system_focal_length()` with `self._system_focal_length_at(wavelength)` in `_calculate_image_distance`. Guard the DC denominator in `_calculate_nyquist_spectral_ratio` (`if dc <= 0: return 0.0`). Add tests for chromatic image distance and the blank-image metric.

nodes.title: fix(physics): place the simulated image at the plane for its wavelength
nodes.body:
## Description

`ImageSimulator._calculate_image_distance(object_distance, wavelength)`
accepted a wavelength and then called `_system_focal_length()`, which always
measures the design index. The class already had a correct wavelength-aware
helper, `_system_focal_length_at(wavelength)`, two methods above - it was
never used here.

The result: the image distance, the magnification and the vignetting derived
from it were identical at every wavelength. For the test singlet the C and F
lines have a ≈1.5 mm EFL difference:

```
image_distance @C: 121.24 | @F: 121.24 | differ: False
_system_focal_length_at(C): 98.05
_system_focal_length_at(F): 96.54
```

A second, adjacent bug: `_calculate_nyquist_spectral_ratio` divided the ring
energy by the DC bin, so a blank image evaluated `0/0` and returned `nan`
with a `RuntimeWarning`.

## What changed

- **`openlens/image_simulator.py`** - `_calculate_image_distance` now uses
  `_system_focal_length_at(wavelength)`, which sets each lens to the index
  for the requested wavelength, measures, and restores the design indices on
  the way out (the same discipline the wavefront sensor uses). The index
  policy is unchanged: a catalog material resolves through the catalog, a
  custom glass keeps its stored index.
- **`_calculate_nyquist_spectral_ratio`** - a DC bin with no energy has
  nothing to normalise against, so the ratio is `0.0` instead of `nan`, and
  no warning is emitted. A normal image is unchanged.
- **`tests/test_image_simulator_api.py`** - the fixture passes `n=1.5` with
  the default `"BK7"` material. Now that the simulator honours the
  wavelength, the catalog index for BK7 at the d-line silently replaced that
  1.5. The fixture uses `material="Custom"`, which is what it always meant.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #612

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New module `tests/test_image_simulator_wavelength.py` - all six tests fail on
the unfixed code:

- `test_the_red_and_blue_image_planes_differ`
- `test_the_image_distance_is_the_lens_equation_at_that_wavelength` (C, d, F)
- `test_the_design_index_is_restored_after_the_measurement`
- `test_simulate_image_reports_the_chromatic_plane`
- `test_a_blank_image_scores_zero_without_a_warning`
- `test_a_delta_image_still_scores_above_zero`

Full local suite: `Ran 2697 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; the five image
simulator suites (54 tests) pass.

title: bug(physics): ghost analysis ignores element decenter and tilt
body:
## Summary

`GhostAnalyzer._interact()` constructs each surface tracer as `LensRayTracer3D(surf["lens"], x_offset=surf["element"].position)`, discarding the element's decenter and tilt. Ghost paths for any decentered/tilted system are traced as if the element were on-axis, even though the rest of the 3D tracer honours the node transform.

## Impact

- Ghost positions and intensities are wrong (often identical to the centered system) whenever an element is decentered or tilted.
- Misleading stray-light/flare estimates exactly for the tilted/decentered configurations where ghosts matter most.
- The analyzer's own 3D tracer supports full transforms, so the omission is accidental, not a documented limitation.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.analysis.ghost import GhostAnalyzer

def signature(decenter, tilt=0.0):
    s = OpticalSystem()
    s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=100.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
                    refractive_index=1.5168, thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0))
    s.elements[0].decenter_y = decenter
    s.elements[0].tilt_z = tilt
    return [(p.reflection_1_index, p.reflection_2_index, round(p.intensity, 8),
             [(round(r.path[-1].x, 4), round(r.path[-1].y, 4)) for r in p.rays])
            for p in GhostAnalyzer(s).trace_ghosts(num_rays=3)]

print("centered == decentered 10mm:", signature(0.0) == signature(10.0))
print("centered == tilted 2deg   :", signature(0.0) == signature(0.0, 2.0))
```

Output:

```
centered == decentered 10mm: True
centered == tilted 2deg   : True
```

## Root cause

`openlens/analysis/ghost.py:188-199`:

```python
tracer = LensRayTracer3D(surf["lens"], x_offset=surf["element"].position)
```

Only the axial position is forwarded; `decenter_y`/`decenter_z` and `tilt_x`/`tilt_y`/`tilt_z` are ignored.

## Expected behaviour

Ghost rays use the element's full global transform, matching `SystemRayTracer3D` (which builds tracers from `node.get_global_transform()`).

## Suggested fix

Build the tracer from the element's node global transform (like `SystemRayTracer3D._prepare`), or construct a transform from `position` + decenter/tilt. Add a test asserting a decentered system produces different ghost paths than the centered one.

nodes.title: fix(physics): trace ghost paths through the element's real transform
nodes.body:
## Description

`GhostAnalyzer._interact()` constructed each surface tracer as

```python
LensRayTracer3D(surf["lens"], x_offset=surf["element"].position)
```

forwarding only the axial position and discarding the element's decenter and
tilt. Ghost paths for a decentered or tilted system were therefore traced as
if every element were on-axis - and the analyzer's own 3D tracer already
supports full transforms, so the omission was accidental.

```
centered == decentered 10mm: True
centered == tilted 2deg   : True
```

## What changed

- **`openlens/analysis/ghost.py`** - the surface list now carries the
  element node's global transform, the same value `SystemRayTracer3D` builds
  its tracers from, and `_interact` constructs `LensRayTracer3D` with it.
- The node walk is the one that produced `system.elements`; if the counts
  ever disagree (a hand-edited flat list), the analyzer logs a warning and
  falls back to the old axial-position behaviour rather than pairing
  elements with the wrong nodes.
- Centered systems trace exactly as before: the transform for an on-axis
  element is the same pure X translation that `x_offset` produced.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #613

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_ghost_alignment.py` - three of its four tests fail on
the unfixed code (the fourth pins the unchanged centered result):

- `test_decentring_the_element_moves_the_ghost_paths`
- `test_tilting_the_element_moves_the_ghost_paths`
- `test_a_decentred_element_reflects_at_its_own_height`
- `test_a_centered_system_is_still_traced_symmetrically`

The tests use `OpticalSystem.set_element_alignment()`, which updates the node
tree and the flat record together - the path the GUI's alignment controls
take. The centered ghost signature is unchanged to the last printed digit.

Full local suite: `Ran 2695 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; the ghost analysis
suites (13 tests) pass.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(performance): SystemRayTracer3D cache is never invalidated on position changes
body:
## Summary

`SystemRayTracer3D` caches the prepared scene and explicitly requires callers to call `invalidate()` after position/structure changes, but there are **zero production call sites**. Long-lived tracer owners (`InteractiveRayTracer`, `SpotDiagram`, `GeometricAnalyzer`, `DiffractionPSFCalculator`, `BeamSynthesisPropagator`, `ParaxialAnalyzer`) keep the stale scene and silently trace the old geometry after an element is moved.

## Impact

- Moving an element in the assembly editor and re-running an analysis can return results for the previous position, with no error.
- Only lens-parameter changes are auto-detected (`_scene_is_current` checks `tracer.matches(lens)`); node positions/transforms are not.
- The cache tests themselves document the hazard: `tests/test_tracer3d_batch_cache.py:180` — "A moved element is only visible after `invalidate()`".
- All production uses listed above are per-instance and never invalidate.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.tracer_3d import SystemRayTracer3D
from openlens.ray import Ray3D
from openlens.vector3 import vec3

s = OpticalSystem()
s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=100.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
                refractive_index=1.5168, thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0))
tracer = SystemRayTracer3D(s)
r1 = Ray3D(vec3(-10, 5, 0), vec3(1, 0, 0)); tracer.trace_ray(r1)
print("before:", r1.path[-1])

s.root.children[0].position = vec3(20, 0, 0)   # what the assembly editor does
r2 = Ray3D(vec3(-10, 5, 0), vec3(1, 0, 0)); tracer.trace_ray(r2)
print("after (no invalidate):", r2.path[-1])      # unchanged

tracer.invalidate()
r3 = Ray3D(vec3(-10, 5, 0), vec3(1, 0, 0)); tracer.trace_ray(r3)
print("after invalidate:", r3.path[-1])           # moved
```

Output:

```
before move: (54.8129, 2.3506, 0.0)
after move (no invalidate): (54.8129, 2.3506, 0.0) | stale: True
after invalidate: (74.8129, 2.3506, 0.0)
```

`grep -rn ".invalidate()" openlens/ tests/` finds only test uses; `openlens/` has none.

## Root cause

- `openlens/tracer_3d.py:699-750` — `invalidate()` exists but is never called by the library.
- `openlens/tracer_3d.py:722-724` — `_scene_is_current()` only compares lens state, not transforms.
- Owners such as `openlens/analysis/spot_diagram.py:22` store a tracer for the analyzer's lifetime.

## Expected behaviour

Position/structure edits are detected automatically on the next trace, or every long-lived owner invalidates the tracer when the system changes.

## Suggested fix

Cheapest robust option: include a cheap scene revision (count + positions/transforms) in `_scene_is_current`, or expose `invalidate()` up through the analyzers and call it from the GUI/analysis refresh path. Add an integration test that moves a node between two `SpotDiagram.trace_spot()` calls and asserts the result changes.

nodes.title: fix(tracer): detect moved elements instead of tracing a stale scene
nodes.body:
## Description

`SystemRayTracer3D` caches the prepared scene (each element's transform and
`LensRayTracer3D`) and relied on callers to call `invalidate()` after a
position or structure change. There were no production call sites: long-lived
tracer owners (`InteractiveRayTracer`, `SpotDiagram`, `GeometricAnalyzer`,
`DiffractionPSFCalculator`, `BeamSynthesisPropagator`, `ParaxialAnalyzer`)
kept the stale scene and silently traced the old geometry after an element was
moved. Only lens-parameter changes were auto-detected.

## What changed

- **`openlens/tracer_3d.py`**
  - `_scene_signature()` describes the scene cheaply: element-node identities,
    local positions/rotations, element-model identities, air-gap stations and
    the aperture stop. It reads attributes only — no matrix is built and no
    global transform is recomputed — so it is cheap enough to run on every ray.
  - `_scene_is_current()` compares that signature as well as the existing
    per-lens `matches()` check. A moved/added element, a replaced element
    model, a re-stationed gap or a changed stop rebuilds the scene
    automatically.
  - `invalidate()` is kept as a forced rebuild, and the docstrings no longer
    claim that position changes require it.
- **`tests/test_tracer3d_batch_cache.py`**
  - Moved node and moved flat element are picked up without `invalidate()`.
  - An added element rebuilds the scene.
  - An integration test moves a node between two `SpotDiagram.trace_spot()`
    calls and asserts the result changes and matches a fresh diagram.
  - The existing "scene walk does not scale with the batch" test still passes:
    the signature does not call `get_global_transform()` per ray.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #614

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2824 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

The issue's reproduction now reports the moved position (`74.81…` instead of
the stale `54.81…`) without calling `invalidate()`.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

nodes.title: fix(performance): let cached tracers see layout edits
nodes.body:
SystemRayTracer3D prepares each element's tracer and transform once and reuses them for the batch. The batch validated only the lens state it snapshotted, so after a layout edit - moving an element, tilting it, or adding an element - a long-lived tracer silently kept tracing the old geometry. invalidate() existed for this, but no production caller used it; the cache's own test documented the hazard.

Re-walking the node tree per ray is exactly what the cache exists to avoid (the batch cache test pins that the walk must not scale with the ray count), so the geometry is tracked as a number instead:

- OpticalSystem keeps a geometry revision, bumped by _update_positions and _rebuild_from_tree (every model edit funnels through them) and by assigning a node's position or rotation (OpticalNode now notifies its owning system).
- SystemRayTracer3D records the revision with the prepared scene and compares it - plus the flat element stations, which cover duck-typed systems without a node tree - on every trace. A mismatch rebuilds the scene once.

invalidate() is still available and still forces an immediate rebuild.

Closes #614

## Merge resolution with master

`#614` was already fixed on master by #729, which compares a per-ray scene signature. This branch keeps that signature as the fallback for duck-typed systems and uses its constant-time geometry revision for `OpticalSystem`:

- every model edit bumps the revision (`_update_positions`, `_rebuild_from_tree`, node position/rotation assignment, and aperture-stop changes);
- `_scene_is_current` compares the revision when present, otherwise the signature;
- `invalidate()` still forces an immediate rebuild.

The conflicted test file keeps both sets of regression tests, plus one for aperture-stop edits.

title: bug: InverseSensitivityAnalyzer ignores the criterion argument
body:
## Summary

`InverseSensitivityAnalyzer.calculate_sensitivities(criterion=...)` accepts a `criterion` argument but never reads it. It always traces `SpotDiagram` and uses `rms_radius`, so callers asking for any other metric silently receive RMS-spot sensitivities. This is inconsistent with `MonteCarloAnalyzer.run`, which validates `criterion` and raises on unsupported values.

## Impact

- Silent wrong-metric results: a caller passing `criterion="mtf"` (or anything else) gets RMS spot sensitivities with no warning.
- Inverse tolerance budgeting then allocates tolerances against the wrong performance metric.
- Inconsistent API: Monte Carlo rejects unsupported criteria; inverse sensitivity silently ignores the argument.

## Reproduction

```python
import inspect
from openlens.tolerancing import InverseSensitivityAnalyzer

src = inspect.getsource(InverseSensitivityAnalyzer.calculate_sensitivities)
body = src.split('"""', 2)[-1]
print("criterion referenced in body:", "criterion" in body)   # False
print("only rms_radius used:", 'res["rms_radius"]' in body)     # True
```

Output:

```
criterion referenced in body: False
only rms_radius used: True
```

## Root cause

`openlens/tolerancing.py:689-704` — the method signature declares `criterion: str = "rms_spot_radius"`, but the body constructs `SpotDiagram` and reads `res_nom["rms_radius"]` unconditionally. Compare `MonteCarloAnalyzer.run` at `:566-593`, which defines `SUPPORTED_CRITERIA` and raises `ValueError` for unsupported values.

## Expected behaviour

Either implement the requested criterion (or the supported subset) or validate it the same way `MonteCarloAnalyzer` does and raise `ValueError` for unsupported metrics. The parameter must not be silently ignored.

## Suggested fix

Add the same `SUPPORTED_CRITERIA` check at the top of `calculate_sensitivities` (reusing the Monte Carlo constant), and dispatch to the matching metric or raise. Document the supported set in the docstring. Add tests for the supported criterion and for an unsupported one raising.

nodes.title: fix(tolerancing): honour the inverse-sensitivity criterion argument
nodes.body:
## Description

`InverseSensitivityAnalyzer.calculate_sensitivities(criterion=...)`
declared a `criterion` argument and never read it. Every call - including
`optimize_limits()` - traced a `SpotDiagram` and read `rms_radius`
unconditionally:

```
criterion referenced in body: False
only rms_radius used: True
```

A caller passing `criterion="mtf"` (or anything else) silently received
RMS-spot sensitivities, and inverse tolerance budgeting then allocated
tolerances against the wrong performance measure. `MonteCarloAnalyzer`, in
the same module, already rejects an unimplemented criterion with a
`ValueError`.

## What changed

- **`openlens/tolerancing.py`** - `InverseSensitivityAnalyzer` now shares
  `MonteCarloAnalyzer.SUPPORTED_CRITERIA` and validates the argument at the
  top of `calculate_sensitivities()`, before any system state is captured or
  traced. An unsupported name raises `ValueError` naming the supported set.
- The docstring documents the argument, the supported value, and the raise.
- Only `"rms_spot_radius"` is implemented today; the validation is what makes
  the parameter meaningful and keeps the two tolerance tools consistent.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #615

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`

- `test_the_supported_set_is_the_monte_carlo_set`

- `test_the_supported_criterion_is_measured`

title: bug: mechanical designer ignores lens thickness and air gaps
body:
## Summary

`MechanicalDesigner` ignores the real optical geometry when sizing lens cells and spacers:

- `design_lens_cells()` estimates cell length from `lens.center_thickness`, but `Lens` only exposes `thickness`. The attribute never exists, so **every** cell gets the 10.0 mm fallback.
- `calculate_spacers()` looks for a non-existent `optical_system.element_spacing`; for a real `OpticalSystem` it falls back to `[10.0] * (n-1)` and never reads `system.air_gaps`.

The generated mechanical stack therefore has no relation to the optical stack length, air gaps, or lens thicknesses.

## Impact

- A 30 mm-thick element gets a 10 mm cell; a 20 mm air gap gets a 10 mm spacer.
- `calculate_total_length()`, `generate_bom()`, `suggest_housing()`, and the STEP housing export inherit the wrong dimensions.
- Clearance and assembly checks run against a mechanical model that cannot contain the actual lenses.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.mechanical_designer import MechanicalDesigner

s = OpticalSystem()
s.add_lens(Lens(thickness=30.0, diameter=25.0))
s.add_lens(Lens(thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0), air_gap_before=20.0)
print("Lens has thickness:", hasattr(s.elements[0].lens, "thickness"))
print("Lens has center_thickness:", hasattr(s.elements[0].lens, "center_thickness"))
print("air gaps:", [(g.position, g.thickness) for g in s.air_gaps])

d = MechanicalDesigner(s)
print("cell lengths:", [c.length for c in d.design_lens_cells()])
print("spacers:", [sp.thickness for sp in d.calculate_spacers()])
print("mechanical length:", d.calculate_total_length())
print("optical length:", s.get_total_length())
```

Observed:

```
Lens has thickness: True | has center_thickness: False
air gaps: [(30.0, 20.0)]
cell lengths: [10.0, 10.0]
spacers: [10.0]
total mechanical length: 30.0
optical total length: 55.0
```

Expected: cell lengths reflecting 30 mm and 5 mm elements (plus a documented margin), a spacer of the actual 20 mm air gap, and a mechanical length consistent with the 55 mm optical stack.

## Root cause

- `openlens/mechanical_designer.py:161-164` — `if hasattr(lens, "center_thickness")` is always false for `Lens`, so `length = 10.0`.
- `openlens/mechanical_designer.py:194-199` — `hasattr(self.optical_system, "element_spacing")` is false for `OpticalSystem`; the fallback ignores `self.optical_system.air_gaps`.
- `openlens/mechanical_designer.py:248-258` — totals sum the fabricated cell/spacer values.

## Expected behaviour

Cell length derives from the actual `lens.thickness` (or edge thickness where appropriate, with an explicit margin), and each spacer thickness equals the corresponding `air_gaps[i].thickness` unless the caller supplies `target_spacing`. The mechanical total should reconcile with the optical total within the documented margins.

## Suggested fix

Use `lens.thickness` for cell length (and subtract the surface sags if edge thickness is wanted). Default `target_spacing` from `[gap.thickness for gap in system.air_gaps]`. Add a test with two different-thickness lenses and a non-default air gap asserting the generated cells/spacers match.

nodes.title: fix(mechanical): size cells and spacers from the optical geometry
nodes.body:
## Description

`MechanicalDesigner` sized the housing from attributes the model had never
exposed:

- `design_lens_cells()` looked for `lens.center_thickness`, which `Lens`
  does not have, so **every** cell got the 10 mm fallback.
- `calculate_spacers()` looked for `system.element_spacing`, which
  `OpticalSystem` does not have, so every spacer was a fabricated 10 mm.

The mechanical stack therefore had no relation to the optical one:

```
air gaps: [(30.0, 20.0)]
cell lengths: [10.0, 10.0]
spacers: [10.0]
total mechanical length: 30.0
optical total length: 55.0
```

`calculate_total_length()`, `generate_bom()`, `suggest_housing()` and the
STEP housing export all inherited the wrong dimensions.

## What changed

- **`openlens/mechanical_designer.py`** - cell length comes from the
  element's own thickness (`Lens.thickness`; a duck-typed `center_thickness`
  is still honoured) plus the documented `CELL_MARGIN_MM = 5.0`. A lens-like
  object exposing neither warns and keeps the 10 mm fallback.
- Spacers default to the system's `air_gaps` in axial order. An explicit
  `target_spacing` still wins, and the old `element_spacing` / 10 mm
  fallbacks remain for duck-typed targets that expose them.
- `calculate_total_length()` documents that the mechanical total exceeds the
  optical stack by one margin per element.

With the report's system the cells are now 35 mm and 10 mm, the spacer is the
actual 20 mm, and the total reconciles: 55 mm optical + 2 × 5 mm margins.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #616

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_mechanical_designer_geometry.py` - four of its six
tests fail on the unfixed code (the other two pin that an explicit
`target_spacing` and a duck-typed `element_spacing` still behave):

- `test_cell_length_follows_the_element_thickness`
- `test_spacers_follow_the_air_gaps`
- `test_the_total_reconciles_with_the_optical_stack`
- `test_the_reported_reproduction`

Full local suite: `Ran 2713 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; the mechanical and
advanced-feature suites (73 tests) pass.

- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

title: bug(data-loss): custom refractive-index edits are never autosaved
body:
## Summary

Editing the refractive index of a `Custom` lens updates the in-memory model but never triggers the debounced database save. The editor emits `lens_updated` for this edit, while the main window only connects `lens_modified`. `lens_updated` has no connections anywhere in the repository, so the change is lost when the window closes.

## Impact

- Data loss: the only way to give a `Custom` lens its index is the index field; editing it is not persisted.
- The value reaches SQLite only if the user later edits another property, presses `Ctrl+S`, or duplicates the lens.
- No warning or dirty indicator; the UI behaves as if the edit were saved.

## Evidence

Code paths:

- `openlens/gui/widgets/lens_editor.py:614` — `_n_input.valueChanged` → `_on_index_changed`.
- `openlens/gui/widgets/lens_editor.py:963-977` — handler updates the model and emits `self.lens_updated` only.
- `openlens/gui/widgets/lens_editor.py:200-202` — `lens_updated` and `lens_modified` are distinct signals.
- `openlens/__main__.py:517` — only `lens_modified` is connected to the autosave.

```console
$ grep -rn "lens_updated.connect" openlens/
(no matches)
$ grep -rn "lens_modified.connect" openlens/
openlens/__main__.py:517: self._lens_editor.lens_modified.connect(self._on_lens_modified)
```

Repro output:

```text
after material switch:  modified= [1.5168] updated= [True]
lens.refractive_index after n edit: 1.75
modified emissions: [1.5168]
updated emissions: [True, True]
```

Switching the material to `Custom` emits `lens_modified` once; typing the actual custom index does not.

## Expected behaviour

Any edit that changes the persisted model, including the custom refractive index, schedules the same debounced save as the radius/thickness/material fields.

## Suggested fix

Emit `lens_modified` (or have the main window connect `lens_updated` as well) from `_on_index_changed`, or route every model mutation through one helper that emits the save-triggering signal. Add a GUI test that edits the index, waits past the debounce, and reads the new value back from SQLite.

nodes.title: fix(data-loss): save a hand-typed refractive index like every other edit
nodes.body:
## Description

Editing the refractive index of a `Custom` lens updated the in-memory model
but never triggered the debounced database save. The editor emitted
`lens_updated` for this edit, while the main window only connects
`lens_modified` - and `lens_updated` has no connections anywhere in the
repository:

```console
$ grep -rn "lens_updated.connect" openlens/
(no matches)
$ grep -rn "lens_modified.connect" openlens/
openlens/__main__.py:517: self._lens_editor.lens_modified.connect(self._on_lens_modified)
```

The typed index therefore reached the in-memory model only, and was lost when
the window closed unless the user happened to edit another property, press
`Ctrl+S`, or duplicate the lens.

## What changed

- `openlens/gui/widgets/lens_editor.py::_on_index_changed` now emits
  `lens_modified` as every other edit handler does, so the custom index goes
  through the same debounced save as the radius, thickness and material
  fields.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #617

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New test module `tests/test_gui_custom_index_autosave.py` (drives a real
`OpenLensWindow` against a temporary database), both failing before the fix:

- `test_the_index_edit_emits_the_save_triggering_signal`
- `test_the_index_edit_reaches_the_database` - the index is read back from
  SQLite after the debounce, with the material edit's own save flushed first
  so the index edit cannot ride on it.

Full local suite: `Ran 2595 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`, `black` clean,
`ruff` clean, `mypy` clean.

title: bug(data-loss): tolerance operand edits are never autosaved
body:
## Summary

The tolerancing tab mutates `_parent._tol_operands` directly and refreshes its table, but never stamps the tolerance set into the lens/assembly metadata or schedules a save. Autosave is driven only by `lens_modified` and assembly `data_updated`, so a tolerance set added after the last lens edit is lost on close.

## Impact

- Data loss: Add Tolerance, Default Set, Load Grade, Remove, Clear, and inline Min/Max edits all survive only until the window closes.
- An explicit `Ctrl+S` does persist them, but nothing indicates that tolerancing bypasses autosave.
- A user can spend time building a tolerance budget and lose it silently.

## Evidence

All of these handlers mutate `self._parent._tol_operands` and refresh the table, but none calls `_sync_tolerances_to_metadata()`, `_save_to_database()`, or emits a save signal:

- `openlens/gui/tabs/tolerancing_tab.py:405-468` — Add Tolerance
- `:470-492` — Default Set
- `:494-506` — Load Grade
- `:508-523` — Remove
- `:525-540` — Clear
- `:542-561` — inline Min/Max edits

Tolerance metadata is only stamped inside `_save_to_database()` (`openlens/__main__.py:267-288`, `316-346`). `closeEvent()` only flushes an active debounced edit timer (`openlens/__main__.py:615-623`, `918-944`).

End-to-end repro: make one name edit (persists an empty tolerance set), add the default set, wait past the 400 ms debounce, close:

```text
after name edit, stored: [('Persisted Lens', 0)]
in-memory operands: 5 target: Persisted Lens
1s after Default Set, stored: [('Persisted Lens', 0)]
after close, stored: [('Persisted Lens', 0)]
```

## Expected behaviour

Adding/removing/editing tolerance operands marks the owning lens or assembly dirty and schedules the same debounced save as other edits; closing the window flushes it.

## Suggested fix

After every tolerance mutation, call `_sync_tolerances_to_metadata()` and trigger the existing debounced save (or emit the appropriate `data_updated`/`lens_modified` signal). Prefer one `_mark_dirty()` helper on the tab so new buttons cannot forget. Add a GUI test that adds an operand, waits, closes, and reopens the database.

nodes.title: fix(data-loss): save the tolerance set when the operands change
nodes.body:
## Description

The tolerancing tab mutated the window's tolerance-operand list and
refreshed its table, but never told the window about it. The tolerance set
is stamped into the target's metadata by the save path, and the save path
only ran for a lens edit - so a tolerance set built after the last lens edit
was lost when the window closed:

```
after name edit, stored: [('Persisted Lens', 0)]
in-memory operands: 5 target: Persisted Lens
1s after Default Set, stored: [('Persisted Lens', 0)]
after close, stored: [('Persisted Lens', 0)]
```

## What changed

- `openlens/gui/tabs/tolerancing_tab.py` gained a `_mark_dirty()` helper that
  stamps the tolerance set into the target's metadata and schedules the
  window's debounced save.
- Every operand mutation goes through it: Add Tolerance, Default Set, Load
  Grade, Remove, Clear and the inline Min/Max edits. A new button cannot
  forget to save.

The parent's helpers are looked up defensively, because the tab is exercised
with partial parent doubles.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #618

New test module `tests/test_gui_tolerance_autosave.py` (drives a real
`OpenLensWindow` against a temporary database), both failing before the fix:

- `test_the_default_set_reaches_the_database`
- `test_removing_an_operand_reaches_the_database`

Full local suite: `Ran 2600 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`, `black` clean,
`ruff` clean, `mypy` clean.

title: bug(data-loss): a database read error can erase the stored library on the next save
body:
## Summary

`LensStorage.load_lenses()` catches every exception and returns `[]`. `LibraryService` therefore reports a successful empty load, the window adopts the default lens, and the next explicit save runs `_reconcile()`, which deletes every stored row missing from the now-empty snapshot. A transient/corrupt read becomes permanent data loss.

## Impact

- Critical data loss: a database read error (corrupt/truncated file, permissions, lock, missing table/column) is indistinguishable from an empty library.
- The user sees "Loaded library: 0 lenses, 0 assemblies" and no error dialog.
- `Ctrl+S` / `File > Save` then treats the in-memory default as the complete library and deletes the rows that failed to load.
- The intended "Load failed" dialog path (`openlens/__main__.py:250-265`) is unreachable for storage read errors.

## Evidence

- `openlens/gui/storage.py:76-115` — `except Exception ... return []`.
- `openlens/gui/services/library_service.py:95-102` — sees a normal empty list and returns `ok=True`.
- `openlens/__main__.py:191-207` — reports "Loaded library: 0 lenses, 0 assemblies".
- `openlens/__main__.py:222-245` — adopts the current default lens into the empty library.
- `openlens/gui/storage.py:207-239` — `_reconcile()` deletes stored ids absent from `items`.
- `openlens/__main__.py:1129` — `Ctrl+S` calls `_save_to_database()` with `reconcile=True`.

Repro: seed two lenses, make the database unreadable for the load, restore access, then run the normal `Ctrl+S` path:

```text
seeded rows (lenses, assemblies, names): (2, 0, ['Lens A', 'Lens B'])
in-memory after failed load: 1 lenses, 0 assemblies
problem dialogs shown: 0
status text: Loaded library: 0 lenses, 0 assemblies
rows still on disk after failed load: (2, 0, ['Lens A', 'Lens B'])
status after Ctrl+S: Saved to database
rows on disk after the next save: (1, 0, ['Default Lens'])
```

## Expected behaviour

A read failure is reported as a failure (`ok=False` + error dialog), the library is not replaced by the default lens, and reconciliation is disabled until a load has succeeded. An empty library should only be assumed when the database was actually read successfully and contains no rows.

## Suggested fix

Stop swallowing load errors: let `load_lenses()` raise or return a result object carrying `error`. Propagate that through `LibraryService`, show the existing error dialog, and set a `loaded_ok` flag that gates `reconcile=True`. As defence in depth, make `_reconcile()` refuse to delete anything when the in-memory snapshot is empty but the database is not. Add tests for a corrupt database, a locked database, and a failed load followed by `Ctrl+S`.

nodes.title: fix(data-loss): a failed library load must not delete the stored library
nodes.body:
## Description

`LensStorage.load_lenses()` caught every exception and returned an empty
list, so a database read error was indistinguishable from an empty library.
The window adopted its default lens, and the next explicit save reconciled
the database against that one-item snapshot - deleting every row that had
failed to load:

```
rows still on disk after failed load: (2, 0, ['Lens A', 'Lens B'])
status after Ctrl+S: Saved to database
rows on disk after the next save: (1, 0, ['Default Lens'])
```

A read failure is now a failure, not an empty library.

## What changed

- `openlens/gui/storage.py::LensStorage.load_lenses` lets the database's
  exception through and records it in `last_error`. The per-item errors stay
  warnings: one corrupt lens must not cost the user the rest of their
  library.
- `openlens/__main__.py::_load_from_database` keeps the in-memory library,
  shows the "Load failed" dialog that was unreachable before, and remembers
  that the library was never read.
- `openlens/__main__.py::_save_to_database` only reconciles after a
  successful load - reconciling against a library that was never read is
  what deleted the rows.
- `openlens/gui/storage.py::LensStorage._reconcile` refuses an empty
  snapshot against a non-empty database, as defence in depth.
- `openlens/gui/services/library_service.py` - docstring updated: the service
  already turned a raised read error into a failure result; the storage
  layer was the one swallowing it.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #619

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New test module `tests/test_gui_failed_load.py` (drives a real
`OpenLensWindow` against a temporary database, with the read patched to
fail), all failing before the fix:

- `test_a_read_failure_is_reported`
- `test_a_failed_load_does_not_replace_the_library`
- `test_a_save_after_a_failed_load_keeps_the_rows`

Full local suite: `Ran 2603 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`, `black` clean,
`ruff` clean, `mypy` clean.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(gui): performance tab's entrance-pupil and object-distance controls do not affect calculations
body:
## Summary

The performance tab reads an "Entrance Pupil" and an "Object Distance" from its spin boxes, prints them in the report as calculation parameters, and never passes either to the aberration calculation. Changing them changes only the two text lines, not the aberrations, f-number, spot size, or any other metric.

## Impact

- Misleading UI: the report presents values as inputs when they are labels.
- A user can believe a design was evaluated at a 1000 mm object distance or a 10 mm pupil when nothing changed.
- `AberrationsCalculator` does expose `object_distance_mm`, but the GUI never supplies it (and the implementation rejects finite object distances), so the control cannot work as shown.

## Evidence

- `openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:151-156` — Entrance Pupil spin box.
- `openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:172-177` — Object Distance spin box.
- `openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:351-354` — both values read from the widgets.
- `openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:404-406` — `calculate_all_aberrations()` called with only `field_angle_deg` and `wavelength_nm`.
- `openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:455-461` — values printed as "Calculation Parameters".

Repro with Entrance Pupil 10 mm / Object Distance 1000 mm, then 100 mm / 100 mm:

```text
first  parameter lines: ['Entrance Pupil: 10.00 mm', 'Object Distance: 1000.0 mm']
second parameter lines: ['Entrance Pupil: 100.00 mm', 'Object Distance: 100.0 mm']
report identical apart from those two lines: True
first f/# line: ['f-number (f/#): 2.43']
second f/# line: ['f-number (f/#): 2.43']
```

## Expected behaviour

Either the controls feed the calculation (pupil size for aperture-dependent metrics, object distance for finite-conjugate aberrations) or they are removed/disabled and the report stops presenting them as inputs.

## Suggested fix

Pass the object distance into `calculate_all_aberrations(object_distance_mm=...)` once the calculator supports finite conjugates; derive the f-number and pupil-dependent metrics from the entrance-pupil value. If finite-conjugate support is out of scope, remove the two spin boxes and the report lines until it lands. Add a GUI test asserting the metric changes when the pupil/object-distance value changes.

nodes.title: fix(gui): make the performance tab evaluate its entrance pupil
nodes.body:
## Description

The Performance tab read an "Entrance Pupil" spin box, printed the value in its
report as a calculation parameter, and built the aberration calculator without
it. Every pupil produced the same numbers:

```
Entrance Pupil: 10.00 mm      Entrance Pupil: 100.00 mm
f-number (f/#): 3.89          f-number (f/#): 3.89
```

The "Object Distance" spin box was worse. `AberrationsCalculator` raises for a
finite `object_distance_mm` - every Seidel estimator assumes an object at
infinity - so the widget's 1000 mm was never usable, yet the report presented
it as the distance the design had been evaluated at.

## What changed

- **`openlens/aberrations.py`** - `AberrationsCalculator` takes an optional
  `entrance_pupil_mm`. It is validated (positive, finite), clamped to the
  element's physical clear aperture (the glass cannot pass more light) and
  used for every aperture-derived quantity: f-number, numerical aperture,
  Airy disk, the marginal-ray traces, and the field metrics. The result
  dictionaries report the effective value as `"entrance_pupil"`.
- **`openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py`** - the tab passes its widget value
  to the calculator and prints the effective (clamped) pupil, so the report
  can no longer show one aperture and evaluate another.
- The finite object-distance control is removed. The report states the actual
  model condition: `Object Distance: infinity (collimated; finite conjugates
  are not modelled)`.

The visible consequence: a 25 mm f/3.9 singlet evaluated at a 10 mm pupil now
reports f/9.7, with the correspondingly larger Airy disk, and moving the
control changes those numbers.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #620

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_aberrations_entrance_pupil.py` - eleven tests fail on
the unfixed code (`TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'entrance_pupil_mm'`):

- `test_the_default_is_the_physical_clear_aperture`
- `test_the_result_reports_the_effective_pupil`
- `test_the_f_number_follows_the_entrance_pupil`
- `test_the_numerical_aperture_follows_the_entrance_pupil`
- `test_the_airy_disk_follows_the_entrance_pupil`
- `test_the_spherical_aberration_shrinks_with_the_pupil`
- `test_a_pupil_wider_than_the_lens_is_clamped`
- `test_a_system_target_honours_the_entrance_pupil`
- `test_a_pupil_as_large_as_the_lens_changes_nothing`
- `test_a_non_positive_pupil_raises` / `test_a_non_finite_pupil_raises` /
  `test_a_non_numeric_pupil_raises`

New module `tests/test_performance_tab_entrance_pupil.py` drives the real tab
with an inline worker; four of its five tests fail on the unfixed code:

title: bug(gui): Save As silently does nothing while an assembly is active
body:
## Summary

`File > Save As...` (`Ctrl+Shift+S`) is always enabled, but `_on_save_as()` returns immediately when `_current_lens` is `None` — which is exactly the state while an assembly is selected. The action produces no dialog, no status message, and no error.

## Impact

- Silent no-op: the user believes a JSON file was written; nothing happens.
- Assemblies are the main multi-element artifact, so this is easy to hit.
- Inconsistent with the enabled menu item, which implies the action is available.

## Evidence

- `openlens/__main__.py:686` — the menu action is always enabled.
- `openlens/__main__.py:1132-1135` — `_on_save_as()` returns immediately when `_current_lens` is `None`.
- `openlens/__main__.py:748-753` — selecting an assembly sets `_current_lens = None`.
- `openlens/gui/services/export_service.py:85-100` — `save_lens_json()` accepts only a `Lens`.

Repro with the save dialog patched to count invocations:

```text
assembly active -> _current_lens: None
assembly active -> save dialog calls: 0
lens active -> save dialog calls: 1
```

## Expected behaviour

The action is disabled (or explains why) when an assembly is active, or it exports the assembly (the JSON interchange path already supports `OpticalSystem.save()`).

## Suggested fix

Enable/disable the action based on the current selection, and implement an assembly JSON export using `OpticalSystem.save()` if the format is meant to cover assemblies. At minimum, show a status message ("Save As is only available for single lenses") instead of silently returning. Add a GUI test for both selection states.

nodes.title: fix(gui): export the active assembly from File > Save As
nodes.body:
## Description

`File > Save As...` (`Ctrl+Shift+S`) is always enabled, but `_on_save_as()`
returned immediately when `_current_lens` was `None` — exactly the state while
an assembly is selected. The action produced no dialog, no file, no status
message and no error, even though assemblies are the main multi-element
artifact.

## What changed

- **`openlens/gui/services/export_service.py`**
  - Added `save_system_json()`, which writes an `OpticalSystem` through the
    same JSON interchange format as `save_lens_json()` (flat radii as `null`,
    `allow_nan=False`) and keeps the failure text that `OpticalSystem.save()`
    swallowed.
- **`openlens/__main__.py`**
  - `_on_save_as()` picks the active lens or assembly and calls the matching
    service method, with a `Save Lens As` / `Save Assembly As` dialog.
  - A successful save sets a `Saved lens/assembly to <path>` status.
  - With nothing active it reports `Nothing to save` instead of returning
    silently.
- **`tests/test_export_service.py`**
  - `save_system_json()` writes the system dict and round-trips through
    `OpticalSystem.load()`.
  - A flat surface is written as `null`, and a failure returns a result.
- **`tests/test_gui_save_as_assembly.py`** (new)
  - An active assembly is exported and reloads; the dialog title says
    `Assembly`.
  - The single-lens path is unchanged.
  - Nothing active reports a status and opens no dialog.
  - A cancelled dialog writes nothing.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #621

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2833 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

The assembly export, assembly round trip and no-selection status tests fail
before the fix; the lens and cancelled-dialog tests guard the existing path.

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(data-loss): Zemax round-trip drops elements or shrinks diameter when clear apertures differ
body:
## Summary

The Zemax exporter writes `DIAM` as `clear_aperture / 2` for each surface, but the importer reconstructs the mechanical diameter from the **back** surface only and then rejects the element if the front clear aperture exceeds it. A lens with a larger front clear aperture is dropped entirely; a lens with a larger back clear aperture silently shrinks to that diameter.

## Impact

- Round-trip data loss: a valid lens (`D=40`, `CA1=38`, `CA2=30`) vanishes from the imported system with only a warning.
- Asymmetric clear apertures are common (front element of an objective, domed windows).
- The opposite asymmetry imports with the wrong mechanical diameter (`D=38` instead of `40`), affecting mounts, spacers, and layout.
- A lens with only `CA2` set (`CA1=None`) is also dropped.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.export_formats import ZemaxSystemExporter, ZemaxSystemImporter

def roundtrip(**kw):
    s = OpticalSystem()
    s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=50.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-50.0,
                    thickness=5.0, diameter=40.0, **kw))
    p = "/tmp/aperture.zmx"
    ZemaxSystemExporter.export_system(s, p)
    return ZemaxSystemImporter.import_system(p)

print([e.lens.diameter for e in roundtrip(clear_aperture_1=38, clear_aperture_2=30).elements])
print([e.lens.diameter for e in roundtrip(clear_aperture_1=30, clear_aperture_2=38).elements])
```

Observed:

```
Zemax import: element 1 dropped, front clear aperture (38.000 mm) exceeds diameter (30.000 mm)
case 1: D=40, CA1=38, CA2=30
  exported: ['DIAM 19.0', 'DIAM 15.0']
  imported elements: 0
case 2: D=40, CA1=30, CA2=38
  imported diameter: 38.0 (expected 40.0)
case 4: D=40, CA1=None, CA2=30
  exported: ['DIAM 20.0', 'DIAM 15.0']
  imported elements: 0
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/export_formats.py:752` / `:777` — exporter writes `DIAM = clear_aperture / 2`.
- `openlens/export_formats.py:1029-1038` — importer sets `diameter = back_diam * 2.0` only.
- `openlens/export_formats.py:889-895` — validation drops the element when `ca1 > diameter`.

## Expected behaviour

`diameter ≥ max(CA1, CA2)` is restored, and the imported diameter equals the source mechanical diameter when both surfaces carry a clear aperture. An element is never dropped because its front aperture is larger than its back aperture.

## Suggested fix

Reconstruct `diameter = 2 * max(front_diam, back_diam)` (or export/parse the mechanical diameter explicitly, e.g. a `DIAM` on one surface plus separate `CA1`/`CA2`). Ensure the validation sees the restored diameter, not the back-only value. Add round-trip tests for `CA1>CA2`, `CA2>CA1`, `CA1=None`, and `CA2=None`.

nodes.title: fix(data-loss): keep a lens with asymmetric clear apertures in a Zemax round trip
nodes.body:
## Description

The Zemax exporter writes one semi-diameter per surface (`DIAM = clear
aperture / 2`), but the importer rebuilt the mechanical diameter from the
**back** surface only. The validation then saw a diameter smaller than the
front clear aperture and dropped the whole element:

```
CA1=38, CA2=30 (D=40)  ->  imported elements: 0
CA1=30, CA2=38 (D=40)  ->  imported diameter: 38.0 (expected 40.0)
CA1=None, CA2=30        ->  imported elements: 0
```

## What changed

- `openlens/export_formats.py::ZemaxSystemImporter` reconstructs the
  mechanical diameter as the **larger of the two clear apertures** - the
  smallest blank that holds both. The `.zmx` dialect has one semi-diameter
  per surface and no field for the blank diameter, so this is the best the
  format can carry.
- The exporter's docstring now states that limitation.

Both clear apertures still round-trip exactly, no element is dropped, and a
lens without clear apertures keeps its diameter.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #622

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New test module `tests/test_zemax_aperture_roundtrip.py` (four of the five
tests fail on the unfixed code):

- `test_a_larger_front_aperture_is_not_dropped`
- `test_a_larger_back_aperture_is_not_dropped`
- `test_only_a_back_aperture_is_not_dropped`
- `test_the_diameter_holds_both_apertures`
- `test_a_lens_without_clear_apertures_keeps_its_diameter`

Full local suite: `Ran 2607 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`, `black` clean,
`ruff` clean, `mypy` clean.

title: bug(io): STEP export writes parabolic and conic surfaces as spheres
body:
## Summary

`StepExporter` computes rim/sag points from the lens model's true surface (parabolic or conic) but always emits both surfaces as `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` with the vertex radius. For a parabola or general conic, the exported sphere does not pass through the rim points, so the B-rep is not closed and the solid is geometrically wrong.

## Impact

- Any parabolic or conic lens exports with the wrong surface shape — a parabola with `R=100`, sag `1.25 mm` at `h=10` becomes a sphere whose sag at `h=10` is `0.50 mm`.
- The rim vertex and surface disagree, so a conforming CAD kernel may reject the solid or stitch it incorrectly.
- Silent: the STEP file looks valid and the repo's minimal reader ignores the geometry, so tests stay green.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.io.step_export import StepExporter

lens = Lens(is_parabolic_1=True, parabolic_sag_1=1.25, diameter=20.0)
s = OpticalSystem(); s.add_lens(lens)
StepExporter(s).export("/tmp/parabola.step")
print(open("/tmp/parabola.step").read())
```

Observed:

```
PARABOLIC front surface (R vertex 100, sag 1.25 at h=10)
  export: SPHERICAL_SURFACE radius = 100.0
  export: rim point = (10.000000, 0, 1.250000)
  sphere sag at h=10.0 = 0.501256
  model get_sag_1(h)  = 1.250000
  rim on the exported sphere? False

CONIC front surface (R=50, K=-2)
  export: SPHERICAL_SURFACE radius = 50.0
  export: rim point = (10.000000, 0, 0.990195)
  sphere sag at h=10.0 = 1.010205
  model get_sag_1(h)  = 0.990195
  rim on the exported sphere? False
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/io/step_export.py:361-373` — rim points use `lens.get_sag_1/2`, which honours parabolic/conic terms.
- `openlens/io/step_export.py:471`, `:488` — the surface entity is always `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` with `abs(r)`; `is_parabolic_*` and `conic_constant_*` are never read.

## Expected behaviour

The exported surface matches the modelled sag at every radius, so the rim lies on the surface and the solid closes.

## Suggested fix

Emit a `TOROIDAL_SURFACE`, `CONICAL_SURFACE`, or a rational B-spline surface for parabolic/conic cases, or tessellate the true sag into a faceted B-rep. At minimum, reject/warn instead of silently exporting a mismatched sphere. Add a test that samples the exported surface at the rim and compares it to `get_sag_*`.

nodes.title: fix(io): refuse STEP export of conic surfaces instead of writing spheres
nodes.body:
## Description

`StepExporter` sampled the rim point from the lens model's true surface - a
parabola or a general conic - but always emitted both caps as
`SPHERICAL_SURFACE` of the stored vertex radius. For a parabola whose model
sags 1.25 mm at the rim, the exported sphere sags 0.50 mm there:

```
#14=CARTESIAN_POINT('e1',(10.000000,0.000000,1.250000));   <- model rim
#35=SPHERICAL_SURFACE('sphere1',#34,100.000000);           <- sags 0.501256
```

The rim does not lie on the surface, so the B-rep does not close and a CAD
kernel may reject or mis-stitch it. The file still looked valid, so nothing
surfaced the error.

A sphere through both the vertex and the rim cannot carry the parabolic
profile either, and the writer has no analytic non-spherical surface entity.
STEP is CAD/manufacturing input, so the exporter now refuses the lens with a
diagnostic instead of emitting a plausible-looking wrong solid:

```
ValueError: STEP export writes spherical and flat surfaces only; lens 'Parabola'
has a parabolic front surface. At the rim (h=10 mm) the model sags 1.250000 mm
but a sphere of radius 100 mm sags 0.501256 mm, so the exported rim would not
lie on the exported surface.
```

The file is only written after every part has been built, so a refused export
leaves no partial file. Spherical and flat surfaces export exactly as before.

A zero-sag parabolic surface (`is_parabolic_*` with `parabolic_sag_* = 0`) is
now exported as a plane. Flatness used to be decided from the radius alone, so
that surface silently became a sphere whose rim did not match either.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #623

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_step_conic_surfaces.py` (8 tests). Five fail on the
unfixed code (`ValueError not raised`, or a `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` where a plane
is expected):

- `test_a_parabolic_front_surface_is_refused` - also pins the diagnostic
  numbers (1.250000 vs 0.501256) and that no file is written
- `test_a_conic_front_surface_is_refused`
- `test_a_parabolic_back_surface_is_refused`
- `test_one_conic_element_refuses_the_whole_assembly` - names the offending
  element, not the first
- `test_a_zero_sag_parabolic_surface_exports_as_a_plane`

Three guard the supported cases:

- `test_a_spherical_lens_exports_a_solid`
- `test_the_rim_of_the_exported_sphere_lies_on_it` - checks the exported rim
  point against the exported sphere radius
- `test_a_conic_constant_on_a_flat_surface_is_still_flat`

Full local suite: `Ran 2747 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; the STEP, atomic-write,
export-service and GUI-export suites (146 tests) pass.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(io): STEP export discards element decenter and tilt
body:
## Summary

`StepExporter.export()` passes only `elem.position` to `_export_lens_solid()`. The element's `decenter_y`, `decenter_z`, `tilt_x`, `tilt_y`, and `tilt_z` are never applied, so every exported solid is centered on the global Z axis.

## Impact

- An intentionally decentered or tilted assembly exports as perfectly aligned.
- The STEP file cannot be used to inspect or manufacture the actual layout.
- Silent: the export reports success and the file is valid, just geometrically wrong.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.io.step_export import StepExporter

def export(path, aligned):
    s = OpticalSystem()
    s.add_lens(Lens(), air_gap_before=0.0)
    if not aligned:
        s.set_element_alignment(0, decenter_y=5.0, decenter_z=2.0,
                                tilt_x=3.0, tilt_y=-2.0)
    StepExporter(s).export(path)

export("/tmp/aligned.step", True)
export("/tmp/tilted.step", False)
a = [l for l in open("/tmp/aligned.step") if "CARTESIAN_POINT" in l]
b = [l for l in open("/tmp/tilted.step") if "CARTESIAN_POINT" in l]
print("point lines identical:", a == b)
```

Observed:

```
element 0 decenter/tilt in the model: 5.0 2.0 3.0 -2.0
point-line count: 9 9
point lines identical: True
   #4=CARTESIAN_POINT('origin',(0.000000,0.000000,0.000000));
   #10=CARTESIAN_POINT('v1',(0.000000,0.000000,0.000000));
   #11=CARTESIAN_POINT('v2',(0.000000,0.000000,5.000000));
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/io/step_export.py:239-243` — only `elem.position` is passed.
- `openlens/io/step_export.py:348` — `_export_lens_solid(self, lens, z_offset)` has no alignment parameters.

## Expected behaviour

Exported solids carry the element's full transform (translation + rotation), matching `SystemRayTracer3D` / the assembly view.

## Suggested fix

Pass the element's decenter/tilt (or its node global transform) into the solid builder and apply it to every `CARTESIAN_POINT`, or emit an `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` per element with the rotation and reference it from the surface. Add a test asserting that a decentered/tilted export differs from the aligned one and that a known point lands at the transformed coordinate.

nodes.title: fix(io): export each element with its decenter and tilt
nodes.body:
## Description

`StepExporter.export()` passed only `elem.position` to `_export_lens_solid()`,
so every solid was built on the global axis. An element intentionally
decentered or tilted - the layout the ray tracer and the assembly view use -
exported perfectly aligned:

```
element 0 decenter/tilt in the model: 5.0 2.0 3.0 -2.0
point lines identical: True
#10=CARTESIAN_POINT('v1',(0.000000,0.000000,0.000000));
```

The file was valid and the export reported success, so nothing surfaced the
mismatch. A STEP file that does not match the designed layout cannot be used
to inspect or manufacture the assembly.

## What changed

- **`openlens/io/step_export.py`** - each element is exported with its global
  transform from the optical tree (`get_global_transform()`), so a transform
  inherited from a group is honoured too. Elements are paired with their tree
  nodes by identity; if the tree and the flat element list disagree, the flat
  record's own `position`/`decenter_y`/`decenter_z`/`tilt_x`/`tilt_y`/`tilt_z`
  fields are used instead, so a stale list cannot apply one element's
  alignment to another.
- Every `CARTESIAN_POINT` of the solid is placed through that transform.
  Rotated elements get their own axis and reference `DIRECTION` entities, so
  the plane normals, rim circles, seam and cylindrical axis follow the tilt.
- The optical model runs along +X with lateral offsets in Y/Z; STEP writes the
  axis along +Z with the cross-section in X/Y. The conversion is explicit:
  `decenter_y` moves the solid along STEP X, `decenter_z` along STEP Y, and the
  axial position along STEP Z.
- Single lenses and aligned systems keep their previous coordinates; the
  global direction entities are reused when an element is only translated.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #624

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_step_element_alignment.py` (7 tests). Four fail on the
unfixed code:

- `test_a_decentered_element_moves_off_the_axis` - the vertex must land on the
  node's global position (STEP `(decenter_y, decenter_z, axial)`); it stayed at
  the origin
- `test_a_decentered_rim_moves_with_the_element`
- `test_a_tilted_element_rotates_its_axis` - a 90 deg tilt about the model Z
  must turn the cylinder axis from STEP +Z to +X; it stayed +Z
- `test_two_differently_tilted_elements_get_two_axes` - both elements shared
  the global `axis_z` entity

Three guard the supported cases:

- `test_the_rim_stays_on_the_curved_surface_after_a_tilt` - the transformed
  rim point is still exactly one radius from the transformed sphere centre
- `test_the_aligned_export_still_uses_the_global_axes`
- `test_each_element_keeps_its_axial_position` - doublet vertices still sit at
  each element's model position

Full local suite: `Ran 2746 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; the STEP,
atomic-write, export-service and GUI-export suites (102 tests) pass.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
