title: bug(io): Zemax import accepts a non-finite CURV and builds NaN geometry
body:
## Summary

`_curv_to_radius()` returns `1.0 / nan = nan` for a non-finite `CURV`. `_build_validated_lens()` substitutes `MAX_RADIUS_OF_CURVATURE` **only for the validation call**, then passes the original `nan` into `Lens(...)`. Validation never sees the NaN, so a corrupted or hand-edited `.zmx` injects a lens with `r1=nan`, `focal_length=nan`, and `sag=0.0`.

## Impact

- The importer is documented as tolerant of untrusted/foreign files; this bypasses its own rejection path.
- NaN geometry propagates through tracing, optimization, and analysis, or is treated as a flat surface by code that ignores NaN.
- No warning; the element is accepted.

## Reproduction

A `.zmx` surface with `CURV nan` (or `CURV 0` / `CURV inf` variants):

```python
from openlens.export_formats import ZemaxSystemImporter
s = ZemaxSystemImporter.import_system("/tmp/nan_curv.zmx")
lens = s.elements[0].lens
print(lens.radius_of_curvature_1, lens.calculate_focal_length(),
      lens.get_sag_1(10.0))
```

Observed:

```
imported elements: 1
r1: nan isnan: True
focal length: nan
sag at 10mm: 0.0
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/export_formats.py:990-993` — `_curv_to_radius` divides by the parsed value without a finiteness check.
- `openlens/export_formats.py:902-904` — validation probes use a clamped radius.
- `openlens/export_formats.py:948-951` — the original `nan` is passed to `Lens`.

## Expected behaviour

A non-finite `CURV` is rejected with a warning, exactly like a negative thickness or oversized diameter, and the remaining surfaces still import.

## Suggested fix

Validate `math.isfinite(curv)` (and the resulting radius) before constructing the lens; drop the element with a clear warning. Also validate the **actual** values passed to `Lens`, not a substituted probe. Add tests for `nan`, `inf`, and `-inf` `CURV`.

nodes.title: fix(io): reject non-finite Zemax curvatures
nodes.body:
## Description

`ZemaxSystemImporter` accepted a non-finite `CURV` and built NaN geometry:

```python
lens = ZemaxSystemImporter.import_system("/tmp/nan_curv.zmx").elements[0].lens
lens.radius_of_curvature_1   # nan
lens.calculate_focal_length()  # nan
lens.get_sag_1(10.0)           # 0.0
```

`_curv_to_radius()` returned `1.0 / nan = nan`, and `_build_validated_lens()`
validated a substituted `MAX_RADIUS_OF_CURVATURE` probe instead of the value
it passed to `Lens(...)`. Validation therefore never saw the NaN, no warning
was logged, and the element was accepted. NaN then propagates through ray
tracing, optimisation and analysis, or is treated as a flat surface by code
that ignores NaN.

The adjacent `CURV inf` / `CURV -inf` cases became a zero radius, which `Lens`
rejected with the misleading "R1 cannot be zero" instead of a diagnostic that
names the real problem. `CURV INFINITY` - the format's plano spelling that the
parser explicitly accepts - was broken for the same reason and silently lost
the element.

## What changed

- **`openlens/export_formats.py`** - `CURV INFINITY` is normalised to `0.0` at
  parse time, so it takes the ordinary plano path (`CURV 0` also stays plano).
- `_curv_to_radius()` validates the curvature it was given: a non-finite value
  returns `None` instead of inventing a radius.
- `_build_validated_lens()` rejects `None` before touching the model and logs
  a warning naming the front or back surface
  (`... element N dropped, front curvature (CURV) is not finite`). The
  remaining surfaces still import, matching the importer's existing policy for
  negative thickness and oversized apertures.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #625

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Four new tests in `tests/test_zemax_roundtrip.py::TestZemaxSystemImportValidation`,
all failing on the unfixed code:

- `test_non_finite_front_curvature_is_rejected` - `nan`, `inf`, `-inf`; also
  asserts a warning explains the drop (NaN produced no warning at all, `inf`
  produced "R1 cannot be zero")
- `test_non_finite_back_curvature_is_rejected` - the closing surface's CURV is
  checked too
- `test_a_non_finite_element_does_not_discard_the_next` - the good element
  after the bad one still imports
- `test_the_explicit_infinity_token_still_means_plano` - `CURV INFINITY` must
  import as a plano surface

Full local suite: `Ran 2743 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; the Zemax round-trip
and export suites (52 tests) pass.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

title: bug(io): Zemax import ignores UNIT INCH and reads inches as millimetres
body:
## Summary

`ZemaxSystemImporter._parse_surfaces()` reads only `SURF` blocks and ignores header keywords. A file declaring `UNIT INCH` is interpreted 1:1 as millimetres, so every radius, thickness, diameter, and gap is 25.4× too small.

## Impact

- Importing an inch-based `.zmx` silently produces a completely different optical system (25.4× scale error) instead of converting or refusing.
- The importer's docstring explicitly claims tolerant handling of foreign sequential files.
- Downstream focal lengths, f-numbers, and tolerances are all wrong by the same factor.

## Reproduction

```text
header: UNIT INCH; thickness 1.0 in = 25.4 mm; DIAM 0.5 in = 12.7 mm semi
imported thickness: 1.0 mm   (expected 25.4)
imported diameter:  1.0 mm   (expected 25.4)
imported radius 1:  25.400000025908 mm (expected 25.4 in = 645.16)
imported air gap:   4.0 mm   (expected 4 in = 101.6)
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/export_formats.py:967-982` — `import_system` rebuilds from parsed surfaces; no unit handling.
- `openlens/export_formats.py:816-817` — parser only recognizes `SURF` lines.
- `openlens/export_formats.py:1031` — `diam * 2.0` is assumed to be mm.

## Expected behaviour

`UNIT INCH`/`UNIT MM` is honoured: every parsed length is converted to mm once, at the parse boundary. Unknown units raise or warn instead of silently assuming mm.

## Suggested fix

Parse the header for `UNIT` (Zemax also uses `UNIT INCH`, `UNIT MM`, and older `MM`/`IN` markers), store a scale factor, and apply it to `CURV` (inverse), `DISZ`, `DIAM`, and thickness/gap values. Add a test with an inch file asserting the converted geometry.

nodes.title: fix(io): convert Zemax inch files to millimetres
nodes.body:
## Description

`ZemaxSystemImporter._parse_surfaces()` read only `SURF` blocks and ignored
the header, so a file declaring `UNIT INCH` was interpreted 1:1 as
millimetres. Every radius, thickness, aperture and gap came out 25.4x too
small, and the import still reported success:

```text
header: UNIT INCH; thickness 1.0 in = 25.4 mm; DIAM 0.5 in = 12.7 mm semi
imported thickness: 1.0 mm   (expected 25.4)
imported diameter:  1.0 mm   (expected 25.4)
imported radius 1:  25.400000025908 mm (expected 25.4 in = 645.16)
imported air gap:   4.0 mm   (expected 4 in = 101.6)
```

Downstream focal lengths, f-numbers and tolerances were all wrong by the same
factor, with nothing in the file or the UI saying so.

## What changed

- **`openlens/export_formats.py`** - a new `_parse_unit_scale()` reads the
  `UNIT` header. `MM` (and the spelled-out millimetre forms) maps to 1.0,
  `IN`/`INCH`/`INCHES` maps to 25.4. A file with no `UNIT` line keeps the
  historical millimetre default, as Zemax does; an explicit unknown unit logs
  a warning and also uses millimetres rather than aborting the import.
- `import_system()` normalises the parsed values to millimetres once: `DISZ`
  and `DIAM` multiply by the factor, `CURV` divides by it (curvature is the
  inverse of a length). Non-finite marker values (`DISZ INFINITY`) pass
  through untouched, and every consumer below stays unit-agnostic.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #626

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Six new tests in `tests/test_zemax_roundtrip.py::TestZemaxUnits`. Four fail on
the unfixed code:

- `test_inch_lengths_are_converted_to_millimetres` - radii 50.8 mm,
  thicknesses 25.4/12.7 mm, diameters 12.7/25.4 mm
- `test_the_gap_between_elements_is_converted` - the 4 in gap is 101.6 mm
- `test_the_inch_spellings_are_recognised` - `UNIT INCH`, `UNIT IN`,
  `unit inch`
- `test_unknown_unit_warns_and_assumes_millimetres`

Two guard the existing behaviour:

- `test_a_millimetre_file_is_unchanged`
- `test_a_missing_unit_line_keeps_millimetres`

The Zemax round-trip, export-format, export-service and import-limit suites
(64 tests) pass after rebasing onto current `master`; full local suite on the
pre-rebase tree: `Ran 2753 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(data-loss): Zemax round-trip drops element alignment and working wavelength
body:
## Summary

The `.zmx` exporter writes only `TYPE`, `CURV`, `CONI`, `DISZ`, `DIAM`, `GLAS`, `COAT`, and `STOP`. It never writes element decenter/tilt or the working wavelength, and the importer has no keywords for them. A round trip therefore resets alignment to zero and the wavelength to the `Lens` default 587.6 nm.

## Impact

- Data loss: `decenter_y=5`, `tilt_x=3°`, and `wavelength=532 nm` become `0`, `0`, `587.6 nm`.
- After a catalog index refresh, the wavelength change alone shifts the EFL from 808.19 mm to 816.40 mm.
- Alignment is a first-class feature (`set_element_alignment`), so this is not a documented format limitation.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.export_formats import ZemaxSystemExporter, ZemaxSystemImporter

s = OpticalSystem()
s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=50.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-50.0,
                thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0, wavelength=532.0))
s.set_element_alignment(0, decenter_y=5.0, tilt_x=3.0)
p = "/tmp/alignment.zmx"
ZemaxSystemExporter.export_system(s, p)
text = open(p).read()
imp = ZemaxSystemImporter.import_system(p)
print("mentions DECE/TILT/WAVE:", any(k in text for k in ("DECE", "TILT", "WAVE")))
print(s.elements[0].decenter_y, s.elements[0].tilt_x,
      imp.elements[0].decenter_y, imp.elements[0].tilt_x,
      imp.elements[0].lens.wavelength)
```

Observed:

```
export mentions DECE/TILT/WAVE: False
source element 0: decenter_y=5.0 tilt_x=3.0
rebuilt element 0: decenter_y=0.0 tilt_x=0.0
source lens wavelength: 532.0 nm
rebuilt lens wavelength: 587.6 nm
source EFL: 808.189 mm
rebuilt EFL: 816.402 mm
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/export_formats.py:715-800` — writer has no alignment/wavelength output.
- `openlens/export_formats.py:816-817`, `:1039-1064` — reader understands only the surface keywords.
- `openlens/export_formats.py:967-982` — importer rebuilds from surfaces alone.

## Expected behaviour

Round-trip preserves the element transform and the design wavelength (or the format explicitly declares them unsupported and the export refuses/warns rather than silently dropping them).

## Suggested fix

Emit Zemax `DECE`/`TILT` (or the project's own documented extension keywords) per surface and a `WAVE`/wavelength header, and parse them back into `LensElement`/`Lens.wavelength`. Add a round-trip test for decenter, tilt, and a non-default wavelength.

## Description

The `.zmx` writer emitted only `TYPE`, `CURV`, `CONI`, `DISZ`, `DIAM`, `GLAS`,

wavelength, and the importer had no keywords for them. A round trip therefore
reset every `decenter_y`/`decenter_z`/`tilt_*` to zero and every
`lens.wavelength` to the 587.6 nm default:

```text
exported decenter_y=5.0, tilt_x=3.0, wavelength=532.0
imported decenter_y=0.0, tilt_x=0.0, wavelength=587.6
```

Alignment is a first-class feature, so this was silent data loss; after a
catalog index refresh the wavelength change alone moves the EFL.

## What changed

- **`openlens/export_formats.py`**
  - Both exporters write `WAVE <nm>` on every element's front surface.
  - The system exporter writes `DECE <dy> <dz>` and `TILT <tx> <ty> <tz>`
    when they are non-zero. The front surface is the element's origin, which
    is exactly where the model applies the element transform.
  - `_parse_surfaces()` learns `WAVE`, `DECE` and `TILT`; a malformed value is
    logged and ignored rather than aborting the import.
  - `import_system()` applies the transform with `set_element_alignment()`
    after adding the element, and passes the wavelength to
    `_build_validated_lens()`.
  - The imported refractive index is resolved **at the imported wavelength**
    (`_material_design_index(material, wavelength)`), so the reconstructed
    lens is at the same design point instead of keeping the d-line index with
    a new wavelength.
  - An invalid `WAVE` (non-numeric, non-finite, outside the supported range)
    logs a warning and falls back to the default wavelength.
- `DECE` is a length, so it follows the `UNIT` factor introduced by #626
  (inch files); `TILT` (degrees) and `WAVE` (nm) do not.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #627

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2771 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Seven new tests in `tests/test_zemax_roundtrip.py`; the six
`TestZemaxAlignmentAndWavelength` tests fail on the unfixed code:

- `test_the_file_declares_alignment_and_wavelength`
- `test_round_trip_preserves_the_element_transform`
- `test_round_trip_preserves_the_design_wavelength`
- `test_round_trip_keeps_the_axial_positions_with_alignment`
- `test_a_single_lens_export_keeps_its_wavelength`
- `test_an_invalid_wavelength_falls_back_to_the_default`

`TestZemaxUnits.test_a_decentred_element_is_scaled_with_the_rest_of_the_file`
covers the interaction with #626: an inch file with `DECE 0.5 0.25` imports a
12.7 mm / 6.35 mm decenter while `TILT 3 -2 1` stays in degrees.

The Zemax round-trip, export-format, export-service and import-limit suites
(71 tests) pass on the rebased tree.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(io): ISO 10110 notes are not XML-escaped, producing invalid SVG
body:
## Summary

The ISO 10110 SVG drawing escapes the system title but interpolates note text — including coating material names — directly into `<text>` elements. A material name containing `&`, `<`, or `>` produces invalid XML, so the exported drawing cannot be opened.

## Impact

- Output corruption: `A&B <AR>` yields a raw `&` and `<AR>`; XML parsing fails at that line.
- Coating layer names are free-form user input, so this is reachable through normal use.
- The file is written successfully and reported as exported; only the consumer discovers it is invalid.

## Reproduction

```python
# Coating material name: "A&B <AR>"
# Export the ISO 10110 drawing, then parse it:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
ET.parse("/tmp/iso10110.svg")
```

Observed:

```
<text ... class="title">ISO 10110 Drawing: A & B <optics></text>
<text ...>6/ Coating: L1: A&B <AR> SLAR/Uncoated.</text>

XML ParseError: not well-formed (invalid token): line 76, column 53
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/io/export.py:220` — coating label interpolated into a note string.
- `openlens/io/export.py:225` — note inserted into `<text>` without `html.escape`/`xml.sax.saxutils.escape`. The title path already escapes correctly.

## Expected behaviour

Every user-controlled string is XML-escaped before insertion, and the exported SVG parses as well-formed XML for any valid material name.

## Suggested fix

Escape all note text at the insertion point (or build the SVG with an XML writer). Add a test with `&`, `<`, `>`, and a quote in a coating name that parses the result with `ElementTree`.

nodes.title: fix(io): XML-escape the ISO 10110 notes before inserting them into the SVG
nodes.body:
## Description

The ISO 10110 SVG drawing escaped the system title and the table values but
interpolated note text directly into `<text>` elements. Coating layer names are
free-form user input, so a stack labelled `A&B <AR>` put a raw `&` and a tag
into the drawing. The file was written and reported as exported, but the
result was not well-formed XML and no consumer could open it.

## What changed

- **`openlens/io/export.py`**
  - `_generate_iso_notes()` now XML-escapes every note at the insertion point.
    The note strings still contain the human-readable coating label, so the
    drawing shows `A&B <AR>` while the file carries `A&B <AR>`.
- **`tests/test_iso_drawing.py`**
  - A system whose name, material and coating all contain `&`, `<`, `>` and
    quotes renders and parses with `xml.etree.ElementTree`.
  - The markup is escaped rather than dropped (the parsed text still contains
    the original labels).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #628

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
  - Before: `ParseError: not well-formed (invalid token)` and the raw
    `A&B <AR>` assertion fails.
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2826 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100`, `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

title: bug(io): ISO 10110 notes are not XML-escaped, producing invalid SVG
body:
## Summary

The ISO 10110 SVG drawing escapes the system title but interpolates note text — including coating material names — directly into `<text>` elements. A material name containing `&`, `<`, or `>` produces invalid XML, so the exported drawing cannot be opened.

## Impact

- Output corruption: `A&B <AR>` yields a raw `&` and `<AR>`; XML parsing fails at that line.
- Coating layer names are free-form user input, so this is reachable through normal use.
- The file is written successfully and reported as exported; only the consumer discovers it is invalid.

## Reproduction

```python
# Coating material name: "A&B <AR>"
# Export the ISO 10110 drawing, then parse it:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
ET.parse("/tmp/iso10110.svg")
```

Observed:

```
<text ... class="title">ISO 10110 Drawing: A & B <optics></text>
<text ...>6/ Coating: L1: A&B <AR> SLAR/Uncoated.</text>

XML ParseError: not well-formed (invalid token): line 76, column 53
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/io/export.py:220` — coating label interpolated into a note string.
- `openlens/io/export.py:225` — note inserted into `<text>` without `html.escape`/`xml.sax.saxutils.escape`. The title path already escapes correctly.

## Expected behaviour

Every user-controlled string is XML-escaped before insertion, and the exported SVG parses as well-formed XML for any valid material name.

## Suggested fix

Escape all note text at the insertion point (or build the SVG with an XML writer). Add a test with `&`, `<`, `>`, and a quote in a coating name that parses the result with `ElementTree`.

title: bug(optimizer): GUI default "spot_size" target is silently ignored
body:
## Summary

The optimization tab builds `OptimizationTarget("spot_size")` and
`OptimizationTarget("spherical")`, but the merit function only implements
`"rms_spot_radius"` and `"spherical_aberration"`. `MeritFunction.evaluate()`
silently skips unknown target names, so the "Minimize RMS Spot Size" checkbox
(the default-checked target) does nothing. If it is the only target selected,
the optimizer "converges" after one iteration with a merit of 0 and returns
the input design unchanged.

## Impact

- The default GUI optimization run ignores spot size; only the focal-length
  target affects the result.
- A user who unchecks focal length and leaves the default spot-size box gets a
  fake success with no change and no warning.
- Any typo or renamed target in API use is silently ignored rather than
  rejected, so callers cannot tell that their merit function is incomplete.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.optimizer import (
    LensOptimizer, MeritFunction, OptimizationTarget, OptimizationVariable,
)

def system():
    s = OpticalSystem("singlet")
    s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=70.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
                    thickness=5.0, diameter=20.0, refractive_index=1.5168))
    return s

for name in ("spot_size", "spherical", "rms_spot_radius", "spherical_aberration"):
    mf = MeritFunction(system(), [OptimizationTarget(name, 0, 1.0, "minimize")])
    print(f"{name:22} -> {mf.evaluate(system())!r}")

variables = [OptimizationVariable("R1", 0, "radius_of_curvature_1",
                                  current_value=70.0, min_value=60.0, max_value=200.0)]
r = LensOptimizer(system(), variables,
                  [OptimizationTarget("spot_size", 0, 1.0, "minimize")]
                  ).optimize_simplex(max_iterations=60)
print("success=%s iterations=%d initial=%r final=%r R1=%r" % (
    r.success, r.iterations, r.initial_merit, r.final_merit,
    r.optimized_system.elements[0].lens.radius_of_curvature_1))
```

Output:

```
spot_size              -> 0.0
spherical              -> 0.0
rms_spot_radius        -> 0.1315120691771384
spherical_aberration   -> 1.678445495055783
success=True iterations=1 initial=0.0 final=0.0 R1=70.0
```

Adding the GUI's `spot_size` target to a focal-length optimization produces a
bit-for-bit identical path and result to the focal-length-only run.

## Root cause

- `openlens/gui/tabs/optimization_tab.py:726` and `:728` pass the names
  `"spot_size"` and `"spherical"`.
- `openlens/optimizer.py:283-292` defines `_TARGET_DISPATCH` with
  `"rms_spot_radius"` and `"spherical_aberration"` only.
- `openlens/optimizer.py:408-410` does `handler = ...; if handler is None:
  continue`, which drops unknown targets without an error or log entry.

## Expected behaviour

The GUI's checkboxes control the corresponding real merit terms, and an
unknown target name is rejected (or at least logged and surfaced) instead of
silently contributing zero.

## Suggested fix

Use the canonical names in the GUI (`"rms_spot_radius"`,
`"spherical_aberration"`), preferably via shared constants so the two sides
cannot drift again. Make `MeritFunction.evaluate()` raise `ValueError` for an
unrecognised target name, or collect unknown names and log a warning. Add a
regression test that builds the targets exactly as the optimization tab does
and asserts a non-zero spot contribution.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): the GUI's spot-size and spherical targets were no-ops
nodes.body:
## Description

The optimization tab built `OptimizationTarget("spot_size")` and
`OptimizationTarget("spherical")`, but the merit function's dispatch table
only knows `rms_spot_radius` and `spherical_aberration` - and an unknown name
was skipped silently:

```
merit for each name (valid geometry, no penalty)
  'spot_size'            -> 0.0
  'spherical'            -> 0.0
  'rms_spot_radius'      -> 0.1315120691771384
  'spherical_aberration' -> 1.678445495055783
```

The default-checked spot-size box therefore did nothing, and an optimization
with only that box selected "converged" after one iteration with a merit of 0
and the design unchanged.

## What changed

- `openlens/gui/tabs/optimization_tab.py` asks for the canonical target
  names. The collection moved into `_collect_targets()` so the names the GUI
  uses can be checked against the dispatch table in a test.
- `openlens/optimizer.py::MeritFunction.evaluate` rejects an unknown target
  name with a `ValueError` that lists the known names, instead of treating it
  as a target that contributes nothing. A mistake in a name must not look
  like a working target.

title: bug(optimizer): cemented doublet is permanently infeasible (1e8 penalty on zero air gap)
body:
## Summary

A cemented interface is represented as an air gap with `thickness == 0`, but
`MeritFunction._penalty_physical()` treats every `air_gaps` entry as a real air
space. It therefore adds a soft penalty because `0 < min_air_gap` and, more
importantly, a hard `1e8` because the edge clearance at the cemented interface
is exactly zero. The built-in `create_doublet_optimizer()` can never reach a
feasible merit: its shipped design finishes at ~`1.00002e8`, yet reports
`success=True`.

## Impact

- The application's own cemented-doublet optimizer is unusable; every
  evaluation is dominated by a constant 1e8 term.
- Genuine further improvements (or regressions) in the optical merit are
  invisible next to the penalty, so the optimizer's reported improvement and
  convergence are meaningless.
- Users cannot optimise any cemented achromat, a standard design form.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.optical_system import create_doublet
from openlens.optimizer import MeritFunction, create_doublet_optimizer

doublet = create_doublet(focal_length=100.0, diameter=50.0)
print("air gaps:", [g.thickness for g in doublet.air_gaps])
mf = MeritFunction(doublet, [])
print("physical penalty:", mf._penalty_physical(doublet))

opt = create_doublet_optimizer(create_doublet(100.0, 50.0), 100.0)
result = opt.optimize(max_iterations=100)
print("success=%s final_merit=%.6f" % (result.success, result.final_merit))
print("physical penalty of result:", opt.merit_function._penalty_physical(result.optimized_system))
```

Output:

```
air gaps: [0.0]
physical penalty: 200126478.71056747
success=True final_merit=100002052.187376
physical penalty of result: 100002000.0
```

The returned elements have positive edge thicknesses
(`[2.319, 3.329]` mm), so the remaining 1e8 comes solely from the cemented
interface: `gap 0` plus coincident mating surfaces gives `edge_clearance == 0`.

## Root cause

- `openlens/optimizer.py:354-356` applies the minimum-air-gap penalty to every
  gap, including a cemented gap.
- `openlens/optimizer.py:368-372` computes edge clearance as
  `gap + sag_front(next) - sag_back(previous)`; for a cemented interface the
  mating sags are equal, so the clearance is exactly 0 and the `<= 0` branch
  adds `1e8`.

Nothing in `AirGap` distinguishes "cemented" from "air", and `create_doublet`
uses `thickness=0` for the cemented surface.

## Expected behaviour

A cemented interface is a valid, manufacturable geometry. It should not be
subject to the minimum air gap or positive edge-clearance requirements, and a
cemented doublet should be able to converge to a merit well below `1e8`.

## Suggested fix

Represent/identify cemented gaps explicitly (e.g. an `AirGap.is_cemented`
flag, or treat `abs(thickness) <= EPSILON` together with coincident mating
sags as cemented) and skip the `min_air_gap` and `min_edge_clearance` checks
for them. Do not simply lower `min_air_gap` to 0: that would also accept
zero-gap uncemented elements that can interpenetrate. Add a regression test
that `create_doublet_optimizer(...).optimize()` returns a design with
`success=True` and `final_merit < 1e6`.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): a cemented interface is a feasible geometry, not an air gap
nodes.body:
## Description

The model represents a cemented doublet as an air gap of zero: the two
elements share a surface. `MeritFunction._penalty_physical()` treated every
gap as an air space, so the cemented interface collected a soft penalty for
the missing air and a hard `1e8` for an edge clearance of exactly zero.

Every cemented doublet was therefore permanently infeasible, and the
application's own doublet optimizer finished at a merit of `1.00002e8` with
the real merit invisible next to the penalty.

## What changed

- `openlens/optimizer.py::_penalty_physical` recognises a zero-thickness gap
  as a cemented interface: it is not subject to the minimum air gap, and it
  has no clearance to keep. A real air gap that is too small is still
  penalised.

```
physical penalty: 0.0
final_merit: 1.607803 (was 100002052.187376)
```

- `test_a_real_air_gap_is_still_penalised`

title: bug(optimizer): thickness variable desynchronizes element positions and air gaps
body:
## Summary

Setting `thickness` as an optimization variable changes
`LensElement.lens.thickness` but not the cached `LensElement.thickness`
wrapper that `OpticalSystem._update_positions()` advances by. The downstream
element therefore does not move and `air_gaps` are not recomputed. The returned
system has an air gap implied by traced positions that differs from
`air_gaps[i].thickness`, so the ABCD/focal-length merit and the 3D spot merit
analyse different geometries. Large thickness values can make adjacent lenses
interpenetrate while the physical penalty stays at zero.

## Impact

- A thickness variable silently has the wrong effect: the 2D/paraxial model
  and the 3D tracer disagree about the same optimized design.
- The optimizer can return a physically impossible system (lenses overlapping)
  without any penalty, and reports the (wrong) paraxial merit as its result.
- Editable thickness through the GUI/CLI is a supported variable type, so this
  affects normal use, not only hand-built API calls.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.analysis.paraxial import find_paraxial_focus
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.optimizer import LensOptimizer, OptimizationVariable

def lens(name, r1):
    return Lens(name=name, radius_of_curvature_1=r1, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
                thickness=5.0, diameter=20.0, refractive_index=1.5168)

system = OpticalSystem("two element")
system.add_lens(lens("L1", 70.0), air_gap_before=0.0)
system.add_lens(lens("L2", 80.0), air_gap_before=10.0)

opt = LensOptimizer(system, [OptimizationVariable("T1", 0, "thickness", 5.0, 1.0, 20.0)], [])
applied = opt._apply_variables([9.0])
print("positions:", [e.position for e in applied.elements])
print("wrappers :", [e.thickness for e in applied.elements])
print("air_gaps :", [g.thickness for g in applied.air_gaps])
print("gap implied by positions:",
      applied.elements[1].position - (applied.elements[0].position +
                                      applied.elements[0].lens.thickness))
print("ABCD BFL  :", applied.calculate_back_focal_length())
last_vertex = applied.elements[-1].position + applied.elements[-1].lens.thickness
print("traced BFL:", find_paraxial_focus(applied) - last_vertex)

overlap = opt._apply_variables([17.0])
print("T1=17 rear vertex:", overlap.elements[0].position + overlap.elements[0].lens.thickness)
print("T1=17 next front :", overlap.elements[1].position)
print("penalty          :", opt.merit_function._penalty_physical(overlap))
```

Output:

```
positions: [0.0, 15.0]
wrappers : [5.0, 5.0]
air_gaps : [10.0]
gap implied by positions: 6.0
ABCD BFL  : 35.681391184494935
traced BFL: 36.802846369966446
T1=17 rear vertex: 17.0
T1=17 next front : 15.0
penalty          : 0.0
```

A control that calls `elements[0].refresh()` after changing the lens gives
positions `[0.0, 27.0]` and keeps the intended 10 mm gap, confirming the
wrapper is the stale value.

## Root cause

- `openlens/optimizer.py:994-995` writes `lens.thickness`.
- `openlens/optimizer.py:965` then calls `system._update_positions()`.
- `openlens/optical_system.py:401` advances with `element.thickness`, a cached
  copy of `lens.thickness` set at construction/refresh
  (`openlens/optical_system.py:59,67-69`), not the live lens value.
- `air_gaps` are left untouched, so they now describe a different spacing from
  the element positions.

## Expected behaviour

A thickness variable updates the element's propagation length, moves all
following elements by the same amount (preserving the air gaps), and the
tracers and ABCD calculations see one consistent geometry. Interpenetration is
detected and penalised.

## Suggested fix

After writing `lens.thickness`, call `system.elements[element_index].refresh()`
(or make `_update_positions()` read `element.lens.thickness` directly) before
`_update_positions()`. Ensure the air-gap bookkeeping is either preserved by
moving subsequent elements or recomputed from the new positions, and add the
same interpenetration check to the physical penalty. Add a regression test
that changes a thickness variable, asserts `positions[i+1] - positions[i] ==
lens.thickness + air_gaps[i].thickness`, and compares the ABCD and traced BFL.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): a thickness variable must move the elements that follow it
nodes.body:
## Description

The thickness variable wrote `lens.thickness` and then called
`_update_positions()`, which advances by the element's **cached** thickness
wrapper - a copy of the lens value taken at construction. The wrapper was
stale, so the element did not move and the air gap the positions implied no
longer matched `air_gaps`:

```
after T1 5 -> 9 mm:
  element positions        : [0.0, 15.0]
  gap implied by positions : 6.0   (air_gaps says 10.0)
  ABCD back focal length   : 35.68
  traced focus             : 36.80  -> the two models saw different systems
```

A thick enough lens even passed through its neighbour with no penalty: the
neighbour stayed at 15 mm while the lens reached 17 mm.

## What changed

- `openlens/optimizer.py::_apply_single_variable` updates the element's
  thickness wrapper together with the lens value, so `_update_positions()`
  moves the element, the air gap is preserved, and the ABCD model and the
  tracer agree again.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #632

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New test module `tests/test_thickness_variable_geometry.py` (all four tests
fail on the unfixed code):

- `test_the_element_moves_with_its_thickness`
- `test_the_air_gap_is_preserved`
- `test_the_abc_and_the_tracer_see_the_same_system`
- `test_a_thick_lens_does_not_pass_through_its_neighbour`

Full local suite: `Ran 2617 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`, `black` clean,
`ruff` clean, `mypy` clean.

title: bug(optimizer): index/Abbe variables overwrite the other glass parameter with model defaults
body:
## Summary

`_apply_single_variable()` switches a catalog lens into model-glass mode for a
`refractive_index` or `abbe_number` variable but seeds only the parameter being
optimised. The other model parameter keeps its class default (`model_nd =
1.5168`, `model_vd = 64.17`). Optimising the index of an SF11 lens therefore
silently replaces its real Abbe number (25.68) with 64.17, and optimising the
Abbe number silently drops the index from 1.78472 to 1.5168. Even evaluating
the variable at its current value changes the lens.

## Impact

- Index and Abbe variables are not independent: changing one corrupts the
  other, so the optimizer evaluates a different glass from the one shown in
  the UI.
- Colour correction and focal length change discontinuously at the first
  evaluation, producing misleading merit improvements.
- The bug affects every catalog glass whose index or Abbe number differs from
  the BK7 defaults, i.e. most real glasses.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.material_database import get_material_database
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.optimizer import LensOptimizer, OptimizationVariable

def sf11():
    s = OpticalSystem("SF11")
    s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=100.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
                    thickness=5.0, diameter=20.0, material="SF11",
                    refractive_index=1.78472))
    return s

catalog_vd = get_material_database().get_material("SF11").vd
system = sf11()
lens = system.elements[0].lens
print("before: nd=%.5f catalog Vd=%.2f model_vd=%.2f LCA=%.4f" % (
    lens.refractive_index, catalog_vd, lens.model_vd,
    system.calculate_chromatic_aberration()["longitudinal"]))
opt = LensOptimizer(system, [OptimizationVariable(
    "N", 0, "refractive_index", lens.refractive_index, 1.3, 2.4)], [])
applied = opt._apply_variables([lens.refractive_index])
lens2 = applied.elements[0].lens
print("after : model=%s nd=%.5f model_vd=%.2f LCA=%.4f" % (
    lens2.model_glass_mode, lens2.model_nd, lens2.model_vd,
    applied.calculate_chromatic_aberration()["longitudinal"]))

system = sf11()
opt = LensOptimizer(system, [OptimizationVariable(
    "V", 0, "abbe_number", 25.68, 20.0, 80.0)], [])
applied = opt._apply_variables([25.68])
lens2 = applied.elements[0].lens
print("abbe: model=%s model_nd=%.5f Vd=%.2f EFL=%.4f" % (
    lens2.model_glass_mode, lens2.model_nd, lens2.model_vd,
    applied.get_system_focal_length()))
```

Output:

```
before: nd=1.78472 catalog Vd=25.68 model_vd=64.17 LCA=2.4298
after : model=True nd=1.78472 model_vd=64.17 LCA=0.9825
abbe: model=True model_nd=1.51680 Vd=25.68 EFL=97.5812
```

The first case keeps the index but changes the longitudinal chromatic
aberration from 2.43 mm to 0.98 mm because Vd changed. The second keeps Vd but
changes nd from 1.78472 to 1.51680, moving the EFL from 64.43 mm to 97.58 mm.

## Root cause

- `openlens/optimizer.py:1001-1005` sets `model_glass_mode = True` and writes
  only `model_nd`.
- `openlens/optimizer.py:1006-1010` sets `model_glass_mode = True` and writes
  only `model_vd`.
- The `Lens` constructor defaults `model_nd = 1.5168` and `model_vd = 64.17`
  (`openlens/lens.py:177-178`), independently of `material`.

The tolerancing code already has the correct seed helper,
`_ensure_model_glass()` (`openlens/tolerancing.py:423-436`), which copies
`lens.refractive_index` and the catalog `Vd` before switching modes.

## Expected behaviour

Applying a refractive-index or Abbe variable to its current value leaves the
lens unchanged. Changing one parameter must preserve the current value of the
other, and the starting point should be the lens's actual glass, not BK7
defaults.

## Suggested fix

Reuse `tolerancing._ensure_model_glass(lens)` before writing either model
parameter, then update only the requested one and call
`lens.update_refractive_index()`. Add tests with a non-BK7 catalog glass
(e.g. SF11) that set each variable to its current value and assert nd, Vd, and
EFL are unchanged.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): an index or Abbe variable must not overwrite its companion
nodes.body:
## Description

The index and Abbe variables switched the lens to model-glass mode and wrote
only the parameter being optimised. The companion value kept the model
default (BK7's 1.5168 / 64.17), so an SF11 lens silently became a different
glass - even when the variable was applied at its own current value:

```
refractive_index variable, applied at its own value:
  before: nd=1.78472 model_vd=64.17 LCA=2.4298
  after : model=True model_nd=1.78472 model_vd=64.17 LCA=0.9825

abbe_number variable, applied at its own value:
  before: nd=1.78472 EFL=64.4252
  after : model=True model_nd=1.51680 Vd=25.68 EFL=97.5812
```

## What changed

- `openlens/lens.py` gained `ensure_model_glass(lens)`: it switches a lens to
  model-glass mode and seeds `model_nd`/`model_vd` from the glass the lens
  actually is. A lens that is already in model-glass mode is left alone - its
  nd/Vd are the glass the user chose.
- `openlens/optimizer.py` uses it for the `refractive_index` and
  `abbe_number` variables, so only the parameter being optimised changes.
- `openlens/tolerancing.py` now calls the same helper instead of its own
  copy, so the two paths cannot drift apart again.

Closes #633

title: bug(optimizer): clear-aperture lens is falsely rejected using mechanical diameter
body:
## Summary

`MeritFunction._penalty_physical()` evaluates the interior surface-intersection
check at `lens.diameter / 2`, although `Lens.calculate_edge_thickness()`
deliberately evaluates the rim at the manufacturing radius (the clear aperture
when it is smaller than the blank). A lens mounted with a small clear aperture
in a larger blank is therefore scored as hard-infeasible (`1e8`) even though
its real edge thickness is positive and it is manufacturable.

## Impact

- Valid mounted/stopped-down lenses are rejected by both the simplex and the
  global optimizers, so they cannot be optimised at all.
- The penalty comes from a region the finished part never reaches, so it
  cannot be fixed by changing the optical prescription within the clear
  aperture.
- This is the exact geometry `Lens.calculate_edge_thickness()` documents as
  valid, so the two pieces of code disagree about the same lens.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.optimizer import MeritFunction, OptimizationTarget

lens = Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=40.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-40.0,
            thickness=2.0, diameter=30.0, refractive_index=1.5168,
            clear_aperture_1=8.0, clear_aperture_2=8.0)
print("manufacturing radius:", lens.get_manufacturing_radius())
print("calculate_edge_thickness():", lens.calculate_edge_thickness())
print("thickness at h=4:", lens.thickness - lens.get_sag_1(4.0) + lens.get_sag_2(4.0))
print("thickness at h=15:", lens.thickness - lens.get_sag_1(15.0) + lens.get_sag_2(15.0))

system = OpticalSystem("mounted")
system.add_lens(lens)
mf = MeritFunction(system, [OptimizationTarget("focal_length", 100.0, 1.0, "target")])
print("_penalty_physical:", mf._penalty_physical(system))
print("total merit      :", mf.evaluate(system))
```

Output:

```
manufacturing radius: 4.0
calculate_edge_thickness(): 1.5989949685295954
thickness at h=4: 1.5989949685295954
thickness at h=15: -3.83801512904337
_penalty_physical: 100000000.0
total merit      : 100003717.07705845
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/optimizer.py:328` sets `y = lens.diameter / 2.0`.
- `openlens/optimizer.py:343-350` evaluates the interior thickness at
  `y * 0.5` and `y * 0.7071`, i.e. at 7.5 mm and 10.6 mm for this lens, both
  outside the 4 mm clear semi-aperture. At those heights the surfaces have
  already crossed, so the loop adds `1e8`.
- `Lens.calculate_edge_thickness()` (`openlens/lens.py:708-731`) uses
  `get_manufacturing_radius()` and returns +1.60 mm for the same lens.

## Expected behaviour

The physical penalty checks the lens where it is actually polished. A lens with
a positive edge thickness inside its clear aperture has no hard geometry
penalty, even when the blank is much larger. The same clear-aperture radius
should be used for the inter-element edge-clearance check
(`openlens/optimizer.py:361`).

## Suggested fix

Use `lens.get_manufacturing_radius()` for `y` and for the inter-element
`max_h`, matching `calculate_edge_thickness()`. Add a regression test with
`D=30`, `CA=8`, `R=±40`, `t=2` asserting `_penalty_physical == 0` and a
companion test with no clear aperture asserting the genuinely infeasible lens
is still penalised.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): judge the physical penalty at the polished aperture
nodes.body:
## Description

`MeritFunction._penalty_physical()` evaluated the interior
surface-intersection check at `lens.diameter / 2` and the inter-element
clearance at the smaller mechanical semi-diameter, although
`Lens.calculate_edge_thickness()` deliberately evaluates the rim at the
*manufacturing* radius (the clear aperture when it is smaller than the
blank).

A lens mounted with an 8 mm clear aperture in a 30 mm blank is therefore
scored hard-infeasible:

```text
R = +/-40 mm, thickness 2 mm, diameter 30 mm, clear aperture 8 mm
edge thickness at the polished rim (h=4 mm):  +1.60 mm
edge thickness at the blank rim     (h=15 mm): -3.84 mm  <- surfaces cross
-> _penalty_physical() = 1e8, so neither optimizer can touch the design
```

The crossing at h=15 mm is in glass the finished part never reaches, and no
variable inside the clear aperture can repair it. The merit function and the
edge-thickness calculation disagreed about the same lens.

## What changed

- **`openlens/optimizer.py`**
  - The interior surface-intersection check now uses
    `lens.get_manufacturing_radius()` instead of `lens.diameter / 2`.
  - The inter-element edge-clearance check uses
    `min(lens1.get_manufacturing_radius(), lens2.get_manufacturing_radius())`
    instead of the smaller blank radius.
  - Both now agree with `calculate_edge_thickness()` and with the geometry the
    part is actually polished to. Lenses without a smaller clear aperture are
    unaffected: the manufacturing radius is the blank radius.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #634

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Three new tests in `tests/test_optimizer_clear_aperture_penalty.py`:

- `test_a_mounted_lens_with_positive_edge_thickness_has_no_penalty` - fails
  before (`1e8 != 0.0`), passes after.
- `test_inter_element_clearance_is_judged_at_the_clear_aperture` - two curved
  neighbours clear by 0.12 mm at h=4 mm but would collide by 0.93 mm at the
  15 mm blank rim; fails before, passes after.
- `test_the_same_lens_without_a_clear_aperture_is_still_infeasible` - guard:
  with no clear aperture the surfaces really do cross, and the hard penalty
  remains.

Optimizer feasibility, API, advanced, assembly, cemented-doublet and global
optimizer suites (45 tests) pass on the rebased tree.

title: bug(optimizer): optimize_robust leaks merit cache and merit function between runs
body:
## Summary

`DesensitizationOptimizer.optimize_robust()` changes two pieces of optimizer
state for the duration of a run but does not scope them to that run:

1. It swaps `self.merit_function` for a `RobustMeritFunction` and restores it
   only on the normal return path. If the callback raises (the GUI's Stop
   button), the robust merit stays installed and the next ordinary
   optimisation silently uses the old tolerance list.
2. It reuses `LensOptimizer._merit_cache`, whose keys are only the variable
   values. A second robust run with a different `sensitivity_weight` scores
   every previously seen design with the old merit function, so the new weight
   has no effect.

## Impact

- Pressing Stop during a robust run corrupts the optimizer instance: a later
  run evaluates a different merit function from the one requested.
- Running robust optimisation twice with different weights (or tolerance sets)
  returns the first run's design and merit, hiding the entire sensitivity term.
  In the repro the reported merit is `4.55e-6` while the true robust merit at
  that design is `10.32`; a fresh optimizer with the same weight returns
  `0.725`.
- GUI sessions reuse the same optimizer object, so this is reachable through
  normal use.

## Reproduction

Stale cache:

```python
from openlens.desensitization import DesensitizationOptimizer
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.optimizer import OptimizationTarget, OptimizationVariable
from openlens.tolerancing import ToleranceOperand, ToleranceType

def system():
    s = OpticalSystem("robust")
    s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=70.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
                    thickness=5.0, diameter=20.0, refractive_index=1.5168))
    return s

variables = [OptimizationVariable("R1", 0, "radius_of_curvature_1", 70.0, 60.0, 200.0, 5.0)]
targets = [OptimizationTarget("focal_length", 100.0, weight=1.0, target_type="target")]
tolerances = [ToleranceOperand(0, ToleranceType.RADIUS_1, -0.5, 0.5),
              ToleranceOperand(0, ToleranceType.THICKNESS, -0.1, 0.1)]

opt = DesensitizationOptimizer(system(), variables, targets)
r0 = opt.optimize_robust(tolerances, sensitivity_weight=0.0, max_iterations=15)
r200 = opt.optimize_robust(tolerances, sensitivity_weight=200.0, max_iterations=15)
print("weight 0  : merit=%r R1=%r" % (r0.final_merit,
      r0.optimized_system.elements[0].lens.radius_of_curvature_1))
print("weight 200: merit=%r R1=%r" % (r200.final_merit,
      r200.optimized_system.elements[0].lens.radius_of_curvature_1))
print("identical:", r0.final_merit == r200.final_merit)
```

Output:

```
weight 0  : merit=4.551077473025656e-06 R1=105.126953125
weight 200: merit=4.551077473025656e-06 R1=105.126953125
identical: True
```

The same run on a fresh optimizer returns merit `0.7251897506031262` and
`R1=104.8828125`, differing from the stale run.

State leak on cancellation:

```python
class Cancelled(Exception):
    pass

opt = DesensitizationOptimizer(system(), variables, targets)
original = opt.merit_function

def cancel(iteration, merit, values):
    if iteration == 2:
        raise Cancelled("user pressed Stop")

try:
    opt.optimize_robust(tolerances, max_iterations=10, callback=cancel)
except Cancelled:
    pass
print("restored:", opt.merit_function is original)
print("now:", type(opt.merit_function).__name__)
```

Output:

```
restored: False
now: RobustMeritFunction
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/desensitization.py:162-180`: `self.merit_function` is assigned
  before `optimize_simplex()` and restored only after it returns; no
  `try/finally`.
- `openlens/optimizer.py:928-939`: the cache key is
  `tuple(round(v, 10) for v in values)` with no dependency on the active merit
  function, and `optimize_robust()` never clears `_merit_cache`.

## Expected behaviour

Each `optimize_robust()` call starts from an empty merit cache (or a cache
keyed by the merit-function configuration), and the previous merit function is
restored even when the run raises or is cancelled.

## Suggested fix

Wrap the run in `try/finally` and restore `self.merit_function` in the
`finally` block. Clear `self._merit_cache` whenever the merit function is
replaced (best done in a small setter/property so all callers are covered).
Add regression tests for: two robust runs with different weights giving
different results, and a callback raising leaving `merit_function` unchanged.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): each robust run must start from a clean state
nodes.body:
## Description

`optimize_robust` swapped the merit function for a robust one and restored
it only on the normal path, and it never touched the merit cache - whose key
is the design alone, not the merit function. A second run on the same instance
therefore scored every design the first run had seen with the first run's
merit function, and the new sensitivity weight had no effect at all:

```
run 1 (sensitivity_weight=0.0):  final_merit = 4.55e-06
run 2 (sensitivity_weight=200.0): final_merit = 4.55e-06  (identical)
true robust merit at that design: 10.32
```

A cancelled run (the GUI's Stop button) also left the robust merit
installed, so the next ordinary optimization on that instance used the old
tolerance list.

## What changed

- `openlens/optimizer.py::LensOptimizer._set_merit_function` installs a merit
  function and drops the cached merits: the cache is keyed by the design
  alone, so a merit function with a different configuration must not read the
  values the previous one produced.
- `openlens/desensitization.py::optimize_robust` swaps through that helper
  and restores the original merit function in a `finally`, so a cancelled run
  leaves the instance as it found it.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #635

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New tests in `tests/test_desensitization.py` (`TestRobustRunState`, all three
failing before the fix):

- `test_a_second_run_does_not_reuse_the_first_ones_merit`
- `test_a_second_run_matches_a_fresh_optimizer`
- `test_a_cancelled_run_restores_the_merit_function`

Full local suite: `Ran 2623 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`, `black` clean,
`ruff` clean, `mypy` clean.

- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

title: bug(optimizer): RobustMeritFunction ignores most tolerance types and cannot perturb refractive index
body:
## Summary

`RobustMeritFunction` is supposed to make a design insensitive to its
tolerances, but its perturbation engine only understands four of the fourteen
`ToleranceType` values. `AIR_GAP`, `ABBE_NUMBER`, `DECENTER_*`, `TILT_*`,
`WEDGE`, `IRREGULARITY`, and `FOCUS` all make `_get_param_value()` return
`None` and are skipped, contributing exactly zero sensitivity. Its
`REFRACTIVE_INDEX` perturbation is also overwritten by the spot analysis, so
even that supported type has zero effect when a spot-based target is used.

## Impact

- "Robust" optimisation is not robust for most of the tolerance list the
  application itself generates. An air-gap tolerance that changes the true
  merit by 15.7 contributes 0; an index tolerance that changes it by 0.0146
  also contributes 0.
- The optimizer reports a nominal-only design as if it had been desensitised,
  giving users false confidence in yield.
- Unsupported types fail silently, so there is no indication that the
  sensitivity model is incomplete.

## Reproduction

```python
import copy
from openlens.desensitization import RobustMeritFunction
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.optimizer import MeritFunction, OptimizationTarget
from openlens.tolerancing import ToleranceOperand, ToleranceType

def system():
    s = OpticalSystem("two element")
    s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=70.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
                    thickness=5.0, diameter=20.0, refractive_index=1.5168),
               air_gap_before=0.0)
    s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=80.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-120.0,
                    thickness=5.0, diameter=20.0, refractive_index=1.5168),
               air_gap_before=10.0)
    return s

targets = [OptimizationTarget("focal_length", 100.0, 1.0, "target"),
           OptimizationTarget("rms_spot_radius", 0.0, 100.0, "minimize")]
nominal = MeritFunction(system(), targets).evaluate(system())

perturbed = copy.deepcopy(system())
perturbed.air_gaps[0].thickness += 0.5
perturbed._update_positions()
true_change = abs(MeritFunction(perturbed, targets).evaluate(perturbed) - nominal)
print("true merit change from +0.5 mm air gap:", true_change)

air_tol = [ToleranceOperand(0, ToleranceType.AIR_GAP, -0.5, 0.5)]
robust = RobustMeritFunction(system(), targets, air_tol, sensitivity_weight=1.0)
print("robust sensitivity contribution:", robust.evaluate(system()) - nominal)

for tol_type in ToleranceType:
    probe = ToleranceOperand(0, tol_type, -0.1, 0.1)
    print(f"{tol_type.name:16} -> {robust._get_param_value(system(), probe)!r}")

# Refractive index with a spot target.
ri_tol = [ToleranceOperand(0, ToleranceType.REFRACTIVE_INDEX, -0.05, 0.05)]
ri_robust = RobustMeritFunction(system(), [targets[1]], ri_tol, 1.0)
ri_nominal = MeritFunction(system(), [targets[1]]).evaluate(system())
real = copy.deepcopy(system())
real.elements[0].lens.model_glass_mode = True
real.elements[0].lens.model_nd += 0.05
real.elements[0].lens.update_refractive_index()
real_change = abs(MeritFunction(real, [targets[1]]).evaluate(real) - ri_nominal)
print("true nd change:", real_change,
      "robust contribution:", ri_robust.evaluate(system()) - ri_nominal)
```

Output (abridged):

```
true merit change from +0.5 mm air gap: 15.705326249149039
robust sensitivity contribution: 0.0
RADIUS_1         -> 70.0
RADIUS_2         -> -100.0
THICKNESS        -> 5.0
REFRACTIVE_INDEX -> 1.5168
DECENTER_X       -> None
DECENTER_Y       -> None
TILT_X           -> None
TILT_Y           -> None
DECENTER_Z       -> None
AIR_GAP          -> None
ABBE_NUMBER      -> None
IRREGULARITY     -> None
WEDGE            -> None
FOCUS            -> None
true nd change: 0.014574303508034125 robust contribution: 0.0
```

For the index case, `SpotDiagram.trace_spot()` calls
`update_refractive_index()`, which recomputes the index from the material or
model glass and overwrites the direct `lens.refractive_index` write.

## Root cause

- `openlens/desensitization.py:98-120` maps only `RADIUS_1`, `RADIUS_2`,
  `THICKNESS`, and `REFRACTIVE_INDEX`; everything else returns `None`.
- `openlens/desensitization.py:71-75` silently drops those operands when
  `_get_param_value()` returns `None`.
- `openlens/desensitization.py:139-144` writes `lens.refractive_index`
  directly. Unlike `openlens/tolerancing.py:369-371`, it does not switch to
  model glass and update `model_nd`, so `Lens.update_refractive_index()`
  recomputes the catalog value at the next trace.

## Expected behaviour

Every tolerance type the tolerance generator can emit contributes a
perturbation, or is rejected loudly if genuinely unsupported. A refractive
index tolerance changes the index used by the trace, including for spot-based
merit functions.

## Suggested fix

Reuse the existing perturbation code in `tolerancing._apply_value()` (and
`_ensure_model_glass()`), rather than duplicating a partial switch. For
sensitivity, evaluate the base value through the same operand semantics
(including air gaps, decenter/tilt, Abbe number, and irregularity). If some
types cannot be represented, raise or log once instead of returning `None`.
Add tests for each `ToleranceType` asserting a non-zero sensitivity where the
perturbation is physically meaningful.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): the robust merit must measure every tolerance it is given
nodes.body:
## Description

`RobustMeritFunction` only understood `RADIUS_1`/`RADIUS_2`, `THICKNESS` and
`REFRACTIVE_INDEX`; every other operand type was skipped, so a tolerance set
full of air gaps, decenters and tilts contributed exactly zero sensitivity:

```
true change from +0.5 mm air gap : 15.919278791630859
robust sensitivity contribution : 0.0
```

The index perturbation was written straight into `lens.refractive_index`, which
the spot analysis then overwrote, so even the supported types could measure
nothing.

## What changed

- `openlens/desensitization.py::RobustMeritFunction.evaluate` now perturbs
  through the same code the Monte Carlo analysis uses
  (`openlens.tolerancing._apply_value`), so the two agree on what a tolerance
  does to a design - and every operand type the Monte Carlo can randomise can
  be measured here. The draw is undone with the inverse delta, so the design
  is restored exactly.
- The operand types that cannot be perturbed - `FOCUS` (a compensator, not a
  geometric quantity) and `IRREGULARITY` (a fringe count whose radius mapping
  is not exactly reversible) - are reported in a warning instead of silently
  contributing zero.
- The dead `_get_param_value`/`_set_param_value` helpers are gone.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #636

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New test module `tests/test_robust_merit_coverage.py` (two of the four tests
fail on the unfixed code):

- `test_an_air_gap_tolerance_contributes` - the contribution equals the true
  merit change
- `test_a_decenter_tolerance_contributes`
- `test_the_design_is_restored_after_the_evaluation`
- `test_an_index_tolerance_is_measured`

Full local suite: `Ran 2624 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`, `black` clean,
`ruff` clean, `flake8` clean, `mypy` clean.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(optimizer): optimization reports success for physically impossible designs
body:
## Summary

`OptimizationResult.success` only checks that the variable values are inside
their bounds. It ignores the physical-constraint penalty computed by the same
merit function, so a design with a hard `1e8` geometry violation is returned
as `success=True` with the message "Converged". The GUI then displays
"Optimization Successful!" and enables applying the impossible design.

## Impact

- Users are told an unmanufacturable lens (here a negative edge thickness of
  -35 mm) converged successfully.
- Automation that trusts `success` will persist, export, or manufacture an
  invalid design.
- The reported `final_merit` (2.13e8) is visibly dominated by penalties, but
  neither the result nor the GUI treats that as failure.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.optimizer import (
    INFEASIBLE_MERIT, LensOptimizer, OptimizationTarget, OptimizationVariable,
)

system = OpticalSystem("impossible")
system.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=20.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-20.0,
                     thickness=5.0, diameter=40.0, refractive_index=1.5168))
print("edge thickness:", system.elements[0].lens.calculate_edge_thickness())

# Index cannot repair the rim, so every point in the box is invalid.
variables = [OptimizationVariable("n", 0, "refractive_index", 1.5168, 1.40, 1.60, 0.01)]
opt = LensOptimizer(system, variables,
                    [OptimizationTarget("focal_length", 100.0, 1.0, "target")])
print("hard penalty:", opt.merit_function._penalty_physical(system))
result = opt.optimize_simplex(max_iterations=60)
print("success=%s message=%r final_merit=%r" % (
    result.success, result.message, result.final_merit))
print("edge thickness of result:",
      result.optimized_system.elements[0].lens.calculate_edge_thickness())
print("hard penalty of result:",
      opt.merit_function._penalty_physical(result.optimized_system))
```

Output:

```
edge thickness: -35.0
hard penalty: 212602500.0
success=True message='Converged after 1 iterations' final_merit=212608866.3369721
edge thickness of result: -35.0
hard penalty of result: 212602500.0
```

`INFEASIBLE_MERIT` is `1e9`; this result is below it, so a simple
`final_merit >= INFEASIBLE_MERIT` test would not catch it.

## Root cause

- `openlens/optimizer.py:501` sets `best_valid` from variable bounds only.
- `openlens/optimizer.py:510` maps `success=best_valid` and `:518` picks the
  "converged" message from the same flag.
- `_penalty_physical()` (`openlens/optimizer.py:298-376`) has already
  computed the hard violations, but they are folded into the scalar merit and
  not exposed as feasibility.

## Expected behaviour

A result whose design has a hard physical violation reports `success=False`
with a message such as "Converged, but the design violates physical
constraints (negative edge thickness)", and the GUI does not claim success.
Soft constraint penalties should still be reported separately.

## Suggested fix

Make feasibility explicit: split `_penalty_physical()` into soft and hard
components (or add `_has_hard_violation(system)`), then set
`success = best_valid and not has_hard_violation(optimized_system)` and choose
the message accordingly. Add a regression test using a geometry that cannot be
repaired by the variables and assert `success is False`, plus a normal design
that still reports success.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): a design that cannot be made is not a success
nodes.body:
## Description

`OptimizationResult.success` only checked that the variable values were inside
their bounds. A design carrying a hard geometry penalty - a negative edge
thickness, vertices that cross, an element inside its neighbour - was returned
as `success=True` with the message "Converged", and the GUI showed
"Optimization Successful!" and offered to apply it:

```
success    : True
message    : Converged after 1 iterations
final_merit: 212608866.3369721
edge thickness of the returned design: -35.0 mm
```

## What changed

- `openlens/optimizer.py::MeritFunction.has_hard_violation` reuses the
  penalty the merit function already computes: a design that collects the
  hard penalty (now the named constant `MeritFunction.HARD_PENALTY`) cannot be
  made.
- `openlens/optimizer.py::LensOptimizer._finalize` reports `success=False`
  and says "Converged, but the design breaks a physical constraint (it cannot
  be made as it is)" for such a design. The out-of-bounds message is
  unchanged.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #637

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New test module `tests/test_optimizer_feasibility.py` (the impossible-design
test fails on the unfixed code):

- `test_an_impossible_design_is_not_a_success`
- `test_a_feasible_design_is_still_a_success`
- `test_a_design_outside_the_variable_box_is_still_reported_as_such`

`tests/test_optimizer_api.py` used a 50 mm lens with a 50 mm radius, whose rim
crosses itself; it now uses a lens that can be made, which is what the test
was about.

Full local suite: `Ran 2629 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`, `black` clean,
`ruff` clean, `flake8` clean, `mypy` clean.

title: bug(optimizer): negative initial_temperature skips annealing despite claiming to clamp
body:
## Summary

`optimize_simulated_annealing()` copies `initial_temperature` into
`temperature` before clamping non-positive values. For
`initial_temperature=-100` the parameter is clamped to `1e-6` (and the log says
so), but the loop variable `temperature` remains -100. The first iteration
then hits `if temperature < 1e-6: break`, so the run performs one greedy step
followed by local simplex refinement instead of simulated annealing. The API
accepts the value and reports success.

## Impact

- A caller asking for annealing with a negative (or zero) starting temperature
  silently gets a different algorithm, with far less exploration and a
  different result.
- The warning explicitly claims a clamp happened, which makes the behaviour
  hard to diagnose.
- The reported iteration counts mix one SA step with the local refinement,
  obscuring that annealing did not run.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.global_optimizer import GlobalOptimizer
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.optimizer import OptimizationTarget, OptimizationVariable

def system():
    s = OpticalSystem("sa")
    s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=70.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
                    thickness=5.0, diameter=20.0, refractive_index=1.5168))
    return s

variables = [OptimizationVariable("R1", 0, "radius_of_curvature_1", 70.0, 60.0, 200.0, 5.0)]
targets = [OptimizationTarget("focal_length", 100.0, 1.0, "target")]

class Recording(GlobalOptimizer):
    def __init__(self, *a, **k):
        super().__init__(*a, **k)
        self.calls = 0
        self.before_simplex = None
    def _evaluate_design(self, values):
        self.calls += 1
        return super()._evaluate_design(values)
    def optimize_simplex(self, *a, **k):
        self.before_simplex = self.calls
        return super().optimize_simplex(*a, **k)

for t0 in (-100.0, 100.0):
    opt = Recording(system(), variables, targets, seed=7)
    res = opt.optimize_simulated_annealing(max_iterations=20, initial_temperature=t0)
    print("T0=%6.1f annealing iterations=%2d total=%d message=%r" % (
        t0, opt.before_simplex - 1, res.iterations, res.message))
```

Output:

```
initial_temperature=-100.0 is not positive; clamping to a small positive value ...
T0=-100.0 annealing iterations= 1 total=26 message='SA Converged after 1 iterations + 25 local steps'
T0= 100.0 annealing iterations=20 total=46 message='SA Converged after 20 iterations + 26 local steps'
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/global_optimizer.py:110` assigns
  `temperature = initial_temperature` before validation.
- `openlens/global_optimizer.py:121-127` clamps only the local parameter
  `initial_temperature` to `1e-6`.
- `openlens/global_optimizer.py:200-201` immediately breaks because the loop
  variable is still negative.

## Expected behaviour

Either reject a non-positive initial temperature with a `ValueError`, or clamp
it before initialising the loop variable so the run performs the requested
number of annealing iterations with a well-defined schedule.

## Suggested fix

Move `temperature = initial_temperature` below the clamp (or assign
`temperature = max(initial_temperature, EPSILON)` once and use it for both the
schedule and the loop). Add a regression test asserting a negative
`initial_temperature` either raises or runs more than one annealing iteration,
and that the number of SA iterations matches `max_iterations` for a small run.

nodes.title: fix(optimizer): apply the annealed temperature clamp to the loop variable
nodes.body:
## Description

`optimize_simulated_annealing()` copied `initial_temperature` into
`temperature` **before** clamping a non-positive value. For
`initial_temperature=-100` the parameter was clamped to `1e-6` (and the log
said so), but the loop variable stayed `-100`, so the first iteration hit
`if temperature < 1e-6: break`. The caller got one greedy step plus local
simplex refinement instead of the requested annealing schedule, and the
reported iteration count obscured that annealing never ran.

## What changed

- **`openlens/global_optimizer.py`**
  - Initialise `temperature` *after* the clamp, so the schedule the warning
    describes is the schedule that runs. A zero/negative start now performs
    the full `max_iterations` annealing loop with the derived cooling factor
    (`1.0` at the floor).
- **`tests/test_global_optimizer_degenerate_configs.py`**
  - A counting subclass records how many evaluations happen before the local
    refinement: negative and zero starting temperatures must run all 20
    annealing iterations.
  - The existing "runs at all" guards stay.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #638

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2826 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Before the fix the reproduction reports
`annealing iterations=1 total=26`; after it reports
`annealing iterations=20 total=42` for `T0=-100` and `T0=0`.
