title: bug(physics): pressure conditioning is discarded by every ray-traced analysis
body:
## Summary

`EnvironmentalAnalyzer.apply_environment()` folds the ambient-pressure
correction into `lens.refractive_index`. Every ray-traced analysis, however,
calls `Lens.update_refractive_index(wavelength_nm=...)` before tracing, which
recomputes the catalog index at the reference pressure (1 atm) and overwrites
the conditioned value. A system conditioned to 2 atm therefore reports a
pressure-shifted EFL/BFL but traces bit-identically to 1 atm.

## Impact

- Pressure simulations are silently ignored by every traced analysis (spot
  diagram, PSF/MTF, paraxial focus, geometric analysis, aberration
  calculations), so the feature produces no usable result.
- The app is internally inconsistent: `get_system_focal_length()` and
  `calculate_back_focal_length()` see the conditioned index, while the tracer
  that is supposed to evaluate the same system does not.
- Users comparing "1 atm" and "2 atm" spot diagrams get identical numbers
  with no warning.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.analysis.environmental import EnvironmentalAnalyzer
from openlens.analysis.spot_diagram import SpotDiagram
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem

def system():
    s = OpticalSystem("BK7")
    s.add_lens(Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=50.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-50.0,
                    thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0, material="BK7",
                    refractive_index=1.5168))
    return s

nominal = system()
conditioned = EnvironmentalAnalyzer.apply_environment(nominal, 20.0, 2.0)
print("nominal   n=%.9f EFL=%.9f" % (nominal.elements[0].lens.refractive_index,
                                     nominal.get_system_focal_length()))
print("2 atm     n=%.9f EFL=%.9f" % (conditioned.elements[0].lens.refractive_index,
                                     conditioned.get_system_focal_length()))

s1 = SpotDiagram(nominal).trace_spot()
s2 = SpotDiagram(conditioned).trace_spot()
print("spot 1 atm: rms=%.12f geo=%.12f" % (s1["rms_radius"], s1["geo_radius"]))
print("spot 2 atm: rms=%.12f geo=%.12f" % (s2["rms_radius"], s2["geo_radius"]))
print("identical:", s1["rms_radius"] == s2["rms_radius"])

lens = conditioned.elements[0].lens
lens.update_refractive_index(wavelength_nm=550.0)
print("index after a wavelength update: %.16f" % lens.refractive_index)
```

Output:

```
nominal   n=1.516800000 EFL=49.212999009
2 atm     n=1.516385416 EFL=49.252058496
spot 1 atm: rms=1.005334942212 geo=1.516902395070
spot 2 atm: rms=1.005334942212 geo=1.516902395070
identical: True
index after a wavelength update: 1.5167984379050088
```

The last line shows the 1 atm Sellmeier value reappearing after the
conditioning.

## Root cause

- `openlens/analysis/environmental.py:138-151` writes the pressure-corrected
  index into `lens.refractive_index`.
- `openlens/lens.py:507-512` (`update_refractive_index` for a catalog glass)
  re-derives the index from the material database at the lens' temperature and
  the reference pressure, discarding any pressure correction.
- The traced analyses call that method before tracing:
  `openlens/analysis/spot_diagram.py:88`, `openlens/analysis/paraxial.py:64`,
  `openlens/analysis/geometric.py:107`, `openlens/aberrations.py:312` and
  `:734`. They save and restore the old index afterwards, so the correction
  survives in the model but is not used by the trace.

## Expected behaviour

A system conditioned to a non-reference pressure traces with the conditioned
index, and the paraxial and traced results agree with each other.

## Suggested fix

Store the ambient pressure on the lens (e.g. `lens.pressure_atm`) and apply
the air-index correction inside `Lens.update_refractive_index()`, so every
consumer of the index gets the same value. Alternatively keep the corrected
index in a dedicated field that the tracer uses. Add a regression test that
traces a system conditioned to 2 atm and asserts the spot radius differs from
the 1 atm trace and that the traced focal shift matches the paraxial one.

nodes.title: fix(physics): keep pressure conditioning through traced analyses
nodes.body:
## Description

`EnvironmentalAnalyzer.apply_environment()` folds the ambient-pressure air
correction into `lens.refractive_index`. Every ray-traced analysis then calls
`Lens.update_refractive_index(wavelength_nm=...)` before tracing, which
recomputed the catalog index relative to air at the reference pressure and
overwrote the conditioned value. A system conditioned to 2 atm reported a
pressure-shifted EFL/BFL but traced bit-identically to 1 atm:

```text
1 atm spot rms_radius: 1.005323... mm
2 atm spot rms_radius: 1.005323... mm   <- same numbers, no warning
```

The feature produced no usable result in the spot diagram, PSF/MTF, paraxial
focus, geometric analysis or aberration calculations.

## What changed

- **`openlens/air_index.py`** (new) - the Edlen air-index formula and its
  ideal-gas scaling, extracted so the model can use it without importing the
  analysis package (which imports `OpticalSystem`, so importing back from
  `Lens` would be a cycle).
- **`openlens/lens.py`**
  - `Lens` gains `pressure_atm` (default 1 atm), serialized with the lens.
  - `update_refractive_index()` resolves the catalog/model index at the
    reference pressure and then applies
    `n_air(T, 1 atm) / n_air(T, pressure_atm)` before storing it. The search
    only runs when a value was actually recomputed, so a lookup failure keeps
    the already-corrected index.
  - `refractive_index_at()` applies the same correction, so coating and other
    non-mutating consumers agree.
- **`openlens/analysis/environmental.py`**
  - `apply_environment()` records the pressure on each lens and lets
    `update_refractive_index(temperature=...)` do the correction, instead of
    multiplying the index by hand and storing a value that the next refresh
    would discard.
  - `calculate_air_index()` keeps its public API and delegates to the new
    module.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #639

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2780 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Six new tests in `tests/test_pressure_traced_analysis.py`, all failing on the
unfixed code:

- `test_a_conditioned_system_traces_to_a_different_focus` - the 2 atm trace
  finds a focus shift of more than a micron (it was 0.0 before).
- `test_the_conditioned_index_survives_a_wavelength_update` - the exact
  regression: the index used to revert by 4.1e-4.
- `test_reindexing_matches_the_pressure_formula` - the refreshed index equals
  `catalog(550 nm) * n_air(1 atm) / n_air(2 atm)`.
- `test_the_conditioned_lens_records_its_pressure`
- `test_the_original_system_is_not_conditioned`
- `test_pressure_round_trips_through_serialization`

Existing environmental tests (`test_pressure_effect_on_index`,
`test_air_gap_expansion`, the housing-CTE tests) pass unchanged on the
rebased tree.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(physics): condition_at_temperature misuses the lens temperature field as an expansion marker
body:
## Summary

`EnvironmentalAnalyzer.condition_at_temperature()` uses the lens' `temperature`
field as a marker meaning "this lens has already been thermally expanded".
That field actually means "the index was last computed at this temperature".
The result is three different wrong behaviours:

1. A lens built with `Lens.for_material("BK7", temperature=120)` (120 °C
   index, 20 °C geometry) is returned unchanged by
   `condition_at_temperature(lens, 120)`, so the CTE expansion never happens
   and the focal length is off by 0.069 mm.
2. A custom glass (no catalog entry) never has its `temperature` field
   updated, so conditioning it to 120 °C twice expands the geometry twice
   (`R1` 100.071 -> 100.142 mm).
3. Conditioning an expanded lens back to 20 °C is a no-op, so the lens can
   never be brought back to reference conditions.

## Impact

- The thermal-analysis feature gives wrong answers depending on how the lens
  was created, and it can silently double-apply the expansion.
- Users cannot undo a conditioning step, so the environment model is not
  reversible.
- The "already conditioned" shortcut also hides a real physical difference:
  index at 120 °C with 20 °C geometry is a different part than a fully
  conditioned one.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.analysis.environmental import EnvironmentalAnalyzer as E
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem

shape = dict(radius_of_curvature_1=100.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0,
             thickness=5.0, diameter=40.0)

# (a) index at 120 C, geometry at 20 C
lens_built_hot = Lens.for_material("BK7", 587.6, 120.0, **shape)
returned = E.condition_at_temperature(lens_built_hot, 120.0)
print("n=%r temperature=%s R1=%.9f thickness=%.9f" % (
    lens_built_hot.refractive_index, lens_built_hot.temperature,
    lens_built_hot.radius_of_curvature_1, lens_built_hot.thickness))
print("same object returned:", returned is lens_built_hot)

nominal = Lens(material="BK7", **shape)
expanded = E.condition_at_temperature(nominal, 120.0)
print("same request from a 20 C lens: R1=%.9f" % expanded.radius_of_curvature_1)
print("focal lengths: unchanged-return %.9f vs expanded %.9f" % (
    returned.calculate_focal_length(), expanded.calculate_focal_length()))

# (b) custom glass conditioned twice
custom = Lens(material="Custom", refractive_index=1.7, **shape)
system = OpticalSystem("custom")
system.add_lens(custom)
hot = E.condition_at_temperature(system, 120.0)
hot_again = E.condition_at_temperature(hot, 120.0)
print("once : R1=%.9f thickness=%.9f temperature field=%s" % (
    hot.elements[0].lens.radius_of_curvature_1, hot.elements[0].lens.thickness,
    hot.elements[0].lens.temperature))
print("twice: R1=%.9f thickness=%.9f temperature field=%s" % (
    hot_again.elements[0].lens.radius_of_curvature_1, hot_again.elements[0].lens.thickness,
    hot_again.elements[0].lens.temperature))

# (c) conditioning the expanded copy back to 20 C
back = E.condition_at_temperature(hot, 20.0)
print("back to 20 C: R1=%.9f same object=%s" % (
    back.elements[0].lens.radius_of_curvature_1, back is hot))
```

Output:

```
n=1.5169957940737389 temperature=120.0 R1=100.000000000 thickness=5.000000000
same object returned: True
same request from a 20 C lens: R1=100.071000000
focal lengths: unchanged-return 97.543663465 vs expanded 97.612919466
once : R1=100.071000000 thickness=5.003550000 temperature field=20.0
twice: R1=100.142050410 thickness=5.007102520 temperature field=20.0
back to 20 C: R1=100.071000000 same object=True
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/analysis/environmental.py:204-214` returns the target unchanged
  when `lens.temperature` already equals the requested temperature.
- `openlens/analysis/environmental.py:131-135` only calls
  `update_refractive_index(temperature=...)` when the glass has a catalog
  entry or is a model glass, so for a custom glass the `temperature` field is
  never updated and the marker stays at its old value.
- `openlens/lens.py:485-486` is the only place that writes
  `lens.temperature`, and `Lens.for_material(...)`
  (`openlens/lens.py:549-576`) sets it without expanding the geometry.
- `apply_environment()` scales the geometry of the object it is given
  (`openlens/analysis/environmental.py:112-124`), so applying it to an
  already-expanded lens expands it again.

## Expected behaviour

Conditioning is idempotent and reversible: conditioning a lens to 120 °C
always produces the same 120 °C geometry, and conditioning it back to 20 °C
restores the reference geometry. The "already conditioned" shortcut must be
based on the geometry state, not on the index's temperature field.

## Suggested fix

Track the thermal state of the lens explicitly (for example
`lens.thermal_state_temperature`, set by `apply_environment()`), and expand
relative to a stored reference temperature so the operation is idempotent and
reversible. Always call `update_refractive_index(temperature=...)` so the
index and the geometry agree, including for custom glasses. Add regression
tests for: conditioning twice gives the same geometry, conditioning back
restores the original, and a lens built at 120 °C is expanded when
conditioned to 120 °C.

nodes.title: fix(physics): track thermal geometry state separately from index temperature
nodes.body:
## Description

`EnvironmentalAnalyzer.condition_at_temperature()` used `Lens.temperature` -
the temperature at which the *refractive index* was last resolved - as a
marker meaning "this lens has already been thermally expanded". Those are
different states, and the conflation produced three wrong behaviours:

```text
Lens.for_material("BK7", 587.6, 120.0, ...)   index at 120 C, geometry at 20 C
condition_at_temperature(lens, 120)            returned unchanged -> CTE
                                               expansion skipped (EFL off 0.069 mm)
custom glass, conditioned to 120 twice          temperature never updated, so the
                                               geometry expanded twice:
                                               R1 100.071 -> 100.142 mm
condition a 120 C copy back to 20 C             no-op; R1 stayed at 100.071 mm
```

The "already conditioned" shortcut was based on the index field instead of
the geometry state.

## What changed

- **`openlens/lens.py`**
  - `Lens` gains `thermal_state_temperature`, the temperature the *geometry*
    is valid at (default 20 C). It is distinct from `temperature` (the index
    state) and is serialized so a reloaded conditioned model is not expanded
    again.
- **`openlens/optical_system.py`**
  - The system carries the same state for the housing/air-gap geometry,
    serialized with the system.
- **`openlens/analysis/environmental.py`**
  - `apply_environment()` expands relative to the recorded state through
    `_thermal_scale()`: `(1 + a(T_target - T_ref)) / (1 + a(T_state - T_ref))`.
    Both endpoints are expressed against the reference geometry, so
    20 -> 120 -> 20 restores the original length and 120 -> 120 is a no-op.
  - It always calls `update_refractive_index(temperature=...)`, including for
    custom glasses: the index is kept when there is no catalog model, but the
    field now agrees with the conditioned geometry.
  - `condition_at_temperature()` returns the original only when the geometry
    state, the index temperature and (for a system) the housing state are all
    already at the target.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #640

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2787 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Seven new tests in `tests/test_environmental_conditioning_state.py`:

- `test_a_lens_built_at_the_target_temperature_is_expanded` - fails before:
  the 120 C-index lens was returned unchanged.
- `test_conditioning_twice_gives_the_same_geometry` - fails before: a custom
  glass expanded twice (`assertIs` and the 100.071 vs 100.142 comparison).
- `test_conditioning_back_restores_the_reference_geometry` - fails before:
  20 C conditioning was a no-op, leaving R1 at 100.071 mm.
- `test_custom_glass_updates_its_temperature_field` - fails before: the field
  stayed at 20 C.
- `test_conditioning_back_restores_the_air_gaps` - housing gaps return to the
  reference length.
- `test_the_thermal_state_survives_serialization` - lens and system state.
- `test_reference_conditions_still_return_the_original` - guard for the
  unchanged fast path.

The existing `tests/test_environmental.py` suite (pressure, air gaps, housing
CTE) and the pressure-conditioning tests from #639 pass unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(physics): lateral color is a bundle-centroid difference, not the documented chief-ray value
body:
## Summary

`ChromaticAnalyzer.analyze_lens()` documents lateral color as the "chief-ray
image-height difference between the extreme wavelengths", but the
implementation returns the separation of the *centroids* of two hexapolar
pupil bundles. The centroid of a pupil bundle is not the chief ray: it mixes
in coma and spherical aberration, so the reported lateral color depends on the
aperture and is not the quantity the docstring promises.

For the same BK7 singlet the true chief-ray lateral colour (F-C) is
0.00300 mm and does not depend on the aperture, while `analyze_lens()` reports
0.0052 mm at 5 mm diameter, 0.0141 mm at 10 mm, 0.0536 mm at 25 mm and
0.0076 mm at 40 mm - an 18x error at 25 mm diameter and non-monotonic in the
aperture.

## Impact

- Lateral colour is used for chromatic tolerance and correction decisions; a
  value that scales with the stop is not a usable metric.
- The public docstring is wrong, so callers have no way to know the number is
  a centroid difference.
- For an off-axis system the centroid difference is dominated by coma, so the
  "lateral color" can even change sign with aperture.

## Reproduction

The chief-ray reference (traced by hand through the lens vertex):

```python
chief-ray lateral color F-C = 0.002995446 mm (aperture independent)
```

The analyzer on the same lens:

```python
from openlens.chromatic_analyzer import ChromaticAnalyzer

BASE = dict(radius1=50.0, radius2=-50.0, thickness=5.0, material="BK7")
analyzer = ChromaticAnalyzer()
for diameter in (5.0, 10.0, 25.0, 40.0):
    result = analyzer.analyze_lens(dict(BASE, diameter=diameter),
                                    wavelengths=[486.1, 587.6, 656.3], num_rays=37)
    print("diameter=%5.1f mm -> lateral_color=%.9f mm" % (diameter, result.lateral_color))
```

Output:

```
diameter=  5.0 mm -> lateral_color=0.005167561 mm
diameter= 10.0 mm -> lateral_color=0.014117635 mm
diameter= 25.0 mm -> lateral_color=0.053649953 mm
diameter= 40.0 mm -> lateral_color=0.007641923 mm
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py:118-119` (public docstring) and `:244-249`
  (helper docstring) describe a chief-ray image-height difference.
- `openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py:286-290` takes `spot["centroid"]` from
  `SpotDiagram.trace_spot()` and returns the separation of the two centroids.
  `SpotDiagram` traces a hexapolar bundle and reports the centroid of the
  traced rays; it does not expose a chief ray.

## Expected behaviour

Lateral colour is the chief-ray image-height difference between the extreme
wavelengths at the reference field, and it must not depend on the aperture
stop. Either the implementation or the documentation has to change.

## Suggested fix

Trace the chief ray explicitly (a single ray through the pupil centre at
`REFERENCE_FIELD_DEG`, intersected with the reference image plane) and use
its height, or rename the metric to reflect that it is a bundle-centroid
difference and document the aperture dependence. Add a regression test that
the reported lateral colour is (nearly) independent of the lens diameter and
matches a hand-traced chief-ray value.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): measure lateral color from the chief ray
nodes.body:
## Description

`ChromaticAnalyzer._lateral_color()` documented and reported "chief-ray image-height
difference", but it traced two hexapolar bundles and subtracted their **centroids**.
A centroid mixes in coma and spherical aberration, so the reported lateral colour
grew with the aperture for the same lens:

```text
BK7 singlet, 5 deg field      lateral_color
D =  5 mm                     0.0052 mm
D = 10 mm                     0.0141 mm
D = 25 mm                     0.0536 mm
chief ray (aperture free)     0.0030 mm
```

Lateral colour is a property of the chief ray, so it must not move when the stop
is opened.

## What changed

- **`openlens/analysis/spot_diagram.py`**
  - Added `SpotDiagram.trace_chief_ray()`. It builds the ray through the centre of
    the entrance pupil at the requested field angle and wavelength and intersects
    it with the reference image plane, so the result carries no aperture-dependent
    aberrations.
- **`openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py`**
  - `_lateral_color()` now traces that single chief ray at each extreme
    wavelength instead of two `trace_spot()` bundles and returns the distance
    between the two image heights. It no longer needs the reference wavelength or
    ray count.
- **`tests/test_chromatic_analyzer.py`**
  - Added `TestLateralColorIsTheChiefRay`: the value is checked against a
    hand-traced chief ray and is identical across 5, 10, 25 and 40 mm apertures.
  - Corrected the old bound, which was derived from `|f_F - f_C| * tan(theta)`
    and therefore encoded the centroid behaviour, to the physical 0.002995 mm.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #641

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2789 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

The new aperture test fails on the old implementation at every diameter except
the value it happened to match (the centroid separation changed by two orders of
magnitude over the same range). The hand-traced test pins the image-height
difference to the ray intersection.

- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

title: bug: get_all_metrics mixes an overridden pupil and wavelength with the lens geometry
body:
## Summary

`PerformanceMetrics.get_all_metrics()` accepts overrides for the entrance
pupil diameter and the wavelength, but only forwards the pupil override to
`calculate_f_number()`. `numerical_aperture`, `airy_disk_radius_mm` and
`rayleigh_limit_urad` keep using the lens' mechanical diameter and the lens'
stored wavelength. The returned dictionary therefore describes two different
apertures and one fixed wavelength at the same time.

With a 25 mm lens and `entrance_pupil_diameter=10`, the same result contains
`f_number = 4.92` (f/10 mm) but `numerical_aperture = 0.2462` (equivalent
f/2.03) and an Airy radius that belongs to the 25 mm lens. `resolution_um`
and `airy_disk_radius_mm` differ by exactly the factor 25/10 = 2.5, and
`rayleigh_limit_urad` stays at 28.6749 urad for 400, 550 and 700 nm because
the wavelength override is never passed to it.

## Impact

- The metrics bundle is internally inconsistent, so any report, dashboard or
  comparison built from it mixes apertures and wavelengths.
- The wavelength override silently does not apply to the angular Rayleigh
  limit, which is the metric most likely to be quoted next to a wavelength.
- These values are surfaced in the GUI performance tab, so users see numbers
  that do not correspond to the optics they are looking at.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.performance_metrics import PerformanceMetrics

lens = Lens(name="singlet", radius_of_curvature_1=50.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-50.0,
            thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0, material="BK7")
metrics = PerformanceMetrics(lens)

m = metrics.get_all_metrics(entrance_pupil_diameter=10.0, wavelength=550.0)
na = m["numerical_aperture"]
print("f_number           = %.4f" % m["f_number"])
print("numerical_aperture = %.4f (equivalent f/# = %.4f)" % (na, 1.0 / (2.0 * na)))
print("resolution_um      = %.4f" % m["resolution_um"])
print("airy_disk_radius   = %.4f um" % (m["airy_disk_radius_mm"] * 1000.0))
print("resolution / airy  = %.3f" % (m["resolution_um"] / (m["airy_disk_radius_mm"] * 1000.0)))

for wavelength in (400.0, 550.0, 700.0):
    m = metrics.get_all_metrics(wavelength=wavelength)
    print("wavelength=%5.1f -> resolution_um=%.4f airy=%.4f um rayleigh_urad=%.4f" % (
        wavelength, m["resolution_um"], m["airy_disk_radius_mm"] * 1000.0,
        m["rayleigh_limit_urad"]))
```

Output:

```
f_number           = 4.9213
numerical_aperture = 0.2462 (equivalent f/# = 2.0310)
resolution_um      = 3.3022
airy_disk_radius   = 1.3209 um
resolution / airy  = 2.500
wavelength=400.0 -> resolution_um=0.9606 airy=0.9606 um rayleigh_urad=28.6749
wavelength=550.0 -> resolution_um=1.3209 airy=1.3209 um rayleigh_urad=28.6749
wavelength=700.0 -> resolution_um=1.6811 airy=1.6811 um rayleigh_urad=28.6749
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/performance_metrics.py:365` forwards the pupil override to
  `calculate_f_number()` only.
- `openlens/performance_metrics.py:366` calls `calculate_numerical_aperture()`
  without the override; that method (`:61-90`) derives the NA from the lens'
  own diameter.
- `openlens/performance_metrics.py:385` calls
  `calculate_airy_disk_radius(wavelength)`, which (`:241-260`) uses the lens'
  diameter for `D`.
- `openlens/performance_metrics.py:384` calls
  `calculate_resolution_rayleigh()`, which (`:163-183`) has no wavelength
  parameter at all and falls back to the lens' stored wavelength or 550 nm.

## Expected behaviour

All metrics in one bundle refer to the same aperture and the same
wavelength. Overriding the entrance pupil or the wavelength must change every
metric that depends on it.

## Suggested fix

Thread `entrance_pupil_diameter` and `wavelength` through
`calculate_numerical_aperture()`, `calculate_airy_disk_radius()` and
`calculate_resolution_rayleigh()`, and give the last one a `wavelength`
argument. Add a regression test asserting that the NA and the Airy radius
correspond to the overridden pupil, and that `rayleigh_limit_urad` scales with
1/lambda.

nodes.title: fix(analysis): thread pupil and wavelength overrides through all metrics
nodes.body:
## Description

`PerformanceMetrics.get_all_metrics()` accepts `entrance_pupil_diameter` and
`wavelength`, but only forwarded the pupil to `calculate_f_number()`. Every
other derived metric ignored both overrides, so one result bundle described
two different optical systems:

```text
lens: f = 50.6 mm, mechanical diameter 25 mm
get_all_metrics(entrance_pupil_diameter=10.0, wavelength=400.0)

f_number              f/5.06     (overridden pupil)
numerical_aperture    0.246      (25 mm mechanical diameter)
airy_disk_radius_mm   f/2.5 value (25 mm mechanical diameter)
resolution_um         f/2.5 value (25 mm mechanical diameter)
rayleigh_limit_urad   28.6749    (400, 550 and 700 nm all identical)
```

The NA did not match the f-number cone, and the Rayleigh limit was independent
of the requested wavelength.

## What changed

- **`openlens/performance_metrics.py`**
  - `calculate_numerical_aperture()` and `calculate_airy_disk_radius()` accept
    an optional `entrance_pupil_diameter`.
  - `calculate_resolution_rayleigh()` accepts an optional `wavelength`.
  - `get_all_metrics()` threads both overrides into all of them.
  - Defaults are unchanged, so callers that pass neither keep the previous
    behaviour.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #642

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2793 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Four tests in `tests/test_performance_metrics.py`:

- `test_the_numerical_aperture_uses_the_overridden_pupil` - NA equals
  `sin(atan(D / 2f))` for the requested pupil.
- `test_the_airy_radius_uses_the_overridden_pupil` - the Airy radius uses the
  same pupil.
- `test_the_angular_rayleigh_limit_scales_with_the_wavelength` - 400 nm and
  800 nm differ by exactly 2x.
- `test_the_bundle_describes_one_aperture` - the f-number, NA, Rayleigh spot
  estimate and Airy radius in the same bundle agree with each other.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(physics): chromatic analyzer applies dn/dT but no thermal expansion, so the thermal defocus sign disagrees with the environmental model
body:
## Summary

`ChromaticAnalyzer.analyze_lens(..., temperature_c=...)` applies the
temperature only to the refractive index. It does not apply the coefficient of
thermal expansion to the geometry, even though the application's own thermal
model (`EnvironmentalAnalyzer.condition_at_temperature`) does. At 120 °C the
expansion dominates the index change, so the two models predict defocus with
opposite signs: the analyzer reports a focal length *decrease* (49.1946 mm)
while the conditioned lens reports an *increase* (49.2295 mm).

## Impact

- Two temperature analyses in the same application disagree about the sign and
  the size of the thermal defocus.
- A user who checks a design at 120 °C with the chromatic analyzer and then
  with the thermal analysis gets contradictory results.
- The analyzer's `temperature_c` parameter is documented as "Temperature in
  Celsius" with no hint that only the index is affected.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.analysis.environmental import EnvironmentalAnalyzer
from openlens.chromatic_analyzer import ChromaticAnalyzer
from openlens.lens import Lens

PARAMS = dict(radius1=50.0, radius2=-50.0, thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0, material="BK7")
analyzer = ChromaticAnalyzer()

def conditioned_focal_length(temperature_c):
    lens = Lens(radius_of_curvature_1=PARAMS["radius1"], radius_of_curvature_2=PARAMS["radius2"],
                thickness=PARAMS["thickness"], diameter=PARAMS["diameter"],
                material=PARAMS["material"])
    return EnvironmentalAnalyzer.condition_at_temperature(lens, temperature_c).calculate_focal_length()

for t in (20.0, 120.0):
    print("T=%5.1f C: analyzer f=%.7f  conditioned f=%.7f" % (
        t,
        analyzer.analyze_lens(PARAMS, wavelengths=[587.6], temperature_c=t).focal_lengths[0],
        conditioned_focal_length(t)))
```

Output:

```
T= 20.0 C: analyzer f=49.2131461  conditioned f=49.2129990
T=120.0 C: analyzer f=49.1945742  conditioned f=49.2295024
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py:159-173` builds the lens for each
  wavelength with the nominal `R1`, `R2` and `d` and only changes the
  refractive index through
  `material_db.get_refractive_index(material_name, wavelength, temperature_c)`.
- `openlens/analysis/environmental.py:112-135` is the full model: it scales
  the radii, the thickness and the diameter by `1 + alpha * dT` and then
  updates the index.

## Expected behaviour

Both modules answer the same question ("what does this lens do at 120 °C?")
the same way, or the chromatic analyzer states clearly that it models the
index only.

## Suggested fix

Apply the CTE to the geometry in the chromatic analyzer as well (reuse the
scaling from `EnvironmentalAnalyzer.apply_environment()` so there is a single
implementation), or rename the parameter to something like
`index_temperature_c` and document that geometry expansion is excluded.
Add a regression test comparing the analyzer's focal length with the
conditioned lens's focal length over a temperature range.

nodes.title: fix(chromatic): condition the analyzer's geometry for temperature too
nodes.body:
## Description

`ChromaticAnalyzer.analyze_lens(..., temperature_c=...)` applied dn/dT to the
refractive index but left `R1`, `R2`, thickness and diameter at their nominal
values. The rest of the application conditions the whole lens: at 120 °C the
CTE expansion dominates the index change, so the analyzer predicted a
focal-length *decrease* while `EnvironmentalAnalyzer` predicted an *increase*.

## What changed

- **`openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py`**
  - Added `_build_lens()`, which builds a wavelength's lens and routes it
    through `EnvironmentalAnalyzer.condition_at_temperature()`.
  - Both the per-wavelength focal-length loop and `_lateral_color()` use it, so
    the CTE expansion has one implementation and the two analyses agree.
  - The analyzer's catalog index remains authoritative for the requested
    wavelength; conditioning only supplies the geometry.
- **`tests/test_chromatic_thermal_expansion.py`** (new)
  - At 60 °C and 120 °C the analyzer's focal length matches the conditioned
    lens exactly (six decimal places).
  - The heated focal length is longer than at 20 °C (expansion dominates).
  - Lateral colour at 120 °C is finite and uses the conditioned geometry.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #643

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
  - Before: the 60 °C and 120 °C comparisons fail, and lateral colour at
    120 °C returns NaN.
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2827 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100`, `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Reproduction after the fix:

```
T= 20.0 C: analyzer f=49.2131461  conditioned f=49.2129990  diff=1.47e-04
T= 60.0 C: analyzer f=49.2209653  conditioned f=49.2209653  diff=0.00e+00
T=120.0 C: analyzer f=49.2295024  conditioned f=49.2295024  diff=0.00e+00
```

The 20 °C difference is the pre-existing catalog lookup difference between the
two entry points, not a thermal effect.

- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

title: bug: axial chromatic aberration depends on the order of the wavelength list
body:
## Summary

`ChromaticAnalyzer.analyze_lens()` computes `focal_shift` as
`max(focal_lengths) - min(focal_lengths)`, but `axial_chromatic` as
`abs(focal_lengths[0] - focal_lengths[-1])`, i.e. it depends on the order in
which the caller happened to list the wavelengths. The `wavelengths` argument
is documented as an arbitrary list with no ordering requirement, so the same
three wavelengths produce different axial chromatic aberrations depending on
their order: `[F, d, C]` gives 0.754 mm, `[d, F, C]` gives 0.234 mm, while
`focal_shift` stays at 0.754 mm in both cases.

## Impact

- A physical quantity silently depends on an argument's ordering, which makes
  the metric untrustworthy and hard to compare between runs or tools.
- `axial_chromatic` and `focal_shift` are reported side by side in the result
  and disagree for the same data, which is confusing at best.
- The value is used for chromatic correction decisions and tolerances.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.chromatic_analyzer import ChromaticAnalyzer

PARAMS = dict(radius1=50.0, radius2=-50.0, thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0, material="BK7")
analyzer = ChromaticAnalyzer()

for label, wavelengths in (("[F, d, C]", [486.1, 587.6, 656.3]),
                           ("[d, F, C]", [587.6, 486.1, 656.3])):
    result = analyzer.analyze_lens(PARAMS, wavelengths=wavelengths, num_rays=11)
    print("%s -> axial_chromatic=%.6f mm  focal_shift=%.6f mm" % (
        label, result.axial_chromatic_aberration, result.focal_shift))
```

Output:

```
[F, d, C] -> axial_chromatic=0.754021 mm  focal_shift=0.754021 mm
[d, F, C] -> axial_chromatic=0.234296 mm  focal_shift=0.754021 mm
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py:200` uses the order-independent
  `max(...) - min(...)` for `focal_shift`.
- `openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py:201` uses
  `abs(focal_lengths[0] - focal_lengths[-1])` for `axial_chromatic`, i.e. the
  first and last entries of the caller-supplied list.
- The lateral-colour helper (`openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py:206-215`) has the
  same dependency: it uses `wavelengths[0]`, `wavelengths[-1]` and the middle
  element as the reference.

## Expected behaviour

The reported axial chromatic aberration does not depend on the order of the
wavelength list, and the extremes used for the lateral colour are the
shortest and longest wavelengths regardless of the input order.

## Suggested fix

Sort (or select the min/max of) the wavelengths internally and use
`max(focal_lengths) - min(focal_lengths)` for the axial colour as well, and
select the extreme wavelengths by value rather than by position. Add a
regression test that the result is identical for permuted wavelength lists.

nodes.title: fix(chromatic): select the wavelength extremes by value, not list position
nodes.body:
## Description

`analyze_lens()` documents `wavelengths` as an arbitrary list, but computed
axial colour from `focal_lengths[0] - focal_lengths[-1]` and passed
`wavelengths[0]`, `wavelengths[-1]` and the positionally middle image plane to
the lateral-colour trace. Permuting the same three wavelengths changed axial
colour from 0.754021 mm to 0.234296 mm while `focal_shift` stayed at
0.754021 mm.

## What changed

- **`openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py`**
  - Sort the wavelength indices once and use the shortest/longest values for
    the lateral-colour trace and the middle **sorted** wavelength's image
    plane.
  - `axial_chromatic` is now the order-independent `max - min`, i.e. the same
    value as `focal_shift`.
- **`tests/test_chromatic_analyzer.py`**
  - All six permutations of `[F, d, C]` produce identical axial colour, focal
    shift and lateral colour.
  - `axial_chromatic_aberration` equals `focal_shift` for a permuted list.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #644

    `[F, d, C]`, and lateral colour changes with the middle entry.

title: bug: chromatic analyzer leaks ZeroDivisionError on unknown material and single-point sweeps
body:
## Summary

Two public methods of `ChromaticAnalyzer` raise a raw `ZeroDivisionError` on
edge inputs where the sibling methods raise a descriptive `ValueError`:

- `calculate_partial_dispersion("NOT_A_GLASS")` divides by `n_F - n_C`
  without the guard that `calculate_abbe_number()` uses for the same material.
- `plot_chromatic_focal_shift(..., num_points=1)` divides by `num_points - 1`
  without validating `num_points >= 2`.

## Impact

- Callers cannot handle the errors uniformly: `calculate_abbe_number` gives
  an actionable message, `calculate_partial_dispersion` gives a bare
  `ZeroDivisionError` for the identical input.
- A GUI or script that guards against `ValueError` still crashes with an
  unexpected exception type.
- The failure modes are reachable from ordinary use (an unknown material name,
  a single-point sweep).

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.chromatic_analyzer import ChromaticAnalyzer

analyzer = ChromaticAnalyzer()
params = dict(radius1=50.0, radius2=-50.0, thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0, material="BK7")

for label, call in (
    ("calculate_abbe_number('NOT_A_GLASS')",
     lambda: analyzer.calculate_abbe_number("NOT_A_GLASS")),
    ("calculate_partial_dispersion('NOT_A_GLASS')",
     lambda: analyzer.calculate_partial_dispersion("NOT_A_GLASS")),
    ("plot_chromatic_focal_shift(num_points=1)",
     lambda: analyzer.plot_chromatic_focal_shift(params, num_points=1)),
):
    try:
        call()
    except Exception as exc:
        print("%s:\n   %s: %s" % (label, type(exc).__name__, exc))
```

Output:

```
calculate_abbe_number('NOT_A_GLASS'):
   ValueError: Material 'NOT_A_GLASS' has no dispersion between the F and C lines (n_F - n_C = 0.0); its Abbe number is undefined.
calculate_partial_dispersion('NOT_A_GLASS'):
   ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero
plot_chromatic_focal_shift(num_points=1):
   ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py:326` returns
  `(n_x - n_y) / (n_F - n_C)` with no zero-dispersion check, unlike
  `openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py:305-313`.
- `openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py:420` computes
  `wl_min + (wl_max - wl_min) * i / (num_points - 1)` without validating
  `num_points`.

## Expected behaviour

Both methods validate their inputs and raise `ValueError` with a message that
says what to fix, consistent with the rest of the class.

## Suggested fix

Reuse the dispersion check from `calculate_abbe_number()` in
`calculate_partial_dispersion()` (extract a small helper), and validate
`num_points >= 2` in `plot_chromatic_focal_shift()`. Add tests for the
unknown-material and single-point cases.

nodes.title: fix(chromatic): raise ValueError for undefined dispersion and bad sweeps
nodes.body:
## Description

Two public methods of `ChromaticAnalyzer` leaked a raw `ZeroDivisionError`
where the sibling methods raise a descriptive `ValueError`:

- `calculate_partial_dispersion("NOT_A_GLASS")` divided by `n_F - n_C` without
  the zero-dispersion guard that `calculate_abbe_number()` uses.
- `plot_chromatic_focal_shift(..., num_points=1)` divided by `num_points - 1`;
  zero and negative counts silently returned an empty sweep.

## What changed

- **`openlens/chromatic_analyzer.py`**
  - Extracted `_f_to_c_dispersion()`, which performs the `1e-12` guard and
    names the requested quantity in the message. `calculate_abbe_number()` and
    `calculate_partial_dispersion()` both use it.
  - `plot_chromatic_focal_shift()` requires `num_points >= 2` and raises
    `ValueError` with the offending count otherwise.
- **`tests/test_chromatic_analyzer.py`**
  - A flat material and an unknown material raise `ValueError` mentioning
    partial dispersion.
  - `num_points` of 1, 0 and -1 raise; 2 still returns a two-point sweep.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #645

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
  - Before: unknown material and `num_points=1` raise `ZeroDivisionError`;
    `num_points` 0/-1 return empty lists.

title: bug: CLI lens editor aborts with an uncaught ValidationError on an invalid lens name
body:
## Summary

`LensManager.modify_lens()` validates the new lens name with
`validate_lens_name()` but does not catch the `ValidationError` it can raise.
The surrounding handler only catches `(ValueError, IndexError)`, and
`ValidationError` derives from `Exception`, so a name longer than 100
characters aborts the whole CLI with a traceback. The create path
(`create_lens()`) handles the same error correctly.

## Impact

- A trivial input error (a long name) kills the interactive session with an
  unhandled exception instead of a message.
- The exception escapes `main()` as well, so the CLI terminates instead of
  returning to the menu.
- The GUI editor validates the same field, so only the CLI path is affected.

## Reproduction

```python
import builtins, os, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "/home/philip/Workspace/openLens")
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.lens_editor import LensManager
from openlens.validation import ValidationError

manager = LensManager(os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "cli.db"))
manager.lenses = [Lens(name="demo", radius_of_curvature_1=100.0,
                       radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0, thickness=5.0,
                       diameter=50.0, refractive_index=1.5168)]

answers = iter(["1", "x" * 101, "", "", "", "", "", "", ""])
builtins.input = lambda prompt="": next(answers)
try:
    manager.modify_lens()
    print("no crash")
except ValidationError as exc:
    print("uncaught ValidationError:", exc)
```

Output:

```
=== All Optical Lenses (1) ===
1. demo - BK7 (Biconvex) - f=97.58mm

Modifying: demo
(Press Enter to keep current value)
uncaught ValidationError: Name must be 100 characters or less
```

In the real CLI the traceback ends the program.

## Root cause

- `openlens/lens_editor.py:234` calls
  `lens.name = validate_lens_name(new_name)` with no `try/except`.
- `openlens/lens_editor.py:292` catches only `ValueError` and `IndexError`.
- `openlens/validation.py:33` defines `class ValidationError(Exception)`, so it
  is not a `ValueError`.
- By contrast `openlens/lens_editor.py:107-111` (create path) catches
  `ValidationError` and reports it.

## Expected behaviour

An invalid name is reported like every other invalid field ("invalid: Name
must be 100 characters or less") and the CLI returns to the menu with the
lens unchanged.

## Suggested fix

Wrap the name assignment in the same `try/except ValidationError` used by the
numeric fields, and catch `ValidationError` in the outer handler as a
safety net. Add a CLI test that feeds an over-long name and asserts the
process does not raise and the stored name is unchanged.

nodes.title: fix(cli): report an over-long lens name without ending the session
nodes.body:
## Description

`modify_lens()` validates a new lens name, but the surrounding handler caught
only `ValueError` and `IndexError`. `ValidationError` derives from `Exception`,
so a name over 100 characters escaped `modify_lens()` and `main()`, ending the
interactive CLI with a traceback. The `#647` restructure already validates the
name inside the per-field handler; the outer safety net was still missing.

## What changed

- **`openlens/lens_editor.py`**
  - The `modify_lens()` outer handler now catches
    `(ValueError, IndexError, ValidationError)`, so an unexpected validation
    error from any later step is reported as invalid input instead of ending
    the session.
- **`tests/test_cli_modify_lens_validation.py`**
  - An over-long name is refused: no exception, the stored name is unchanged
    and nothing is saved.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #646

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression test. With the pre-`#647` handler (no per-field catch
  and no `ValidationError` in the outer clause) the test fails with the
  escaping `ValidationError`; it passes now.

title: bug: CLI lens editor stores lenses that fail its own physical feasibility check
body:
## Summary

The CLI lens editor checks the physical feasibility of a lens when it is
created (`create_lens()` calls `check_physical_feasibility()`), but not when it
is modified. `modify_lens()` writes the new radii, thickness and diameter
straight into the lens, so the CLI can store - and persist to the database - a
lens whose surfaces intersect inside the clear aperture (edge thickness
-35 mm in the repro).

## Impact

- The library can contain lenses that the application's own create path
  refuses, so the CLI is not able to reproduce the invariants it enforces
  elsewhere.
- Downstream consumers (optimizers, mechanical design, tolerancing) treat the
  stored lens as valid; the optimizer's own merit function will score it
  hard-infeasible (1e8).
- The user is told "Lens updated successfully!" for a lens that cannot be
  made.

## Reproduction

```python
import builtins, os, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "/home/philip/Workspace/openLens")
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.lens_editor import LensManager
from openlens.validation import check_physical_feasibility

manager = LensManager(os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "cli.db"))
manager.lenses = [Lens(name="demo", radius_of_curvature_1=100.0,
                       radius_of_curvature_2=-100.0, thickness=5.0,
                       diameter=50.0, refractive_index=1.5168)]

# lens number -> name -> R1 -> R2 -> thickness -> diameter -> index -> type -> material
answers = iter(["1", "", "20", "-20", "5", "40", "1.5168", "", ""])
builtins.input = lambda prompt="": next(answers)
manager.modify_lens()

lens = manager.lenses[0]
print("stored: R1=%s R2=%s t=%s D=%s" % (lens.radius_of_curvature_1,
                                         lens.radius_of_curvature_2,
                                         lens.thickness, lens.diameter))
print("edge thickness:", lens.calculate_edge_thickness())
print("feasibility check says:", check_physical_feasibility(
    lens.radius_of_curvature_1, lens.radius_of_curvature_2,
    lens.thickness, lens.diameter))
print("saved to the database:", manager.save_lenses())
```

Output:

```
stored: R1=20.0 R2=-20.0 t=5.0 D=40.0
edge thickness: -35.0
feasibility check says: (False, 'Surfaces intersect within the clear aperture
(edge thickness -35.00mm <= 0). ...')
saved to the database: True
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/lens_editor.py:143-146` (create path) calls
  `check_physical_feasibility(r1, r2, thickness, diameter)` and refuses to
  store an infeasible lens.
- `openlens/lens_editor.py:236-276` (modify path) validates each field
  individually (`validate_radius`, `validate_thickness`, `validate_diameter`)
  but never re-checks the combination, and it applies each field as it is
  read, so a partially applied edit is possible as well.

## Expected behaviour

The modify path enforces the same cross-parameter feasibility rule as the
create path, applies the edit atomically (all fields or none), and reports
"cannot update lens: <reason>" instead of "Lens updated successfully!".

## Suggested fix

Collect the edited values first, run `check_physical_feasibility()` on the
result, and only then write them to the lens and save. Add a CLI test that
modifies a lens into an infeasible geometry and asserts the lens is unchanged
and not saved.

nodes.title: fix(cli): validate the whole edited lens before applying it
nodes.body:
## Description

`create_lens()` validates the finished geometry with
`check_physical_feasibility()`, but `modify_lens()` checked each field on its
own and wrote every answer into the lens as it was read. A combination whose
surfaces intersect inside the clear aperture - each radius, thickness and
diameter individually valid - was stored and saved:

```text
R1 100 -> 20, R2 -100 -> -20, t 5, D 50 -> 40
edge thickness at the 40 mm rim: -35 mm
CLI: "Lens updated successfully!"
create_lens() with the same numbers: refused
```

A partly applied edit was also left behind when a later field failed.

## What changed

- **`openlens/lens_editor.py`**
  - `modify_lens()` now collects the edits first (blank keeps the current
    value, invalid single values keep the current value).
  - It runs the same cross-parameter `check_physical_feasibility()` on the
    resulting geometry, passing the lens's parabolic/conic surfaces and clear
    aperture so mounted lenses are judged at the polished aperture.
  - Only when the combination is feasible does it write all fields and save
    once. On failure the lens is untouched and nothing is persisted.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #647

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2796 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Three tests in `tests/test_cli_modify_lens_validation.py`:

- `test_an_infeasible_edit_is_refused_and_nothing_is_applied` - the -35 mm
  edge edit leaves every field (including name, index, type and material)
  unchanged and never calls `save_lenses()`.
- `test_a_feasible_edit_is_applied_and_saved` - a valid edit is still applied
  and persisted.
- `test_an_invalid_single_field_keeps_the_current_value` - the documented
  per-field fallback still works.

The existing create-path validation, material loading, mount and panel suites
pass unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug: the CLI create-lens defaults are rejected by the CLI own feasibility check
body:
## Summary

The default values offered by the CLI's "Create new lens" prompt (R1 = 100 mm,
R2 = -100 mm, thickness = 5 mm, diameter = 50 mm) describe a lens whose
surfaces intersect inside the clear aperture: the edge thickness is -1.35 mm.
The CLI's own feasibility check rejects it, so pressing Enter on every prompt
fails with "cannot create lens: Surfaces intersect within the clear
aperture". The defaults of the GUI editor are feasible.

## Impact

- The first thing a new user does - accept the defaults - fails, and the
  error message blames the user's input rather than the defaults.
- The failure is non-obvious: every individual value is within its own
  validation range, so the user has to work out that the combination is
  impossible.

## Reproduction

```python
import builtins, os, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "/home/philip/Workspace/openLens")
from openlens.lens_editor import LensManager
from openlens.validation import check_physical_feasibility

manager = LensManager(os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "cli.db"))
answers = iter(["demo", "", "", "", "", "", "", ""])  # every prompt default
builtins.input = lambda prompt="": next(answers)
print("create_lens() with all defaults returned:", manager.create_lens())
print("default geometry feasible?", check_physical_feasibility(100.0, -100.0, 5.0, 50.0))
```

Output:

```
=== Create New Optical Lens ===
  cannot create lens: Surfaces intersect within the clear aperture (edge thickness -1.35mm <= 0). Increase center thickness, reduce diameter, or flatten the radii.
create_lens() with all defaults returned: None
default geometry feasible? (False, 'Surfaces intersect within the clear aperture (edge thickness -1.35mm <= 0). ...')
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/lens_editor.py:113-134` supplies the defaults
  (`100.0`, `-100.0`, `5.0`, `50.0`, `1.5168`).
- `openlens/lens_editor.py:143-146` then runs `check_physical_feasibility()`
  on exactly those values and rejects them, because for a biconvex lens with
  R = 100 mm the sag at h = 25 mm is 3.18 mm per surface, so a 5 mm centre
  thickness leaves a negative rim.

## Expected behaviour

The defaults offered by the prompt are a valid lens, and the create path
accepts them. If a default combination is infeasible, the prompt should
default to a feasible geometry (e.g. a smaller diameter or a larger
thickness) rather than failing.

## Suggested fix

Change the CLI defaults to a feasible set (for example D = 25 mm or t = 8 mm
with R = 100 mm) and add a test that runs the create path with all defaults
and asserts a lens is created. Consider deriving the default diameter from
the radii so the defaults stay feasible if the radii change.

nodes.title: fix(cli): use the shared constants for the create-lens defaults
nodes.body:
## Description

The create-lens prompt offered `R1 = 100`, `R2 = -100`, `t = 5`, `D = 50`.
Each value passes its own validator, but the combination has an edge thickness
of **-1.35 mm**, so the CLI's own `check_physical_feasibility()` rejected the
defaults: a new user pressing Enter on every prompt got
"cannot create lens: Surfaces intersect within the clear aperture". The GUI
uses `DEFAULT_DIAMETER = 40 mm`, which is feasible.

## What changed

- **`openlens/lens_editor.py`**
  - Import `DEFAULT_RADIUS_1`, `DEFAULT_RADIUS_2`, `DEFAULT_THICKNESS`,
    `DEFAULT_DIAMETER` and `REFRACTIVE_INDEX_BK7` from `constants`.
  - Build both the prompt labels and the accepted values from those constants,
    so the displayed default and the value cannot drift apart. The default
    diameter is now 40 mm (the feasible GUI default).
- **`tests/test_cli_create_lens_validation.py`**
  - Pressing Enter on every prompt creates a `Lens` whose edge thickness is at
    least `MIN_EDGE_THICKNESS`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #648

- [x] Added regression test that fails before this change and passes after
  - Before: `create_lens()` returns `None` for the defaults.

title: bug(gui): reordering assembly elements desyncs the flat element list from the node tree
body:
## Summary

The assembly tab's "Move element up" / "Move element down" buttons swap two
entries of `OpticalSystem.elements` - the *flat* list - and nothing else. The
node tree (`system.root`), which is the authority for the 3D tracer and for
every rebuild of the flat lists, keeps the original order, and the element
positions are not recomputed. After a reorder the flat list and the tree
describe different systems: the element positions are no longer monotonic
along the axis, the paraxial/2D analyses fail or return different numbers,
and the 3D trace still describes the old order.

## Impact

- Pressing "move up"/"move down" silently breaks the paraxial focus search
  (it returns `None` in the repro) and changes the ABCD back focal length
  while the 3D trace is unchanged, so the GUI shows contradictory results for
  the same assembly.
- The element list and the 3D visualisation can disagree with the numbers
  reported by the spot/PSF/MTF tabs.
- The reordered flat list is what gets persisted
  (`OpticalSystem.to_dict()` serialises `self.elements`), so the database
  records the new order while the in-memory tree still holds the old one.

## Reproduction

```python
from openlens.analysis.paraxial import find_paraxial_focus
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem
from openlens.tracer_3d import Ray3D, SystemRayTracer3D
from openlens.vector3 import vec3

def make_lens(name, r1, r2, n):
    return Lens(name=name, radius_of_curvature_1=r1, radius_of_curvature_2=r2,
                thickness=5.0, diameter=30.0, refractive_index=n)

system = OpticalSystem("three element")
system.add_lens(make_lens("L1", 60.0, -60.0, 1.5168), air_gap_before=0.0)
system.add_lens(make_lens("L2", -80.0, -80.0, 1.6200), air_gap_before=10.0)
system.add_lens(make_lens("L3", 100.0, -100.0, 1.5168), air_gap_before=10.0)

def tree_order(s):
    return [n.element_model.name for n, _ in s.root.get_flat_list()
            if getattr(n, "is_element", False)]

def traced_focus(s):
    tracer = SystemRayTracer3D(s)
    start = s.root.children[0].position.x
    ray = Ray3D(vec3(start - 50.0, 0.001, 0), vec3(1, 0, 0), wavelength=0.00055)
    tracer.trace_ray(ray)
    return None if ray.terminated else ray.path[-1].x

print("before:", [e.lens.name for e in system.elements], tree_order(system))
print("  positions:", [e.position for e in system.elements])
print("  ABCD BFL:", system.calculate_back_focal_length())
print("  paraxial focus:", find_paraxial_focus(system))
print("  3D traced focus:", traced_focus(system))

# exactly what assembly_tab._on_move_lens_up does
current = 1
(system.elements[current], system.elements[current - 1]) = (
    system.elements[current - 1], system.elements[current])

print("after :", [e.lens.name for e in system.elements], tree_order(system))
print("  positions:", [e.position for e in system.elements])
print("  ABCD BFL:", system.calculate_back_focal_length())
print("  paraxial focus:", find_paraxial_focus(system))
print("  3D traced focus:", traced_focus(system))
```

Output:

```
before: ['L1', 'L2', 'L3'] ['L1', 'L2', 'L3']
  positions: [0.0, 15.0, 30.0]
  ABCD BFL: 23.711880186282038
  paraxial focus: 58.39251878048472
  3D traced focus: 84.9999999857929
after : ['L2', 'L1', 'L3'] ['L1', 'L2', 'L3']
  positions: [15.0, 0.0, 30.0]
  ABCD BFL: 29.10172513820875
  paraxial focus: None
  3D traced focus: 84.9999999857929
```

The tree order is unchanged, the positions are no longer increasing along the
axis, and the flat-list analyses now describe a different system.

## Root cause

- `openlens/gui/tabs/assembly_tab.py:533-547` and `:549-563` swap entries in
  `self._optical_system.elements` only. No node in `system.root` is moved, and
  `_update_positions()` / `_rebuild_from_tree()` are not called.
- `openlens/optical_system.py:311-326` (`_rebuild_from_tree`) shows the tree is
  the authority: the flat lists are regenerated from it.
- `openlens/tracer_3d.py:720` traces `system.root.get_flat_list()`, while
  `openlens/tracer_2d.py:692` and the ABCD matrix
  (`openlens/optical_system.py:738-767`) use `system.elements`.

## Expected behaviour

Reordering an element changes the axial order of the assembly everywhere: the
node tree, the flat list, the air gaps and the element positions stay
consistent, and the 2D and 3D results describe the same system.

## Suggested fix

Reorder the node tree (move the corresponding `OpticalElement` node inside
`root.children`) and then call `_rebuild_from_tree()` / `_update_positions()`,
instead of swapping flat-list entries. Ideally the model should expose a
`move_element(index, delta)` method so the GUI does not manipulate the
internal lists at all. Add a regression test that reorders a three-element
system and asserts that the flat order equals the tree order, that the
positions are monotonic, and that the paraxial focus matches the 3D trace.

nodes.title: fix(gui): reordering an assembly must move the element in the tree
nodes.body:
## Description

The assembly tab's **Move element up / Move element down** buttons swapped two
entries of `OpticalSystem.elements` - the *flat* list - and nothing else. The
node tree (`system.root`), which is the authority for the 3D tracer and for
every rebuild of the flat lists, kept the original order, and the element
positions were not recomputed. After a reorder the two views described
different systems:

```
after the swap:
  flat order  : ['L2', 'L1', 'L3']
  tree order  : ['L1', 'L2', 'L3']
  positions   : [15.0, 0.0, 30.0]
```

Element positions were no longer monotonic along the axis and the paraxial
focus search returned `None`, while the 3D trace still described the old
order - the GUI showed contradictory results for the same assembly.

## What changed

- **`OpticalSystem.move_element(index, delta)`** - the model now owns the
  reorder. It moves the `OpticalElement` node inside its parent and exchanges
  the two axial stations, then rebuilds the flat lists from the tree. The
  spacing between the stations - the air gaps - stays what the user set,
  and only the axial component moves: the lateral offset and the tilt belong
  to the element and travel with it.
- It returns `False` (and leaves the system untouched) at either end of the
  list and when the neighbour lives in another assembly: reparenting is not a
  reorder, so the move is refused rather than guessed.
- **`openlens/gui/tabs/assembly_tab.py`** - both buttons now call
  `move_element` and do nothing when it returns `False`. The whole-system
  undo command still sees the change because `to_dict()` serialises the tree.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #649

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_move_element.py` - all 10 tests fail with
`AttributeError: 'OpticalSystem' object has no attribute 'move_element'` on
the unfixed code:

- `test_the_flat_list_and_the_tree_agree_after_a_move`
- `test_the_positions_still_increase_along_the_axis`
- `test_the_air_gaps_are_preserved`
- `test_the_alignment_follows_the_element`
- `test_the_first_element_cannot_move_up` / `test_the_last_element_cannot_move_down`
- `test_moving_down_keeps_the_positions_increasing`
- `test_the_paraxial_focus_survives_the_move` - the symptom in the report
- `test_nested_siblings_swap_inside_their_assembly`
- `test_a_move_across_an_assembly_is_refused`

Full local suite: `Ran 2696 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; 126 assembly /
optical-system / paraxial tests pass.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: bug(gui): the lens editor never sees the glass catalog because it imports a flag from the wrong module
body:
## Summary

The lens editor populates its material combo box from the glass catalog, but
it imports the availability flag from the wrong module:
`from ...material_database import MATERIAL_DB_AVAILABLE, get_material_database`.
`MATERIAL_DB_AVAILABLE` is defined in `openlens/lens.py`, not in
`openlens/material_database.py`, so the import always raises `ImportError`.
The surrounding `except Exception` swallows it, and the combo box is
silently filled from the static `DEFAULT_MATERIAL_INDICES` table instead of
the material database.

The editor therefore offers 6 entries (BK7, Fused Silica, SF11, Crown Glass,
Flint Glass, Sapphire) while the database holds 7 catalog glasses (BK7,
E-FD60, F2, FUSEDSILICA, N-BK7, S-LAH79, SF11): F2, N-BK7, S-LAH79 and
E-FD60 are unreachable from the editor, and three of the offered names
("Crown Glass", "Flint Glass", "Sapphire") are not catalog materials at all.
The static table also carries a different index for SF11 (1.78) than the
catalog (1.78472).

## Impact

- Users cannot select most catalog glasses when editing a lens; the editor
  silently offers a short, partly fictional list.
- The values shown differ from the ones the rest of the application uses for
  the same glass, which is exactly the disagreement the function's own
  docstring says it was written to remove.
- The failure is invisible: the fallback is the documented behaviour
  ("falling back to the static per-material defaults"), so nobody can tell
  that the catalog was never consulted.

## Reproduction

```python
import openlens.material_database as md
print("defines MATERIAL_DB_AVAILABLE:", hasattr(md, "MATERIAL_DB_AVAILABLE"))

from openlens.gui.widgets.lens_editor import _materials_with_indices
pairs = _materials_with_indices()
print("editor list:", [name for name, _ in pairs])

db = md.get_material_database()
catalog = [m.name for m in db.materials.values()]
print("database   :", sorted(catalog))
print("missing    :", [n for n in catalog if n not in {p[0] for p in pairs}])

try:
    from openlens.material_database import MATERIAL_DB_AVAILABLE  # noqa: F401
except Exception as exc:
    print("the editor's import raises:", type(exc).__name__, exc)
```

Output:

```
defines MATERIAL_DB_AVAILABLE: False
editor list: ['BK7', 'Fused Silica', 'SF11', 'Crown Glass', 'Flint Glass', 'Sapphire', 'Custom']
database   : ['BK7', 'E-FD60', 'F2', 'FUSEDSILICA', 'N-BK7', 'S-LAH79', 'SF11']
missing    : ['N-BK7', 'F2', 'FUSEDSILICA', 'S-LAH79', 'E-FD60']
the editor's import raises: ImportError: cannot import name 'MATERIAL_DB_AVAILABLE' from 'openlens.material_database'
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/gui/widgets/lens_editor.py:180-182` imports
  `MATERIAL_DB_AVAILABLE` from `...material_database` and gates the catalog
  lookup on it.
- `openlens/lens.py:38-44` is where `MATERIAL_DB_AVAILABLE` is actually
  defined; `openlens/material_database.py` defines no such flag.
- `openlens/gui/widgets/lens_editor.py:185-186` catches `Exception` around the
  whole block, so the `ImportError` is logged at debug level only and the
  static table is used.

## Expected behaviour

The material combo lists the glasses from the material database, with the
catalog's names and reference indices, and falls back to the static table
only when the database is genuinely unavailable.

## Suggested fix

Import the flag from the module that defines it (or drop the flag and rely on
`get_material_database()` succeeding), and narrow the `except` so an
`ImportError` of the wrong name cannot masquerade as "the catalog is
unavailable". Note that the catalog names ("FUSEDSILICA") and the static
table names ("Fused Silica") differ, so the editor also needs the same
name-resolution path the rest of the application uses (see #607). Add a test
asserting that the editor's material list contains every catalog glass.

nodes.title: fix(gui): populate the lens editor materials from the glass catalog
nodes.body:
## Description

The lens editor populates its material combo from the glass catalog, but
`_materials_with_indices()` imported `MATERIAL_DB_AVAILABLE` from
`openlens.material_database`, where it does not exist. The import always raised,
the surrounding `except Exception` swallowed it, and the combo silently fell
back to the static table. Even after fixing the import, catalog entries were
read as dicts although `list_materials()` returns strings, so the catalog still
contributed nothing.

The editor offered BK7, Fused Silica, SF11, Crown Glass, Flint Glass and
Sapphire while the catalog held BK7, E-FD60, F2, FUSEDSILICA, N-BK7, S-LAH79
and SF11: four catalog glasses were unreachable and three offered names were
not catalog materials. SF11 also used the static 1.78 instead of the catalog
index.

## What changed

- **`openlens/gui/widgets/lens_editor.py`**
  - `_materials_with_indices()` reads the names returned by
    `list_materials()` and takes each reference index from the catalog. The
    static table is used only when the database genuinely cannot be read;
    the import-flag indirection is gone.
  - `load_lens()` resolves a static display name ("Fused Silica") through the
    catalog's alias handling, so an older lens shows the canonical entry
    instead of falling through to Custom.
- **`tests/test_lens_editor_material_load.py`**
  - The "uncatalogued material" cases now use `Unobtainium`; N-BK7 is a
    catalog glass and is expected to load as such.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #650

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
  - `Ran 2801 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

Five tests in `tests/test_gui_material_catalog.py`:

- every material the catalog reports is offered by the editor;
- every offered catalog index equals `get_refractive_index(name, d-line)`
  (including SF11, which was 1.78 in the static table);
- Crown Glass, Flint Glass and Sapphire are no longer offered when the
  catalog is available;
- loading "Fused Silica" shows "FUSEDSILICA" and keeps the index read-only;
- a genuinely unknown material still falls back to Custom with an editable
  index.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

title: bug(data-loss): a library lens that is also an assembly member loses its metadata on every save
body:
## Summary

The metadata blob that the database stores for a lens has two different shapes
depending on which writer produced it, and the read path merges the whole blob
into the model's `metadata` attribute. A library lens that is also an element
of a stored assembly therefore **loses its own metadata** (the GUI's tolerance
set) on every save, because the GUI always writes the assemblies last.

- The standalone-lens writer flattens the user's `metadata` into the top
  level of the blob.
- The assembly-element writer keeps the `"metadata"` key nested one level
  deeper.
- `Lens.from_dict()` subtracts the model's own serialised keys - which
  include `"metadata"` - from the blob, so the nested user data is dropped.

The same mechanism also leaks the database's own bookkeeping (`row_type`,
`is_library`) into the user's metadata dict after a load/save cycle.

## Impact

- The tolerance set the user configured for a lens that is also used in an
  assembly is silently wiped from the database on every autosave and every
  explicit save. (This is a different layer from #618: there the GUI never
  stamps the metadata at all; here the metadata *is* stamped and then
  discarded by the storage layer.)
- The lens model's `metadata` dict - the GUI's namespace for user settings -
  ends up holding `{"is_library": 1, "row_type": "Lens"}` instead of the
  user's data.
- The outcome depends on the order of the items in one save call, so the same
  data survives or is lost depending on an implementation detail.

## Reproduction

```python
import os, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "/home/philip/Workspace/openLens")
from openlens.gui.services.library_service import LibraryService
from openlens.gui.storage import LensStorage
from openlens.lens import Lens
from openlens.optical_system import OpticalSystem

def run(order):
    path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="opencode-meta-"), "m.db")
    service = LibraryService(lambda: LensStorage(path))

    lens = Lens(name="Tol", radius_of_curvature_1=50.0, radius_of_curvature_2=-50.0,
                thickness=5.0, diameter=25.0, material="BK7")
    lens.metadata = {"tolerances": {"radius_1": {"min": 49.0, "max": 51.0}}}
    asm = OpticalSystem(name="Asm")
    asm.add_lens(lens, air_gap_before=0.0)          # the same object, as the GUI does

    items = [lens, asm] if order == "lens-first" else [asm, lens]
    service.save(items, reconcile=True)
    for item in service.load().lenses:
        print("  reloaded %-6s metadata=%s" % (item.name, item.metadata))

print("order lens-first (what the GUI does):"); run("lens-first")
print("order assembly-first:"); run("assembly-first")
```

Output:

```
order lens-first (what the GUI does):
  reloaded Tol    metadata={}
order assembly-first:
  reloaded Tol    metadata={'tolerances': {'radius_1': {'min': 49.0, 'max': 51.0}}}
```

A standalone lens (not a member of any assembly) keeps its metadata in both
orders, so the loss is specific to lenses that are also assembly members.

Bookkeeping pollution:

```python
from openlens.database import DatabaseManager
db = DatabaseManager(os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "m.db"))
db.save_library([lens.to_dict()], library_lens_ids=[lens.id], demote=True)
row = next(r for r in db.load_all() if r.get("row_type") == "Lens")
db.save_library([row], library_lens_ids=[lens.id], demote=True)   # write the row back
row2 = next(r for r in db.load_all() if r.get("row_type") == "Lens")
print(Lens.from_dict(row2).metadata)
```

Output:

```
{'is_library': 1, 'tolerances': {'radius_1': {'min': 49.0, 'max': 51.0}}, 'row_type': 'Lens'}
```

## Root cause

- `openlens/database.py:553-587` (`_save_lens_row`) builds the blob from
  "every key without a dedicated column" and only flattens the model's
  `metadata` when `flatten_metadata=True`.
- `openlens/database.py:661` (`_save_assembly_rows`) calls the same writer with
  `flatten_metadata=False`, so the assembly element's blob keeps a nested
  `"metadata"` key.
- `openlens/database.py:72-73` (`_metadata_merge`) returns the whole blob.
- `openlens/lens.py:643` (`from_dict`) removes the keys in
  `_LENS_SERIALIZED_KEYS`, which contains `"metadata"`
  (`openlens/lens.py:155`), so the nested user data is subtracted.
- `openlens/__main__.py:339` saves `self._lenses + self._assemblies`, i.e. the
  assembly write is always last and always wins.

## Expected behaviour

The user metadata of a lens survives a save/load round-trip regardless of
whether the lens also belongs to an assembly, and the model's `metadata`
attribute only ever holds user data.

## Suggested fix

Make the blob shape canonical: one writer, one reader. Always flatten the
model's `metadata` into the blob's top level, and make `_metadata_merge`
return only the keys that are not part of the model (or use an explicit
allow-list of user-metadata keys instead of "everything without a column",
which also keeps `row_type` and `is_library` out of the blob). Add a
regression test that saves a lens that is also an assembly member and asserts
its metadata survives.

nodes.title: fix(data-loss): a library lens that is also an assembly member keeps its metadata
nodes.body:
## Description

The lens row's metadata blob was built differently by the two writers: a
standalone lens folded the model's metadata into the blob's top level, an
assembly element kept it nested one level deeper. The reader subtracts the
model's own keys from the blob, and `metadata` is one of them - so the
nested copy was dropped and the user's settings (the tolerance set) were lost
on every save of a lens that belonged to an assembly:

```
the stored blob keys: [... 'metadata', ...]
reloaded lens.metadata: {}
```

## What changed

- `openlens/database.py::_save_lens_row` writes one blob shape for every
  lens: the model's metadata is always folded into the blob's top level. The
  row markers (`row_type`, `is_library`) stay out of it - they are
  bookkeeping, not user settings.
- `openlens/lens.py::Lens.from_dict` rescues a row written by an older
  version, whose blob still carries the nested copy, instead of dropping it.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #651

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a regression test that fails before this change and passes after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`

New test module `tests/test_library_member_metadata.py` (all three tests fail
on the unfixed code):

- `test_the_metadata_survives_the_save`
- `test_the_blob_has_one_shape`
- `test_a_legacy_nested_blob_is_rescued`

Full local suite: `Ran 2636 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`, `black` clean,
`ruff` clean, `flake8` clean, `mypy` clean.
